events.title: Paul Revere Is Born
events.description: Paul Revere, an American patriot famous for making his midnight ride through the Massachusetts countryside to warn people about incoming British troops, is born in Boston.

events.title: The Emancipation Proclamation Is Issued
events.description: At the urging of Black leaders, President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation, which freed all enslaved people in the Confederate States.

events.title: Potlatch Ban Goes Into Effect In Canada
events.description: The Potlatch Ban goes into effect in Canada. The law forbad the practice of potlatch, or ceremonies held by First Nations, until 1951. This ban significantly impacted the production of totem poles among Pacific Northwest tribes.

events.title: Randolph McCoy's Cabin Is Attacked By Hatfields
events.description: A group of Hatfield family members attack McCoy family patriarch Randolph McCoy's cabin, killing two of his children, badly beating his wife, and burning the cabin to the ground, in one of the worst moments of violence in the Hatfields and McCoys feud.

events.title: Ellis Island Opens
events.description: The Ellis Island immigration station opens in New York Harbor. Over the next 60 years, more than 12 million immigrants would enter the United States through this facility. The first immigrant to pass through Ellis Island on its opening day was Annie Moore, a teenager from County Cork, Ireland.

events.title: J.D. Salinger, Author Of Catcher In The Rye, Is Born
events.description: J.D. Salinger, author of Catcher In The Rye, is born in New York City. Before becoming a famous author, Salinger served as a soldier in the Second World War. While abroad, he made friends with other writers like Ernest Hemingway with whom he shared his writing. In 1951, a publishing house decided to publish The Catcher In The Rye, Salinger's most famous piece to date. The book spoke to generations of young people, and has even inspired acts of political violence. Today, it remains the second most taught novel in American schools.

events.title: The Rosewood Massacre Begins
events.description: The aftermath of the Rosewood Massacre as seen on January 9, 1923.

events.title: Fidel Castro Seizes Power
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesCrowds celebrate the removal of Fulgencio Batista and the arrival of Fidel Castro's rebels in Havana.

events.title: Jules Brunet, "The Last Samurai" Is Born In France
events.description: Jules Brunet (front row, second to left) fought alongside Tokugawa samurai during Japan's Boshin War.

events.title: Louis Daguerre Takes The First Known Photo Of The Moon
events.description: French photographer and inventor Louis Daguerre, creator of the daguerreotype photographic process, uses this method to take the first known photo of Earth's moon. Unfortunately, Daguerre's laboratory burned down just two months later, destroying his records and the image of the moon. The next year, John W. Draper took the first surviving daguerreotype of the moon from his rooftop watchtower at New York University.

events.title: TIME Names Adolf Hitler "Man of the Year
events.description: The Duke and Duchess of Windsor with Adolf Hitler in Munich.

events.title: All 33 Members Of The Duquesne Spy Ring Are Sentenced
events.description: The 33 members of the Duquesne Spy Ring are sentenced to a total of more than 300 years in prison. The Duquesne Spy Ring was a German espionage network led by Fritz Joubert Duquesne that worked within the United States during World War II. Its members were all found guilty in the largest espionage case that ended with convictions in American history.

events.title: The "Yorkshire Ripper" Is Arrested
events.description: Express Newspapers/Getty ImagesPeter Sutcliffe, a.k.a. the Yorkshire Ripper, on his wedding day on August 10, 1974.

events.title: Martin Luther Is Excommunicated From The Catholic Church
events.description: Pope Leo X issues the papal bull Decet Romanum Pontificem, excommunicating Martin Luther from the Catholic Church. Three years earlier, Luther would write his 95 Theses, protesting certain practices of the Church, which the Pope deemed as heresy. Luther's excommunication led to the advancement of the Lutheran church and the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: J.R.R. Tolkien Is Born
events.description: J.R.R. Tolkien, author of the The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings series, is born to English parents in South Africa. Tolkien became a professor of Old English at the University of Oxford, where he began writing his famous fantasy tales.

events.title: King Tutankhamun's Sarcophagus Is Discovered
events.description: MOHAMED EL-SHAHED/AFP/Getty ImagesThe linen-wrapped mummy of King Tutankhamun, displayed in his climate-controlled glass case.

events.title: The Sullivan Brothers Enlist In The Navy
events.description: The Sullivan brothers — George, Francis, Joseph, Madison, and Albert — enlist in the U.S. Navy. After appealing to the Navy to serve together, they were assigned to the same ship, the USS Juneau, which was tragically destroyed by a Japanese torpedo in the Pacific in November 1942.

events.title: John Wayne Gacy Murders His First Victim
events.description: John Wayne Gacy as Pogo the Clown.

events.title: A Chinese Spacecraft Lands On The Far Side Of The Moon
events.description: At 2:26 a.m. UTC, the Chinese spacecraft Chang'e-4 becomes the first to ever touch down on the mysterious dark side of the moon. Because it takes the moon just as long to rotate on its axis as it does to orbit the Earth, its far side is never visible from Earth. Shortly after landing, the spacecraft's rover, Yutu-2, took the first detailed photos of the far side's surface.

events.title: Isaac Newton Is Born
events.description: Portrait of Isaac Newton by M. Keynes. Oil on canvas.

events.title: Charles Stratton Is Born
events.description: Charles Stratton, a famous sideshow performer known as "General Tom Thumb" because of his small stature, is born in Bridgeport, Connecticut.

events.title: Solomon Northup Gains His Freedom
events.description: Solomon Northup is released from slavery and becomes a free man once again. Northup was born free in New York, but in 1841, two white men offered him a job as a fiddler for their traveling circus. They then kidnapped him and sold him into slavery in Louisiana, where he remained for 12 years. Northup went on to write the famous memoir 12 Years a Slave.

events.title: Juliane Koepcke Is Rescued From The Peruvian Jungle
events.description: Juliane Koepscke is rescued after spending 11 days in the Peruvian jungle. While traveling with her mother to Peru, Juliane Koepcke's plane hit a massive thunderstorm and broke into pieces after being struck by lightning.

events.title: Ted Bundy Attacks His First Victim
events.description: Bettmann/Contributor/Getty ImagesTed Bundy during his trial in 1978.

events.title: The Burj Khalifa Opens In Dubai
events.description: The world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa, opens in the United Arab Emirates. Standing at 2,722 feet tall, the skyscraper stretches more than half a mile into the sky. It beat the previous record holder, Taipei 101, by over 1,000 feet. The Burj Khalifa is a multi-use building that features apartments, restaurants, a hotel, and office space inside.

events.title: Pope Clement VII Tells Henry VIII He May Not Remarry
events.description: A portrait of Henry VIII.

events.title: Robert-François Damiens Attempts to Assassinate King Louis XV
events.description: Louis XV of France is stabbed in the chest with a penknife while entering his carriage at the Palace of Versailles. Robert-François Damiens was arrested for attempted regicide. At the time, the traditional punishment for regicide was drawing and quartering, in which an executioner publicly disembowels and dismembers a criminal. Three months later, Damiens became the last person in France to be executed in this manner.

events.title: Bonnie And Clyde Meet
events.description: Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow meet for the first time — and soon embark on a crime spree as "Bonnie and Clyde."

events.title: Construction Begins On The Golden Gate Bridge
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesWorkers standing on one edge of the future Golden Gate Bridge in 1935.

events.title: Amelia Earhart Is Legally Declared Dead
events.description: Amelia Earhart with her Lockheed Electra in 1937.

events.title: Police Search Joyce Vincent's Apartment In London
events.description: Police find the body of Joyce Vincent in her London apartment. In one of the most bizarre cases in history, police find the badly decomposed body of Joyce Vincent laying on her apartment floor. An autopsy would confirm that she had died two years prior.

events.title: Joan of Arc Is Born
events.description: Joan of Arc was born a peasant and had no military training when she led French forces to defeat the English at the historic Battle of Orleans in 1429.

events.title: Henry VIII Marries His Fourth Wife, Anne Of Cleves
events.description: After divorcing his first wife, beheading his second, and losing his third, Henry VIII marries his fourth wife, Anne of Cleves. The English king was disappointed with Anne since he didn't think she looked like her portrait and she didn't speak much English. After six months, they divorced.

events.title: Former President Theodore Roosevelt Dies
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt posing alongside a large globe in 1903.

events.title: Mother Teresa Arrives In Kolkata, India
events.description: A young nun born Agnes Gonxha Bojaxhiu, later known as Mother Teresa, arrives in Kolkata, India. She spent nearly two decades teaching girls from poor families before branching out from the school to educate children living in slums. In 1979, she won the Nobel Peace Prize for Peace and was canonized as a saint in 2016.

events.title: Ho Chi Minh Wins Vietnam's First-Ever General Election
events.description: Ho Chin Minh's Viet Minh party (League for the Independence of Vietnam) wins Vietnam's first-ever general election. Though Ho hoped to lay the groundwork for an independent Vietnam, France integrated the country into the French Union that March. Conflicts between the French and the Vietnamese escalated into the First Indochina War that December.

events.title: Nancy Kerrigan Is Attacked
events.description: American figure skater Nancy Kerrigan is injured by attackers in Detroit, Michigan. Kerrigan's assault had been planned by Jeff Gillooly, the ex-husband of Kerrigan's fellow skater Tonya Harding.

events.title: Protestors Storm The U.S. Capitol
events.description: TapTheForwardAssist/Wikimedia CommonsSupporters of Donald Trump gather at the U.S. Capitol.

events.title: Galileo Discovers Jupiter's Moons
events.description: Stefano Bianchetti/CorbisGalileo Galilei is one of the most famous astronomers in the world.

events.title: The First 'Discovery' Of Bigfoot
events.description: Explorer David Thompson finds strange footprints in Alberta, Canada, which measure "fourteen inches in length by eight inches in breadth." Some have taken Thompson's discovery as proof that Bigfoot exists. Since then, people across the world have reported finding similar prints and even catching glimpses of the elusive beast.

events.title: Asa-Harmon McCoy Is Killed
events.description: Asa-Harmon McCoy is murdered in Pike County, Kentucky, arguably triggering the infamous Hatfield and McCoy feud.

events.title: Writer Zora Neale Hurston Is Born
events.description: Zora Neale Hurston is born in Notasulga, Alabama. The daughter of slaves, she went on to write novels, short stories, and plays, about Black life in the American South and participate in the Harlem Renaissance. Her most famous work is the 1937 novel Their Eyes Were Watching God.

events.title: Inventor Nikola Tesla Dies In New York City
events.description: Nikola Tesla died impoverished and alone in 1943.

events.title: Vietnamese Troops Overthrow Pol Pot And Khmer Rouge
events.description: Pol Pot liked to have his picture taken in humble surroundings. This was part of a nationwide effort to win over peasants.

events.title: President Bill Clinton's Senate Impeachment Trial Begins
events.description: Bill Clinton and Monica Lewinsky's affair captivated the nation and launched an impeachment trial.

events.title: Rosemary Kennedy Dies
events.description: Rosemary Kennedy, the first born daughter of Rose and Joe Kennedy and sister of JFK, dies at the age of 86 in Wisconsin after spending most of her life in an institution following a botched lobotomy in 1941.

events.title: Two Gunmen Attack The Charlie Hebdo Office In Paris
events.description: Two gunmen, angry at depictions of the Prophet Mohammad in the French publication Charlie Hebdo, attack its offices. Brothers Chérif and Saïd Kouachi killed twelve people with assault rifles before fleeing the scene. In the aftermath, the hashtag #JeSuisCharlie trended worldwide in solidarity with the victims.

events.title: Italian Astronomer Galileo Galilei Dies
events.description: Galileo Galilei dies in Arcetri, Italy at the age of 77. Found guilty of heresy in 1633 because he claimed that the Earth orbited the sun, the astronomer died while under house arrest. Three hundred and fifty years later, the Catholic Church apologized and admitted Galilei was right.

events.title: The German Coast Slave Uprising Begins
events.description: The largest slave revolt in American history begins on a plantation near New Orleans. Led by a man named Charles Deslondes, the uprising began with just 25 people but quickly snowballed as the men marched toward the city. State militia clashed with the hundreds of slaves two days later, suppressing the revolt and executing dozens of participants.

events.title: Elvis Presley Is Born
events.description: PixabayElvis Presley's style, voice, and performances enchanted Americans.

events.title: Britain Announces First World War II Food Rations
events.description: The British government introduces food rations as Europe plunges into World War II. Men, women, and children were given a ration book with coupons that they could use to purchase items like meat, cheese, and sugar. The rationing system continued into the 1950s.

events.title: The Watergate Trial Begins
events.description: The Watergate trial eventually led to Richard Nixon's resignation in August 1974.

events.title: El Chapo Is Recaptured After A Prison Escape
events.description: Drug lord Joaquin 'El Chapo' Guzman is recaptured six months after escaping from a maximum-security prison in Mexico. After escaping through a tunnel in the prison showers, Guzman was re-arrested in the city of Los Mochis. He's currently serving a life sentence in a Colorado supermax prison.

events.title: Joan Of Arc's Trial Begins
events.description: The trial of Joan of Arc begins in Rouen, France. Driven by "divine instruction," Joan had supported the claim of Charles VII to the French throne. But the English captured her in 1430, accused her of heresy, found her guilty, and burned her at the stake on May 30.

events.title: Diane De Poitiers, Mistress of Henry II Of France, Is Born
events.description: Diane de Poitiers, mistress and political advisor of Henry II of France, is born in Saint-Vallier.

events.title: President Richard Nixon Is Born
events.description: and Records AdministrationRichard Nixon was the 37th president of the United States and the first to resign.

events.title: Dorothea Puente Is Born
events.description: Dorthea Puente is born in Redlands, California. Known for her innocent grandmother look, Puente shocked the city of Sacramento after police found seven bodies buried in her backyard. Known in her community as a kind woman, Puente frequently opened her home to "shadow people," individuals who lived on the margins of society. An investigation would find Dorothea Puente guilty of murdering at least nine of her tenants and cashing in their social security checks. Her crimes are some of the most notable in the city of Sacramento's history.

events.title: 'Monster' Murderer Aileen Wuornos Arrested
events.description: Serial killer Aileen Wuornos — whose story was depicted in the 2003 film Monster — is arrested in Port Orange, Florida. Wuornos later admitted to killing at least seven motorists who she claimed had attempted to rape her. She was sentenced to death and executed on October 9, 2002.

events.title: Steve Jobs Introduces The First iPhone
events.description: Blake Patterson/Wikimedia CommonsSteve Jobs revolutionized technology and culture when he introduced the iPhone.

events.title: Julius Caesar Crosses The Rubicon
events.description: General Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon river into Rome with an army, an act prohibited under Roman law. His crossing sparked the five-year Roman Civil War which established Caesar as "dictator for life." It also marked the end of the Roman Republic and the beginning of the Roman Empire.

events.title: Thomas Paine Publishes 'Common Sense'
events.description: Writer Thomas Paine publishes Common Sense, a pro-independence pamphlet on the eve of the Revolutionary War. Paine's highly popular pamphlet sold one copy for every five people in the colonies and urged colonists to choose independence over monarchy. "We have it in our power," he wrote, "to begin the world over again."

events.title: The London Underground Begins Operations
events.description: A tube station in 1900.

events.title: John D. Rockefeller Founds Standard Oil Company
events.description: AFP/Getty ImagesJohn D. Rockefeller controlled, at his peak, over 90 percent of all the oil in the United States.

events.title: The Treaty Of Versailles Takes Effect
events.description: The Treaty of Versailles goes into effect. Signed six months earlier at the Palace of Versailles in Paris, France, it marked the end of World War I and made peace between the Allied powers and Germany. However, the Treaty's harsh terms triggered resentment among Germans and later helped fuel the rise of Adolf Hitler.

events.title: Fashion Icon Coco Chanel Dies
events.description: Three outfits designed by Coco Chanel in 1917.

events.title: Alexander Hamilton Is Born
events.description: Alexander Hamilton circa 1792.

events.title: Francis Scott Key Dies
events.description: A portrait of Francis Scott Key circa 1825.

events.title: Theodore Roosevelt Declares Grand Canyon A National Monument
events.description: President Theodore Roosevelt designates 800,000 acres of the Grand Canyon as a national monument, saying: "Let this great wonder of nature remain as it now is." Environmental conservation was a cornerstone of Roosevelt's presidency, as he would protect 230 million acres of land.

events.title: The Perron Family Moves Into The Conjuring House
events.description: YoutubeThe Perron family's home in Rhode Island where they claimed they witnessed paranormal activity.

events.title: Illinois Governor Commutes 167 Death Row Prisoners' Sentences
events.description: Illinois Governor George Ryan commutes the death sentences of all 167 death row inmates in the state. Calling the system "haunted by the demon of error," and as "arbitrary as who gets hit by a bolt of lightning," he made the announcement just a few days before leaving office. Illinois subsequently abolished the death penalty in 2011.

events.title: John Hancock Is Born
events.description: Boston Museum of Fine Arts John Hancock, oil on canvas by John Singleton Copley, 1765.

events.title: Anglo-Zulu War Begins
events.description: The Anglo-Zulu War begins in South Africa. After the British North America Act of 1867 granted Canada independence, leaders in the Zulu Kingdom of South Africa believed a combination of military campaigns and political appeals would grant them the same opportunity. Britain sent troops the the region after peace talks failed, and bloody battles took place for nearly five months. In the end, British troops prevailed, and the Zulu kingdom was portioned.

events.title: Bass Reeves Dies
events.description: Bass Reeves, the Black Wild West lawman who purportedly arrested 3,000 outlaws during his career, dies of Bright's disease in Muskogee, Oklahoma, at the age of 71.

events.title: Big Four Leaders Meet In Paris
events.description: The "Big Four" leaders from left to right: Prime Minister David Lloyd George of Great Britain, Prime Minister Vittorio Emanuele Orlando of Italy, Premier Georges Clemenceau of France, President Woodrow Wilson of the United States of America.

events.title: Christa Pike Murders Colleen Slemmer
events.description: YouTubeChrista Pike was just 18 when she murdered Colleen Slemmer.

events.title: A Magnitude 7.0 Earthquake Hits Haiti
events.description: A devastating magnitude 7.0 earthquake strikes Haiti. One of the world's worst natural disasters, it displaced a million people and killed somewhere between 40,000 and 316,000 people. Haitians also suffered in the weeks that followed as a cholera outbreak killed several thousands more.

events.title: Émile Zola Exposes The Drefyus Affair
events.description: Novelist Émile Zola publishes his famous "J'accuse!" letter. In this open letter to the president published in L'Aurore, Zola accused the French government of antisemitism in the case of Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish army officer accused of treason. Dreyfus would later be exonerated, but not before spending five years at the notoriously brutal Devil's Island penal colony.

events.title: Johnny Cash Performs At Folsom State Prison
events.description: Silver Screen Collection/Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesJohnny Cash performing in 1965.

events.title: Amber Hagerman Is Kidnapped
events.description: Nine-year-old Amber Hagerman is kidnapped in Arlington, Texas by a stranger in a black pickup truck. Four days later, her body was found in a stream. Though Hagerman's killer has never been found, her kidnapping inspired the AMBER Alert system that's used to find abducted children to this day.

events.title: Serial Killer Harold Shipman Is Found Dead In Prison
events.description: Greater Manchester Police/Getty ImagesHarold Shipman, nicknamed "Dr. Death," was an English doctor who killed as many as 250 of his patients, most of whom were elderly women, by giving them lethal overdoses of pain medication.

events.title: The Costa Concordia Sinks Off Italian Coast
events.description: Rvongher / Wikimedia CommonsThe Costa Concordia on the day after its devastating sinking.

events.title: Mark Antony Is Born
events.description: Carole Raddato/Wikimedia CommonsA bust possibly depicting Roman leader Mark Antony.

events.title: Henry III marries Eleanor of Provence
events.description: King Henry III of England marries Eleanor of Provence at Canterbury Cathedral. Henry was 28; Eleanor was just 12. They would have five children together, including future king Edward I of England.

events.title: Lewis Carroll Dies
events.description: Lewis Carroll's children's stories became enduring classics.

events.title: Ans Van Dijk Is Executed
events.description: Ans Van Dijk, a Nazi collaborator who some believe led the Nazis to Anne Frank and her family, is executed by firing squad at the age of 42.

events.title: The Human 'Be-In' Launches The Summer Of Love
events.description: The Human Be-In featured Timothy Leary, Allen Ginsberg, the Grateful Dead, and Jefferson Airplane.

events.title: Mary Jane Rathbun Is Arrested
events.description: Mary Jane Rathbun, otherwise known as Brownie Mary, is arrested at her San Francisco home after baking marijuana brownies. She would later pass out her cannabis baked goods to AIDS and cancer patients before successfully advocating for the legalization of medical marijuana in California.

events.title: Beloved British Actor Alan Rickman Dies
events.description: Alan Rickman, best known for portraying Severus Snape in the Harry Potter films dies. He was 69 years old. He died of pancreatic cancer, a diagnosis he kept private.

events.title: Jordan Turpin Escapes House Of Horrors
events.description: Jordan Turpin escapes from her family's house of horrors in California. In harrowing police body cam footage, observers can see just how terrified Jordan Turpin was after she escaped her family's home, ran out into the street, and called police using a phone she had secretly purchased. She relayed to the officer how her siblings were starved, beaten, and chained up. Police officers eventually validated these claims after searching the home and finding indescribable conditions there.

events.title: Elizabeth I Is Crowned Queen Of England
events.description: Queen Elizabeth I ruled England for 44 years.

events.title: The First Afrikaans Newspaper Is Published In South Africa
events.description: The first newspaper written in Afrikaans is published in South Africa. Called the Die Afrikaanse Patriot, it faced criticism from those who didn't believe that Afrikaans was a "real language." Yet subscriptions to the paper quickly grew from 50 to 3,000 over three years, and the newspaper remained in circulation until it shut down in 1904.

events.title: The Boston Molasses Flood Takes Place
events.description: Boston Public Library/FlickrThe disaster made headlines the following day, superseding news of the latest U.S. state to ratify prohibition. The death toll eventually rose to 21.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Is Born
events.description: Stephen F. Somerstein/Getty ImagesMartin Luther King Jr. was the most prominent leaders of the American civil rights movement.

events.title: The "Black Dahlia" Is Found Dead
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesElizabeth Short was just 22 years old when she was gruesomely murdered in Los Angeles in 1947.

events.title: The 'BTK Killer' Murders His First Victims
events.description: Dennis Rader kills his first victims, Joseph and Julie Otero, along with their two children Josephine and Joseph, in Witchita, Kansas. Known as the BTK Killer — for his method of binding, torturing, and killing his victims — Rader went on to kill six more.

events.title: Actor Brad Renfro Dies
events.description: Actor Brad Renfro, who got his start at just 10 years old in Joel Schumacher's The Client, died from an accidental drug overdose. Renfro played many prominent roles in '90s films, including Huckleberry Finn in Tom and Huck. Unfortunately, the actor also struggled with substance abuse from a young age. He was 25 years old when he died.

events.title: The 'Miracle On The Hudson' Takes Place
events.description: Pilot Sully Sullenberger safely lands United Airways Flight 1549 on the Hudson River near New York City after the plane hit a flock of geese in the so-called "Miracle on the Hudson."

events.title: Augustus Becomes The First Emperor Of The Roman Empire
events.description: Octavian, dubbed "Augustus," takes power over the Roman Empire. The heir and successor of Julius Caesar, Augustus had long battled Mark Antony for total power in Rome. Having defeated Antony, Augustus went on to rule for four decades, establishing a powerful empire that lasted in various forms for roughly 1,500 years.

events.title: Ivan The Terrible Becomes Czar Of Russia
events.description: Ivan the Terrible developed a violent reputation during his long reign.

events.title: Louis XVI Is Sentenced To Death
events.description: Executioner Charles-Henri Sanson shows Louis XVI's head to the crowd just after his beheading.

events.title: Prohibition Of Alcohol In The United States Is Ratified
events.description: The U.S. Congress officially ratifies the 18th Amendment to the Constitution, prohibiting the production and sale of alcoholic beverages. After prohibition went into effect a year and a day later, sheriffs, police officers, and federal agents across the country began confiscating and dumping untold quantities of alcohol. From New York to California, bottles were emptied down storm drains while barrels were smashed with axes and picks.

events.title: Albert Fish Is Executed
events.description: Albert Fish is executed by electric chair at the age of 65 at Sing Sing Prison in New York. A vicious serial killer, rapist, and cannibal, Fish brutally murdered at least three children between 1924 and 1928. And although it remains unverified, Fish himself claimed to have taken as many as 100 victims.

events.title: Operation Desert Storm Begins
events.description: Steve Liss/Getty ImagesThree men reading about the commencement of Operation Desert Storm.

events.title: El Salvadorian Civil War Ends
events.description: The El Salvadorian Civil War ends, resulting in the signing of the Chapultepec Peace Accords in Mexico City. The war began after a 1979 coup and the subsequent murder of anti-coup protestors and activists. From this year until the signing of the peace accords, an estimated 75,000 people died in the conflict.

events.title: The Papacy Returns To Italy
events.description: The papacy, after spending decades in Avignon, France, is returned to Italy by order of Pope Gregory XI.

events.title: Benjamin Franklin Is Born
events.description: Benjamin Franklin, John Adams, and Thomas Jefferson review a draft of the Declaration of Independence in 1776./span>

events.title: Conjoined Twins Chang and Eng Bunker Die
events.description: Conjoined twins Chang and Eng Bunker die at the age of 62 in North Carolina. Chang died first of a blood clot, and Eng died soon afterward.

events.title: Queen Liliuokalani Of Hawaii Is Overthrown
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesQueen Liliuokalani was overthrown with the tacit support of the American government.

events.title: Prohibition Goes Into Effect
events.description: Prohibition begins in the United States as the 18th amendment goes into effect. The new law — which banned the manufacture, transportation, and sale of intoxicating liquors — resulted in the proliferation of illegal bootlegging by gangsters like Al Capone, and the loss of millions of dollars in tax revenue. It lasted until 1933 with the ratification of the 21st amendment.

events.title: Betty White Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesWhen asked if there was one thing in Hollywood that she hadn't done yet that she'd like to do, her response was, "Robert Redford."

events.title: Patrice Lumumba Is Assassinated
events.description: Douglas Miller/Keystone/Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesPatrice Lumumba in July 1960, about six months before his assassination.

events.title: The Monica Lewinsky Scandal Breaks
events.description: The Monica Lewinsky scandal breaks after the Drudge Report publishes a story saying that Newsweek was withholding information about Lewinsky's affair with President Bill Clinton. Indeed, Lewinsky, a White House intern, and Clinton, the married president, had an affair that started in November 1995. The subsequent scandal engulfed the country and led to Clinton's acquittal at an impeachment trial in February 1999.

events.title: Henry VII Marries Elizabeth Of York
events.description: King Henry VII marries Elizabeth of York at Westminster Abbey. A descendant of the House of Lancaster, Henry had triumphed over Richard III of the House of York at the Battle of Bosworth. His defeat of Richard, and marriage to Elizabeth, united the two houses and ended the War of the Roses.

events.title: Anna Haining Bates Gives Birth To World's Largest Baby
events.description: Anna Haining Bates, one of the world's tallest women, gives birth to the world's largest baby. The baby, nicknamed "Babe," weighed 22 pounds and measured 28 inches tall at birth.

events.title: A.A. Milne Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA.A. Milne and his son, Christopher Robin, in 1925.

events.title: The Endurance Gets Trapped In Ice
events.description: Ernest Shackleton's ship, Endurance, gets trapped in ice the Weddell Sea while exploring Antarctica.

events.title: The Battle Of Hayes Takes Place
events.description: Members of the Klu Klux Klan and the Lumbee tribe clash in Maxton, North Carolina in the so-called Battle of Hayes Pond. The KKK had come to Maxton to intimidate the indigenous population, but the Lumbee — many of whom were WWII veterans — stood up to them. Outnumbering the KKK 500 to 1, they stole the KKK's banner, cross, and PA system as their members fled.

events.title: The 'Boston Strangler' Is Sentenced To Life In Prison
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesAlbert DeSalvo confessed to being the Boston Strangler and was linked by DNA to one of the victims, though some believe that the murders were committed by more than one person.

events.title: The Sierra Leone Civil War Ends
events.description: The Sierra Leone Civil War ends. The conflict, which was waged between rebels of the Revolutionary United Front and supporters of President Joseph Saidu Momoh, raged for almost 11 years. It resulted in between 50,000 and 200,000, as well as widespread raping and the use of child soldiers.

events.title: Henry V Captures Normandy
events.description: Henry V captures the capital of Normandy during the 100 Years' War. Henry, the king of England, besieged the Norman capital of Rouen at the end of July 1418. By January, the French surrendered, and Henry went on to capture most of the rest of Normandy as well as large swaths of France.

events.title: Henry Howard, Earl Of Surrey, Is Executed
events.description: Henry Howard was found guilty of treason and beheaded.

events.title: Edgar Allan Poe Is Born
events.description: A daguerreotype of Edgar Allan Poe in the spring of 1849, just six months before his death.

events.title: L'Auto Announces The First Tour De France
events.description: French magazine L'Auto announces the first Tour de France. The three-year-old magazine had struggled to gain subscribers since its founding and decided to hold a bicycle race as a way to boost sales. It was a hit, and the Tour de France continues to this day.

events.title: The First Reported Sighting Of A Crop Circle In Tully, Australia
events.description: Australian banana farmer George Pedley notices a large, circular area of his field has been flattened — in the same spot where he claimed to have seen a "vapor-like" saucer lift off. Pedley dubbed it a "saucer nest," but it really marks the first reported discovery of a crop circle.

events.title: Anthony Casso Is Arrested
events.description: A surveillance image of Anthony Casso from the 1980s.

events.title: King Edward II Is Deposed
events.description: King Edward II of England is deposed and replaced with his teenage son, Edward III. The campaign to remove the king from power was led by his own wife, Isabelle, who invaded England in 1326 with the help of Roger Mortimer, possibly her lover. Edward II died less than a year later and the timing of his death has led some historians to speculate that he was murdered.

events.title: King George V Dies
events.description: Print Collector/The Print Collector/Getty ImagesKing George V's death was hastened by a possibly fatal injection of drugs.

events.title: Nazi Leaders Discuss 'Final Solution' At Wannsee Conference
events.description: The Wannsee Conference is held among Nazi leaders in Berlin, Germany. Convened by Reinhard Heydrich, chief of the Reich Security Main Office (RSHA), the purpose of the meeting was to secure support for the Nazi's "Final Solution," the systematic murder of Europe's population of 11 million Jews. By the end of the Holocaust, some six million Jews had been killed.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Is Inaugurated
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJohn F. Kennedy speaking at his inauguration in Washington D.C. 1961.

events.title: Audrey Hepburn Dies
events.description: Audrey Hepburn, famed actress and humanitarian, dies in Switzerland. Born and raised in an aristocratic family, Hepburn spent her time ballet dancing and acting in plays and films. Her first big role was in Roman Holiday in 1953. She later went on to star in several Hollywood blockbusters, including Breakfast at Tiffany's and Sabrina. Today she is one of only 18 people today that hold an Oscar, Grammy, Emmy, and Tony awards. After her career in Hollywood, Hepburn devoted herself to the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF).

events.title: Louis XVI Is Executed
events.description: Louis XVI is executed by guillotine in Paris at the age of 38. The French king had been found guilty of high treason by the National Convention during the French Revolution and sentenced to death.

events.title: Vladimir Lenin Dies
events.description: Universal History Archive/Getty ImagesVladimir Lenin in Moscow's Red Square in 1919.

events.title: Charles Starkweather Murders His Girlfriend's Family
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesCaril Ann Fugate and Charles Starkweather before they went on their infamous killing spree.

events.title: Actor Carl Switzer Is Fatally Shot
events.description: Actor Carl Switzer, best known for playing "Alfalfa" in Our Gang, is shot to death over a dispute about a dog in Mission Hills, California.

events.title: The Battle Of Khe Sanh Begins
events.description: Bettmann Archive/Getty ImagesU.S. Marines at Khe Sanh during the siege.

events.title: First Commercial Concorde Flight Takes Off
events.description: The first commercial Concorde flight takes off from Heathrow Airport in London. After 12 years of joint research from both British and French engineers, the sound barrier-breaking plane was ready for commercial use. The Concorde planes flew 1,350 miles an hour while cruising, cutting typical travel time in half.

events.title: The First Swiss Guards Arrive In Vatican City
events.description: The first Swiss guardsmen, numbering 150, arrive in Vatican City. Suggested by Bishop Matthäus Schiner, on behalf of Pope Julius II, the Swiss Guards were put in place to guard the pope. Their service continues to this day.

events.title: Philip Hamilton Is Born
events.description: Philip Hamilton, the first child of Alexander Hamilton and Eliza Schuyler Hamilton, is born in Albany, New York.

events.title: Queen Victoria Dies
events.description: Bassano/Spencer Arnold/Getty ImagesQueen Victoria's death heralded the end of the Victorian Age.

events.title: The Bloody Sunday Massacre Takes Place
events.description: Thousands of workers led by priest Georgy Apollonovich Gapon march to the Winter Palace in St. Petersburg, Russia. The workers, believing that Czar Nicholas II was unaware of their brutal working conditions, wished only to present a petition. But Russian soldiers fired upon the crowd, killing hundreds in a massacre dubbed "Bloody" or "Red" Sunday.

events.title: Apple Starts Selling Macintosh
events.description: The first Apple Macintosh computers are sold. In a famous Superbowl ad a few days before, Apple announced: "Apple will introduce Macintosh. And you'll see why 1984 won't be like '1984'."

events.title: Budd Dwyer Dies By Suicide On Live TV
events.description: R. Budd Dwyer warns others to stay back just seconds before fatally shooting himself in front of television cameras on January 22, 1987.

events.title: Heath Ledger Is Found Dead In His New York Apartment
events.description: Carlo Allegri/Getty ImagesHeath Ledger in 2006.

events.title: King Ferdinand II Dies
events.description: De Agostini/Getty ImagesKing Ferdinand II ruled for over 30 years.

events.title: The Deadliest Earthquake In History Strikes Shaanxi Province In China
events.description: An earthquake strikes Shaanxi province in northern China. Believed to be the strongest earthquake in human history, the quake had an estimated magnitude of eight. It injured or killed some 830,000 people, reducing the population of Shaanxi and a neighboring province by an estimated 60 percent.

events.title: The Principality Of Liechtenstein Is Founded
events.description: The principality of Liechtenstein is founded. Made up of the two lordships of the Holy Roman Empire, Vaduz, and Schellenberg, Liechtenstein became independent in 1866. Today, it boasts a population of less than 40,000.

events.title: The Marias Massacre
events.description: U.S. Army soldiers perpetrated one of the worst massacres of the Indian Wars when they slaughtered approximately 200 men, women, and children of the Blackfoot tribe in present-day Montana. Though they had actually been ordered to attack a different camp, the soldiers stormed into the settlement and used guns, butcher knives, axes, and torches to murder everyone before destroying the camp entirely.

events.title: Jerusalem Becomes The Capital Of Israel
events.description: The Knesset, Israel's parliament, votes to make Jerusalem the capital of Israel a year and a half after the State of Israel was founded. Following the 60-2 vote, the legislators declared "Jerusalem is, and has always been, the capital of Israel." Though Israelis claim the city as their capital to this day, Palestinians claim that East Jerusalem is the capital of the Palestinian state.

events.title: Humans Explore The Deepest Point Of Ocean
events.description: Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh during their historic descent.

events.title: Roman Emperor Caligula Is Assassinated
events.description: Heritage Art/Heritage Images via Getty ImagesA medal depicting Caligula.

events.title: Gold Is Discovered In California
events.description: A carpenter named James Wilson Marshall finds gold flakes in the American River near Coloma, California. Marshall's discovery launched the California Gold Rush, during which thousands of hopeful gold miners flooded the state. Up until 1855, when the gold rush ended, $2 billion worth of gold was found.

events.title: Maria Tallchief Is Born
events.description: Jack Mitchell/Getty ImagesMaria Tallchief at the NYC Ballet. September 19, 1963.

events.title: Winston Churchill Dies
events.description: The British Prime Minister from 1940 to 1945, and again from 1951 to 1955, Winston Churchill steered England through the stormy days of World War II.

events.title: Ted Bundy Is Executed
events.description: Ted Bundy is executed by electric chair at Florida State Prison at the age of 42.

events.title: Claudius Is Declared Emperor Of Rome
events.description: Claudius is declared emperor of Rome following the assassination of Caligula, his nephew, by the Praetorian Guard. Though sickly and studious, Claudius proved to be an able ruler who completed Rome's annexation of Britain.

events.title: Henry VIII Marries Anne Boleyn
events.description: Fine Art Images/Heritage Images/Getty ImagesA depiction of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn's first meeting.

events.title: The Simpsonville Massacre Takes Place
events.description: Twenty-two Black Union soldiers are killed by Confederate guerillas in a bloody ambush near Simpsonville, Kentucky.

events.title: Nellie Bly Completes Her Journey Around The World
events.description: A 19th-century journalist, Nellie Bly is best known for penning Ten Days in a Mad-House. Bly's undercover investigation of a New York insane asylum revealed the deplorable conditions that patients lived under.

events.title: The First Winter Olympic Games Begin
events.description: The first Winter Olympic Games take place in the French Alps in Chamonix, France. Lasting until Feb. 5, the games — originally described as "International Winter Sports Week" — drew 250 athletes representing 16 countries who competed in sports like skiing and figure skating. The event was such a success that the International Olympic Committee amended its charter the next year, officially establishing the Winter Olympics.

events.title: Al Capone Dies
events.description: Miami Police DepartmentAl Capone was considered "Public Enemy Number One" before his arrest.

events.title: Tom And Eileen Lonergan Are Lost At Sea
events.description: Married couple Tom And Eileen Lonergan are accidentally left behind 25 miles off the coast of Queensland during a scuba diving trip. Tragically, it took two days for anyone to notice that the Lonergans were missing. Despite a lengthy search, the couple was never found, and most assume that they drowned or were eaten by sharks.

events.title: The First English Prisoners Arrive In Australia
events.description: Eleven ships carrying more than 700 prisoners arrive in Australia. Originally a penal colony, the convicts were brought to Australia by Captain Arthur Phillip, who was tasked with establishing an agricultural work camp. The colony prospered, however, and Australians consider January 25 as "Australia Day," though indigenous Australians often call it Invasion Day.

events.title: Bessie Coleman Is Born
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesBessie Coleman with her plane, circa 1920.

events.title: The World's Largest Diamond Is Found
events.description: The world's largest diamond is discovered at the Premier No.2 mine in Cullinan, South Africa. The 3,106-carat diamond, weighing about 1.33 pounds, was named the Cullinan Diamond after the owner of the mine. It was cut down into nine large stones and about 100 smaller ones worth millions of dollars, many of which belong to the British royal family's crown jewels.

events.title: Petrograd Is Renamed Leningrad
events.description: Petrograd is renamed Leningrad five days after the death of Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin. The city hadn't been called Petrograd for long — Peter the Great had named the city St. Petersburg in the 18th century, but the city was renamed Petrograd in 1914 to remove any connotation with Germany. In 1991, however, voters in Russia decided to change the city's name again and resorted it to its old name, St. Petersburg.

events.title: The Beaumont Children Disappear In Australia
events.description: To this day, no one knows what happened to the three Beaumont children.

events.title: President Bill Clinton Denies Extramarital Affair
events.description: In a televised address, President Bill Clinton tells the nation that he did not have sexual relations with that woman, [Monica] Lewinsky." However, the truth of the matter became one of the biggest presidential sex scandals in U.S. history and helped lead to the impeachment trial against Clinton.

events.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart Is Born
events.description: GraphicaArtis/Getty ImageA depiction of a young Mozart practicing. Etching by Victor Focillon, 1897.

events.title: The First Documented Discovery Of Antarctica
events.description: The first documented discovery of Antarctica takes place when two Russian ships — the Vostok and the Mirnyi — spot the continent. Captained by Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen and Mikhail Lazarev, the Russian expedition recorded what came to be known as the Fimbul Ice Shelf.

events.title: Captain Edward Smith Is Born
events.description: Edward Smith, captain of the RMS Titanic, is born in Hanley, Stoke-on-Trent, United Kingdom.

events.title: Vladimir Lenin's Body Is Put On Display
events.description: © Hulton-Deutsch Collection/CORBIS/Corbis via Getty ImagesVladimir Lenin lying in state in Moscow in 1924.

events.title: The Red Army Liberates Auschwitz
events.description: The Soviet Red Army arrives in Auschwitz, Poland, and liberates survivors imprisoned at the Nazi concentration camp there. Established in 1941, the camp was the site of mass death during the Holocaust, with an estimated 1.1 million people killed over five years. When the Soviets arrived, they liberated the 7,000 surviving prisoners, most of whom were sick or dying.

events.title: Charlemagne Dies
events.description: Charlemagne dies in Aachen, Francia (present-day Germany), at the age of 66 after several years of ill health. The first Holy Roman Emperor, Charlemagne was originally the king of the Franks before he conquered much of Christian Europe. Today, he's known as the "Father of Europe."

events.title: King Henry VIII Dies
events.description: Henry VIII's death led to the rapid succession of his three surviving children, Edward VI, Mary I, and Elizabeth I.

events.title: Fyodor Dostoyevsky Dies In St. Petersburg
events.description: Fyodor Dostoyevsky dies in St. Petersburg, Russia. Dostoyevsky was a Russian novelist and journalist known for his raw portraits of the human condition. His works include Crime and Punishment, The Brothers Karamazov, and Notes from Underground. Dostoyevsky caught the attention of the Tsarist Russian government after joining a banned book club. He would serve four years in a work camp and six years in exile for this crime before being able to return to Russia and write once more. During his final days, Dostoyevsky suffered multiple hemorrhages before finally passing away in St. Petersburg at the age of 59.

events.title: The Shanghai Incident Takes Places
events.description: Japanese troops provoke an uprising in Shanghai, China. The suppression of the uprising led to a short war between Japan and China. Though it lasted only until March 3, tens of thousands of civilians are estimated to have died.

events.title: The Space Shuttle Challenger Explodes
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA man stares up at the trail of smoke left behind by the Challenger explosion.

events.title: Thomas Paine Is Born
events.description: Thomas Paine is born in Thetford, England. A writer and philosopher who emigrated to North America in 1774, Paine's ideas heavily influenced American colonists as the Revolutionary War escalated. His popular pamphlet, Common Sense, critiqued the English monarchy, bolstering the argument for independence.

events.title: The Bear River Massacre Takes Place
events.description: Chief Sagwitch, a survivor of the Bear River Massacre, with his wife. Circa 1875 to 1880.

events.title: Liliʻuokalani Is Crowned Queen Of Hawaii
events.description: Unknown/Library of CongressA signed photograph of Queen Liliuokalani.

events.title: Claudine Longet Is Born
events.description: Claudine Longet, a French-American singer, is born. Longet gained notoriety after shooting her Olympic Skier boyfriend, Vladimir "Spider" Sabich, with a .22-caliber pistol in 1976. Friends and family noted that the couple had an explosive relationship from the beginning. She spent 30 days in jail for the crime, and later remarried and moved into a house not far from the crime scene. Her crime made headlines and gained her the label "femme fatale."

events.title: Brenda Ann Spencer Commits A Mass Shooting At An Elementary School
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesWhen asked why she fired at the school, Brenda Ann Spencer replied: "I don't like Mondays. This livens up the day."

events.title: Charles I Is Beheaded
events.description: Though England became a republic after Charles I's execution, it later returned to a monarchy with Charles' son as king.

events.title: America's First Presidential Assassination Attempt Takes Place
events.description: Andrew Jackson survives the first presidential assassination attempt in American history when he fends off an attack by would-be assassin Richard Lawrence in Washington, D.C.

events.title: Franklin Delano Roosevelt Is Born
events.description: Franklin Delano Roosevelt is born in Hyde Park, New York. The 32nd president of the United States — and the longest-serving American president — Roosevelt was first elected in 1933 and remained in power until his death in 1945. He served amid a number of major historical events, including the end of the Great Depression, the attack on Pearl Harbor, and America's involvement in World War II.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Is Named Chancellor Of Germany
events.description: Fox Photos/Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesHermann Göring, far left, exchanges a word with Adolf Hitler, second from right, during Hitler's 50th birthday parade in Berlin on April 20, 1939.

events.title: Mahatma Gandhi Is Assassinated
events.description: Mondadori Portfolio via Getty ImagesNathuram Godse, the man who assassinated Mahatma Gandhi.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr.'s Home Is Bombed
events.description: Segregationists bomb the Montgomery, Alabama, home of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., who was becoming one of the most prominent leaders of the American civil rights movement. He had started to build a national reputation during the Montgomery Bus Boycott of 1955 — and drew the attention of angry segregationists. Though his wife and seven-month-old daughter were inside his home at the time of the bombing, they were unhurt.

events.title: The Beatles Play Their Final Concert
events.description: When music started coming from the roof of Apple Records' London headquarters at 3 Savile Row around 12:30 p.m., passersby on the street were initially startled and confused. Soon enough, however, everyone realized that they were hearing an impromptu concert from none other than The Beatles, the most famous band in the world.

events.title: Bloody Sunday Takes Place In Northern Ireland
events.description: British paratroopers open fire on a crowd of protestors in Londonderry (Derry), Northern Ireland, killing 14 people and injuring at least 15 more. The massacre, dubbed Bloody Sunday, erupted following months of tension between the British government and citizens of Northern Ireland, who opposed the arrests of suspected members of the Irish Republican Army without giving them a trial.

events.title: Guy Fawkes Is Executed
events.description: A 19th-century depiction of Guy Fawkes' capture.

events.title: Charles Edward Stuart Dies
events.description: National Galleries Of Scotland/Getty ImagesCharles Edward Stuart, the Young Pretender.

events.title: The 13th Amendment Is Passed
events.description: The U.S. Congress passes the 13th Amendment, which abolished slavery. It states: "Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude, except as a punishment for crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted, shall exist within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction." After its passage in Congress, the 13th amendment was ratified on December 6, 1865.

events.title: Jackie Robinson Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJackie Robinson made history when he joined the L.A. Dodgers in 1947.

events.title: Carroll A. Deering Is Found Abandoned
events.description: The Carroll A. Deering, an American ship, is found abandoned in North Carolina's Outer Banks with no sign of her crew.

events.title: The Battle Of Hue Begins
events.description: During the Vietnam War, the NVA and Viet Cong launch the Tet Offensive, orchestrating an attack on multiple cities throughout South Vietnam. Most conflicts ended quickly and decisively for the South Vietnamese and American troops, but the Battle of Hue proved to be one of the bloodiest conflicts of the war and changed American public perception of the war overall.

events.title: Abdelbaset Ali Mohmed al-Megrahi Is Convicted For The Pan Am Flight 103 Bombing
events.description: Abdelbaset Ali Mohmed al-Megrahi is convicted for the Pan Am Flight 103 bombing over Lockerbie, Scotland. On December 21, 1988, Pan Am Flight 103 blew up over Lockerbie, Scotland shortly after taking off from London Heathrow Airport, killing 270 people. Years of investigation would point to al-Megrahi, a Libyan national and head of security for Libyan Arab Airlines. A Scottish panel of judges found al-Megrahi guilty on 270 counts of murder and sentenced him to life in prison. Al-Megrahi was released from prison in 2009 after being diagnosed with terminal prostate cancer.

events.title: Langston Hughes Is Born
events.description: James Mercer Langston Hughes is born in Joplin, Missouri. A celebrated writer famous as a leader of the Harlem Renaissance, Hughes penned a number of iconic poems like The Negro Speaks of Rivers (1921), The Weary Blues (1924), and I, Too, Sing America (1945). His most famous poem is perhaps Harlem (1951), which opens with the immortal line: "What happens to a dream deferred?"

events.title: The North Sea Flood Devastates Europe
events.description: English Heritage/Heritage Images/Getty ImagesFlooding in Suffolk, England, following the North Sea Flood of 1953.

events.title: Nine Die In The Dyatlov Pass Incident
events.description: The hikers of the Dyatlov Pass Incident make their way through the snow on February 1, 1959 — the day they met their mysterious fate.

events.title: The "Saigon Execution" Photo Is Taken
events.description: AP Photo/Eddie Adams, FileThe Saigon Execution photo remains one of the most well-known images from the Vietnam War.

events.title: Otto I Is Crowned Emperor Of The Romans
events.description: Otto I, also called Otto the Great, is crowned Emperor of the Romans by Pope John XII. A German king, Otto had united the region's tribes, defended Western Europe from Hungarian invasions, and conquered the Kingdom of Italy. As emperor, Otto laid the foundations for the Holy Roman Empire.

events.title: Charles I Becomes King Of England
events.description: The tyrannical policies of Charles I eventually resulted in the abolishment of the English monarchy in 1649.

events.title: James Joyce Is Born
events.description: James Augustine Aloysius Joyce is born in Dublin, Ireland. An Irish writer who wrote novels, short stories, poems, and plays, Joyce penned iconic works like his short story collection Dubliners (1914) and his novel Ulysses (1922). He died in 1941 following a surgical procedure for an ulcer. To this day, he remains one of the most celebrated writers in the history of English literature.

events.title: Balto Arrives In Nome, Alaska
events.description: Balto was considered a lowly "scrub dog" before he joined the Great Race of Mercy.

events.title: The Battle Of Stalingrad Ends
events.description: The Battle of Stalingrad ends after more than five months of brutal fighting. The battle, which pitted the Soviet Union against Nazi Germany and its allies, resulted in the destruction of much of this Soviet city and an estimated 1.2 million deaths. In the end, this bloody clash greatly weakened Germany's armed forces and is considered to be a turning point of World War II.

events.title: Sid Vicious Dies
events.description: Richard E. Aaron/Redferns/Getty ImagesTo this day, a number of haunting questions remain about the deaths of Sex Pistols bassist Sid Vicious and his girlfriend Nancy Spungen.

events.title: Philip Seymour Hoffman Dies
events.description: Actor Philip Seymour Hoffman dies at the age of 46 from a drug overdose in New York City.

events.title: Johannes Gutenburg, Inventor Of The Printing Press, Dies
events.description: Johannes Gutenburg, inventor of the printing press, dies in Mainz, Germany. Gutenburg was a craftsman and inventor who created the most popular moveable printing press. His invention led to a literacy boom in Europe, leading to the rapid spread of information. This increase in knowledge facilitated the Reformation and the Renaissance, a period of enlightenment and intellectual curiosity in Europe. Today, scholars refer to him as one of the most influential figures in human history.

events.title: Norman Rockwell Is Born
events.description: Norman Rockwell's famous Freedom From Want, published March 6, 1943.

events.title: The Battle Of Manila Begins
events.description: The Battle of Manila begins in the Philippines near the close of World War II. Fought between the United States and the Philippines against Japan, the battle lasted a full month and destroyed the city of Manila while causing the deaths of 100,000 civilians. It resulted in a victory for the United States and its allies, ending almost three years of Japanese occupation.

events.title: The First News Story About The SS Ourang Medan Is Published
events.description: The spine-tingling story about the SS Ourang Medan, an infamous ghost ship, is first published in the Dutch-Indonesian newspaper De locomotief.

events.title: Buddy Holly Dies In A Plane Crash
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesDespite his extremely brief career, Buddy Holly influenced generations of rock and roll artists.

events.title: Karla Faye Tucker Is Executed
events.description: Karla Faye Tucker is executed by lethal injection in Huntsville, Texas, at the age of 38. A convicted murderer who was found guilty of killing a man in a robbery gone wrong, Tucker elicited widespread sympathy while on death row for converting to Christianity. Tucker had suffered an abusive childhood and claimed to have been on drugs during the murder, but her appeals for clemency didn't sway the then-governor of Texas, George W. Bush.

events.title: Mary Boleyn, "The Other Boleyn Girl" Gets Married
events.description: Mary Boleyn, "The Other Boleyn Girl" gets married to William Carey. Known as one of Henry VIII's mistress, Mary Boleyn gave birth to two of the king's children. Henry VIII and Mary Boleyn never married, as Henry VIII became infatuated with her sister, Anne Boleyn, while Mary was pregnant. After William Carey' death, Mary married William Stafford in secret. This caused a scandal within the English court, and both Henry VIII and Anne agreed to banish Mary from the court. She lived out the rest of her life in relative obscurity.

events.title: Shays' Rebellion Flounders
events.description: Shays' Rebellion ends after roughly five months. The rebellion was started by former Revolutionary War soldiers-turned-farmers who found themselves struggling with debt and the high taxes levied by the state of Massachusetts. Led by war veteran Daniel Shay, the rebellion was ultimately put down by local militias. However, it convinced many that the young United States needed the Constitutional Convention in order to reform its government.

events.title: Philippine-American War Begins
events.description: The Philippine-American War begins after an American solider fatally shoots two Filipino soldiers, sparking the Battle of Manila.

events.title: Franz Reichelt Dies While Testing His Homemade Flying Suit
events.description: Franz Reichelt hoped to prove that his parachute worked by jumping off the Eiffel Tower — but his invention failed.

events.title: Rosa Parks Is Born
events.description: Rosa Parks is born in Tuskegee, Alabama. An iconic civil rights activist, Parks made history when she refused to give up her seat in the whites-only section of a segregated Montgomery bus on December 1, 1955. Her actions helped launch the Montgomery bus boycott and inspired the larger American civil rights movement. She was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1996 and remains an heroic figure in American history to this day.

events.title: Neal Cassady Dies
events.description: Neal Cassady, a member of the Beat Generation who inspired Jack Kerouac and Allen Ginsberg, dies in Mexico at the age of 41.

events.title: Patty Hearst Is Kidnapped
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesPatty Hearst publicly pledged her loyalty to her kidnappers, but later claimed that she'd been brainwashed.

events.title: Facebook Is Founded
events.description: Mark Zuckerberg launches TheFacebook, a website originally only available to students at Harvard University. It would eventually become accessible to additional universities across the United States and the United Kingdom, before becoming available worldwide and amassing nearly 3 billion monthly active users.

events.title: The Punic Wars End
events.description: The Punic Wars come to an end. The 120-year-long series of conflicts, which pitted the Roman Republic against Carthage, resulted in a Roman victory. With the fall of Carthage, Rome took over much of North Africa and became the preeminent power in the ancient world, a position it held for centuries to come.

events.title: Belle Starr Is Born
events.description: Belle Starr after an arrest in 1886.

events.title: The Mexican Constitution Is Approved
events.description: Spearheaded by soon-to-be President Venustiano Carranza, the Constitution of Mexico is approved. The document, which established ideas like the separation of church and state and the restoration of land to native people, came after almost seven years of the Mexican Revolution. However, it took years for the ideas in the constitution to be put into practice. Eventually, the constitution's tenets took hold and it remains the country's governing document to this day.

events.title: Reader's Digest Publishes Its First Issue
events.description: To this day, Reader's Digest remains one of the most popular magazines in the United States.

events.title: Hank Aaron Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesHank Aaron with the baseball that broke Babe Ruth's home run record in 1974.

events.title: France Recognizes U.S. Independence
events.description: A depiction of the signing of the Treaty of Amity and Commerce. Benjamin Franklin stands in the center of the frame.

events.title: The Dalton Gang Commits Its First Train Robbery
events.description: The dead bodies of the Dalton Gang following their demise in the shootout during the 1892 Coffeyville bank robbery.

events.title: Babe Ruth Is Born
events.description: Mark Rucker/Transcendental Graphics/Getty ImagesBabe Ruth during batting practice at Yankee Stadium in 1923.

events.title: The Weimar Republic Is Formed
events.description: The Weimar Republic is formed in Germany. Following Germany's defeat in World War I, Emperor William II abdicated the throne. The national assembly met in Weimar, Germany to discuss the new government. The assembly would eventually create a new constitution, preserving the country's federal structure and strengthening the central government's power. It provided Germany with a foundation for democracy, but came with several problems. The Weimar Republic would eventually collapse with the rise of the Nazis in 1933.

events.title: King George VI Dies And Elizabeth II Becomes Queen
events.description: King George VI dies in his sleep at the age of 56 following a long battle with cancer. He had reigned for 15 years and steered the country through World War II, after serving in the Royal Air Force during World War I. His death elevated his 25-year-old daughter Elizabeth to the throne. Her lavish coronation would follow on June 2, 1953.

events.title: John Wayne Gacy Goes To Trial
events.description: The trial of serial killer John Wayne Gacy begins in Chicago — with a whopping 33 murders on the list of charges. After police found dozens of bodies inside the crawl space of his home, the local media coverage was so intense that the jury had to be selected from a city about 100 miles away in hopes that people living there would be less aware of the case. And once the trial began, it was turbulent from the first day to the last.

events.title: Sir Thomas More Is Born
events.description: VCG Wilson/Corbis via Getty ImagesThomas more was later deemed a martyr and a saint by the Catholic Church.

events.title: Europeans Land On Tristan da Cunha For The First Time
events.description: Europeans land on the island of Tristan da Cunha for the first time. Today, the island is the most remote place on the planet.

events.title: The Siege Of Gibraltar Is Lifted
events.description: The Great Siege of Gibraltar is lifted after more than three and a half years. The siege, led by Spain and France, aimed to capture Gibraltar from the British during the American Revolution. Ultimately, however, the British emerged victorious and Gibraltar remains a British Overseas Territory to this day.

events.title: Charles Dickens Is Born
events.description: Hulton-Deutsch Collection/CORBIS/Corbis via Getty ImagesTo this day, Charles Dickens remains one of England's best-known novelists.

events.title: Largest Earthquake In The Contiguous U.S. Strikes Along New Madrid Fault
events.description: The largest earthquake to hit the contiguous U.S. east of the Rocky Mountains strikes along the New Madrid fault. At nearly four in the morning, a 7.4 to 8.6 magnitude earthquake struck the town of New Madrid, Missouri. The town was completely destroyed, and people as far at St. Louis, Missouri reported extensive damage to their homes, buildings, and other property.

events.title: The Beatles Arrive In America
events.description: The Beatles wave to crowds of screaming fans just after landing in New York.

events.title: Big Pun Dies
events.description: Rapper Christopher Lee Rios, otherwise known as Big Pun, dies. After suffering from respiratory failure and a heart attack, Big Pun passed away at the age of 28 at a hospital in New York.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots Is Beheaded
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesThough Mary, Queen of Scots, was beheaded by the English, her son eventually became the English king.

events.title: The Dawes Act Passes
events.description: The Dawes Act is passed by Congress. Also called the Dawes Severalty Act or the General Allotment Act, the law permitted the federal government to break up Native American tribal land and give it to Native Americans as individual plots. Though the act aimed to push Native Americans into farming and agriculture, it ended up taking millions of acres of land away from Native Americans and transferring it to non-Indigenous people.

events.title: The Russo-Japanese War Begins
events.description: Russian soldiers retreat during the Battle of Mukden in March 1905.

events.title: The Boy Scouts Of America Is Founded
events.description: The Boy Scouts of America are incorporated by William Boyce, a publisher who encountered a helpful Boy Scout in England who aided him while he was lost. The movement had begun in England two years earlier with the publication of Robert Baden-Powell's Scouting for Boys, which led to a proliferation of Boy Scout groups across the British Commonwealth. Boyce brought the idea back to the United States and, to this day, some 110 million Americans have participated in the Boy Scouts of America.

events.title: Lana Turner Is Born
events.description: Hollywood star Lana Turner is born Julia Jean Turner in Wallace, Idaho.

events.title: Neal Cassady Is Born
events.description: Neal Cassady, whose friendship with Jack Kerouac and Allen Ginsberg would inspire some of their greatests works, including Kerouac's "On The Road," is born in Salt Lake City, Utah.

events.title: James Dean Is Born
events.description: John Kobal Foundation/Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesJames Dean on the set of Rebel Without a Cause in 1955.

events.title: Lepa Radíc Is Executed By The Nazis
events.description: Lepa Radić is executed by the Nazis in the Independent State of Croatia at the age of 17. A fearsome resistance fighter, Radíc was a member of the Yugoslav Partisans, a group that sought to overthrow the Axis powers and establish an independent socialist Yugoslav state. Radíc's executioners promised to let her go at the last minute if she revealed the names of her collaborators but Radíc refused, telling them, "I am not a traitor of my people."

events.title: 'Good Times' Premieres On CBS
events.description: Good Times, the first television sitcom to feature a two-parent African-American family, premieres on CBS with Esther Rolle as matriarch Florida Evans.

events.title: The First Published Study Of Kumimanu fordycei Is Published
events.description: The first study of Kumimanu fordycei, a giant prehistoric penguin species, is published. The Guinness World Records has recognized this species as the largest penguin to ever roam the Earth.

events.title: William Henry Harrison Is Born
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesWilliam Henry Harrison died just a month after his inauguration in 1841.

events.title: Volleyball Is Invented
events.description: Volleyball — then called mintonette — is invented by William G. Morgan in Holyoke, Massachusetts. The director of physical education at the local YMCA, Morgan believed that the new sport of basketball was too taxing for older people and wanted to come up with an alternative. Though he originally experimented with batting a basketball across a net, he eventually decided it was too heavy and came up with a lighter version of the ball.

events.title: Adolph Coors Is Kidnapped
events.description: Adolph Coors III is kidnapped by Joe Corbett. The grandson of Adolph Coors and heir to the Coors Brewing Company, Coors' remains were found in a dump near Sedalia, Colorado, about seven months later. Police traced a car that witnesses had seen around the time of the kidnapping to Corbett, who protested his innocence but was eventually found guilty of first-degree murder.

events.title: Ted Bundy Marries Carole Ann Boone
events.description: TwitterCarole Ann Boone with Ted Bundy and their daughter.

events.title: Hae Min Lee's Body Is Discovered
events.description: The body of 18-year-old Hae Min Lee is discovered in Leakin Park in West Baltimore, Maryland. Lee's ex-boyfriend, Adnan Syed, was found guilty of first-degree murder in 2000 but had his conviction vacated in September 2022 following renewed efforts to get him released due to his being featured in the popular podcast Serial. Today, the case into Lee's murder is open and ongoing.

events.title: Maura Murray Disappears
events.description: Maura Murray MissingThe disappearance of Maura Murray has remained a mystery since she went missing in 2004.

events.title: The French And Indian War Ends
events.description: George Washington (on horseback) leads his troops during the French and Indian War's Battle of the Monongahela in 1755.

events.title: Queen Victoria Marries Prince Albert
events.description: A depiction of Queen Victoria and Prince Albert's 1840 wedding.

events.title: Brigham Young Leaves Illinois
events.description: MPI/Getty ImagesBrigham Young brought Mormons to Utah and established a settlement there that endures to this day.

events.title: The Largest Mafia Trial In History Begins
events.description: The Maxi Trial, the largest and most significant trial against the Mafia in history, begins in Palermo, Sicily. Presided over by judge Giovanni Falcone, the trial included 475 defendants facing charges ranging from drug smuggling to murder and took place in a specially built bunker-style courtroom for protection. In the end, the majority were found guilty and sentenced to a total of 2,665 years in prison, with 19 bosses given life sentences.

events.title: Garry Kasparov Plays The Computer 'Deep Blue'
events.description: Garry Kasparov, world chess champion, plays Deep Blue, an IBM chess computer. The first match was held in Philadelphia, and Kasparov won. Man and machine faced off again a day later, resulting in a victory for the IBM computer. In total, Kasparov and Deep Blue played six games.

events.title: Israel Keyes Abducts His Last Victim, Samantha Koenig
events.description: Serial killer Israel Keyes abducts his last victim, Samantha Koenig, in Anchorage, Alaska. Israel Keyes was an American serial killer known for leaving "kill kits" across the United States. He would attack at random, and with no definitive victim preference, investigators struggled to track him down. Police would catch a break after Keyes abducted Samantha Koenig. After requesting ransom from her family, Keyes used Koenig's bank cards to access the funds. Police would later recognize his car from bank surveillance footage and arrest him outside a hotel in Texas.

events.title: Japan Is Founded
events.description: Japan is founded with the crowning of its first emperor, Jimmu Tennō. This founding day, called Kigensetsu, was celebrated as a holiday until after World War II, when it was abolished. However, it was reestablished in 1966 as National Foundation Day.

events.title: King Henry VIII Becomes Supreme Head Of The Church Of England
events.description: DeAgostini/Getty ImagesHenry VIII altered the course of English history by proclaiming himself the head of the Church of England.

events.title: Sacagawea Gives Birth
events.description: Sacagawea gives birth to her son, Jean Baptiste Charbonneau, in present-day Washburn, North Dakota. Sacagawea, a Lemhi Shoshone woman who assisted in the Lewis and Clark expedition, was aided during the birth by explorer Meriwether Lewis. He helped hasten Sacagawea's painful labor by giving her a reputedly effective potion made from bits of a rattle from a rattlesnake mixed with water.

events.title: Sylvia Plath Dies By Suicide
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesSylvia Plath was just 30 years old when she was took her own life.

events.title: Maureen Starkey Marries Ringo Starr
events.description: Hairdresser Maureen Starkey marries Beatles drummer Ringo Starr in London.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Is Released From Prison
events.description: Allan Tannenbaum/The LIFE Images Collection via Getty Images/Getty ImagesNelson Mandela and his wife Winnie raise their fists upon his release from prison after 27 years.

events.title: Johnny Frank Garrett Is Executed
events.description: Johnny Frank Garrett is executed by lethal injection at the Texas State Penitentiary at Huntsville at the age of 28. A convicted murderer, Garrett was found guilty of raping and killing a 76-year-old Catholic nun named Sister Tadea Benz in Amarillo, Texas in 1981. Garrett's last meal was ice cream and his last words were allegedly: "I'd like to thank my family for loving me and taking care of me. The rest of the world can kiss my ass."

events.title: Lady Jane Grey Is Beheaded
events.description: VCG Wilson/Corbis via Getty ImagesA depiction of the execution of Lady Jane Grey.

events.title: King Adolf Fredrick Of Sweden Dies
events.description: King Adolf Frederick of Sweden dies in Stockholm, Sweden, at the age of 60, after allegedly eating himself to death. As king, Adolf Frederick didn't accomplish much. But he perished in a memorable fashion after reportedly eating a kingly meal of lobster, caviar, kippers, sauerkraut, boiled meats, and turnips, washed down with champagne, with Swedish pastries for dessert. However, many consider such stories to be mere myth, though the truth about his death remains uncertain to this day.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Is Born
events.description: Abraham Lincoln, as photographed by Alexander Gardner in 1863.

events.title: The NAACP Is Established
events.description: The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) is established in New York City. It was founded by both white and Black progressives, including W.E.B. Du Bois, Mary Church Terrell, and Mary White Ovington, in response to systemic violence against African Americans in the United States. Since its founding, the NAACP has supported causes like anti-lynching legislation and the civil rights movement.

events.title: The First Newspaper Report Of The Snallygaster Is Published
events.description: The Middletown Valley Register publishes the first account of a Snallygaster sighting — the bird-like cryptid of Maryland that was used to intimidate Black voters.

events.title: The Last Emperor Of China Abdicates
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesHsian-T'ung, later Henry Pu Yi, the last emperor of China.

events.title: Hassan al-Banna Is Assassinated
events.description: Hassan al-Banna is assassinated by the Egyptian secret police in Cairo. The founder of the Muslim Brotherhood, al-Banna called for the Islamization of society and considered Muslim countries one nation. Though Egyptian authorities saw al-Banna and his ideas as a threat — leading to his assassination – the Muslim Brotherhood endures to this day.

events.title: Actor Sal Mineo Is Murdered
events.description: Actor Sal Mineo from Rebel Without A Cause is murdered outside of his apartment in Los Angeles after returning home from a rehearsal.

events.title: Robert Thomas And Jon Venables Kidnap And Murder James Bulger
events.description: James Bulger's killers Jon Venables (holding the boy's hand) and Robert Thompson (walking directly in front of the boy) abduct their victim just before killing him, as captured by a surveillance camera.

events.title: Catherine Howard Is Beheaded
