events.description: Kean Collection/Getty ImagesCatherine Howard was only 18 or 19 when she was beheaded.

events.title: The Massacre Of Glencoe Takes Places
events.description: Thirty members of the MacDonald clan of Glencoe are murdered in Glen Coe, Scotland. The clan members were allegedly killed for their refusal to swear allegiance to William III, King of England, Scotland, and Ireland. Though the massacre was meant to quash any resistance to the new monarch, it only deepened the resentment of many Scots toward England.

events.title: Jesse James Commits His First Bank Robbery
events.description: The first daytime bank robbery in American history takes place at the Clay County Savings Association in Liberty, Missouri. It's likely that one of the bandits was Jesse James, the notorious Wild West outlaw who would soon make a name for himself as a bank robber. However, some say that James' first robbery wasn't until December 7, 1869, when he and his brother Frank robbed Daviess County Savings Association in Gallatin, Missouri, and killed the bank teller there, possibly in retaliation for the death of their friend "Bloody Bill" Anderson.

events.title: Dresden Is Firebombed
events.description: Hulton-Deutsch Collection/CORBIS/Corbis via Getty ImagesThe bombing of Dresden, Germany killed an estimated 25,000 people.

events.title: The Delphi Murders Take Place
events.description: YouTubeAbby Williams and Libby German, the victims of the Delphi murders.

events.title: Kim Jong-nam Is Assassinated
events.description: Kim Jong-nam, the elder brother of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un — and once the heir apparent to their father, Kim Jong-il — is assassinated at Kuala Lumpur airport in Malaysia.

events.title: Saint Valentine Is Beheaded
events.description: A Roman priest named Valentine is beaten with clubs and beheaded. Valentine had drawn the ire of the Roman emperor Claudius by continuing to marry young couples even after Claudius had forbidden it in an attempt to lure more men into the Roman army. He was named a saint after his death circa 270 C.E. and Pope Gelasius renamed a pagan festival of love — the Feast of Lupercalia — as St. Valentine's Day in 496 C.E.

events.title: King Richard II Dies
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesNo one knows exactly how Richard II, the former king of England, died.

events.title: Captain James Cook Is Killed
events.description: Captain James Cook is killed by natives in the Hawaiian Kingdom at the age of 50. An English explorer, Cook had made a name for himself by circumnavigating the globe, exploring Australia and New Zealand, and becoming one of the first — if not the first — Europeans to visit Hawaii.

events.title: The League Of Women Voters Is Established
events.description: The League of Women Voters is founded in Chicago. It combined a number of suffrage groups under one banner six months before the 19th Amendment passed, which gave women the right to vote. However, the organization has been criticized for its exclusionary policies toward women of color.

events.title: The St. Valentine's Day Massacre Takes Place
events.description: Chicago History MuseumVictims of the St. Valentine's Day Massacre.

events.title: Malcolm X's Home Is Firebombed
events.description: An iconic Ebony magazine photo dramatizing Malcolm X's defense of his home and family while the Nation of Islam was threatening his life.

events.title: The Pale Blue Dot Image Is Taken
events.description: The "Pale Blue Dot" image is taken by space probe Voyager 1. The image, taken 6 billion miles from Earth, features our Solar System and Earth as a pale blue dot.

events.title: Galileo Galilei Is Born
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesGalileo Galilei is sometimes referred to as the "father of modern science."

events.title: The U.S.S. Maine Explodes
events.description: The U.S.S. Maine entering the Harbor of Havana in January 1898, just three weeks before its destruction.

events.title: The First Teddy Bear Goes On Sale
events.description: The first Teddy bear goes on sale. The toy was popularized after the public learned that President Theodore Roosevelt had refused to shoot a bear that his aides had tied up for him to kill during a hunt. A cartoonist depicted the incident in the Washington Post, which led to the widespread sale of teddy bear toys.

events.title: "Butcher Baker" Serial Killer Robert Hansen Is Born
events.description: Anchorage Daily News/Tribune News Service via Getty ImagesRobert Hansen was an avid hunter who decorated his home with hunting trophies, but he didn't just hunt game.

events.title: The Maple Leaf Becomes Canada's Official Flag
events.description: The maple leaf is inaugurated as Canada's national flag. The maple leaf had long been a symbol of Canadian identity and this new flag replaced previous versions that featured the British Union Jack. Ever since, February 15th has been celebrated as National Flag of Canada Day.

events.title: Ernst Haeckel Is Born
events.description: Ernst Haeckel is born in Potsdam, Germany. A German zoologist, Haeckel is credited with discovering and naming thousands of new species. His colorful illustrations of various species made him a popular naturalist in his day, though he has since been criticized for his racist views on white superiority.

events.title: Tutankhamun's Tomb Is Opened
events.description: Pictorial Parade/Getty ImagesBritish Egyptologist Howard Carter and his assistant Arthur Callender on the steps leading to the entrance of the tomb of Pharaoh Tutankhamun, or King Tut, in 1922.

events.title: Margot Frank Is Born
events.description: Margot Frank, the older sister of Holocaust diarist Anne Frank, is born in Frankfurt, Germany. Margot and Anne later died together at the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp in 1945.

events.title: Fidel Castro Becomes The Prime Minister of Cuba
events.description: Fidel Castro is sworn in as the prime minister of Cuba. The communist revolutionary leader came to power after spearheading a successful guerrilla campaign against the Cuban dictator General Fulgencio Batista. He then established Cuba as the first communist power in the Western hemisphere, but also persecuted anyone who spoke out against his regime. Despite numerous attempts on his life, he led the country until 2008, when his deteriorating health caused him to pass his position to his brother, Raúl.

events.title: Arne Cheyenne Johnson Kills His Landlord And Says The "Devil" Made Him Do It
events.description: Bettmann Archive/Getty ImagesArne Cheyenne Johnson arriving at court in March 1981.

events.title: Travis The Chimp Attacks
events.description: Travis the Chimp attacks Carla Nash in Connecticut. Owned as a pet by Jerome and Sandra Herold, Travis was only a baby when he was introduced to Sandra's friend Carla. Travis was almost another child to the Herolds; he would eat dinner with the family, use the computer, and reportedly loved baseball. In 2009, Travis escaped the Herolds' home, and when Carla tried to lure him back to house with a toy, he attacked her. The attack would leave Carla horribly disfigured, and it is considered one of the most brutal exotic pet attacks in history.

events.title: Thomas Jefferson Is Elected President
events.description: Thomas Jefferson is elected as the third president of the United States. At 33, Jefferson became a Founding Father after drafting the American Declaration of Independence. Jefferson strongly opposed a strong centralized government, and frequently attacked Federalist policies in the new United States. As president, Jefferson cut the budget, eliminated taxes, and reduced national debt. His most famous legacy as president stemmed from his purchase of the Louisiana Territory in 1803, which doubled the territory of the United States. In his second term as president, Jefferson fell out of favor after placing an embargo on American shipping. After his presidency, he retired peacefully at his estate in Virginia, and died on American Independence Day.

events.title: The War Of 1812 Comes To An End
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesAmerican victories in battles like the Battle of New Orleans, fought in January 1815 and depicted here, reinforced the idea that the U.S. won the War of 1812 — although both sides ultimately had to return conquered territory.

events.title: Apache Chief Geronimo Dies
events.description: Geronimo was a naturally gifted hunter and it's said that he ate the heart of his first kill in a symbolic gesture to protect himself from those who might hunt him.

events.title: Michael Jordan Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesTo this day, many consider Michael Jordan to be the greatest basketball player of all time.

events.title: Breck Bednar Is Murdered
events.description: Fourteen-year-old Breck Bednar is murdered by 18-year-old Lewis Daynes in Grays, England. The two had developed a friendship online before Daynes lured Bednar to his apartment, where he bound Bednar with duct tape and stabbed him in the neck. Daynes later pleaded guilty to Bednar's murder and was sentenced to 25 years in prison.

events.title: Kublai Khan Dies
events.description: Kublai Khan dies in Khanbaliq, present-day Beijing, after suffering from obesity and gout, at the age of 79. The founder of the Yuan dynasty and the grandson of Genghis Khan, Khan was the first Mongol to rule over all of China. But the deaths of his wife and oldest son, as well as failed attempts to conquer Japan, Burma, and Java, weighed on Khan at the end of his life, and he withdrew from his administrative duties before his death.

events.title: Queen Mary I Is Born
events.description: The Print Collector/Getty ImagesQueen Mary I of England had a short and violent reign, earning her the nickname "Bloody Mary."

events.title: The Lincoln County War Begins
events.description: A cropped version of the sole fully authenticated photo of Billy the Kid. Circa 1879-1880.

events.title: Nerissa Bowes-Lyon Is Born
events.description: Nerissa Bowes-Lyon, the cousin of Elizabeth II, is born. The British public was outraged following tabloid publications in the 1980s that revealed that Nerissa Bowes-Lyon, along with her sister, Katherine, were institutionalized in their youth and declared dead despite being alive.

events.title: Manchukuo Is Established
events.description: Manchukuo is established by Imperial Japan in present-day China. Though ostensibly led by Puyi, the last Qing emperor of China, Manchukuo was in fact a puppet state of Japan, which prized the area for its natural resources. Ultimately, after committing a series of atrocities there, Japan lost control of the territory after the Soviet invasion of Manchuria in August 1945 at the close of World War II.

events.title: Gary Ridgway Is Born
events.description: Elaine Thompson-Pool/Getty ImagesGary Ridgway in court during his sentencing on December 18, 2003, in Seattle, Washington.

events.title: The First Church Of Scientology Is Established
events.description: The Church of Scientology, the infamous religious institution founded by science fiction author L. Ron Hubbard, opens its first church in Los Angeles, California. Of the church, Hubbard said, "A civilization without insanity, without criminals and without war, where the able can prosper and honest beings can have rights, and where man is free to rise to greater heights, are the aims of Scientology."

events.title: Frank Costello Dies
events.description: Frank Costello dies of a heart attack in New York City at the age of 82. The boss of the Luciano crime family, Costello managed his underworld empire by making strategic alliances with fellow mobsters as well as government officials. He's thought to be one of the main inspirations for the character of Don Corleone in The Godfather (1972), and actor Marlon Brando even studied Costello's throaty half-whisper when he developed his portrayal of this iconic character.

events.title: Nicolaus Copernicus Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA depiction of Nicolaus Copernicus looking through a telescope.

events.title: Rescuers Reach The Donner Party
events.description: The first wave of rescuers reaches the Donner Party. This band of 87 pioneers had first set out from Illinois in the spring of 1846, but they eventually became snowbound in the Sierra Nevada mountains on their way to the West Coast. After running out of food and supplies, the Donner Party allegedly turned to cannibalism to survive and just 48 of its members survived the trek to California.

events.title: Executive Order 9066 Orders Japanese-Americans Into Internment Camps
events.description: Eliot Elisofon/The LIFE Picture Collection/Getty ImagesThe first group of Japanese Americans arrive at the Manzanar internment camp in Inyo County, California on March 21, 1942.

events.title: AC/DC Frontman Bon Scott Dies
events.description: FG/Bauer-Griffin/Getty ImagesBon Scott performing in August 1979, roughly six months before his death.

events.title: The Body Of Elisa Lam Is Discovered
events.description: The body of 21-year-old Elisa Lam is discovered in a water tank on the roof of the Cecil Hotel in Los Angeles, California. Lam, who was visiting California from Canada, had been reported missing by her parents roughly two weeks earlier when they didn't hear from her on the day she was supposed to check out. The location of her body, as well as surveillance footage of Lam seemingly hiding from an unseen assailant in an elevator, has led some to speculate that she was murdered, though her death was ultimately ruled accidental.

events.title: The U.S. Post Office Department Is Founded
events.description: President George Washington signs the Postal Service Act establishing the U.S. Post Office Department. The act reinforced Congress' right to establish new mail routes, allowed inexpensive newspaper deliveries, and established a right to mail privacy by making it illegal for postal officials to open letters and packages. The Postal Service remained a cabinet department until President Richard Nixon signed the Postal Reorganization Act of 1970.

events.title: History's First Dinosaur Is Identified And Named
events.description: A portrait of William Buckland from 1833.

events.title: Frederick Douglass Dies
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesFrederick Douglass' speeches and books made a profound impact on American history.

events.title: Isadore Greenbaum Storms A Nazi Rally At Madison Square Garden
events.description: Twenty-six-year-old Isadore Greenbaum charges the stage of a Nazi rally held at New York's Madison Square Garden. A Jewish plumber's assistant from Brooklyn, Greenbaum had snuck into the rally and became enraged as he listened to Fritz Kuhn, the leader of the pro-Hitler German-American Bund, speak to the crowd of 22,000. Crying "Down with Hitler!" Greenbaum stormed the stage and was beaten by Nazi guards (Ordnungsdienst) before police dragged him away and arrested him.

events.title: Kurt Cobain Is Born
events.description: Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagicKurt Cobain performing in 1993, the year before he died by suicide.

events.title: Ireland Begins Allowing The Sale Of Contraceptives
events.description: The Irish government votes to allow the sale of contraceptives. Starting in 1979, people in Ireland could purchase contraception for "bona fide family planning purposes" as long as they had a prescription, but many believed that this still limited access to an unfair degree. In an 83-80 decision opposed by the Catholic Church, the government declared that people over 18 could purchase condoms and spermicides without a prescription and that hospitals and clinics could provide condoms and spermicides to their patients.

events.title: Hunter S. Thompson Dies By Suicide
events.description: Michael Ochs Archive/Getty ImagesHunter S. Thompson died from a gunshot to the head at his Colorado home on February 20, 2005.

events.title: Mikhail Romanov Becomes Tsar Of Russia
events.description: General Photographic Agency/Getty ImagesMikhail Fyodorovich Romanov, the founder of the Romanov dynasty.

events.title: The Communist Manifesto Is Published
events.description: The Communist Manifesto is published in London. Written by Karl Marx, with help from Friedrich Engels, the pamphlet predicted the inevitable victory of the working class — or the proletariat — which they argued would fundamentally change the course of human history by ending capitalism and establishing a society based on workers. Communism swiftly grew in popularity after the book's publication and ultimately led to the Russian Revolution in 1917.

events.title: The World's First Phone Book Is Issued
events.description: The world's first phone book is released in New Haven, Connecticut. Published by the Connecticut District Telephone Company, it contained the names and addresses of 391 subscribers. There were no phone numbers, however — users would contact an operator instead of dialing a number. Furthermore, it wasn't technically a book at all and was instead printed on a single piece of cardboard, and subscribers paid $22 per year for this service.

events.title: The Washington Monument Is Dedicated
events.description: The Washington Monument is dedicated in Washington, D.C. Built to honor George Washington, the 555-foot marble obelisk design was initially proposed in 1783. Though its cornerstone was laid in 1848, events like the Civil War delayed construction, and the monument wasn't completed until December 1884.

events.title: Carmine Galante Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA 1930 mugshot of Carmine Galante.

events.title: Malcolm X Is Assassinated
events.description: Malcolm X is taken out of the Audubon Ballroom on a stretcher just after being shot on February 21, 1965.

events.title: Workers In Mexico City Stumble On The Coyolxāuhqui Stone At Templo Mayor
events.description: Electricians working in Mexico City stumble on the Coyolxāuhqui Stone, an Aztec stone depicting the famous myth of Coyolxauhqui's defeat at Coatepec. The discovery would launch a full excavation of Templo Mayor, the Aztec Empire's most famous pyramid.

events.title: George Washington Is Born
events.description: VCG Wilson/Corbis via Getty ImagesA portrait of George Washington, the first president of the United States.

events.title: Deadwood, South Dakota Becomes An Incorporated Town
events.description: Deadwood, famous for its rowdy and lawless wild west reputation, is formally incorporated. Settlement began in the area illegally in 1876, violating the 1868 Treaty of Fort Laramie, which promised the sacred Black Hills land to the Lakota people.

events.title: Robert Wadlow Is Born
events.description: /New York Daily News ArchiveRobert Wadlow comparing shoe sizes with the Ringling Bros' Major Mite, a little person traveling with the circus.

events.title: Battle Of Ramree Island Ends
events.description: The Battle of Ramree Island between Japanese and Allied forces ends with an Allied victory. Japanese troops occupying Ramree Island in the Bay of Bengal opted to escape the humiliation of surrender and meet up with a larger battalion by wadding through eight miles of crocodile-infested waters. Several British observers noted that crocodiles began attacking the Japanese soldiers, killing an estimated 620 troops. The experience is noted by the Guinness Book of World Records as the largest crocodile attack in history.

events.title: First Attack In The Texarkana Moonlight Murders
events.description: Late on the night of February 22, the Texarkana phantom killer made his first attack on a young couple on lovers' lane. The masked man attacked Jimmy Hollis and Mary Jeanne Larey, forcing the couple out of the car. Miraculously, the couple survived the attack. However, the phantom killer would go on to murder five people in the Texarkana region.

events.title: Rosa Parks' Mugshot Is Taken
events.description: Months after her initial arrest for refusing to give up her seat on a city bus in Montgomery, Alabama, Rosa Parks is arrested alongside dozens of other civil rights leaders during the Montgomery bus boycott as the city attempted to intimidate them. Parks' mugshot, taken on this day, became one of the most defining images of the civil rights movement.

events.title: Steve Irwin "The Crocodile Hunter" Is Born
events.description: Steve Irwin, known as one of Australia's most famous TV personalities and naturalists, is born outside of Melbourne.

events.title: Keith Sapsford Falls To His Death
events.description: John GilpinKeith Sapsford's fatal fall was accidentally captured on film.

events.title: The "Miracle On Ice" Occurs During The Winter Olympics
events.description: The U.S. hockey team beats the Soviet team during the Olympic Winter Games in Lake Placid, New York, in the so-called "Miracle on Ice." The Soviets, who had won gold at the last four Olympics, were the easy favorites to win. But they were shockingly defeated by the scrappy American team, who won the hockey gold medal two days later after defeating the Finland team.

events.title: Andy Warhol Dies
events.description: Andy Warhol dies at New York Presbyterian Hospital in New York following gallbladder surgery.

events.title: Roman Emperor Diocletian Orders The Persecution Of Christians
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA statue of the Roman Emperor Diocletian.

events.title: W.E.B. DuBois Is Born
events.description: William Edward Burghardt "W.E.B." DuBois is born in Great Barrington, Massachusetts. A scholar, writer, and activist, DuBois helped found the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in 1909. He also penned a number of groundbreaking books and essays on African American life, including The Souls of Black Folk.

events.title: The "Raising The Flag On Iwo Jima" Photo Is Taken
events.description: "Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima," taken by Joe Rosenthal, is one of the most well-known photos in American history.

events.title: The First Polio Vaccines Are Administered
events.description: Children from Arsenal Elementary School in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, receive the first dose of the polio vaccine. Developed by Dr. Jonas Salk, the vaccine proved extremely effective and caused polio rates in the United States to plummet. Today, different polio vaccines have succeeded in reducing polio cases by 99 percent across the world.

events.title: The Boy In The Box Is Found
events.description: Investigators handed out a flyer about the boy to nearby communities.

events.title: William Bonin Is Executed
events.description: Serial killer William Bonin is executed by lethal injection, the first death row inmate to die by this method in California.

events.title: Holy Roman Emperor Charles V Is Born
events.description: Fine Art Images/Heritage Images/Getty ImagesCharles V oversaw many monumental events in European history as emperor.

events.title: First Union Prisoners Of War Arrive At Andersonville Prison
events.description: The first Union prisoners of war arrive at Andersonville Prison (Camp Sumter) in Georgia. Built to hold 10,000 prisoners, the notorious Civil War prison camp held nearly 45,000 by 1865. Brutal conditions at Andersonville, including overcrowding, disease, and lack of food and water, caused the deaths of 12,920 men.

events.title: The Cuban War Of Independence Begins
events.description: The Cuban War of Independence begins with uprisings across Cuba. The battle against Spanish rule lasted almost three years. It came to an end in 1898 after American intervention. This led to Cuban independence and the loss of Spain's territories in Guam, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines, to the United States.

events.title: Steve Jobs Is Born
events.description: Justin Sullivan/Getty ImagesBefore his death at the age of 56, Steve Jobs profoundly changed the world as the co-founder of Apple.

events.title: SeaWorld Trainer Dawn Brancheau Is Killed By An Orca
events.description: SeaWorld trainer Dawn Brancheau is killed by an orca named Tilikum while performing with the whale in Orlando, Florida. As horrified guests watched, Tilikum grabbed Brancheau and pulled her underwater. The 40-year-old trainer drowned and suffered horrific injuries, including a fractured jaw, a dislocated ear, knee, and arm, and broken ribs and vertebrae.

events.title: Pope Pius V Excommunicates Queen Elizabeth I
events.description: Pope Pius V excommunicates Queen Elizabeth I of England. Declaring the Protestant monarch a heretic, the pope stated that English Catholics did not have to remain loyal to Elizabeth and should remove her from the throne. However, Elizabeth's subjects did not heed the pope's command.

events.title: Robert Devereux Is Beheaded
events.description: Fine Art Images/Heritage Images/Getty ImagesRobert Devereux was a royal favorite of Queen Elizabeth I before their relationship soured.

events.title: Pierre-Auguste Renoir Is Born
events.description: Pierre-Auguste Renoir is born in Limoges, France. A famed painter, Renoir helped develop the Impressionist style. He's famous for artworks like Bal du moulin de la Galette, Luncheon of the Boating Party, Girls at the Piano, and more.

events.title: The "Battle Of Los Angeles" Takes Place
events.description: Residents of Los Angeles report seeing sirens, explosions, and searchlights in the wee hours of the morning. The so-called "Battle of Los Angeles" came just months after Pearl Harbor, leading many to surmise that the city was under attack by Japan. However, the true cause of the commotion is unknown to this day and may have actually been sparked by panicking servicemen opening fire on a military weather balloon.

events.title: Muhammad Ali Wins His First Title
events.description: Stanley Weston/Getty ImagesBoxer Muhammad Ali, pictured in 1962.

events.title: Cameron Hooker Is Sentenced For The Abduction And Rape Of Colleen Stan
events.description: YoutubeCameron Hooker, the abductor of Colleen Stan, is brought to trial in 1988.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Escapes From Exile
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesA depiction of Napoleon Bonaparte's 1815 escape from Elba.

events.title: "Buffalo Bill" Cody Is Born
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty Images"Buffalo Bill" Cody in front of a circus tent, circa 1915.

events.title: Boxer Rebellion Leaders Are Publicly Executed
events.description: Chi-Hsin and Hsu-Cheng-Yu are beheaded in Peking, China. Leaders of the Boxer Rebellion, their execution was ordered by Imperial edict. By that September, the rebellion — which had begun in 1899 and sought to drive out foreigners from China — had come to an end.

events.title: Hans Schmidt Marries Anna Aumuller
events.description: Infamous killer Hans Schmidt secretly marries Anna Aumuller. A Catholic priest, Schmidt's marriage to Aumuller was forbidden. When she became pregnant, he brutally murdered her to cover up their relationship and was later executed for his crime, becoming the only priest executed in the history of the United States.

events.title: The World Trade Center Is Bombed
events.description: Listen above to the History Uncovered podcast, episode 59: History Happy Hour, February 2023, also available on Apple and Spotify.

events.title: Monika Fritzl Is Born
events.description: Monika Fritzl, the fourth of child of Elisabeth Fritzl, who was being held captive by her father Josef Fritzl in their family basement, is born in Austria.

events.title: The First New Orleans Mardi Gras Celebration Takes Place
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA depiction of Mardi Gras in New Orleans, published in Harper's Weekly in 1873.

events.title: The Dominican Republic Declares Independence
events.description: The Dominican Republic declares independence. Previously ruled by the French and the Spanish, the country eventually proclaimed that it was an independent nation from its neighboring country, Haiti. Though Haiti controlled the Dominican Republic at that time, the Dominican War of Independence led to the official separation of the two.

events.title: Elizabeth Taylor Is Born
events.description: Silver Screen Collection/Getty ImagesElizabeth Taylor was famous for her accomplishments as an actress and for her seven husbands.

events.title: Joe Gallo Kidnaps Members Of The Profaci Crime Family
events.description: New York mobster Joe Gallo kidnaps high-ranking members of his own criminal organization, the Profaci crime family, to demand that less tribute be kicked up to Mafia bosses. This incident would spark the First Colombo War.

events.title: The Presidential Palace In Saigon Is Bombed
events.description: Independence Palace in Saigon, South Vietnam, is bombed by two dissidents from the Republic of Vietnam Air Force. The dissidents had hoped to assassinate the president, Ngô Đình Diệm, but he escaped the attack. Three palace staff members died, however, and 30 other people were injured.

events.title: Fred Rogers Dies At 74
events.description: Beloved television icon Fred Rogers dies at age 74 following a battle with stomach cancer. He perished peacefully inside his Pittsburgh home with his wife of 50 years, Joanne, by his side. Immediately, tributes came from all corners of the country.

events.title: T.J. Lane Perpetrates The Chardon High School Shooting
events.description: Jeff Swensen/Getty ImagesMemorial for the victims of the Chardon High School shooting.

events.title: Cuauhtémoc Is Executed
events.description: Cuauhtémoc is hanged by the forces of Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés. The last Aztec emperor, Cuauhtémoc was executed because Cortés feared that the ruler would rebel against him and other Spaniards. He is a celebrated figure in Mexico today.

events.title: Bugsy Siegel Is Born
events.description: American Stock/Getty ImagesBenjamin "Bugsy" Siegel lighting a cigar. 1940.

events.title: James Watson And Francis Crick Discover The Double Helix Of DNA
events.description: Famed scientists James Watson and Francis Crick announce that they've discovered that DNA exists in the form of a three-dimensional double helix. With this discovery, the two experts were able to determine that DNA replicates itself in order to pass on genes. Since then, DNA has been used for a variety of purposes, from detective work to medical studies.

events.title: Persian Gulf War Ends
events.description: The Persian Gulf War ends with an Iraqi defeat. The president of Iraq, Saddam Hussein, ordered the invasion of Kuwait in August of 1990. The conflict stemmed from oil production disputes between the two countries. After not receiving the desired compensation for lost oil revenues, Iraq began bombing Kuwait's capital city. An invasion followed, and Kuwait quickly fell.

events.title: Federal Agents Raid The Branch Davidian Compound
events.description: Robert Daemmrich Photography Inc/Sygma via Getty ImagesThe Branch Davidian compound in Waco, Texas, on the day of the first raid.

events.title: The First Leap Day Is Recognized
events.description: The first leap day is recognized after the adoption of the Julian Calendar. Created by Julius Caesar, it was somewhat similar to the Egyptian model but with a key difference: Instead of watching astronomical objects to determine when an intercalary month needed to be inserted, the Julian Calendar would include an extra day in February every fourth year.

events.title: The Salem Witch Trials Begin
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA depiction of the Salem witch trials, which led to 25 deaths.

events.title: Hattie McDaniel Wins An Oscar
events.description: Hattie McDaniel wins the Best Supporting Actress Oscar for her role as Mammy in Gone With The Wind. The first Black person to win an Oscar, McDaniel told the crowd: "I sincerely hope that I shall always be a credit to my race and the motion picture industry." However, she continued to face racism despite her win and struggled to find roles that differed from Mammy.

events.title: Richard Ramirez Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesRichard Ramirez makes a gesture while in court in 1985.

events.title: Katherine Knight Kills John Price
events.description: Katherine Knight kills her lover John Price in Australia. Knight had a troubled upbringing and a string of failed and often violent relationships before meeting John Price. After an argument with Price, Knight became enraged and plotted to kill him. Days later, Knight stabbed him 37 times in the chest, and in a horrific turn of events, she cooked his body parts and served it to his children. Police quickly arrested her for the crime, and she became the first woman in Australian history to receive a sentence of life in prison.

events.title: Yellowstone Becomes The First U.S. National Park
events.description: President Ulysses S. Grant signs an act to "set apart a certain tract of land lying near the head-waters of the Yellowstone River as a public park." The act prevented the land from being settled or sold, and Yellowstone became the first national park in the United States. Today, the National Park System boasts 63 national parks across America and 423 total protected "units," including historical monuments, battlefields, and memorials.

events.title: Jack McCall Is Executed
events.description: Jack McCall, who murdered "Wild Bill" Hickok by shooting him in the back of the head at a Deadwood, South Dakota, saloon, is hanged for his crimes.

events.title: Albert Berry Makes The First Successful Parachute Jump From A Moving Plane
events.description: National Air and Space MuseumAlbert Berry completing the first parachute jump from an airplane.

events.title: The Lindbergh Baby Is Kidnapped
events.description: FBIYoung Charles Lindbergh, Jr., shortly before his kidnapping and murder.

events.title: The Castle Bravo Nuclear Test Takes Place
events.description: The U.S. military conducts the Castle Bravo test, dropping the country's most powerful nuclear device — and one 1,000 times more powerful than the bomb dropped on Hiroshima — at Bikini Atoll.

events.title: Weather Underground Bombs The U.S. Capitol Building
events.description: Weather Underground, a radical far-left organization, bombs the U.S. Capitol building in Washington, D.C. The explosion caused $300,000 in damage, but there were no casualties. The group claimed they carried out the bombing in protest of the invasion of Laos, which the U.S. government was backing. Weather Underground also bombed 24 other locations over the course of seven years, including the Pentagon, to protest American imperialism.

events.title: Charlie Wilkinson Murders The Caffey Family
events.description: Charlie Wilkinson, the boyfriend of 16-year-old Erin Caffey, breaks into her home in Emory, Texas armed with a gun and a sword and kills her mother and two brothers, then burns her house to the ground. Wilkinson's friend, Charles Waid, assists with the deadly attack. It was later revealed that Caffey had helped Wilkinson plan the murders because she was angry with her religious parents for ordering her to break up with him. Erin Caffey's father, Terry, ended up surviving the rampage. Both Wilkinson and Caffey were sentenced to life in prison, though Caffey will eventually be eligible for parole.

events.title: Texas Declares Independence From Mexico
events.description: In the midst of the Texas Revolution, the Republic of Texas formally declares independence from Mexico. During the Convention of 1836, delegates approved a draft of the Texas Declaration of Independence, and the territory became its own nation. David Burnet was declared provisional president, and Sam Houston became the commander-in-chief of Texan forces. It wasn't until 1845 that Texas would become part of the United States of America.

events.title: Dr. Seuss Is Born
events.description: Dr. Seuss with his famous book The Cat in the Hat in 1957.

events.title: Puerto Rico Becomes A U.S. Territory
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson signs the Jones-Shafroth Act, making Puerto Rico a U.S. territory and granting American citizenship to Puerto Ricans. The bill recognized the island as an "organized but unincorporated" territory of the U.S. It also restructured Puerto Rico's government, allowing it limited political autonomy.

events.title: Shoko Asahara Is Born
events.description: Wojtek Laski/Getty ImagesShoko Asahara in 1994.

events.title: The Concorde Takes Its Maiden Flight
events.description: The Concorde, the supersonic jet that could travel between London and New York in roughly three hours, takes its maiden flight in Toulouse, France.

events.title: Natascha Kampusch Is Kidnapped
events.description: Natascha Kampusch is kidnapped by Wolfgang Přiklopil in Austria. Pulled into a van while walking on the street, Kampusch spent the next 3,000 days in her abductor's cellar. Kampusch used her empathy to relate to her abductor, gaining his trust by asking him for favors and affection. Eight years into her captivity, Kampusch was able to escape by running away from the property and calling for help. Before police could arrest Přiklopil, he committed suicide.

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell Is Born
events.description: Scientist and inventor Alexander Graham Bell is born in Edinburgh, Scotland. He began inventing at an early age, creating a wheat de-husking machine when he was just 12 years old. However, Bell is best known for patenting the first telephone in 1876. He famously refused to have a phone in his office, as he said it interfered with his real work as a scientist and engineer. Bell also helped found the American Telephone and Telegraph Company (AT&T) in 1885.

events.title: Emperor Alexander II Frees Serfs In The Russian Empire
events.description: Emperor Alexander II of Russia frees serfs in the Russian Empire. The Emancipation Reform of 1861 granted 23 million serfs freedom to marry without approval from a lord, the right to own property, and the right to own a business. Serfs were peasants who worked a noble's land without pay. Usually, the serf was attached to the land, meaning that a lord could not sell an individual serf, but they could transfer the land on which the serf worked to another, effectively "selling" or "trading" the serf to another lord. After the Emancipation Reform of 1861, serfs were able to buy land of their own for the first time.

events.title: The First Issue Of TIME Is Published
events.description: Twitter/The Daily StarThe first cover of TIME magazine.

events.title: "The Star-Spangled Banner" Becomes The U.S. National Anthem
events.description: President Herbert Hoover declares "The Star-Spangled Banner" America's official national anthem. The lyrics were written more than 100 years prior by Francis Scott Key during the War of 1812, and they were eventually set to the tune of the English song "To Anacreon in Heaven." Though most branches of the armed forces had considered "The Star-Spangled Banner" the national anthem during the 19th century, it wasn't until 1931 that the government officially adopted it.

events.title: Los Angeles Police Beat Rodney King
events.description: YouTubeA screenshot of the video that ultimately sparked the Los Angeles riots of 1992.

events.title: Edward IV Becomes King Of England
events.description: An oil painting of King Edward IV, circa 1540.

events.title: Antonio Vivaldi Is Born
events.description: A probable portrait of Vivaldi from 1723.

events.title: First Meeting Of The U.S. Congress Takes Place
events.description: The newly-formed Senate of the United States meets for the first time in New York City. Only eight members were present, and 12 were necessary to make the meeting valid, so it wasn't until April 6, 1789, that they were able to complete their first official task as Senate: certifying George Washington's election to the presidency.

events.title: Swan Lake Premieres
events.description: The world's first performance of Swan Lake takes place at Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow, Russia. The original production was choreographed by Julius Reisinger, though a more popular version choreographed by Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov that premiered in 1895 is more commonly performed today. The score was composed by Pyotr Tchaikovsky, who also famously wrote the music for The Nutcracker ballet.

events.title: Nosferatu Premieres In Berlin
events.description: The iconic vampire film Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror — a blatant rip off of Bram Stoker's Dracula by German filmmakers — premieres in Berlin.

events.title: Pamela Smart Trial Begins In New Hampshire
events.description: Pamela Smart, convicted of manipulating her teenage lover to kill her husband, goes to court for America's first televised murder trial.

events.title: John Candy Dies
events.description: Alan Singer/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal/Getty ImagesJohn Candy on Saturday Night Live in 1983.

events.title: King Henry II Of England Is Born
events.description: Henry II, who served as King of England from 1154 to 1189, is born in Le Mans, France. Henry was the first king of the House of Plantagenet, which would rule for the next 300 years. He was known for expanding England's realm and laying the foundation for English Common Law. Henry's marriage to Eleanor of Aquitaine produced eight children, including the future King Richard I.

events.title: The Boston Massacre Takes Place
events.description: The Boston Massacre breaks out in Massachusetts, leaving five colonists dead. British troops were stationed in order to enforce Britain's tax laws, which were unpopular among colonists. On the day of the massacre, a crowd of Patriots was violently threatening a British soldier, who eventually struck a colonist and called for reinforcements. One of the soldiers who arrived fired a shot, and others followed suit. Two soldiers were eventually convicted of manslaughter for the incident.

events.title: Joseph Stalin Dies
events.description: Joseph Stalin circa 1942, about a decade before he died at his dacha.

events.title: Jim Morrison Is Accused Of Exposing Himself During A Concert
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJim Morrison arrives in court to face his charges for indecent exposure.

events.title: John Belushi Dies
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesCrowds gather as John Belushi's body is transported to the coroner's office after his death.

events.title: Michelangelo Is Born
events.description: A portrait of Michelangelo by Daniele da Volterra, circa 1545.

events.title: The Alamo Falls
events.description: The Fall of the Alamo by Robert Jenkins Onderdonk. 1903.

events.title: The Dred Scott Case Is Decided
events.description: The United States Supreme Court decides the case of Dred Scott v. Sandford in favor of the defendant — a landmark result in American judicial history. An enslaved man, Dred Scott had been taken by his owners from Missouri, where slavery was legal, to Illinois and the Wisconsin territory, where it was illegal. Scott then sued for his freedom, arguing that because his owners had taken him into free territory, he thus became free.

events.title: Bayer Patents Aspirin
events.description: German pharmaceutical company Bayer patents the anti-inflammatory drug aspirin, also known as acetylsalicylic acid. The active ingredient in the medication, salicin, had been used as far back as ancient Greece for pain relief. However, Bayer employee Felix Hoffmann discovered a way to create a more stable form of the drug — and aspirin was born. Its name comes from "a" for acetyl, "spir" for spirea, one of the sources of salicin, and "in" as a common suffix for medications. Today, it's still one of the most commonly used drugs in the world.

events.title: The Rosenberg Espionage Trial Begins
events.description: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg in 1951.

events.title: Marianne Bachmeier Shoots Her Daughter's Killer Dead In Court
events.description: Marianne Bachmeier fatally shoots Klaus Grabowski, the man accused of murdering her seven-year-old daughter, right in the middle of a West German courtroom. In 1980, police found seven-year-old Anna Bachmeier dead near a canal in Lübeck. Grabowski's fiancé then tipped off the police and he was arrested.

events.title: Viktor Bout Is Arrested In Thailand
events.description: Viktor Bout, a prolific Russian arms dealer, is arrested in a sting operation in Thailand. Bout was later found guilty by a U.S. jury of conspiracy to kill American citizens and officials, the delivery of anti-aircraft missiles, and providing aid to a terrorist organization. He was sentenced to 25 years in jail before being exchanged for U.S. basketball player Brittney Griner, who was detained in Russia, in 2022.

events.title: Marcus Aurelius Becomes Emperor Of Rome
events.description: Marcus Aurelius becomes the Emperor of Rome upon the death of his adoptive father, Antoninus Pius. Marcus ruled alongside his adoptive brother, Lucius Verus, until Lucius' death in 169, and he was known as the last of the so-called "Five Good Emperors." He was also the last emperor of the Pax Romana, a period of relative peace that the Roman Empire had experienced for 200 years, before the disastrous rule of his son Commodus.

events.title: Joseph Nicéphore Niépce Is Born
events.description: Joseph Nicéphore Niépce, a French inventor who took the first photo ever taken, is born in Chalon-sur-Saône, France.

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell Receives A Patent For The Telephone
events.description: Scottish-born American inventor Alexander Graham Bell patents the first telephone, forever changing the future of communication. Bell sought to improve on the concept of Samuel Morse's telegraph, which had been developed in the 1840s. Aided by Thomas Watson, Bell created a device that used vibrations and electrical currents to replicate a sound across a distance. The first message spoken over the telephone was reportedly, "Mr. Watson, come here, I need you."

events.title: The First Monopoly Game Is Created
events.description: The Strong National Museum of PlayAn original Monopoly set from 1933.

events.title: The First Class of Tuskegee Airmen Graduates
events.description: The first class of Tuskegee Airmen graduate from the Tuskegee Army Air Field, becoming the first Black military pilots in American history.

events.title: The "Bloody Sunday" Attack Takes Place In Alabama
events.description: John Lewis (right, wearing light coat) and other marchers just before clashing with police on "Bloody Sunday."

events.title: "Amazon Review Killer" Todd Kohlhepp Is Born
events.description: Todd Kohlhepp, later known as the "Amazon Review Killer," is born in Ft. Lauderdale. Committing violent acts like abduction and rape since his youth, Kohlhepp spent most of his childhood incarcerated. After his release at 30-years-old, Kohlhepp moved to South Carolina and started his own real estate business. It is here where he began committing crimes once again, this time escalating to murder.

events.title: Hachikō, The Famous Japanese Akita, Dies
events.description: Hachikō, the loyal Akita who became famous for waiting at Shibuya Station every day for over nine years after his owner Hidesaburō Ueno passed away in 1925, dies.

events.title: Queen Anne Takes The English Throne
events.description: King William III of England dies shortly after breaking his collarbone while falling from his horse, and Queen Anne ascends to the throne. Anne ruled over England, Scotland, and Ireland for 12 years, overseeing the Acts of Union between England and Scotland that turned them into the sovereign state of Great Britain. Anne had 17 pregnancies, but none of her children survived to adulthood, so she was the last monarch of the House of Stuart.

events.title: The February Revolution Begins In Russia
events.description: Protesters in Petrograd in March 1917.

events.title: Eduardo Dato Is Assassinated
events.description: Eduardo Dato, the prime minister of Spain, is assassinated in Madrid while riding from the Parliament building. His chauffeur was also reportedly killed by the gunfire. Dato's assassins were Luis Nicolau, Pedro Mateu, and Ramón Casanellas, Catalan anarchists who drove behind Dato's car and fired several revolver shots until they murdered him.

events.title: The Lonely Hearts Killers Are Executed
events.description: Raymond Martinez Fernandez and Martha Jule Beck, the "Lonely Hearts Killers."

events.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 Vanishes Over The Indian Ocean
events.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 mysteriously disappears while flying from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. Air traffic control lost communication with the crew 40 minutes after takeoff, but military radar tracked the aircraft as it deviated from its flight path for another hour until it left the radar's range and investigators were forced to use satellite data. The most expensive underwater search in history followed, but the airplane was never found, and all 239 people onboard are presumed dead.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Marries Joséphine De Beauharnais
events.description: The future French emperor Napoleon Bonaparte, then the commander of the Army of Italy, weds Joséphine de Beauharnais, the widow of a French political figure who was beheaded during the Reign of Terror. Napoleon famously adored his first wife. However, they separated in 1810 after Joséphine failed to produce an heir, though they reportedly remained in contact.

events.title: The Barbie Doll Debuts
events.description: A 1959 Barbie doll with brunette hair.

events.title: Hiroo Onoda Surrenders
events.description: JIJI PRESS/AFP/Getty ImagesHiroo Onoda surrendering his sword to Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos.

events.title: "Silent Twins" Jennifer Gibbons dies
events.description: "Silent Twins" Jennifer Gibbons dies, leaving behind her twin, June. For nearly 30 years, Jennifer and June Gibbons only spoke to each other. Speaking often in their own private language, the twins were nicknamed the "Silent Twins." In school, the duo would only speak to each other, refuse to write, and even mirror each other's actions. As the women got older, they began committing petty crimes and eventually landed in a psychiatric facility. It is here where Jennifer Gibbons would pass away from sudden inflammation of the heart. After, June began speaking as if she had been doing it her whole life.

events.title: The Notorious B.I.G. Is Murdered
events.description: American rapper Christopher George Latore Wallace, better known as the Notorious B.I.G. or Biggie Smalls, is killed in a drive-by shooting in Los Angeles. Biggie was in L.A. to attend the Soul Train Music Awards, and he was leaving an after-party when a Chevy Impala pulled up alongside the vehicle he was traveling in. An occupant of the Impala fired several shots, and Biggie was struck by four bullets. The 24-year-old died during emergency surgery at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.

events.title: The Battle Of The Aegates Occurs
events.description: The naval fleets of Rome and Carthage meet during the Battle of the Aegates during the First Punic War. The battle took place off the coast of Sicily, and Rome's victory led them to win the 23-year-long war. As a result of the battle, Carthage was forced to surrender Sicily to Rome and pay hefty damages, and Rome increased its military power in the Mediterranean.

events.title: Harriet Tubman Dies
events.description: Harriet Tubman in the final years of her life.

events.title: Christine Collins' Son, Walter Collins, Disappears in Los Angeles
events.description: Christine Collins' son, Walter Collins, disappears in Los Angeles after asking his mother for money to go see a movie. Months would go by with no leads, then suddenly a boy in Illinois claimed to be Walter Collins. Christine knew immediately that the boy was not her son, but the police were adamant that he was. The police would eventually put Christine in a psychiatric ward for refusing to take care of the boy.

events.title: The Firebombing Of Tokyo Takes Place
events.description: Galerie Bilderwelt/Getty ImagesBurnt corpses litter the streets after the firebombing of Tokyo.

events.title: James Earl Ray Pleads Guilty To Assassinating Martin Luther King Jr.
events.description: James Earl Ray pleads guilty to the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr. in April 1968 in order to avoid the death penalty and is sentenced to 99 years in prison. Just three days after entering the plea, however, Ray moved to withdraw it. He claimed he was set up as part of a large conspiracy, but his motion was denied and his sentence was upheld. Ray died while incarcerated nearly 30 years later in 1998.

events.title: Māori Warriors Burn Kororāreka
events.description: During the Flagstaff War between New Zealand's Indigenous Māori population and British colonizers, the Māori burn the town of Kororāreka during a bloody battle. Ngāpuhi chief Hōne Heke Pōkai led hundreds of warriors into the town, which is now known as Russell, and began fighting against British forces. The Māori destroyed troops' reserve ammunition, causing the British to retreat, and then burned the rest of the settlement over the following days.

events.title: The Great Blizzard Of 1888
events.description: New York City during the Great Blizzard of 1888.

events.title: "Cropsey Killer" Andre Rand Is Born
events.description: Andre Rand, also known as the "Cropsey Killer" and the "Pied Piper of Staten Island," is born Frank Rushan in New York City. In 1983, Rand kidnapped 11 children from a Staten Island YMCA, loaded them onto a school bus, and drove them to an airport. The kids were unharmed, but Rand was sentenced to 10 months in prison for the abduction. Five years later, Rand was convicted of kidnapping 12-year-old Jennifer Schweiger, and he's suspected of killing her as well as several other young victims.

events.title: The Fukushima Nuclear Disaster
events.description: Damage to the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant after the 2011 tsunami and earthquake.

events.title: The Lululemon Murder
events.description: The Lululemon murders occur in Bethesda, Maryland. Rachel Oertli, manager of the athletic store Lululemon, called police after finding two badly beaten women in the back of the store. Police arrived on scene to find Jayna Murray dead and Brittany Norwood severely traumatized. Norwood told police that two men entered the store around closing time, raped her and Murray, and then stabbed Murray to death. Inconsistencies with Norwood's story, as well as physical evidence pointing to her guilt, eventually led police to arrest her for the murder.

events.title: Gothic Siege Of Rome Ends
events.description: After a year, the first siege of Rome by the Ostrogothic army comes to an end. Part of the Gothic War, the siege began in March 537 C.E. when the Ostrogoths marched on Rome and set up camps at all major access routes to the city in an attempt to starve the citizens. They also blocked aqueducts that provided drinking water. The siege ended when the Goths abandoned Rome to defend their capital city of Ravenna.

events.title: Girl Scouts Is Founded
events.description: Juliette Gordon Low founds the Girl Scouts of the USA, a youth organization that seeks to empower young girls and teach them leadership skills. After meeting Robert Baden-Powell, the founder of the worldwide Scout Movement, Low, a Savannah, Georgia native, reportedly called her cousin and said, "I've got something for the girls of Savannah, and all of America, and all the world, and we're going to start it tonight!"

events.title: Gandhi's Salt March Begins
events.description: Gandhi leads his followers during the Salt March.

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt Holds The First "Fireside Chat"
events.description: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt addresses the nation over the radio in what would become known as his first "Fireside Chat." Between 1933 and 1944, Roosevelt gave these addresses about things like the Great Depression and World War II, speaking to Americans with familiarity and self-assurance in terms that made sense to the average listener. The president always began the speeches with "my friends," setting the tone for the chats that kept him in high regard with the general public.

events.title: Sammy Gravano Is Born
events.description: Jeffrey Markowitz/Sygma via Getty Images"Sammy the Bull" Gravano prepares to testify against his fellow gangsters in a New York courtroom in 1992.

events.title: Olga Hepnarová Is Executed
events.description: Mass murderess Olga Hepnarová of Czechoslovakia is put to death for fatally hitting eight people with a truck in Prague in 1973. Hepnarová had intentionally driven a large truck into a group of people standing on the sidewalk, claiming that she wanted to "pay back" her "haters" because she despised society. She was hanged for her crimes and became the last woman ever executed in Czechoslovakia.

events.title: William Herschel Discovers Uranus
events.description: Though widely known as an astronomer, William Herschel was also a noted composer.

events.title: Czar Alexander II Is Assassinated
events.description: Czar Alexander II of Russia is assassinated in St. Petersburg by young revolutionary Ignacy Hryniewiecki. The assassin, who was a member of the political group Narodnaya Volya, or "People's Will," threw a bomb at him, causing a deafening explosion. The czar was taken to his palace, where doctors discovered that his legs had been partially blown off, and he soon bled to death.

events.title: The "Great Blizzard" Rocks America's East Coast
events.description: A collapsed awning in New York City during the Blizzard of 1888.

events.title: An Assassination Attempt Fails To Take Adolf Hitler's Life
events.description: Conspirators within the German military try and fail to kill Adolf Hitler via multiple methods. Hitler was in Smolensk, Russia on his way back to Germany after a visit to the Eastern Front. It was there that ringleaders Henning von Tresckow, Fabian von Schlabrendorff, and Georg von Boeselager tried to make multiple attempts on his life in quick succession.

events.title: Kitty Genovese Is Murdered
events.description: Kitty Genovese, whose murder led to studies on the "bystander effect."

events.title: The Dunblane Massacre Takes Place
events.description: Thomas Hamilton fatally shoots 16 students and a teacher, then kills himself, at Dunblane Primary School near Stirling, Scotland. Hamilton, 43, had previously been accused of inappropriate behavior toward young boys. The Dunblane massacre was the deadliest school shooting in British history, and the tragedy led to heavy firearm restrictions in the United Kingdom, largely outlawing the private ownership of handguns.

events.title: The Phoenix Lights UFO Incident Occurs
events.description: A recreation of the V-shaped craft seen during the Phoenix Lights incident of 1997.

events.title: Eli Whitney Patents The Cotton Gin
events.description: American inventor Eli Whitney receives a patent for the cotton gin, a new piece of technology that greatly improves the processing of cotton. The cotton gin removed seeds from cotton fiber, a previously labor-intensive process. Plantation owners were able to plant even more cotton because of the device, thus increasing the demand for the labor of enslaved people who would be forced to pick the crop.

events.title: Albert Einstein Is Born
events.description: Albert Einstein, German-Swiss theoretical physicist, with his first wife Mileva, circa 1905.

events.title: Nicholas Winton Rescues Jewish Children From Prague
events.description: Yad Vashem Photo Archives/United States Holocaust Memorial MuseumNicholas Winton saved over 600 children during the Holocaust.

events.title: The FBI Releases The First Ten Most Wanted List
events.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) releases its first list of the "Ten Most Wanted Fugitives," hoping to enlist the American public in their hunt for the country's most dangerous criminals. Since its debut, the list has led to the capture of at least 163 offenders thanks to tips from the public. To date, 529 fugitives have been featured on the list over the years, with only 11 of them being women.

events.title: Jack Ruby Is Sentenced To Death
events.description: Jack Ruby shot Lee Harvey Oswald with a .38-caliber revolver.

events.title: Julius Caesar Is Assassinated
events.description: The Murder of Caesar by Karl von Piloty, 1865.

events.title: Christopher Columbus Completes His First Voyage To The New World
events.description: After traveling to the New World and claiming lands for Spain, Christopher Columbus arrives back in Europe. Upon landing in Spain, Columbus wrote to King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella informing them of his "discoveries." The explorer also brought gold, native flora and fauna, and even several Native Americans he'd kidnapped back to Europe with him as proof of the New World.

events.title: Czar Nicholas II Abdicates The Russian Throne
events.description: As a result of the February Revolution, Czar Nicholas II of Russia is forced off of the throne by insurgents. Nicholas grew unpopular among much of the Russian population after he withdrew promises of a representative government, and when his people began starving during World War I, they demanded reforms. The Romanovs were imprisoned in various palaces before they were killed in 1918.

events.title: Ruth Bader Ginsburg Is Born
events.description: Ruth Bader Ginsburg in 2016.

events.title: The NKVD Ceases Operations
events.description: The Soviet secret police known as the NKVD is reorganized into the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MVD) and the Ministry of State Security (MGB). The NKVD was the force responsible for orchestrating the Great Purge and executing hundreds of thousands of ethnic minorities in the Soviet Union.

events.title: The Syrian Civil War Begins
events.description: The Syrian Civil War begins between the Syrian Arab Republic led by Syrian President Assad and various opposing forces. The unrest began after the Arab Spring, a series of anti-government protests that swept across the Middle East and Northern Africa in the 2010s, inspired groups to oppose Assad. Violence broke out, and so far over half a million people have died in the conflict. The civil war also sparked the largest refugee crisis in the world, with 14 million Syrians fleeing to seek asylum in other countries.

events.title: Caligula Becomes Emperor Of Rome
events.description: Emperor Tiberius dies in Misenum, and Caligula takes over as the ruler of the Roman Empire. Though 77-year-old Tiberius likely died of natural causes, ancient historian Suetonius wrote that Caligula may have murdered him. Few records remain documenting his reign, but those that survive paint him as a cruel tyrant who devolved into insanity before conspirators assassinated him just four years after he became emperor.

events.title: Samoset Contacts Plymouth Colonists
events.description: Samoset, an English-speaking member of the Abenaki tribe, walks into Plymouth Colony and greets the Pilgrims in their own language, establishing contact between the settlers and local Native Americans.

events.title: Nathaniel Hawthorne Publishes The Scarlet Letter
events.description: American author Nathaniel Hawthorne publishes The Scarlet Letter to immediate success. The book became an instant best-seller, with the first 2,500 printed copies selling out in just 10 days. The story of Hester Prynne, the young woman who births a child out of wedlock and is forced to wear a scarlet "A" on her clothes as a symbol of her adultery, was one of the first mass-produced books in America.

events.title: Judge Roy Bean Dies
events.description: The courthouse of Judge Roy Bean, circa 1900.

events.title: The My Lai Massacre Takes Place
events.description: The road out of My Lai, littered with dead bodies.

events.title: Tammi Terrell Dies Of Brain Cancer
events.description: Tammi Terrell, an American Motown artist, dies of brain cancer at 24 years old.

events.title: Gary Plauché Kills Son's Rapist In The Airport
events.description: Gary Plauché kills Jeff Ducet, his son's rapist, at the Baton Rouge Airport in Louisiana. After Ducet abducted and sexually assaulted his son, Plauché vowed that he would kill the man. Plauché reportedly found out that Ducet would fly into the Baton Rouge Airport to face trial in Louisiana. With his face hidden, Plauché arrived at the airport, spotted Ducet and his police officer escorts, and shot Ducet in the head.

events.title: Rachel Corrie Is Killed
events.description: Rachel Corrie, a 23-year-old American activist, is crushed to death by an Israeli bulldozer while acting as a "human shield" in front of homes in Gaza.

events.title: Josef Fritzl's Trial Begins
events.description: The trial of Josef Fritzl, the Austrian man accused of imprisoning his daughter, Elisabeth, for 24 years in the cellar beneath their home, begins. Fritzl eventually plead guilty to all charges against him and was sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole for 15 years.

events.title: Marcus Aurelius Dies
events.description: Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius dies. His death marked the end of the Pax Romana, the longest period of uninterrupted peace in Roman history.

events.title: Saint Patrick Dies
events.description: A woodcut of Ireland's patron saint in the Nuremberg Chronicle of 1493.

events.title: Victor Emmanuel II Becomes King Of Italy
events.description: Victor Emmanuel II assumes the title of King of Italy, becoming the first king of the united country since the sixth century. He had ruled as the King of Sardinia since 1849, but when the various states of the Italian Peninsula came together into a single country 1861 during the Wars of Italian Unification, Victor Emmanuel was proclaimed king by the new Parliament. Under his rule, the unification of the country was completed.

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt Marries Eleanor Roosevelt
events.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and MuseumEleanor and Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1906.

events.title: John Wayne Gacy Is Born
events.description: American serial killer John Wayne Gacy is born in Chicago, Illinois to an abusive father and a mother who tried and failed to protect him. He was sexually assaulted by a family friend as a child, and he reportedly began molesting other children at a young age.

events.title: Mount Vesuvius Erupts
events.description: Mount Vesuvius — which destroyed Pompeii in 79 C.E. — erupts, prompting the evacuation of Allied troops stationed nearby during World War II.

events.title: Hello Kitty Murder Victim Is Abducted
events.description: Hello Kitty Murder victim Fan Man-yee is abducted by Chan Man-lok and his henchmen. Twenty-three-year-old Fan Man-yee was working as a hostess and prostitute in Hong Kong when she met Chan Man-lok, a 34-year-old drug dealer and socialite. Reportedly, Fan stole Chan's wallet, making off with the $4,000 inside it.

events.title: Morgan Earp Is Assassinated In Tombstone, Arizona
events.description: Lawman Morgan Earp is assassinated in Tombstone, Arizona months after participating in the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

events.title: King George I Of Greece Is Assassinated
events.description: George I, the King of Greece, is assassinated by Alexandros Schinas while on an afternoon walk in Thessaloniki. When he was arrested, Schinas reportedly told police that he'd killed the king because he wouldn't give him money. The assassin described himself as a socialist, though his political beliefs were likely more anarchist. The Greek government, however, denied that the assassination was political, claiming Schinas was simply a mentally ill alcoholic.

events.title: Alexei Leonov Walks In Space
events.description: Science Photo LibraryAlexei Leonov during the first-ever spacewalk.

events.title: Marien Ngouabi Is Assassinated
events.description: Marien Ngouabi, the third president of the People's Republic of the Congo, is assassinated at his Brazzaville residence. He reportedly "died fighting" and was found with his weapon still in his hand. The president had come to power during a coup in 1968, and he had survived several other attempts to overthrow his administration. Several of his political rivals were accused in the attack, and a few of them were executed, including Ngouabi's predecessor, former president Alphonse Massamba-Débat.

events.title: John Favara Accidentally Runs Over Frank Gotti
events.description: John Favara fatally runs over Frank Gotti, son of Mafia boss John Gotti, in New York City. When Frank Gotti biked across the street to play, and intoxicated Favara struck the boy with his car and dragged his body for 200 feet as people screamed for him to stop. Later, Favara expressed no remorse for his actions, instead blaming the young Gotti for being reckless.

events.title: The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum Heist Takes Place
events.description: David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty ImagesThe empty frames of the stolen works of art remain on the walls of the museum.

events.title: David Livingstone Is Born
events.description: David Livingstone in 1861.

events.title: Wyatt Earp Is Born In Monmouth, Illinois
events.description: Lawman Wyatt Earp is born in Monmouth, Illinois. Earp, alongside his brothers, would go on to play a large role in the gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona.

events.title: U.S. President Woodrow Wilson Establishes Daylight Savings Time
events.description: Woodrow Wilson establishes daylight savings time by signing the Calder Act. This act required all Americans to set their clocks to standard time. Then on March 31, they would be required to abandon standard time and push their clocks ahead in the country's first experiment with daylight savings. Within a year, the act was repealed after Americans complained about its effects on their lives and even their religion. Despite the act's repeal, several states decided to uphold daylight savings, and Congress passed the 1996 Uniform Time Act, which required states to adhere to six months of standard time and six of daylight saving.

events.title: Nevada Legalizes Gambling
events.description: The state of Nevada votes to legalize gambling in an effort to combat economic hardships brought on by the Great Depression. The state's gold and silver mines that had first brought settlers to the area were declining, and government officials realized they needed a new way to bring in revenue.

events.title: The Academy Awards Are First Broadcast On Television
events.description: Listen above to the History Uncovered podcast, episode 62: History Happy Hour, March 2023, also available on Apple and Spotify.

events.title: David Bowie Marries His First Wife, Angie Bowie
events.description: Performer David Bowie marries his first wife, Angie Bowie, in England. The duo had a decade-long unorthodox marriage that produced David Bowie's son, Duncan Jones.

events.title: The War In Iraq Begins
events.description: RAMZI HAIDAR/AFP via Getty ImagesAn air raid on Baghdad in the first days of the War in Iraq.

events.title: Ovid Is Born
events.description: Roman poet Pūblius Ovidius Nāsō, better known as Ovid, is born in Sulmo, Italy. Along with Virgil and Horace, Ovid is frequently considered one of the greatest poets of Roman literature. His most well-known work is Metamorphoses, a collection of mythological stories about humans transforming into other objects. Ovid was extremely popular during his lifetime, but he was banished to an island on the Black Sea by Emperor Augustus, possibly for adultery.

events.title: Henry V Ascends To The English Throne
events.description: National Portrait Gallery/Wikimedia CommonsA portrait of King Henry V of England, painted in the late 16th or early 17th century.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Returns From Exile
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte returns to Paris from his 11-month exile in Italy, marking the beginning of the "Hundred Days," or the War of the Seventh Coalition. Back in Paris, he raised an army in an effort to regain power.

events.title: Harriet Beecher Stowe Publishes Uncle Tom's Cabin
events.description: Uncle Tom's Cabin, Harriet Beecher Stowe's famous anti-slavery novel, is published to immense success. Within just three months, more than 300,000 copies had been sold. The book greatly influenced much of America's views on slavery, and Abraham Lincoln reportedly said to Stowe in 1862, "So this is the little lady who made this big war." Today, the novel — reportedly inspired by a real-life enslaved man named Josiah Henson — remains one of the most important texts in American history.

events.title: Fred Rogers Is Born
events.description: Family Communications Inc./Getty ImagesFred Rogers posing with a trolley from his beloved children's show Mister Rogers' Neighborhood in 1980.

events.title: Patty Hearst Is Convicted Of Armed Robbery
events.description: San Mateo County Sheriff's Office/Wikimedia CommonsPatty Hearst's mugshot following her arrest for armed robbery.

events.title: Pocahontas' Funeral Is Held
events.description: John Gadsby Chapman/U.S. CapitolJohn Gadsby Chapman's Baptism of Pocahontas that depicts her conversion to Christianity just a few years before her death.

events.title: Johann Sebastian Bach Is Born
events.description: Johann Sebastian Bach, the celebrated Baroque composer, is born in Eisenach, Germany. He began his musical education at a young age, but during his lifetime he was mainly known for his skill at playing the organ. It wasn't until after his death in 1750 that he came to be regarded as one of the greatest composers in history. Some of his most well-known works include the Brandenburg Concertos and The Well-Tempered Clavier.

events.title: New Orleans Is Destroyed By Fire
events.description: The Great New Orleans Fire breaks out at a home on Chartres Street and destroys the vast majority of the city. Because the fire started on Good Friday, priests wouldn't allow church bells to be used as alarms, and the blaze spread rapidly. Out of 1,100 buildings in the city, 856 were destroyed within hours, including the armory, jail, and army barracks. The wooden structures were replaced with buildings of masonry and wrought iron, many of which are still standing in the French Quarter today.

events.title: Alcatraz Prison Closes
events.description: National Park ServiceAlcatraz as seen from a ship in 1951.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Begins Marching To Montgomery
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. leads 3,200 civil rights activists in a march from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama following brutal attacks by police on demonstrators in Selma two weeks earlier. King had been in Atlanta at the time of the "Bloody Sunday" incident, but upon hearing the news, he returned to Selma to lead the march himself. Federal troops escorted the activists across Edmund Pettus Bridge and the Alabama Freedom March reached Montgomery four days later.

events.title: Amy Lynn Bradley Boards The Rhapsody Of The Seas
events.description: YoutubeAmy Lynn Bradley with her brother on the Rhapsody of the Seas

events.title: The Jamestown Massacre Takes Place
events.description: A woodcut illustration depicting the Jamestown Massacre by Matthaeus Merian from 1628.

events.title: The British Government Passes The Stamp Act
events.description: British Parliament passes the Stamp Act, which required American colonists to pay taxes on things like paper, documents, and even playing cards in order to pay for British troops stationed in the territory during the Seven Years' War. However, colonial legislatures had not approved the tax, and many residents considered it "taxation without representation." The act and others like it helped set in motion the eventual fight for American independence from the British.

events.title: Persia Is Renamed Iran
events.description: The country formerly known as Persia officially begins going by the name Iran. The term "Persia" was an exonym — or a name given by an outside force — created by the Greeks, but the people of the area had been using the name "Iran" as far back as 1000 B.C.E. In the 1930s, Iranian leader Reza Shah took steps to make Iran the formal name of the country.

events.title: Karl Wallenda Falls To His Death
events.description: YouTubeKarl Wallenda lost his balance and fell to his death from 121 feet in the air in 1978.

events.title: David Parker Ray Is Arrested
events.description: David Parker Ray, "The Toybox Killer" is arrested in Elephant Butte, New Mexico after a victim escapes his property. Ray abducted and tortured at least a dozen women in his home-built torture chamber. His crimes made national headlines due to their sheer brutality. He would later die in prison of a heart attack.

events.title: Patrick Henry Says "Give Me Liberty Or Give Me Death!"
events.description: An 1876 illustration of Patrick Henry giving his famous speech.

events.title: The Wright Brothers File A Patent For The Airplane
events.description: Orville and Wilbur Wright file a patent application for what they call a "Flying Machine" several months before their first successful flight. Their initial application was denied, so they then hired an Ohio patent attorney named Henry Toulmin to help them in their endeavor. With Toulmin's aid, the brothers were finally granted U.S. Patent 821,393 in May 1906, and they have gone down in history as the inventors of the airplane.

events.title: The Paris Gun Is Shot For The First Time
events.description: German forces fire the Paris Gun, the largest gun of World War I, for the first time.

events.title: Mussolini Founds The Fascist Party
events.description: Future Italian dictator Benito Mussolini establishes the Fasci di Combattimento, commonly known as the Fascist Party. This right-wing group advocated Italian nationalism and partook in violent intimidation tactics against leftists as well as any and all enemies, perceived and otherwise. The Blackshirts, so called because of the dark clothing they wore, went on to march on Rome in 1922, and by 1925, Italy was proclaimed a Fascist state with Mussolini as its leader.

events.title: Philip Zimbardo Is Born
events.description: Philip Zimbardo, the pioneering psychologist who designed the infamous Stanford Prison Experiment, is born in New York City.

events.title: Assia Wevill And Her Daughter Die In A Murder-Suicide
events.description: Assia Wevill tragically kills herself and her daughter. Wevill had been having an affair with poet Ted Hughes since before Sylvia Plath's suicide in 1963. Wevill was an aspiring poet and had a successful career in advertising.

events.title: Carlo Gambino Is Arrested
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesCarlo Gambino's 1970 arrest.

events.title: Desmond Doss Dies
events.description: Desmond Doss, the World War II medic whose story inspired Hacksaw Ridge, dies from a respiratory ailment.

events.title: Élan School Announces Its Closing
events.description: The notorious Élan school in Maine announces its closing. First opened in 1970 as a reform school for wayward youth, the Élan school gained a reputation as a "hellhole." Former students claimed that school staff humiliated, restrained, and isolated them. In 1982, a student even died at the school. Its legacy is deeply controversial, with former students both decrying and praising the institution.

events.title: Actress And AIDS Activist Elizabeth Taylor Dies
events.description: Elizabeth Taylor, known for films such as Cleopatra and Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?, dies from congestive heart failure at the age of 79.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth I Dies
events.description: Queen Elizabeth I was famously known as the "Virgin Queen" because she never married or had children.

events.title: Bach Dedicates The 'Brandenburg Concertos'
