events.description: Johann Sebastian Bach dedicates six concertos to Margrave Christian Lewis of Brandenburg. These pieces are now known as his iconic Brandenburg Concertos for this reason. The margrave had asked to see some of Bach's work, and the composer wrote to him in response:

events.title: Harry Houdini Is Born
events.description: WikipediaHarry Houdini performing the "Chinese Water Torture Cell" escape.

events.title: Clyde Barrow Is Born
events.description: Clyde Barrow, who later achieved infamy as one half of the crime duo Bonnie and Clyde, is born in Ellis County, Texas.

events.title: Jack The Ripper Suspect Aaron Kosminski Dies
events.description: Aaron Kosminski, a 23-year-old Polish barber possibly linked to the Whitechapel Murders, dies in Leavesden Asylum in Hertfordshire, England at age 53. DNA evidence found on a shawl belonging to Catherine Eddowes revealed the presence of Kosminski's blood and seminal fluid, though he has not been officially named as Jack the Ripper.

events.title: Virginia Hill Dies
events.description: Virginia Hill, girlfriend of notorious gangster Bugsy Siegel, dies by suicide after taking an overdose of sleeping pills at the age of 49.

events.title: Josefina Riveria Escapes Serial Killer Gary Heidnik
events.description: Josefina Riveria escapes serial killer Gary Heidnik in Philadelphia after months of captivity. Riveria was Heidnik's first victim, and as time passed, Heidnik used her to kidnap at least five other women. All Heidnik's victims were locked in his basement, and several were forced into a boarded up pit. Heidnik subjected his victims to horrific torture, rape, and even acts of cannibalism. While running errands with Heidnik, Riveria walked away while Heidnik was distracted and successfully called the police on a pay phone. They later raided the house of horrors and promptly arrested him.

events.title: The Exxon Valdez Oil Spill
events.description: Chris Wilkins/AFP/Getty ImagesWorkers try to clean up oil along the Alaskan shoreline following the devastating spill.

events.title: Venice Is Founded
events.description: The city of Venice is founded at noon when the first stone of the church of San Giacometo is placed, according to legend. Though no historical records survive, March 25th is still celebrated today as the traditional birthdate of the city. Legend also says that the original population of Venice was made up of refugees from Roman cities who were fleeing invasions from Germanic tribes. In 2021, the city officially celebrated its 1,600th birthday.

events.title: Robert The Bruce Is Crowned King Of Scotland
events.description: Robert the Bruce is crowned king of Scotland. Scottish people looked to Robert the Bruce as the force that would free them from English tyranny under Edward I, otherwise known as "Longshanks." After Edward I died en route to crush Bruce's forces, Bruce easily defeated Edward's heir and granted independence to Scotland. More years of fighting between Bruce, the Scots, and English forces would occur, but Scotland maintained its independence until 1707.

events.title: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
events.description: Firefighters battle the blaze that killed 146 factory workers.

events.title: Yoshiko Kawashima Is Killed
events.description: A highly-publicized photo of Yoshiko Kawashima's body following her execution.

events.title: Gangster Neil McCauley Dies
events.description: American gangster Neil McCauley dies in a shootout with police, inspiring the film Heat.

events.title: The Bronx Happy Land Fire
events.description: National Fire Protection AssociationThe 1990 Happy Land fire was the worst blaze in New York City in 80 years.

events.title: Ludwig Van Beethoven Dies
events.description: German composer Ludwig van Beethoven dies at the age of 56, potentially from the effects of lead poisoning or liver failure from heavy alcohol consumption. He had fallen ill several months prior with symptoms like jaundice, swollen limbs, and breathing difficulties. A friend who was present at the time of the musician's death noted that there was a clap of thunder, and "Beethoven opened his eyes, lifted his right hand and looked up for several seconds with his fist clenched... not another breath, not a heartbeat more."

events.title: Robert Frost Is Born
events.description: American poet Robert Frost is born in San Francisco. Frost published his first poem in his high school's magazine as a teenager, and at the age of 20, he first sold a poem to a newspaper. He published his first book of poetry, called A Boy's Will, while living in England in 1912, but it wasn't until 1924 that he became widely known after winning his first Pulitzer Prize. To this day, perhaps his most famous work is the poem "The Road Not Taken."

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. And Malcolm X Meet
events.description: Universal History Archive/Getty ImagesThough Malcolm X and Martin Luther King Jr. were two of the most renowned Black leaders of the 1960s, they only met one time.

events.title: Heaven's Gate Cult Members Found Dead
events.description: David McNew/Getty ImagesOne of the 39 members of the Heaven's Gate religious group who committed suicide in their Rancho Santa Fe, California mansion in 1997.

events.title: President Vladimir Putin Is Elected As President Of Russia
events.description: President Vladimir Putin is elected as the president of Russia for the first time. During his first time as president, Putin tackled a power struggle between the federal government and powerful oligarchs, addressed separatist issues in Chechnya, and focused on building up the nation's economy. Putin was reelected as president in 2004, 2012, and 2018. Putin also served as prime minister of Russia from 2008 to 2012. In April 2021, after a referendum, Putin signed a constitutional amendment allowing him to run for reelection twice more, making it possible for him to retain the presidency until 2036.

events.title: James Cameron Descends To Challenger Deep
events.description: Film director James Cameron becomes the third person — and the first solo explorer — to descend some 34,000 feet to Challenger Deep, the deepest part of the ocean.

events.title: King Louis XVII Is Born
events.description: Louis XVII of France is born in the Palace of Versailles in Paris to King Louis XVI and Queen Marie Antoinette. Young Louis had an older brother, but when he died just before the outbreak of the French Revolution, Louis became the heir to the French throne.

events.title: Guglielmo Marconi Sends The First International Radio Transmission
events.description: Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi successfully sends the first international radio transmission across the English Channel, from northern France to Kent, England. The message was broadcast to The Times newspaper and said:

events.title: The Good Friday Earthquake Devastates Alaska
events.description: Just some of the damage that left parts of downtown Anchorage in ruins.

events.title: The Tenerife Airport Disaster
events.description: The wreckage of KLM Flight 4805, one of the airplanes involved in the collision.

events.title: Bobby Joe Long Murders His First Victim
events.description: Bobby Joe Long, the "Classified Ad Rapist."

events.title: Maurizio Gucci Is Murdered
events.description: Laurent MAOUS/Gamma-Rapho/Getty ImagesRoberto Gucci, Giorgio Gucci, and Maurizio Gucci attend a store opening in Paris, France, on September 22, 1983.

events.title: Barnum And Bailey's "Greatest Show On Earth" Opens
events.description: A poster for Barnum And Bailey's "Greatest Show On Earth."

events.title: William Armstrong Purchases Bamburgh Castle
events.description: Industrialist William Armstrong purchases Bamburgh Castle in Northumberland, England.

events.title: Constantinople Becomes Istanbul
events.description: The Turkish city of Constantinople is officially renamed Istanbul. The city was originally called Byzantium by the ancient Romans, but the name Constantinople became dominant around 330 C.E. when the emperor Constantine moved the capital of the Roman Empire to the city. In 1916, however, the Turkish government began a push for countries around the world to use the official Turkish names for the area's towns and cities, and Constantinople soon became Istanbul.

events.title: The Spanish Civil War Ends
events.description: The Spanish Civil War, fought between Republicans and Nationalists comes to an end when the Nationalists take over Madrid. The war lasted three years, and up to a million people died during the conflict. Fascist dictator Francisco Franco ruled for the next 36 years and killed tens of thousands with his totalitarian policies while also ushering in a period of economic prosperity in Spain.

events.title: Virginia Woolf Dies By Suicide
events.description: Virginia Woolf just two years before her death.

events.title: The Three Mile Island Nuclear Accident
events.description: AFP/AFP/Getty ImagesThe Three Mile Island nuclear plant on March 28, 1979.

events.title: Battle of Towton
events.description: The Battle of Towton by Richard Caton Woodville Jr., 1922.

events.title: John Pemberton Makes The First Batch Of Coca-Cola
events.description: Coca-Cola inventor John Pemberton brews the first batch of the soft drink as a non-alcoholic wine alternative.

events.title: The Rosenbergs Are Convicted Of Espionage
events.description: Married couple Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are convicted of espionage for passing nuclear secrets to the Soviets following a sensational trial. They had been arrested in June 1950 after a string of other spies named them as the head of an operation that collected and shared information about atomic bombs and the Manhattan Project to the Soviet Union. The Rosenbergs were executed in 1953.

events.title: The Last American Troops Leave Vietnam
events.description: Bettmann/Contributor via Getty ImagesArmy Chief Master Sergeant Max Bielke, the last U.S. serviceman to leave Vietnam.

events.title: The Terracotta Army Is Found
events.description: A group of farmers in Xi'an, China discovered the buried army of Terracotta warriors after looking for a suitable spot to build a well. A total of 7,000 Terracotta soldiers, horses, and recreations of rivers and lakes were buried for over two thousand years. The army was created to honor China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huangdi, and was buried under rubble after rebel Xiang Yu raided the city. It is considered the greatest archaeological find of the 20th century.

events.title: Britain Wins The Second Anglo-Sikh War, Resulting In The Exchange Of The Koh-i-Noor Diamond
events.description: Britain wins the Second Anglo-Sikh War, resulting in the exchange of the famous Koh-i-Noor diamond, one of the world's largest cut diamonds.

events.title: Vincent Van Gogh Is Born
events.description: A section of Vincent van Gogh's famous self-portrait from 1889.

events.title: The Pencil Eraser Is Patented
events.description: A stationery salesman named Hymen Lipman patents the built-in pencil eraser. Lipman described his invention as a "combination of the lead and India rubber or other erasing substance [embedded] in the holder of a drawing-pencil."

events.title: The U.S. Purchases Alaska
events.description: A depiction of the signing of the Alaska Treaty of Cessation, in which the U.S. purchased Alaska from Russia.

events.title: Ronald Reagan Is Almost Killed In An Assassination Attempt
events.description: U.S. president Ronald Reagan is almost assassinated by John Hinkley Jr. in Washington, D.C. After becoming obsessed with the film Taxi Driver and the actress Jodi Foster, John Hinkley Jr. decided to kill U.S. President Ronald Reagan to get Foster's attention. Outside of a Hilton hotel, Hinkley shot the president and several Secret Service members. Thankfully, no one died, but many sustained injuries. A year later, Hinkley was found not guilty by reason of insanity and sent to a psychiatric ward.

events.title: Donald Harvey Dies
events.description: YouTubeDonald Harvey standing before a chart listing the names of his victims at trial.

events.title: René Descartes Is Born
events.description: Philosopher and mathematician René Descartes is born in Touraine, France. He's often referred to as the father of modern philosophy, as he developed the first major theory of dualism — the idea that the mind and body are separate. Descartes is known for his famous quote, "I think, therefore I am." He also developed analytic geometry, which allows geometric problems to be solved using algebra.

events.title: The Eiffel Tower Is Completed
events.description: Roger Viollet/Getty ImagesThe Eiffel Tower under construction.

events.title: Construction Of The RMS Titanic Begins
events.description: Construction of the RMS Titanic begins at the Harland and Wolff shipyard in Belfast, Ireland.

events.title: Oklahoma! Debuts On Broadway
events.description: The musical Oklahoma! makes its Broadway premiere. It was the first collaboration of composer Richard Rodgers and lyricist Oscar Hammerstein, who would go on to create such hits as South Pacific and The Sound of Music. A massive success, the show ultimately set a Broadway record with 2,212 performances before it closed five years later.

events.title: Brandon Lee Is Killed
events.description: TwitterBrandon Lee with his mother Linda Lee Cadwell and his sister Shannon Lee.

events.title: Selena Quintanilla Is Murdered
events.description: FacebookSelena and Yolanda Saldívar pictured together in March 1994, almost exactly a year before Saldívar fatally shot the singer.

events.title: The Pilgrims And Wampanoag Make Peace
events.description: SSPL/Getty ImagesA depiction of the Pilgrims and Wampanoag meeting.

events.title: April Fools' Tradition Begins
events.description: The official April Fools' tradition starts in Western Europe. Though the tradition has existed in different forms for centuries, its exact origins are unknown. Today, it's celebrated in countries across the world.

events.title: The Battle Of Okinawa Begins
events.description: © CORBIS/Corbis via Getty ImagesWounded American soldiers await transfer to the hospital ship anchored off the shore of Okinawa.

events.title: Marvin Gaye Is Murdered
events.description: Afro American Newspapers/Gado/Getty ImagesMarvin Gaye was a successful performer before his father murdered him in 1984.

events.title: Brian Shaffer Goes Missing
events.description: Brian Shaffer disappears from the Ugly Tuna Saloona in Colombus, Ohio. The 27-year-old medical student at the University of Ohio was last seen around 2 a.m. before he vanished. Despite a years-long search, Shaffer remains missing to this day.

events.title: The Japan Times Reports That The Hachikō Statue Has Been Stolen
events.description: As an April Fools' prank, The Japan Times reports that the statue of Hachikō, Japan's famous Akita, has been stolen by "suspected metal thieves."

events.title: Arthur Prince Of Wales Dies
events.description: Arthur, Prince of Wales and heir to Henry VII, dies at the age of 15. Arthur's death meant that his younger brother Henry would go on to become King Henry VIII and marry Arthur's bride, Catherine of Aragon.

events.title: Juan Ponce de León Claims Florida For Spain
events.description: After setting out from Puerto Rico in search of new land, Juan Ponce de León claims Florida for Spain. Though Native Americans had lived in the territory for thousands of years, de León marked it as Spanish territory and called it Florida because he'd "discovered" it during the Easter feast (Pascua Florida). De León later tried to colonize Florida but sustained a mortal wound in 1521 after being attacked by Native Americans.

events.title: Hans Christian Andersen Is Born
events.description: Corbis via Getty ImagesA portrait of writer Hans Christian Andersen.

events.title: Woodrow Wilson Asks Congress To Declare War On Germany
events.description: U.S. President Woodrow Wilson asks Congress to declare war on Germany. The vote in the House of Representatives came out to 373 in favor, 50 against (with eight representatives abstaining). In the Senate, 82 senators voted in favor of war while six voted against (eight senators abstained). With this, the United States officially joined the First World War on the side of the Allies. The war would end in an Allied victory over a year later.

events.title: Famed Cowboy Bill Pickett Dies
events.description: Bill Pickett traveled the world to show off his cattle-wrestling skills.

events.title: Argentina Invades The Falkland Islands
events.description: Rafael WOLLMANN/Gamma-Rapho via Getty ImagesArgentinian soldiers during the invasion of the Falkland Islands.

events.title: Jesus Christ Is Crucified
events.description: Jesus Christ is crucified (according to some scholars' estimates and theories) just outside Jerusalem, at Golgotha. After being put on trial for blasphemy, Christ was sentenced to death by the Roman governor of Judea, Pontius Pilate.

events.title: The Pony Express Begins
events.description: Universal History Archive/Getty ImagesAn illustration of a Pony Express rider crossing "hostile" territory.

events.title: Jesse James Is Murdered
events.description: A young Jesse James, many years before his 1882 murder.

events.title: Vito Genovese Is Found Guilty Of Narcotics Trafficking
events.description: After a public trial in which his wife, Anna, testified against him, Mafia leader Vito Genovese and 14 others are found guilty of conspiracy to violate the federal narcotics law. Genovese was sentenced to 15 years in federal prison, but died 10 years into his sentence.

events.title: Martin Luther King Delivers His "I've Been To The Mountaintop" Speech
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesMartin Luther King Jr. giving his "I've Been To The Mountaintop" speech on the night before his assassination.

events.title: The First Cell Phone Call Is Made
events.description: The first handheld cell phone call is made. It was made in New York City by Martin Cooper, a Motorola engineer, who called his rival, Joel Engel of Bell Laboratories at AT&T.

events.title: Operation Babylift Begins In Vietnam
events.description: As Saigon falls and the Vietnam War draws to a close while U.S. forces begin pulling out, the American government initiates a daring, last-ditch effort called Operation Babylift. But this was no military offensive. Instead, the plan was to evacuate as many orphaned children as possible and find them safe haven in homes across America and abroad.

events.title: The "Unabomber" Is Arrested
events.description: Kaczynski Family PhotoTed Kaczynski outside his Montana cabin in 1971.

events.title: William Henry Harrison Dies
events.description: William Henry Harrison dies at the age of 68 in Washington D.C., possibly from pneumonia, though contaminated drinking water is also suspected.

events.title: Maya Angelou Is Born
events.description: Consolidated News Pictures/Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesMaya Angelou reciting her poem 'On the Pulse of Morning' at the inauguration of President Bill Clinton in Washington D.C. on January 20, 1993.

events.title: Cheryl Crane Stabs Johnny Stompanato To Death
events.description: Cheryl Crane stabs Johnny Stompanato to death in Beverly Hills, California. The 14-year-old daughter of actress Lana Turner, Crane allegedly killed Stompanato because he was abusive toward her mother. A court ultimately ruled that Stompanato's death was a "justifiable homicide."

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Is Assassinated
events.description: Donald Uhrbrock/Getty ImagesMartin Luther King Jr. was just 39 when he was assassinated.

events.title: The World Trade Center Opens In New York
events.description: Jamel Shabazz/Sights in the City, New York PhotographsThe World Trade Center in 1982.

events.title: "Evil Genius" Marjorie Diehl-Armstrong Dies In Prison
events.description: Marjorie Diehl-Armstrong, the mastermind behind the 2003 Pizza Bomber scheme, dies in prison at age 68.

events.title: Pocahontas Weds John Rolfe
events.description: MPI/Getty ImagesPocahontas was baptized as "Rebecca" shortly before her marriage to John Rolfe.

events.title: Britain Passes The Sugar Act In The American Colonies
events.description: Britain passes the Sugar Act in the American Colonies. This act taxed sugar, wine, coffee, and regulated the export of lumber and iron. The act was meant to control smuggling, which was rampant in the region. The tax on molasses disrupted the American whiskey industry, causing strong resistance from the Colonists. Additionally, the act controlled where Colonists could purchase raw goods, effectively limiting the economy and the markets. British officials reserved the right to inspect any American vessel for smuggled goods. The Sugar Act caused massive protests in the American Colonies.

events.title: Charles Darwin Sends His Publishers The First Chapters Of On the Origin of Species
events.description: Charles Darwin submits the first chapters of On the Origin of Species to his publishers. Darwin's book, which presented the theory of "natural selection" for the first time, helped lay the foundations for humanity's understanding of evolution.

events.title: FDR Establishes Civilian Conservation Corps
events.description: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt establishes the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC), a government work program that provided young men employment during the Great Depression.

events.title: Winston Churchill Steps Down
events.description: Topical Press Agency/Getty ImagesWinston Churchill shortly before tendering his resignation with Queen Elizabeth II.

events.title: Kurt Cobain Dies
events.description: ImgurThis photo is from Kurt Cobain's last photoshoot, taken by Jesse Frohman for the London Observer.

events.title: The Siege Of Constantinople Begins
events.description: For 53 days, the capital of the Byzantine Empire was surrounded by Ottoman forces, commanded by 21-year-old Sultan Mehmed II. On May 29, the city fell, marking the end of the Middle Ages and the beginning of the Renaissance.

events.title: Joseph Smith Founds The Church Of Jesus Christ Of Latter-Day Saints
events.description: De Agostini/Getty ImagesA depiction of Joseph Smith reading the Book of Mormon to a group of his first followers.

events.title: The First Modern Olympic Games Begin
events.description: The first modern Olympic Games are held in Athens, Greece. Held for the first time since their cancellation 1,500 years ago by Roman Emperor Theodosius I, the games drew 60,000 spectators and athletes from 13 nations. In 2022, the Winter Olympic games drew athletes from 91 countries and were watched by more than 2 billion people worldwide.

events.title: Explorer Robert E. Peary And Team Make It To The North Pole
events.description: Explorer Robert E. Peary, along Native Inuit people on dog sleds, make it to the North Pole, claiming to be the first people to make it there. Peary's account of his travels were later approved by the National Geographic Society and the Naval Affairs Subcommittee of the U.S. House of Representatives. However, whether his expedition was really the first to make it to the North Pole is disputed.

events.title: The United States Enters World War I
events.description: The United States officially enters World War I. Though the U.S. had long tried to stay neutral in the conflict, numerous events — including the May 1917 sinking of the Lusitania, allegedly by German U-Boats, in which 123 Americans died — drew the country into the war. After the Lusitania incident, President Woodrow Wilson called on Congress to declare war on Germany, which it promptly did.

events.title: Ram Dass Is Born
events.description: Robert Altman/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesRam Dass famously took LSD hundreds of times and penned several inspirational books.

events.title: The Battle Of Metaxas Line And Dimitrios Itsios' Execution
events.description: The Nazi invasion of Greece begins with the Battle of Metaxas Line. During the offensive, Sergeant Dimitrios Itsios for the Greek army leads a small crew of soldiers in killing over 200 Nazis while defending the Pillbox fort. Itsios was subsequently taken prisoner by the Nazis and executed. Itsios is still remembered today for his bravery.

events.title: Keith Hunter Jesperson Is Born
events.description: Keith Hunter Jesperson is born in Chilliwack, British Columbia. A long-haul trucker and serial killer known as the Happy Face Killer because of how he signed letters to the police and messages left in bathrooms, Jesperson killed at least eight women between 1990 and 1995. He claims, however, that he killed 166.

events.title: The Rwandan Genocide Begins
events.description: Scott Peterson/LiaisonA soldier stands near the site of the plane crash that killed Rwandan President Juvénal Habyarimana and 11 others.

events.title: Con Artist Elaine Parent Dies In Panama City
events.description: Con artist and murderer Elaine Parent commits suicide after police show up at her door in Panama City, Florida. Parent was wanted for the 1990 murder of Beverly McGowan and a known con artist who stole dozens of identities.

events.title: Toussaint L'Ouverture Dies
events.description: Toussaint L'Ouverture dies while imprisoned at Fort-de-Joux, France from pneumonia and starvation at the age of 59. The leader of the Haitian independence movement, L'Ouverture's rebellion succeeded in gaining control over the entire island of Hispaniola and ending slavery. However, he remained an enemy of the French, who arrested L'Ouverture in 1802.

events.title: Billie Holiday Is Born
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesBillie Holiday recording an album in December 1957.

events.title: Josip Broz Tito Declared President Of Yugoslavia For Life
events.description: The new Yugoslavia constitution declares Tito as the country's president for life. Born Josip Broz, Tito rapidly rose through the ranks of the Communist Party of Yugoslavia and was elected as the Yugoslav premier after World War II. He remained in power until his death in 1980.

events.title: Joe Gallo Is Murdered
events.description: Umberto's Clam House in New York City, where Joe Gallo was killed.

events.title: The Chippendales Murders Begin
events.description: The Chippendale murders begin in New York. In the 1980s and 1990s, the founder of the male dance group Chippendales, Steve Banerjee, plotted several murders across the United States to protect his brand. In 1979, Banerjee ordered someone to burn down "Moody's Disco," a rival nightclub. In 1987, Banerjee ordered the murder of choreographer Nick De Noia. The FBI later caught up to Banerjee after a hitman got cold feet, and before a court could sentence him for his crimes, Banerjee committed suicide.

events.title: The Rwandan Genocide Begins
events.description: Scott Peterson/LiaisonA soldier stands near the site of the plane crash that killed Rwandan President Juvénal Habyarimana and 11 others.

events.title: Gautama Buddha Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA giant Buddha statue in Japan.

events.title: The First Synagogue Is Dedicated In New York
events.description: Named Shearith Israel, the synagogue was founded in Lower Manhattan and was the city's only synagogue until 1818. Shearith Israel exists to this day, though it has since moved to Manhattan's Upper West Side neighborhood.

events.title: French Navy Officer Witnesses The Discovery Of The Venus de Milo in Melos
events.description: French Navy Officer Olivier Voutier watches as a farmer on the island of Melos pulls the Venus de Milo from an ancient wall. Voutier, alongside the French ambassador to the Ottoman Empire, later negotiated to buy the statue.

events.title: Felix Gallardo Is Arrested
events.description: Felix Gallardo is arrested in Mexico. A drug lord known as the "Jefe de jefes" or "Boss of bosses," Gallardo lay the foundations of modern drug smuggling by establishing ties with drug lords in Colombia and orchestrating the shipment of cocaine to the United States. He was released from prison in 2022 after serving 33 years of a 40-year sentence due to his ill health.

events.title: Ryan White Dies Of AIDS
events.description: Kim Komenich/Getty ImagesRyan White contracted AIDS from a blood transfusion and was shunned at his school.

events.title: Kurt Cobain Is Found Dead
events.description: Several days after escaping from rehab and cutting off contact with his loved ones, rock icon Kurt Cobain is found dead by suicide at age 27 in the greenhouse above the garage at his Seattle home. Photos from the scene of Cobain's death show assorted drug paraphernalia, the shotgun he used to shoot himself, and the suicide note he left behind.

events.title: Somali Pirates Attack Maersk Alabama
events.description: Four armed Somali pirates hijack the MV Maersk Alabama off the coast of Somalia. After a scuffle with the crew, the captain, Richard Phillips, was kidnapped, leading to a dramatic rescue led by Navy SEALs. Three of the four pirates were killed and the survivor was sentenced to over 33 years in prison.

events.title: Halden Prison Officially Opens
events.description: Halden Prison, often considered the most humane prison in the world, opens in Norway. It is the country's second largest prison. It focuses on rehabilitation rather than punishment, and hosts many activities and freedoms unavailable in American prisons, such as a rock wall, en-suite bathrooms, and unbarred cell windows.

events.title: King Leopold II Of Belgium Is Born
events.description: King Leopold II is born in Brussels, Belgium. Leopold II is most known for his extreme brutality in Belgium's Congo Free State. Under his leadership, Leopold turned the Congo was turned into a playground for his economic interests. He sent mercenaries to enforce strict production quotes across the country and harshly punished anyone who stepped out of line. Millions of people died under Leopold's rule.

events.title: Robert E. Lee Surrenders To Ulysses S. Grant
events.description: Timothy H. O'Sullivan/Library of CongressSoldiers wait outside the court house in Appomattox, Virginia as the official terms of surrender are determined.

events.title: Billy The Kid Is Found Guilty Of Murder
events.description: Billy the Kid is one of the best known Wild West outlaws.

events.title: Bataan Death March Begins
events.description: The Bataan Death March begins in the Philippines during World War II. After surrendering during the Battle of Bataan, 75,000 Filipino and American troops were forced to march for 65 miles toward prison camps by Japanese troops. An estimated 650 American and 16,500 Filipino soldiers were killed during the march.

events.title: The Weather Station in Alert, Canada Begins Operations
events.description: The weather station, as part of a joint operation between the United States and Canada, begins operations in the remote town of Alert in Canada's Nunavut territory. It marks the beginning of Alert as the northernmost continual inhabited town in the world. Less than 100 people live there year-round today.

events.title: Baghdad Falls To U.S. Forces
events.description: Gilles BASSIGNAC/Gamma-Rapho via Getty ImagesA statue of Saddam Hussein is pulled down in Baghdad, Iraq, on April 9, 2003.

events.title: Halley's Comet Makes Its Closest Ever Pass By Earth
events.description: Halley's Comet comes closer to Earth than it ever had before. The comet, known as a "periodic comet," passes by our planet roughly every 75 years. It caused a panic when it came close to Earth in 1910, last passed by in 1986, and is estimated to return in 2061.

events.title: Mount Tambora Erupts
events.description: An aerial view of the caldera of Mount Tambora, as seen in 2011.

events.title: The LaLaurie Mansion Catches On Fire, Exposing The Horrors Inside
events.description: The LaLaurie Mansion in New Orleans, Louisiana, catches on fire, exposing the horrific abuse that Madame LaLaurie had been inflicting on enslaved people living there. Contemporaneous reports stated that at least eight people were found in a state of mutilation and violent captivity, prompting LaLaurie herself to flee the country and never return.

events.title: The Great Fire Of Pittsburgh
events.description: A section of View of the Great Fire of Pittsburgh, an 1846 painting by a witness named William Coventry Wall.

events.title: The ASPCA Is Founded
events.description: The American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (ASPCA) is founded in New York City by Henry Bergh. A philanthropist and diplomat, Bergh had been horrified by the treatment of carriage horses while posted in Russia. Bergh set out to establish an organization to aid "these mute servants of mankind." The ASPCA continues its work to this day.

events.title: The RMS Titanic Sets Sail
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesThe RMS Titanic on its doomed maiden voyage in April 1912.

events.title: Emiliano Zapata Is Assassinated
events.description: Emiliano Zapata is assassinated in Morelos, Mexico. A Mexican revolutionary, Zapata was killed by men working with Venustiano Carranza, the president of Mexico who opposed Zapata's ideas regarding land reform. Zapata's ideas endured, however, and were later included in the 1917 Mexican Constitution.

events.title: Ruth Ellis Murders David Blakely
events.description: Ruth Ellis shoots and kills her lover David Blakely in London. After being found guilty of murder, Ellis became the last woman ever hanged in the United Kingdom.

events.title: Former Beatles Member Stuart Sutcliffe Dies
events.description: Stuart Sutcliffe, a one-time member of The Beatles, dies of a brain hemorrhage in Germany at just 21 years old.

events.title: The Beatles' Breakup Becomes Public
events.description: Chris Walter/Getty ImagesThe Beatles' George Harrison, Paul McCartney, Ringo Starr, and John Lennon in 1967.

events.title: The Brixton Riots Begin
events.description: The Brixton riots break out in London. Fueled by tensions between the Black residents of Brixton and the neighborhood's largely white police force, the riot lasted for two days. It caused £7.5 million in damages, left some 300 people injured, and revealed the nation's deep racial divide.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Is Exiled To Elba
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte is exiled to Elba. After rising to power at the end of the 18th century, Napoleon established himself as the emperor of France and waged war across Europe. He agreed to abdicate his throne and go to Elba after the Sixth Coalition captured Paris, but later escaped and briefly returned as France's emperor before being exiled to the more distant island of Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Gives His Final Speech
events.description: Abraham Lincoln gives his final public speech, during which he expressed support for limited Black suffrage. Among the listening crowd was Lincoln's assassin John Wilkes Booth, who exclaimed: "That means n-- citizenship! Now, by God, I'll put him through. That is the last speech he will ever make."

events.title: Joseph Merrick Dies
events.description: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty ImagesJoseph Merrick, known as the "Elephant Man" because of his severe deformities.

events.title: The RMS Carpathia Departs From New York
events.description: The RMS Carpathia sets sail from New York toward Fiume, Austria-Hungary (present-day Rijeka, Croatia). Shortly after midnight on April 15, the Carpathia responded to distress calls from the RMS Titanic after the other ship hit an iceberg and sank, and rescued 705 people from the frigid waters.

events.title: The First Live Sporting Event Is Broadcast Over Radio
events.description: The first sporting event is broadcast on the radio when KDKA in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, covers a boxing match between Johnny Ray and Johnny Dundee. As listeners tuned in, Ray won the match in ten rounds. Other sporting events were quickly covered on the radio as well, including another boxing match and a baseball game.

events.title: Buchenwald Is Liberated
events.description: The concentration camp of Buchenwald is liberated by U.S. troops, shortly after prisoners seized control of the camp.

events.title: The 1968 FBI Miami Shootout
events.description: Two bank robbers, William D. Matix and Michael Lee Platt, engage in a violent confrontation with FBI agents in a residential area of Miami, Florida, resulting in the deaths of two agents, five more wounded, and both robbers dead.

events.title: Wayne Nance Kills His First Victim
events.description: Wayne Nance murders his first victim, Donna Pound, in Missoula, Montana. A serial killer who murdered six people in the city between 1974 and 1986, Nance was known to police as the "Missoula Mauler." It wasn't until a would-be victim was able to kill him that his murder spree came to a halt.

events.title: Ugandan Dictator Idi Amin Is Overthrown
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesIdi Amin at a military parade in 1975.

events.title: Keddie Cabin Murders Are Committed
events.description: Keddie Cabin murders are committed in Keddie, California. Glenna "Sue" Sharp and three others were murdered while staying at a resort cabin. In total, seven people were sleeping in the cabin when an unknown assailant broke in and began his or her brutal assault. Luckily, police found two young boys in the cabin unharmed in their beds.

events.title: Galileo Galilei Is Accused Of Heresy
events.description: The Italian astronomer was accused of heresy because of his belief that the Earth rotates around the sun, which the Catholic Church considered heretical. He was found guilty and sentenced to house arrest, where he would remain until his death in 1642.

events.title: The American Civil War Begins At Fort Sumter
events.description: VCG Wilson/Corbis via Getty ImagesThe bombardment of Fort Sumter in April 1861.

events.title: The Great Locomotive Chase Takes Place
events.description: The Great Locomotive Chase, also known as Andrews' Raid, takes place when a group of Union spies steal a Confederate train called "The General" and attempt to drive it north. Though they made it almost 90 miles, the men were eventually caught by the Confederates and hanged or imprisoned.

events.title: The Shanghai Massacre Begins
events.description: The Shanghai Massacre begins in Shanghai, China. The massacre, which lasted until April 15, resulted in the deaths of thousands of communists by supporters of nationalist General Chiang Kai-shek. The incident sparked the Chinese Civil War, which would claim over six million lives until it ended in 1949.

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt Dies
events.description: FDR Presidential Library & MuseumThe last photograph taken of Franklin D. Roosevelt, who died the next day.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin Becomes The First Man In Space
events.description: ITU Pictures/ FlickrCosmonaut Yuri Gagarin.

events.title: Miyamoto Musashi Defeats Sasaki Kojiro
events.description: Miyamoto Musashi kills Sasaki Kojiro in a duel. The two samurais were rivals and Musashi initiated the duel to prove that he was the better swordsman. Musashi won the bout and is considered one of history's greatest samurai, though he then swore off dueling to the death.

events.title: Thomas Jefferson Is Born
events.description: Burstein Collection/Corbis/VCG via Getty ImagesThe third president of the United States, Thomas Jefferson's legacy has been re-evaluated in recent years.

events.title: Butch Cassidy Is Born
events.description: An iconic Wild West outlaw, Butch Cassidy was a notorious cattle rustler and bank robber in the 19th century.

events.title: The Metropolitan Museum Of Art Is Established
events.description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art is established by the Legislature of the State of New York. Tasked with "encouraging and developing the study of the fine arts," the museum's first building opened 10 years later at 1000 Fifth Avenue in New York City. Today, the Met displays thousands of international artifacts including paintings, sculptures, and even partial Egyptian temples.

events.title: The Amritsar Massacre Takes Place
events.description: The Amritsar Massacre, also called the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, takes place in Amritsar, India. There, British and Gurka troops opened fire on hundreds of people gathering at the Jallianwala Bagh park, some Indian nationalists, and some revelers of the Sikh Baisakhi festival. At least 379 were killed and thousands injured when British troops emptied their rifles onto the crowd, convincing Mohandas Gandhi that India must break free from British rule.

events.title: An Oxygen Tank Explodes On Apollo 13
events.description: Space Frontiers/Getty ImagesThe crew of the Apollo 13 lunar landing mission — Commander James A. Lovell Jr, Command Module pilot John L. Swigert Jr, and Lunar Module pilot Fred W. Haise Jr. — in April 1970.

events.title: Stephen Stucker Dies
events.description: Commedian Stephen Stucker died due to complications related to AIDS after struggling with the disease for multiple years. Best known for his roles in the comedy films Airplane! and Kentucky Fried Movie, Stucker was one of the first actors to go public with his AIDS diagnosis in 1984.

events.title: Tiger Woods Wins His First Masters Tournament
events.description: Eldrick "Tiger" Woods wins his first Masters Tournament in Augusta, Georgia. The 21-year-old won in a record 12 strokes and established himself as a champion golfer. Today, Woods is widely considered one of the greatest golfers of all time.

events.title: Webster's American Dictionary Is First Printed
events.description: The American Dictionary of the English Language is printed by Noah Webster. A Yale-educated lawyer fascinated by language, Webster spent two decades putting the dictionary together with a special emphasis on American words. His dictionary helped inform American spelling (versus British) though some spelling that Webster chose, like tung instead of tongue, never caught on.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Is Shot By John Wilkes Booth
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA depiction of President Abraham Lincoln's assassination by John Wilkes Booth.

events.title: William Howard Taft Throws Out The Ceremonial First Pitch
events.description: William Howard Taft throws out the ceremonial first pitch at a Major League Baseball game between the Washington Senators and the Philadelphia Athletics, establishing a presidential tradition that endures to this day.

events.title: The RMS Titanic Hits An Iceberg
events.description: Just four days after launching on its maiden voyage, the RMS Titanic hits an iceberg in the North Atlantic Ocean at 11:40 PM about 400 miles off the coast of Newfoundland. After two hours and 40 minutes, the ship sank into the frigid ocean. Roughly 1,500 perished in the infamous sinking, including 800 passengers and nearly 700 crew members.

events.title: The 'Black Sunday' Dust Bowl Storm Takes Place
events.description: National Weather ServiceA photograph of the dust storm approaching Spearman, Texas.

events.title: Boko Haram Kidnaps 275 Girls From A Boarding School
events.description: Boko Haram, an Islamist terrorist group in Nigeria, kidnaps 275 girls from their private school in Chibok, Nigeria. Boko Haram's main mission is to make Nigeria a Muslim state by installing an Islamic leader. The group is responsible for thousands of deaths, primarily in Nigeria's Borno, Yobe, and Adamawa states. In 2014, the group entered the Government Girls Secondary School and took 275 girls hostage. They forced the girls into trucks and took them to Boko Haram camps. The event sparked the #BringBackOurGirls movement. Over 100 of the girls remain missing today.

events.title: Seventy-Seven Slaves Attempt To Escape In The 'Pearl Incident'
events.description: The Pearl Incident, the largest recorded attempted slave escape in American history, takes place in Washington D.C., during which 77 enslaved people snuck onto a schooner called Pearl and attempted to sail to New Jersey, a free state. Thwarted by high wind, they were recaptured and brought back to Washington D.C., and many of them were sold to slavers in the South.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Dies
events.description: Fotosearch/Getty ImagesA depiction of the death of Abraham Lincoln, who passed away the morning after being shot by John Wilkes Booth.

events.title: Andrew Johnson Is Sworn In
events.description: Just a month after becoming vice president, Andrew Johnson is sworn in as the nation's 17th president on the third floor of Kirkwood House in Washington, D.C., following the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.

events.title: Corrie ten Boom Is Born
events.description: Corrie ten Boom, who would save 800 Jews during World War II alongside her family and the Dutch resistance, is born in Haarlem, Netherlands.

events.title: The RMS Titanic Sinks
events.description: A famous depiction of the RMS Titanic sinking that was created by Willy Stöwer in 1912.

events.title: The Titanic Iceberg Is Photographed
events.description: Stephan Rehorek, a passenger on the steamer Bremen, snaps a photo of an iceberg as the steamer passes the site of the Titanic sinking. Though other possible Titanic iceberg photos exist, Rehorek's photo matches up with eyewitness testimony of the iceberg resembling the "Rock of Gibraltar."

events.title: The Precursor To The Gulag Is Approved
events.description: The All-Russian Central Executive Committee passes a decree which approves the formation of forced labor camps across the Soviet Union. These camps, under Joseph Stalin, became known as Glavnoye Upravleniye Lagerey (Main Camp Administration) or GULAG.

events.title: Bergen-Belsen Concentration Camp Is Liberated
events.description: Mondadori via Getty ImagesWomen formerly imprisoned at Bergen-Belsen after the British Army liberated the camp.

events.title: Pol Pot Dies
events.description: Millions of people died in 1970s Cambodia as Pol Pot tried to make it into an agrarian utopia.

events.title: Notre Dame Cathedral Catches On Fire
events.description: Notre Dame cathedral in Paris catches on fire. As horrified Parisians watched below, flames engulfed the 850-year-old cathedral, causing its famous spire to snap off. The cathedral is currently undergoing an $865 million renovation and is expected to reopen in 2024.

events.title: Francisco Goya Dies
events.description: Francisco Goya, famous Spanish painter, dies in Bordeaux, France. Goya was a renowned romantic painter who created both lighthearted and disturbing pieces, including Saturn Devouring His Son — the world's most disturbing painting.

events.title: The First Passenger Railway In India Opens
events.description: The first passenger rail in India opens, running on a 20-mile track that connected the cities of Bombay and Thane. It contained 14 cars and carried 400 passengers on its maiden voyage.

events.title: Alfred Packer, The Colorado Cannibal, Returns From His Ill-Fated Journey
events.description: After leading a group of five other men into the Colorado mountains to look for gold, Alfred Packer returns to the Los Pinos Indian Agency in Gunnison, Colorado, alone. After an interrogation, Packer revealed that he had, in fact, killed and eaten the other members of his party in order to survive.

events.title: Charlie Chaplin Is Born
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesCharlie Chaplin in The Gold Rush (1925).

events.title: Vladimir Lenin Returns To Russia From Exile
events.description: Bolshevik leader Vladimir Lenin addresses a crowd in Moscow on May 25, 1919, during the Russian Civil War.

events.title: Albert Hofman Accidentally Discovers LSD
events.description: Albert Hofmann accidentally consumes LSD-25, a synthetic drug he'd created, in Basel, Switzerland. For two hours the Swiss chemist experienced the world's first LSD "high." The hallucinogenic drug later became popular in the United States in the 1960s but was outlawed in 1965.

events.title: Cheyenne Brando Dies/h2> Cheyenne Brando, the last child of actor Marlon Brando, dies from suicide at her mother's home in Tahiti. 2007: The Virginia Tech Shooting Takes Place
events.description: Chip Somodevilla/Getty ImagesThousands of people attend a candlelight vigil on the day after the Virginia Tech shooting in 2007.

events.title: Benjamin Franklin Dies
events.description: Stock Montage/Stock Montage/Getty ImagesBenjamin Franklin played a crucial role in the American Revolution.

events.title: Mary Surratt Is Arrested
events.description: Despite unwaveringly declaring her innocence along with the support of several priests, Mary Surratt was sentenced to death.

events.title: The First Sino-Japanese War Ends
events.description: The First Sino-Japanese War ends with a Japanese victory. The war broke out in July of 1894 after Japanese and Chinese forces sought control over Korea. Japanese forces had superior organization and technology, so their victory over China was swift. As part of the peace terms, China had to relinquish control of Taiwan to Japan and recognize Korea as an independent country. The war marked the end of China's status as a cultural and political hegemon in Asia and turned Japan into a formidable power on the world stage.

events.title: Constantin Von Economo Describes Encephalitis Lethargica For The First Time
events.description: Amid an outbreak of a strange condition, Austrian doctor Constantin von Economo medically describes the disease encephalitis lethargica, otherwise known as the "sleeping sickness." No cure was ever discovered for the disease, nor a direct cause, but no other widespread outbreak has ever occurred.

events.title: The Bay Of Pigs Invasion Is Launched
events.description: Sovfoto/Universal Images Group via Getty ImagesCaptured mercenaries following the Bay of Pigs Invasion.

events.title: Cambodia Falls To The Khmer Rouge
events.description: Cambodia falls to the Khmer Rouge when soldiers enter Phnom Penh after five years of fighting. Led by Pol Pot, the Khmer Rouge swiftly executed its plan to turn Cambodia into a rural utopia by forcing millions of people from Cambodian cities onto farms. Though the Khmer Rouge was overthrown in 1979, up to 2 million people are estimated to have died in the genocide that took place under their rule.

events.title: Elvis Impersonator Paul Kevin Curtis Is Arrested For Sending A Ricin-Laced Letter To President Obama
events.description: Paul Kevin Curtis, an Elvis impersonator from Tupelo, Mississippi, is arrested for allegedly sending a ricin-laced letter to President Barack Obama and two other government officials. Investigators would later discover that Curtis had been framed by his rival, Everett Dutschke.

events.title: Paul Revere Embarks On His 'Midnight Ride'
events.description: Paul Revere rides from Boston to Lexington, Massachusetts. A silversmith and supporter of the nascent American Revolution, Revere and others were tasked with alerting local residents that British troops were on the move and warning Samuel Adams and John Hancock that they were in danger of being arrested. Revere's "Midnight Ride" was made celebrated roughly a century later when Henry Wadsworth Longfellow published his famous — but somewhat inaccurate — poem, "Paul Revere's Ride," in 1861.

events.title: Leonarda Cianciulli Is Born
events.description: Leonarda Cianciulli is born in Montella, Italy. An Italian serial killer called the "Soap-Maker of Correggio," Cianciulli murdered three women between 1939 and 1940 and used their remains to make soap and teacakes. She allegedly decided to murder the women as human sacrifices, in hopes that doing so would keep her son, Giuseppe, safe from harm during World War II.

events.title: The Great San Francisco Earthquake Takes Place
events.description: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty ImagesRuins in San Francisco, California, following the 1906 earthquake.

events.title: Survivors From The Titanic Arrive In NYC
events.description: Seven hundred survivors from the RMS Titanic arrive in New York City. Three days earlier, in the wee hours of April 15, the luxury ocean liner had sunk in the North Atlantic Ocean after striking an iceberg. Of the 2,240 passengers and crew, just 706 people managed to survive.

events.title: Albert Einstein Dies
events.description: Albert Einstein dies in Princeton, New Jersey, after suffering an abdominal aortic aneurysm at the age of 76. Though the famous physicist, perhaps best known for developing the theory of relativity, could have had surgery, he refused. "I want to go when I want," Einstein said. "It is tasteless to prolong life artificially. I have done my share, it is time to go. I will do it elegantly."

events.title: Grace Kelly Marries Prince Rainier
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesGrace Kelly and Prince Rainier leaving the Cathedral of St. Nicholas in Monaco on their wedding day.

events.title: The American Revolution Begins
events.description: The American Revolution begins in Lexington, Massachusetts. British troops and American militiamen met in Lexington Green, where someone — to this day, it's unclear who — fired a shot. The "shot heard 'round the world'" led to the American Revolution, which raged for seven years and resulted in the United States' independence from Britain.

events.title: Lord Byron Dies
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesThe poet Lord Byron died at the age of 36 while supporting Greek independence from the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising Begins
events.description: Ullstein bild/Getty ImagesSS commander Jürgen Stroop (center) during the Warsaw Uprising.

events.title: Dr. Albert Hofmann Creates Bicycle Day
events.description: Dr. Albert Hofmann takes the first psychedelic trip on LSD and cycles back to his home after, thereby creating Bicycle Day. Today, Bicycle Day is celebrated annually in honor of the psychedelic revolution.

events.title: The Waco Siege Ends
events.description: The siege of the Branch Davidian compound in Waco, Texas, ends after 51 days. Two months earlier on February 28, 1993, agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms had embarked on a disastrous raid of the compound in search of illegal guns and explosives that left several dead on both sides. The FBI took over the operation and attacked the Christian cult compound, breaking the siege but killing dozens of the Branch Davidians, including several children and the cult's leader, David Koresh.

events.title: The Oklahoma City Bombing Takes Place
events.description: J. Pat CarterThe aftermath of the attack in Oklahoma City.

events.title: The Siege Of Derry Begins
events.description: Culture Club/Getty ImagesA 17th-century depiction of the Siege of Derry.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Is Born In Austria
events.description: Adolf Hitler is born to Alois and Klaire Hitler in Braunau am Inn, Austria. The leader of the Nazi party, Hitler was one of the main architects of the Holocaust, which killed an estimated 11 million people during World War II, including six million Jews. He died by suicide when Germany was on the brink of losing World War 2, taking his own life in his Berlin bunker on April 30, 1945.

events.title: Marie And Pierre Curie Isolate Radium
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesMarie Curie in her lab, circa 1905.

events.title: The Columbine School Shooting
events.description: Jefferson County Sheriff's Department via Getty ImagesColumbine high school shooters Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold in a surveillance tape in the cafeteria at Columbine High School.

events.title: The Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill Takes Place
events.description: The oil drilling rig Deepwater Horizon explodes in the Gulf of Mexico. Eleven workers were killed and the subsequent oil spill was the largest in recorded history. Four million barrels of oil poured from the rig for almost 90 days before the spill was finally capped in July 2010.

events.title: Rome Is Founded
events.description: According to ancient Roman mythology, the city that would become the heart of the Roman Empire was established by twins Romulus and Remus, who had been abandoned at birth and raised by a she-wolf. Romulus allegedly killed Remus and named the city after himself, but this myth — and the precise date of Rome's founding — didn't emerge until hundreds of years later.

events.title: General Santa Anna Is Captured
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA depiction of General Santa Anna, the Mexican dictator.

events.title: USS Maine Blows Up, Sparking The Spanish-American War
events.description: The USS Maine blows up in the Havana Harbor in Cuba, prompting the United States to declare war on Spain.

events.title: Mark Twain Dies
events.description: Samuel Clemens, better known as Mark Twain, dies in Redding, Connecticut, at the age of 74. A writer, humorist, and social critic, Twain penned iconic American works like The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876) and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1884). He was also known for his sharp wit and quotes like "Do the right thing. It will gratify some people and astonish the rest."

events.title: The "Red Baron" Is Killed
events.description: Baron Manfred von Richthofen is killed in action in France during World War I. A German flying ace known as the "Red Baron," Richthofen became famous for both his red airplane and his kill count (he shot down 80 Allied planes during his career, including 21 in the month of April 1917). On the day he died, Richthofen flew deep into French territory and was either shot down by Canadian Air Force pilot Captain Arthur Roy Brown or an Australian gunner.

events.title: "Proof" Of The Loch Ness Monster Is Published
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesThe 1934 photo that alleged to show the Loch Ness Monster.

events.title: Prince Dies
events.description: Prince Rogers Nelson, later known as Prince and The Artist Formerly Known as Prince, dies at the age of 57 in Chanhassen, Minnesota, from an accidental drug overdose. A singer and songwriter, Prince rose to fame with albums like 1999 (1982), Purple Rain (1984), and Sign O' The Times (1987). Prince's death shocked his fans, and a subsequent investigation found that he'd accidentally died from a "self-administered" overdose of fentanyl.

events.title: Michelle McNamara Dies
events.description: Michelle McNamara, true crime sleuth responsible for calling greater attention to the Golden State Killer case, dies of a drug overdose in Los Angeles.

events.title: Hernán Cortés Establishes Veracruz
events.description: Art Media/Print Collector/Getty ImagesA depiction of the city of Veracruz from the 17th century.

events.title: The Oklahoma Land Rush Begins
events.description: The Oklahoma Land Rush begins at noon. At that moment, thousands of eager settlers flooded a 1.9 million acre swath of land in Indian Territory that the U.S. government had recently opened up for settlement. The land had technically never been designated to any one tribe, but settlers were able to eventually control greater and greater portions of land that was reserved for certain tribes. By 1905, white settlers controlled most of the territory.

events.title: German Forces Use Chlorine Gas For The First Time
events.description: German troops deploy chlorine gas as a weapon of war for the first time during a battle just north of Ypres, Belgium. The gas stunned and terrified Allied troops, who had no means of protecting themselves. Before long, however, gas — and gas masks — became a defining feature of World War I.

events.title: Bettie Page Is Born
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesBettie Page posing for a portrait circa 1952.

events.title: The Inaugural Earth Day Is Observed
events.description: The first "Earth Day" is observed in the United States. Meant to raise awareness about environmental issues worldwide, the event was promoted by Senator Gaylord Nelson, who hoped that young people would fight for the Earth with the same energy that they'd fought against the war in Vietnam. Today, Earth Day is observed in more than 193 countries.

events.title: Richard Nixon Dies
events.description: Richard Nixon dies in New York City at the age of 81, shortly after suffering a stroke. A congressman, senator, and the 37th president of the United States, Nixon's accomplishments as president include his historic 1972 trip to China and the reduction of tension between the United States and the Soviet Union. However, he is best remembered for his role in the Watergate coverup, which rocked his presidency and led to his resignation from office in 1974.

events.title: King Aethelred II Dies
events.description: King Aethelred II dies in London, England, around the age of 50. The king of England from 978 to 1013 then again from 1014 until he died in 1016, Aethelred was dubbed Aethelred "The Unready" because of his perceived mismanagement of the Danish invasion of England. His nickname roughly means "bad counsel," a nod to Aethelred's name meaning "good counsel."

events.title: William Shakespeare Is Born
events.description: Stock Montage/Getty ImagesWilliam Shakespeare is considered by some the greatest playwright of all time.

events.title: Charles II Of England Is Crowned
events.description: Charles II of England is coronated at Westminster Abbey. The son of King Charles I, Charles II was forced to flee the country amid the English Civil Wars after his father's 1649 execution. Though Oliver Cromwell took power in his stead, Cromwell's death in 1658 resulted in the restoration of the monarchy and Charles's return from years of exile.

events.title: Lee Miller Is Born
events.description: Elizabeth "Lee" Miller, one of the few female war correspondents during World War II, is born in Poughkeepsie, New York.

events.title: Frederick William "Fritz" Niland Is Born
events.description: Frederick William "Fritz" Niland, later the inspiration for the film Saving Private Ryan, is born in Tonawanda, New York.

events.title: Elvis Presley Makes His Debut In Vegas
events.description: Elvis Presley makes his debut in Las Vegas.

events.title: Timothy McVeigh Is Born
events.description: Timothy McVeigh, who later masterminded the 1995 Oklahoma City Bombing, is born in Lockport, New York.

events.title: Sirhan Sirhan Receives The Death Penalty
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesPolice portraits of Sirhan Sirhan from the night he assassinated Robert Kennedy.

events.title: Jasmine Richardson Murders Her Parents
events.description: Jasmine Richardson and her boyfriend, Jeremey Steinke, murder her parents in Medicine Hat, Canada. Before Richardson met Steinke, friends and family knew her as a happy girl. At just 12-years-old, Richardson's personality shifted, and she became more interested in the "goth lifestyle." Her and 23-year-old Steinke met at a punk rock concert, and the two became inseparable. Obviously unhappy with her relationship, Jasmine's parents forbid her from seeing him. This sparked the beginning of a crime that would shock Canada to its core.

events.title: The Library Of Congress Is Established
events.description: President John Adams approves a congressional act that both moves the nation's capital from Philadelphia to Washington, D.C., and sets aside $5,000 for books to be used by Congress. Though a fire destroyed the Library's original collection of 3,000 books during the War of 1812 — and subsequent fires destroyed many of the books purchased from Thomas Jefferson to replace them — the Library of Congress contains more than 170 million items today, including 51 million books.

events.title: The Armenian Genocide Begins
events.description: Photo12/Universal Images Group via Getty ImagesJust a few of the many people killed during the Armenian Genocide.

events.title: The Easter Rebellion Begins
events.description: Launched by Irish nationalists led by Patrick Pearse, the Easter Rebellion sought to end British rule and establish Irish independence. Though a British counteroffensive swiftly quashed the rebellion — Pearse and more than a dozen nationalist leaders were subsequently executed — the Easter Rebellion laid the groundwork for later acts of resistance and the establishment of the Irish Free State in 1921.

events.title: Vladimir Komarov Becomes First Man To Die In Space
events.description: Vladimir Komarov becomes the first man to die in space. In 1964, Komarov commanded Voskhod 1, the first space flight to carry more than one crew member. His second time in space was with the Soyuz 1, on which he served as a solo pilot. Upon attempting to return to Earth, the Soyuz 1's parachute failed, causing the vessel to slam into the ground at a speed of 98 feet per second. The impact severely mutilated Komarov's body, which was put on display at his funeral to show just how dangerous space travel could be.

events.title: The "Golden State Killer" Is Arrested
events.description: Sacramento County Sheriff's Department via Getty ImagesThe booking photo of "Golden State Killer" Joseph James DeAngelo.

events.title: Robinson Crusoe Is Published
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA cover for The Life and Strange Adventures of Robinson Crusoe from circa 1900.

events.title: The Guillotine Is Used For The First Time
events.description: The guillotine is used for the first time in Paris, France. The beheading device was developed as a "humane" way to kill criminals, and as a way to spare the executioner from difficult executions with a sword. The first victim of the guillotine was Nicolas-Jacques Pelletier, who had been found guilty of robbery and murder, and his execution was carried out by executioner Charles Henri Sanson, who would also oversee the execution of Queen Marie Antoinette and King Louis XVI. France continued to use the guillotine until 1977.

events.title: Ella Fitzgerald Is Born
events.description: Anthony Bruno/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesElla Fitzgerald poses for a portrait, circa 1945.

events.title: The Hubble Space Telescope Goes Into Orbit
events.description: Launched by the shuttle Discovery, the Hubble Space Telescope moves five miles per second while orbiting more than 300 miles above the earth. To date, it has captured more than one million observations including the birth and deaths of stars and far-off galaxies.

events.title: Kathmandu Earthquake Strikes
events.description: Kathmandu earthquake strikes in Nepal, killing nearly 9,000 people and injuring 20,000. The earthquake's magnitude was between 7.8 and 8.1. The earthquake triggered an avalanche on Mount Everest, killing 22 people. Hundreds of thousands of Nepalese lost their homes and villages. Several important historical and religious buildings were destroyed as well. Following the initial quake, aftershocks terrorized the region, killing more people and destroying what remained. In total, $3 billion was raised to help fund rescue efforts, rebuild, and care for those who had lost their homes in the earthquake.

events.title: The 'Female Paul Revere' Rides From New York To Connecticut
events.description: Sybil Ludington allegedly races 40 miles from Fredericksburg, New York on horseback to alert her father, Henry, that the British had attacked the nearby town of Danbury, Connecticut. Ludington's story, first published in a family memoir about her father, elicited comparisons between her ride and the more famous ride of Paul Revere. However, historians have expressed doubts in recent years over whether or not Ludington's ride actually happened.

events.title: John Wilkes Booth Is Killed
events.description: Kean Collection/Getty ImagesA depiction of John Wilkes Booth's death in 1865.

events.title: Ma Rainey Is Born
events.description: Gertrude Pridgett, later known as Ma Rainey, is born in Columbus, Georgia. A blues singer dubbed the "Mother of the Blues," Rainey became a popular entertainer in the early 20th century by belting songs like "Bo-Weevil Blues" (1923), "Shave 'Em Dry" (1924), and "Ma Rainey's Black Bottom" (1927). Her life was depicted in August Wilson's 1988 play, 1988 Ma Rainey's Black Bottom, which was adapted for film in 2020.

events.title: Hermann Göring Creates The Gestapo
events.description: Hermann Göring announces the creation of the "Geheime Staatspolizei," or the Gestapo. Secret state police loyal to the Nazis, the Gestapo's mission was to "investigate and combat all attempts to threaten the state." They coordinated the deportation of Jews, repressed resistance movements, and killed and tortured many of those that they arrested.

events.title: The 'Grauballe Man' Is Discovered
events.description: The Grauballe Man, a 2,000-year-old bog body, is discovered in a peat bog near the village of Grauballe in Jutland, Denmark.

events.title: Studio 54 Opens In New York City
events.description: Studio 54, the infamous disco club known for hosting celebrities, opens in New York City. The club hosted over 4,000 people on its opening night.

events.title: The Chernobyl Disaster Takes Place
events.description: Igor Kostin/Laski Diffusion/Getty ImagesChernobyl nuclear power plant a few weeks after the disaster.

events.title: The World's Deadliest Known Tornado Hits Bangladesh
events.description: A tornado strikes the Manikganj district of Bangladesh. The world's deadliest known tornado, the storm smashed a path one mile wide and ten miles long through the towns of Manikgank Sadar and Saturia. More than 1,000 people were killed, some 12,000 injured, and 80,000 lost their homes.

events.title: Josef Fritzl Is Arrested
events.description: Josef Fritzl, who had imprisoned his daughter Elisabeth in 1984 in the family cellar, forcing her to be his sex slave and to bear his children, is arrested in Austria.

events.title: Ferdinand Magellan Is Killed
events.description: Science Source/Photo Researchers History/Getty ImagesA depiction of Ferdinand Magellan from the 16th century.

events.title: John Milton Sells Paradise Lost
events.description: John Milton sells his epic poem, Paradise Lost, to publisher Samuel Simmons. The terms of their contract stated that Milton would receive £5 immediately and £5 more if the poem sold more than 1,300 copies, plus £10 more for future editions. Milton's death in 1674 meant that he only received £10 in total for his work, though Paradise Lost has since become a beloved masterpiece of the English language.

events.title: The Sultana Explodes
events.description: The Sultana explodes on the Mississippi River. The worst maritime disaster in American history, the explosion killed 1,700 passengers, including hundreds of recently freed Union prisoners of war. Though stories have persisted that sabotage sank the ship, an official inquiry found that insufficient water in the ship's boiler triggered the disaster.

events.title: Andrew Cunanan Begins Killing Spree
events.description: Jamie Scott Lytle/Sygma via Getty ImagesA high school photograph of Andrew Cunanan.

events.title: The Tomb Of Herod The Great Is Discovered
events.description: Archaeologists discover the tomb of Herod the Great near Jerusalem, Israel. The King of Judaea, Herod plays an important role in the Bible for allegedly ordering the deaths of all male infants in Bethlehem in hopes of killing the prophesized "King of the Jews." He died in 4 B.C.E.

events.title: Emperor Constantius II Arrives In Rome
events.description: Emperor Constantius II arrives in Rome for the first time. The third son of Emperor Constantine, Constantius was born in present-day Serbia and initially shared power with his brothers. Upon their deaths, he solidified his rule by riding to Rome with great fanfare, entering the city in a golden coach.

events.title: Benito Mussolini Is Executed
events.description: Keystone/Getty ImagesBenito Mussolini addressing a crowd in 1938.

events.title: Afghan President Daoud Is Overthrown
events.description: Afghanistan President Sardar Mohammed Daoud is overthrown and killed by pro-communist rebels. He was replaced by Nur Mohammed Taraki, the Soviet-friendly head of the Afghan Communist Party, but Taraki was overthrown and killed the next year. The situation in the country quickly devolved and led to the Soviet-Afghan War, which lasted until 1989.

events.title: The Port Arthur Massacre Begins
events.description: Fairfax Media via Getty ImagesMourners leave flowers at the site of the Port Arthur Massacre.

events.title: Bill McGuire, Husband Of The "Suitcase Killer," Goes Missing/h2> Bill McGuire goes missing from Woodbridge Township, New Jersey. A month later, suitcases containing human body parts appeared in the Chesapeake Bay, prompting police to launch a criminal investigation. Police determined that the remains belonged to Bill McGuire, and they went to interview his wife, Melanie. His wife stated that they had fought the night he went missing, and that he decided to walk out and never return. Forensic evidence would eventually show that Melanie drugged her husband, shot him, and then dismembered his body. 2004: CBS 60 Minutes II Releases Photographs From Abu Ghraib Prison Showing Abuse
events.description: After photographs from inside Abu Ghraib prison showing Military Police torturing and abusing Iraqi prisoners are leaked by an insider at the prison, CBS shows the photographs to the American public on 60 Minutes II. The photographs featured several people, but most of the attention was turned on Private First Class Lynndie England, seen smiling in many photos as prisoners are forced to strip nude and pose with bags over their heads.

events.title: Joan Of Arc Arrives In Orleans
events.description: Joan of Arc leads French forces into Orleans, France. Driven by "divine" instruction to drive out the English and place the dauphin Charles (later Charles VII) on the French throne, Joan brought troops to the besieged city and expelled English forces. Just over a year later, however, the English would capture Joan, find her guilty of heresy, and burn her at the stake.

events.title: William Randolph Hearst Is Born
events.description: PhotoQuest/Getty ImagesWilliam Randolph Hearst in 1926.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Marries Eva Braun
events.description: Adolf Hitler marries Eva Braun while hiding in Hitler's Berlin bunker. The Führer's long-term mistress, Braun had been with Hitler for 14 years. But her marriage to the German dictator was much more short-lived, as both Braun and Hitler died by suicide just hours after their marriage.

events.title: Dachau Is Liberated
events.description: The concentration camp of Dachau is liberated by U.S. forces.

events.title: The L.A. Riots Begin
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA news photographer runs past a burning guard shack in a parking lot in downtown Los Angeles, California, April 29, 1992.

events.title: Prince William Marries Kate Kiddleton
events.description: Prince William weds Kate Middleton at Westminster Abbey in London, England. The heir to the English throne, William met Kate while they were both studying at the University of St. Andrews. They were engaged in 2010 following a long courtship and have three children.

events.title: The Louisiana Purchase Is Completed
events.description: The Louisiana Purchase Treaty is signed between the United States and France. Robert Livingston and James Monroe agreed to pay France $15 million (more than $300 million today) for 828,000 square miles of land that lay west of the Mississippi River. The area was greater than Great Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal combined, and greatly expanded the United States's territory.

events.title: The Discovery Of Electrons Is Announced
events.description: Oxford Science Archive/Print Collector/Getty ImagesSir Joseph John "J.J." Thomson in his lab in 1900.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Dies By Suicide
events.description: ullsetein bild/Getty ImagesTaken on April 29, 1945, just one day before his suicide, this is widely believed to be the last photo of Adolf Hitler (right), seen here surveying the ruins of the Reich chancellery in Berlin with his adjutant, Julius Schaub.

events.title: The 'Fall Of Saigon' Takes Place
events.description: © Jacques Pavlovsky/Sygma/CORBIS/Sygma via Getty ImagesNorth Vietnamese troops entering Saigon.

events.title: Anton Lavey Founds The Church Of Satan
events.description: Anton Lavey founds the Church of Satan on Walpurgisnacht, the "Night Of The Witches." Despite its name, Lavey's church didn't encourage evil but rather worshiped "His Infernal Majesty" as a humanist who embodied values like self-assertion and justified rebellion. Lavey's church operates to this day and attracted celebrity members like Jayne Mansfield.

events.title: Vodou Becomes An Official Religion
events.description: Despite being practiced by Haitians since at least the 17th century, Vodou had never been declared an official religion. That changed in 2003, however, when the Haitian officially recognized Vodou as a religion.

events.title: Joey Testa Released On Parole
events.description: Joey Testa, one of the infamous Gemini Twins, is released from prison on parole due to ongoing health issues, despite a life sentence.

events.title: Christopher Columbus Proposes Sailing Westward To India
events.description: Most people know that Italian explorer Christopher Columbus landed in the New World while pursuing a westward sea passage to India in 1492. What many may not know, however, is that this historic endeavor languished in the planning phase for more than a decade.

events.title: The First Adhesive Postage Stamp Is Released
events.description: The world's first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, is introduced in the United Kingdom. Until the introduction of the adhesive stamp, letters were weighed individually and priced accordingly, and the person receiving the mail was the one who paid. However, if the recipient refused, the post office lost money. The one-cent postage stamp ensured that all mail was paid for and made sending letters affordable for the general public.

events.title: Calamity Jane Is Born
events.description: Known for her legendary skills with a gun, Calamity Jane remains among the most fabled figures of the Wild West to this day.

events.title: The Empire State Building Is Dedicated
events.description: President Herbert Hoover dedicates the Empire State Building in New York City by symbolically pushing a button from the White House to "light up" the structure.

events.title: Evelyn McHale Dies By Suicide
events.description: Robert Wiles/Wikimedia CommonsThe "most beautiful suicide" of Evelyn McHale.

events.title: Mountaineer George Mallory's Body Is Found On Everest
events.description: Pictorial Press Ltd/Alamy Stock PhotoGeorge Mallory with fellow climber Andrew Irvine in the last photo of them on their fatal Everest climb in 1924.

events.title: Chandra Levy Disappears
events.description: Chandra Levy disappears in Washington, D.C., launching a media frenzy over the 24-year-old intern's fate and her relationship with an older, married congressman named Gary Condit. Levy's body was discovered about a year later in a local park.

events.title: Aron Ralston Amputates His Own Arm
events.description: Aron Ralston/YouTubeAron Ralston just before he amputated his own arm.

events.title: Anne Boleyn Is Jailed For Adultery
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesA depiction of King Henry VIII with his second wife, Anne Boleyn.

events.title: Catherine The Great Is Born In Prussia
events.description: Catherine the Great, empress of Russia from 1762 to 1796, is born in the Kingdom of Prussia.

events.title: The Washburn Mill Explosion Takes Place
events.description: Hennepin County LibraryThe aftermath of the Washburn Mill explosion.
