events.title: The First Known Sighting Of The Loch Ness Monster Is Reported
events.description: The famous 1934 "surgeon's photograph" of the Loch Ness Monster that's now known to be a hoax.

events.title: The Attempted Assassination Of Frank Costello
events.description: Frank Costello, the legendary crime boss who inspired The Godfather, is attacked by Vincent "The Chin" Gigante on orders of Vito Genovese. The attempt on Costello's life failed, and he later refused to name his attacker, making peace with Genovese and bringing their years-long feud to an end.

events.title: J. Edgar Hoover Dies
events.description: J. Edgar Hoover, the first director of the FBI, in 1961.

events.title: Osama Bin Laden Is Killed
events.description: Osama bin Laden, the leader of the terrorist group al-Qaeda, is killed by Navy SEALs in Abbottabad, Pakistan. President Barack Obama approved the risky mission in which operatives raided bin Laden's compound and finally ended the decade-long search for the man behind the 9/11 terrorist attacks. After flying his body to Afghanistan for identification, U.S. forces buried bin Laden over the Arabian Sea within 24 hours of his death, per Islamic tradition.

events.title: Niccolò Machiavelli Is Born
events.description: A 16th-century portrait of Niccolò Machiavelli by proto-Baroque painter Santi di Tito.

events.title: Columbus Encounters The Island Of Jamaica
events.description: Columbus encounters the island of Jamaica. Columbus had heard about Jamaica from natives on modern-day Cuba. They claimed that Jamaica was an island of gold. Columbus never found gold on Jamaica, but he did claim it for the Spanish Empire, calling it Santiago. In its early days, Jamaica served as a supply base for Spaniards. In 1655, the English attacked Spaniards on Jamaica and claimed the island for themselves. Under English rule, Jamaica became an economically and politically important island in the Western Hemisphere.

events.title: The Panic Of 1893 Begins
events.description: The Panic of 1893, which had been building for months, begins in earnest. The economic depression ultimately lasted until 1897.

events.title: Margaret Thatcher Becomes The First Female Prime Minister Of Great Britain
events.description: Britain's Conservative Party defeats the Labour Party by winning a majority in the House of Commons during parliamentary elections, making Conservative Party leader Margaret Thatcher the first female prime minister. She became known as the "Iron Lady" for her strident leadership style and anti-communist beliefs. Significant events from her time in office include the Falklands War, the final years of the Cold War, and an attempt on her life made by the Irish Republican Army.

events.title: Cari Lightner Is Killed By A Drunk Driver
events.description: We Save Lives Highway Safety AdvocatesCari Lightner was killed by a drunk driver at the age of 13.

events.title: Madeleine McCann Goes Missing
events.description: Madeleine McCann shortly before her disappearance in 2007.

events.title: The Haymarket Riot Breaks Out
events.description: The Haymarket Riot breaks out at a Chicago labor protest, leading to the deaths of at least four civilians and seven police officers plus dozens of injuries. Labor activists had organized the rally to protest the police killings of several other workers at a strike the day before, and it turned violent when someone threw a bomb at the authorities. Eight protesters were convicted, though there was little evidence against them, and the riot ultimately proved to be a major setback for America's organized labor movement.

events.title: Construction Begins On The Panama Canal
events.description: President Teddy Roosevelt sitting in a steam shovel at the Panama Canal in 1906.

events.title: Audrey Hepburn Is Born
events.description: One of the most celebrated performers of the 20th century, Audrey Hepburn is one of the few people to have ever won an Emmy, Oscar, Grammy, and Tony.

events.title: The 'Eagle's Nest' Is Captured By U.S. Troops
events.description: Adolf Hitler's mountaintop retreat known as "Eagle's Nest" in Berchtesgaden, Germany is seized by American troops.

events.title: The Freedom Riders Begin Their Historic Journeys
events.description: A group of 13 Freedom Riders board a Greyhound bus in Washington, D.C. and head to New Orleans to celebrate the anniversary of the Brown v. Board of Education ruling. The riders planned to protest segregated bus terminals, lunch counters, and restrooms during their journey, though violence from white protesters and police officers soon broke out along the route. Nevertheless, their journey inspired other Freedom Rides and brought significant attention to civil rights issues in the United States.

events.title: The Kent State Massacre Leaves Four Dead
events.description: John Paul Filo/Library of CongressJeffrey Miller was one of four students killed during the Kent State Massacre.

events.title: David Reimer Commits Suicide
events.description: David Reimer, a man who was forced to live as a girl, commits suicide at 38. After a botched circumcision left Reimer's penis damaged, his parents decided to take one doctor's advice: raise Reimer as a girl. Motive for this advice came partly out of intellectual curiosity. John Money, a sexologist, believed that gender was something learned at a young age, and Reimer's case presented a rare opportunity to test that theory. Unfortunately, Reimer experienced terrible gender dysphoria until his parents revealed the truth. He lived as a male, taking testosterone supplements and receiving a prosthetic penis, until his death.

events.title: Karl Marx Is Born
events.description: Groundbreaking economist and philosopher Karl Heinrich Marx is born in Trier, Germany. Marx is best known for co-writing The Communist Manifesto, an historic 1848 pamphlet that criticized capitalism and called for a "forcible overthrow of all existing social conditions."

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Dies
events.description: Napoleon's death mask.

events.title: Mexico Wins The Battle Of Puebla
events.description: Mexico wins the Battle of Puebla as part of the Second French Intervention in Mexico. After Mexican President Benito Juarez declined to pay loan payments from French, British, and Spanish creditors for two years, French and Spanish forces invaded the country. At the Battle of Puebla, French forces retreated and Mexico reclaimed the city of Puebla, forcing French troops to the coast. The victory was celebrated every year under the name "Cinco de Mayo," and represents Mexico's sovereignty and strength in the wake of foreign invasion.

events.title: Nellie Bly Is Born
events.description: Elizabeth Cochrane Seaman, better known as Nellie Bly, the pen name she used as an investigative journalist, is born in Cochrans Mills, Pennsylvania.

events.title: Alan Shepard Becomes The First American In Space
events.description: NASAAlan Shepard climbs aboard the Freedom 7 in preparation for its historic launch.

events.title: Bobby Sands Dies
events.description: PA Images via Getty ImagesBobby Sands died after refusing to eat for more than two months.

events.title: Sigmund Freud Is Born
events.description: Neurologist and psychoanalyst Sigmund Freud is born in Freiberg, a Morovian town within the Austrian Empire. Freud is best known for founding the discipline of psychoanalysis, a collection of therapeutic techniques that deal with the unconscious mind. Some of his most famous ideas include the Oedipus complex and the psychic structure of the id, ego, and super ego. A Jewish man, Freud fled Austria in 1938 to avoid Nazi persecution, and he died in London the following year at the age of 83.

events.title: The Hindenburg Bursts Into Flames
events.description: The Hindenburg airship explodes in as it attempts to dock in New Jersey.

events.title: English Channel Tunnel Opens
events.description: The Channel Tunnel, also known as the "Eurotunnel" or the "Chunnel," opens to train traffic. The longest undersea tunnel in the world, the Channel Tunnel took six years to build. It connects Folkestone, England to Sangatte, France, and allows passenger and freight trains to travel between the island of Great Britain and the European mainland in as little as 35 minutes.

events.title: Former CIA Director William Colby Drowns
events.description: William Colby, the former director of the Central Intelligence Agency, is found dead on a riverbank in Maryland after leaving for a solo canoe trip. Colby drowned, but his death has been the subject of conspiracy theories and his son claimed that Colby had died by suicide.

events.title: Steve Jobs Introduces The iMac Computer
events.description: Steve Jobs introduces the iMac computer to the world for the first time. At Macworld, Jobs announced that the new consumer desktop computer would allow users to access the internet quickly, present a sleek design unrivalled in the market, and even change the education field. And he was right.

events.title: Ariel Castro's Victims Are Rescued
events.description: The home where Ariel Castro held three women — and later a child — for over a decade.

events.title: Beethoven Debuts Symphony No. 9
events.description: An 1820 portrait of Beethoven by Joseph Karl Stieler.

events.title: H. H. Holmes Is Hanged
events.description: American serial killer H. H. Holmes is hanged in Philadelphia after his conviction for the murder of Benjamin Pitezel. While he was executed for just one murder, Holmes confessed to killing 27 people between 1891 and 1894, many of them in his Chicago "Murder Castle." In his confession, he stated, "I was born with the devil in me. I could not help the fact that I was a murderer, no more than a poet can help the inspiration to sing."

events.title: The Sinking Of The Lusitania
events.description: An illustration of the sinking of the RMS Lusitania.

events.title: Eva Perón, First Spouse Of Argentina, Is Born
events.description: Eva Perón, the first spouse of Argentina, is born Los Toldos, Argentina. While studying to be an actress in Buenos Aires, Eva met Colonel Juan Perón and married him a year later. Juan Perón was elected as Argentina's president in 1946, and Eva suddenly found herself in Argentina's political world. As the First Spouse, Eva began multiple campaigns meant to bolster social services in Argentina. She also worked hard to legalize women's suffrage and even ran for vice president. Although Eva died from cervical cancer at the age of 33, her legacy was long lasting in Argentina long after her death.

events.title: Leonid Brezhnev Becomes General Secretary Of The U.S.S.R.
events.description: Leonid Brezhnev becomes the Chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet, the equivalent of president of the U.S.S.R. Brezhnev had been a close associate of his predecessor Nikita Khrushchev for decades, and when Khrushchev became the leader of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union after Joseph Stalin's death, he named Brezhnev president — a largely symbolic role.

events.title: Miguel Hidalgo Is Born
events.description: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, a Roman Catholic priest and the father of Mexican independence, is born in Guanajuato, Mexico. In 1810, Hidalgo gave an impassioned speech known as the Cry of Dolores, urging the Mexican people to rise up against Spanish colonizers. This call to arms sparked the Mexican War of Independence. Hidalgo gathered an army of 90,000 farmers and poor citizens in his march across Mexico, but he was captured and executed in 1811.

events.title: The First Coca-Cola Is Sold
events.description: Dr. John Pemberton, the inventor of Coca-Cola, sells the first glass of his new soda at Jacobs' Pharmacy in Atlanta. He had created the drink about a month earlier and brought a jug of it to the pharmacy on May 8th to test its potential as a retail product. It was sold for five cents per glass, and for the first year, an average of nine drinks were sold each day.

events.title: Mount Pelée Erupts
events.description: The aftermath of the Mount Pelée eruption in Saint-Pierre, Martinique.

events.title: V-E Day
events.description: People celebrate the surrender of Nazi Germany in the streets of London.

events.title: The Tollund Man Is Found
events.description: Silkeborg MuseumThe Tollund Man was found almost completely naked and posed in the fetal position.

events.title: Bill Clinton Allegedly Sexually Harasses Paula Jones
events.description: Arkansas civil servant Paula Jones is allegedly sexually harassed by then-Governor Bill Clinton during a conference at the Excelsior Hotel in Little Rock. These allegations eventually captured widespread attention amid the other charges of misconduct, sexual and otherwise, that were brought against Clinton later in the decade.

events.title: Riley Gaul Is Sentenced To Life In Prison For The Murder Of Emma Walker
events.description: Tennessee high schooler Riley Gaul is sentenced to life in prison for the murder of Emma Walker. Formerly Walker's boyfriend, Gaul was obsessed with maintaining their relationship, even going so far as to fake his own kidnapping to get Walker's attention.

events.title: Columbus Launches His Final Voyage
events.description: Columbus launches his final voyage to the New World. Departing from Cádiz, Spain, Columbus and his crew set sail for Martinique. While in the Caribbean, Columbus and his crew had to ride out a hurricane in modern day Dominican Republic. After the hurricane, Columbus sailed to Central America to explore the region. While there, the native people introduced Columbus and his crew to cocoa for the first time. By September of 1504, Columbus had returned to Spain.

events.title: John Brown Is Born
events.description: John Brown in 1846.

events.title: Buffalo Bill's Wild West Show Opens In London
events.description: Buffalo Bill and Sitting Bull during a performance in Montreal in 1885.

events.title: Willie Francis Faces The Electric Chair For The Second Time
events.description: Willie Francis was just 18 years old when he was put to death by electric chair.

events.title: The First Birth Control Pill Is Approved
events.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves the first commercially-produced birth control pill, Enovid-10. The search for a practical and effective form of birth control had been in progress for several decades, led in part by Margaret Sanger. In the 1950s, John Rock and Gregory Pincus began testing a pill that used synthetic forms of progesterone and estrogen to stop women from ovulating. The contraceptive proved successful, and the FDA's approval of the pill was a milestone for women's reproductive freedom.

events.title: Bacon's Rebellion Begins
events.description: Bacon's Rebellion begins in Virginia. Raids against Native American tribes in the area caused Virginia governor Sir William Berkeley to issue declarations in hopes of securing peace between Native Americans and colonists. However, a young man named Nathaniel Bacon Jr. gained the support of local anti-Native American militia groups and intimidated Berkeley into allowing him to raid Native American lands indiscriminately and drive them out of the colony entirely. On October 26, 1676, Bacon abruptly died of a disease brought on by body lice. After Bacon's death, Berkeley regained control and hanged the major leaders of the rebellion.

events.title: Paul Revere Dies
events.description: Paul Revere, an American patriot famous for his midnight ride through the Massachusetts countryside, dies in Boston.

events.title: John Wilkes Booth Is Born
events.description: John Wilkes Booth, who would go on to assassinate President Abraham Lincoln in April 1865, is born in Bel Air, Maryland.

events.title: The Transcontinental Railroad Is Completed
events.description: The builders of the Transcontinental Railroad who'd been working from the east and the west meet at Promontory Summit, Utah on May 10, 1869.

events.title: J. Edgar Hoover Takes Charge Of The FBI
events.description: J. Edgar Hoover becomes FBI director after being appointed by the U.S. attorney general. As director of the FBI, Hoover made several institutional changes, including firing agents that were little more than political appointees, requiring physical fitness testing, and conducting thorough background checks on interviewees. Under Hoover's leadership, the FBI became an integral part of the U.S. federal government. Hoover remained director of the FBI until his death in 1972, nearly 48 years after his initial appointment.

events.title: Winston Churchill Becomes Prime Minister Of Britain
events.description: Winston Churchill giving his signature "V for Victory" gesture.

events.title: Actress Joan Crawford Dies
events.description: Hollywood icon Joan Crawford dies in hospital, reportedly telling nurses who prayed for her, "Don't you dare ask God to help me."

events.title: Nelson Mandela Inaugurated As President Of South Africa
events.description: Nelson Mandela during his trip to Washington, D.C. in 1994, the year he became president of South Africa.

events.title: The 'Killer Clown' John Wayne Gacy Is Put To Death
events.description: John Wayne Gacy, Chicago's infamous serial killer who dressed as "Pogo the Clown" is put to death via lethal injection. Throughout the 1970s, Gacy abducted, tortured, sexually assaulted, and killed 33 young men and boys, burying most of their bodies on his own property.

events.title: Constantinople Is Consecrated
events.description: Constantinople is consecrated and named in honor of Constantine. Considered to be the cradle of Orthodox Christianity, Constantinople was the largest and wealthiest city in Europe for centuries. The city is famous for its architectural masterpieces, most notably the Hagia Sofia and the Imperial Palace. Constantinople, previously called Byzantium, was considered the Nova Roma (New Rome) after Roman emperor Constantine I officially declared the city the new capital of Rome.

events.title: Conjoined Twins Chang And Eng Bunker Are Born
events.description: Conjoined twins Chang and Eng Bunker, connected by a fleshy band at their sternum, are born in Siam (present-day Thailand).

events.title: The Pullman Strike Begins In Chicago
events.description: Chicago History Museum/Getty Images Railway workers burned railcars during the Pullman Strike.

events.title: The Battle Of Hamburger Hill Begins
events.description: United States Army Military History InstituteWounded 101st Airborne soldiers are loaded into medevac helicopters after Operation Apache Snow.

events.title: Bob Marley Dies
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesBob Marley raises his first while singing onstage in 1977.

events.title: Beck Weathers "Dies" on Mount Everest
events.description: Beck Weathers "dies" on Mount Everest. After collapsing in the snow, Beck Weathers was considered as good as dead to his team. In fact, they called his wife to tell her that her husband had died on the mountain. Rescuers tried to save Weathers, but they ultimately decided he was too far gone. Later, Weathers surprised his whole team when he strolled back into camp. He showed that, despite being stranded under the snow of Mount Everest, he was still very much alive. Weather's story is one of the most miraculous Mount Everest survival tales in history.

events.title: Playwright Thomas Kyd Is Arrested For Libel
events.description: Thomas Kyd is arrested for libel and subsequently tortured in London. Born in 1558, Kyd was an English playwright most known for his work The Spanish Tragedy. After an official decree called for the arrest of authors of lewd and libelous work, Kyd was imprisoned and his home was searched by authorities.

events.title: Florence Nightingale Is Born
events.description: London Stereoscopic Company/Getty ImagesPhotograph of Florence Nightingale in 1870.

events.title: Otto Frank Is Born
events.description: Otto Frank, the father of Anne Frank who survived the Holocaust and later published Anne's diaries, is born in Frankfurt.

events.title: The Lindbergh Baby Is Found Dead
events.description: Federal Bureau of Investigation Photograph of Charles Lindbergh, Jr. shortly before his kidnapping.

events.title: The First Alcoholics Anonymous Meeting Takes Place
events.description: Alcoholics Anonymous is founded in Akron, Ohio. Bill W., a New York stockbroker, and Dr. Bob S., an Akron surgeon, created Alcoholic Anonymous to help alcoholics achieve sobriety after battling their own addictions to alcohol. In 1939, the group published its basic textbook titled Alcoholics Anonymous and listed their core beliefs, now called the Twelve Steps of recovery. Groups across the United States popped up and membership increased over the ensuing decades. Today, Alcoholics Anonymous operates in 180 countries and is composed of 123,000 groups.

events.title: The Soviet Union Lifts The Blockade Of Berlin
events.description: After World War II, Allied countries divided up Germany into zones that each Allied nation could manage. Germany's capital, Berlin, was entirely inside the Soviet zone, and in 1948, Joseph Stalin called for a blockade of the entire city of Berlin after British, French, and American officials expressed a desire to create a unified West Germany with a common currency. With this blockade, nearly three million people in West Berlin were without food and supplies. The United States and Britain carried out the largest air relief operation in history, transporting 2.3 million tons of supplies into West Berlin over a period of 11 months.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots Is Defeated By Scottish Protestants
events.description: Mary, Queen of Scots is defeated at the Battle of Langside in Glasgow. At just six days old, Mary became Queen of Scotland after the death of her father, King James V. Raised in France, Mary returned to Scotland to claim the throne after the death of her first husband. In 1567, Mary married the Earl of Bothwell, enraging the nobility and forcing her to abdicate the throne.

events.title: Settlers Arrive In Virginia
events.description: Cultivation of tobacco at Jamestown in 1615.

events.title: The U.S. Declares War On Mexico
events.description: The United States declares war on Mexico as part of a bitter clash over control of what's now Texas. After war was declared, American troops moved into the disputed territory and eventually marched on to Mexico City. In 1848, the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo was signed, establishing the Rio Grande as the U.S.-Mexican border. As part of the treaty, Mexico recognized the annexation of Texas and agreed to sell California to America for $15 million. The U.S. gained roughly 525,000 square miles (1,359,743.76 square kilometers) as a result of the treaty.

events.title: Robert Smalls Escapes Slavery By Stealing A Ship
events.description: A photograph of Robert Smalls taken sometime between 1870 and 1880.

events.title: The MOVE Bombing In Philadelphia
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesAerial view of smoke rising from the smoldering rubble of the MOVE bombing in Philadelphia on May 13, 1985.

events.title: The Colony Of Jamestown Is Established
events.description: Settlers from England arrive in Jamestown, Virginia, and establish the first permanent English settlement in North America.

events.title: Edward Jenner Tests History's First Smallpox Vaccine
events.description: Edward Jenner tests his first smallpox vaccine. For centuries, smallpox devasted populations around the globe. Smallpox has killed 300 million people since 1900 alone, and its history dates as far back as 10,000 B.C. An English physician, Edward Jenner, took the first step in developing a smallpox vaccine after noticing that dairymaids who had been exposed to cowpox became immune to smallpox. He experimented by exposing a young boy to cowpox; once the boy recovered, Jenner exposed the boy to smallpox and noted that the disease did not develop. This experiment would set the foundation for later vaccines that would virtually eradicate smallpox globally.

events.title: Lewis And Clark Begin Their Expedition Of The American West
events.description: Amon Carter Museum of American ArtLewis and Clark on the Lower Columbia, by Charles Marion Russel, 1905.

events.title: Lina Medina Becomes The Youngest Person To Ever Give Birth
events.description: At just five years old, a Peruvian girl named Lina Medina becomes the youngest person in history to give birth. After noticing Lina's growing abdomen, her parents transported her to the hospital for examination, where doctors confirmed that she was seven months pregnant. Six weeks later, Lina gave birth to a healthy baby boy by caesarean section. The doctors noted that she had a fully mature reproductive system due to what's known as precocious puberty. The biological father of the child was never revealed. Later in her life, Medina remarried and had another son.

events.title: The State of Israel Is Founded
events.description: Israel Ministry of Foreign Affairs David Ben Gurion, who was to become Israel's first Prime Minister, reads the Declaration of Independence on May 14, 1948 in Tel Aviv.

events.title: Frank Sinatra Dies
events.description: Known as "The Chairman of the Board" and "Ol' Blue Eyes," Frank Sinatra remains one of the most iconic entertainers of the 20th century.

events.title: Brandon Swanson Vanishes
events.description: Brandon Swanson, a 19-year-old college student, vanishes after crashing his car in Minnesota. While on the phone with his father, he shouted: "Oh, shit!" and has never been seen since.

events.title: Anne Boleyn Is Sentenced To Death
events.description: There are very few contemporaneous images of Anne Boleyn because Henry VIII had many of them destroyed after her death.

events.title: The Seven Years' War Begins
events.description: The Seven Years' War begins. After years of fighting in North America, England and France declared war on one another, setting off a global conflict that spanned five continents. Under the leadership of William Pitt, British forces successfully defeated the French. Under the terms of the Treaty of Paris, Britain gained control over Canada, Louisiana, and Florida. In Europe, the Seven Years' War was mainly fought between Prussia and Russia. Under the leadership of Frederick the Great, Prussia won the Seven Years' War and bolstered its power and influence.

events.title: L. Frank Baum Is Born
events.description: Lyman Frank Baum is born in Chittenango, New York. Writing under the name L. Frank Baum, he later penned the enduring classic The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, which was published in 1900 and made into an iconic film starring Judy Garland in 1939. Baum died at the age of 62 in Los Angeles in 1919.

events.title: Emily Dickinson Dies
events.description: An excerpt of the only authenticated portrait of Emily Dickinson after her childhood.

events.title: The First McDonald's Opens For Business
events.description: The restaurant that would eventually become the first McDonald's begins serving customers in San Bernardino, California.

events.title: Bomb-Equipped Bats Accidentally Destroy A U.S. Air Force Base
events.description: In the midst of testing Project X-Ray — a World War II plan to outfit bats with bombs and send them into Japanese territory — the U.S. military accidentally releases dozens of these bats into an Air Force base, causing the whole thing to go up in flames.

events.title: Arthur Bremer Shoots Governor George Wallace
events.description: Arthur Bremer at the campaign rally for George Wallace just before he shot him.

events.title: Climber David Sharp Dies On Mount Everest
events.description: David Sharp, an experienced climber, freezes to death while descending Mount Everest. He attempted the climb with no supplemental oxygen. Sharp's death sparked controversy, as it was unclear if any of the numerous climbers that passed his dying body radioed for help or attempted to aid him.

events.title: Voltaire Is Imprisoned
events.description: French writer Voltaire is sent to Paris' Bastille prison. After satirically suggesting that Philippe Duc d'Orléans, who ruled France as a regent, had an incestuous relationship with his own daughter, Voltaire was sent to prison for almost a year. Nine years later, Voltaire was sent to the Bastille again after insulting an aristocrat, who then arranged to have him beat up and locked away.

events.title: Marie Antoinette Marries Louis XVI
events.description: Marie Antoinette was beheaded in 1792, nine months after her husband.

events.title: The First Academy Awards Are Held
events.description: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences hands out its now-famous annual film awards for the first time in Hollywood, California. Though the film Wings won Best Picture (then called Outstanding Picture), it took no one by surprise, because, unlike today, winners had been announced three months before the event.

events.title: Mao Zedong Releases The May 16 Notification
events.description: Mao Zedong in 1966.

events.title: Rey Rivera Disappears
events.description: Rey Rivera disappears in Baltimore, Maryland. Authorities found his body in an abandoned conference room at the historic Belvedere Hotel in Baltimore. It appeared that he plunged through the roof, leaving a gaping hole. Authorities ruled that Rivera likely committed suicide, but his family disagreed. According to his wife, Rivera rushed out of their home on the night of his disappearance. The case includes other strange details, including malfunctioning security cameras, mysterious notes, and a connection to the Free Masons.

events.title: Sandro Botticelli Dies
events.description: Sandro Botticelli's "The Birth of Venus," painted around 1485.

events.title: The New York Stock Exchange Is Created
events.description: Twenty-four stockbrokers and merchants gather on Wall Street in New York City and lay the foundation for the New York Stock Exchange. They signed the "Buttonwood Agreement" — allegedly under a buttonwood tree — which created the United States' first stock exchange. In 1817, this was codified into the New York Stock and Exchange Board.

events.title: The First Kentucky Derby Takes Place
events.description: The inaugural Kentucky Derby takes place in Louisville, Kentucky. Fifteen horses ran the race in front of a crowd of 10,000 people with a horse named Aristides winning the first competition. The famous horse race has grown in popularity since then, and has recently drawn more than 150,000 attendees.

events.title: Brown V. Board Of Education Deems Segregation Unconstitutional
events.description: Linda Brown, one of the children at the center of Brown v. Board of Education, walks past the segregated Sumner Elementary School in Topeka, Kansas, in 1953.

events.title: Alissa Turney Disappears
events.description: Alissa Turney disappears in Phoenix, Arizona. In 2001, Turney was a junior in high school and lived with her stepfather, Michael, and her sister. On the day of her disappearance, Turney told her boyfriend that Michael was picking her up early from school. She was never seen again.

events.title: Napoleon Proclaims Himself Emperor
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte declares that France is an empire and that he is its emperor. Just 34 years old, the bold military commander had risen to power in the aftermath of the French Revolution and quickly set about strengthening his position both at home and abroad. In 1799, he engineered a coup and officially took power in France and later codified his status as emperor at his December 1804 coronation. As emperor, he led his armies into nearly every corner of Europe, from Spain to Russia, before finally being defeated by a British-led coalition army at the Battle of Waterloo in present-day Belgium in 1815.

events.title: Pope John Paul II Is Born
events.description: Pope John Paul II in 1991.

events.title: The Bath School Massacre Leaves 45 Dead
events.description: The front of the school in the aftermath of the bombing.

events.title: Mount St. Helens Erupts
events.description: The eruption of Mount St. Helens in 1980.

events.title: Grunge Legend Chris Cornell dies
events.description: Grunge legend Chris Cornell dies from suicide in his Detroit hotel room. As the lead singer of Soundgarden and Audioslave, Cornell made his mark on the grunge scene. On the night of his death, Cornell spoke to his wife on the phone and was reportedly slurring his words heavily. His wife was concerned, and she asked for others to check on him. By the time they did, it was already too late. Even today, his death is surrounded in controversy: Was it really suicide? Was anyone involved?

events.title: Anne Boleyn Is Beheaded
events.description: Anne Boleyn is executed at the Tower of London. Though she had risen to power through her marriage to King Henry VIII, Anne and Henry failed to produce a male heir. The king, desperate for a son, charged her with adultery and witchcraft and had her beheaded.

events.title: Ringling Brothers Circus Opens
events.description: A Ringling Brothers Circus poster from 1899.

events.title: Oscar Wilde Is Released From Prison
events.description: Oscar Wilde is released from Reading Gaol prison in Berkshire, England. Two years earlier, Wilde had been found guilty of "gross indecency" and sodomy, then sentenced to hard labor. His time in prison inspired him to write The Ballad of Reading Gaol, but Wilde never recovered and died in 1900 at the age of just 46.

events.title: Pol Pot Is Born
events.description: Millions of people died in Cambodia as Pol Pot tried to make it into an agrarian utopia.

events.title: Lawrence Of Arabia Dies
events.description: Thomas Edward Lawrence, best known as "Lawrence of Arabia" dies at the age of 46 in Dorset, England, following a motorcycle accident. An archaeologist, soldier, and author, Lawrence wrote extensively about his time in the Middle East, where he helped lead the Arab Revolt as well as the Sinai and Palestine Campaign against the Ottoman Empire during World War I. His life — and his book Seven Pillars of Wisdom — inspired the 1962 film Lawrence of Arabia.

events.title: Diane Downs Attempts to Murder Her Three Children
events.description: Downs FamilyDiane Downs and her three children.

events.title: Vasco da Gama Arrives In India
events.description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama arrives in India. The first European to reach India by sea, he had set sail from Lisbon on July 8, 1497. His initial voyage to India took him through the Cape of Good Hope, which became the first link between Europe and Asia by sea and kickstarted a new wave of global interaction. Unfortunately, da Gama made a poor impression on native Indians, and his return voyage during monsoon season resulted in the deaths of two thirds of his crew.

events.title: Christopher Columbus Dies
events.description: Christopher Columbus was plagued by a variety of maladies over the last 14 years of his life.

events.title: Toussaint L'Ouverture Is Born
events.description: Toussaint L'Ouverture as depicted in 1802.

events.title: Homestead Act Is Signed Into Law
events.description: Abraham Lincoln signs the Homestead Act into law, providing over a million families with land grants in the American West.

events.title: Levi Strauss Patents Blue Jeans
events.description: Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis are given a patent for blue jeans. Strauss, a successful businessman who sold clothing, fabric, and dried goods, teamed up with Davis, a tailor, to make the pants. Davis had come up with the idea for pants secured with metal rivets and Strauss agreed to fund it. Levi Strauss jeans were primarily created for sale to miners during the California Gold Rush. Today, Levi Strauss is worth an estimated $6.6 billion and is the largest maker of denim jeans in the world.

events.title: Cuba Gains Its Independence From The United States
events.description: Cuba gains its independence from the United States. In 1898, the USS Maine sunk in Havana's harbor, sparking the Spanish-American War. The United States was victorious and received control over Cuba as part of the peace treaty. The United States occupied Cuba until the island nation created a new constitution allowing for extensive American interference in Cuban government and politics. After the adoption of this constitution, the United States withdrew from Cuba and it became an independent nation.

events.title: Ernest Shackleton Reaches The Stromness Whaling Station
events.description: Ernest Shackleton and two of his shipmates reach the Stromness whaling station on South Georgia Island almost seven months after they were forced to abandon their ship, Endurance, when it became hopelessly trapped in ice.

events.title: Israel Kamakawiwo'ole Is Born
events.description: A monument to Israel Kamakawiwo'ole.

events.title: Gilda Radner Dies Of Cancer
events.description: Original Saturday Night Live cast member Gilda Radner died from complications related to her ovarian cancer. She had been diagnosed with the disease in 1986 after nearly a year of misdiagnoses. Today, she is remembered not only for her comedic talents, but for the efforts done in her name to increase ovarian cancer awareness and early screening after her death.

events.title: Hernando de Soto Dies
events.description: Hernando de Soto dies at the age of 41 along the banks of the present-day Mississippi River after suffering from a high fever. De Soto, a Spanish explorer and conquistador, participated in the conquests of civilizations in Central America and Peru. Leading trailblazing expeditions into what's now the United States, de Soto trekked through present-day Florida, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, and Arkansas. He's perhaps best known for "discovering" the Mississippi River.

events.title: Ona Judge Escapes From George Washington
events.description: Ona Judge, an enslaved woman owned by George Washington, escapes. Born at Washington's Mount Vernon plantation, Judge had spent all her life enslaved but had a taste of freedom while accompanying the president to Philadelphia. She eventually fled and, despite efforts by the Washington family to recapture her up until George's death in 1799, Judge remained free all her life. She was interviewed for the abolitionist newspaper The Liberator 50 years after her escape and detailed the incredible story of her journey to freedom.

events.title: Mary Anning Is Born
events.description: Pioneering paleontologist and fossil collector Mary Anning is born in Lyme Regis, United Kingdom.

events.title: The American Red Cross Is Founded
events.description: Clara Barton, the founder of the American Red Cross.

events.title: Nathan Leopold And Richard Loeb Murder Bobby Franks To Create The "Perfect Crime"
events.description: Nathan Leopold and Richard Loeb, two college students in Chicago, murder 14-year-old Bobby Franks in an attempt to commit the perfect crime. The duo would later be sentenced to life in prison in what what was considered the trial of the decade.

events.title: Charles Lindbergh Completes His Transatlantic Flight
events.description: Charles Lindbergh posts next to the Spirit of St. Louis, the plane in which he completed his historic journey.

events.title: Jeffrey Dahmer Is Born
events.description: Yearbook photo of Jeffrey Dahmer in his fourth year of high school.

events.title: The War Of The Roses Begins
events.description: Lithograph depicting the Battle of Barnet, a pivotal event in the War of the Roses.

events.title: The First Major Wagon Train Goes West On The Oregon Trail
events.description: The first major wagon train heads to Oregon. Though pioneers had trickled west before, the party that left from Elm Grove, Missouri, consisted of 1,000 men, women, and children, 100 wagons, and 5,000 oxen and cattle.

events.title: Congressman Preston Brooks Beats Senator Charles Sumner With A Cane
events.description: A depiction of the caning of Charles Sumner from 1856.

events.title: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle Is Born
events.description: Sir Arthur Ignatius Conan Doyle is born in Edinburgh, Scotland. Doyle later became famous for his iconic character, Sherlock Holmes, a cunning detective who uses his strong powers of observation to solve crimes. However, Doyle long thought that his Holmes stories unfairly overshadowed his more serious historical fiction. Outside of writing fiction, Doyle was a medical doctor and volunteered as a military doctor in the Second Boer War.

events.title: The Pact Of Steel Is Signed
events.description: The Pact of Steel is signed between Italy and Germany, forming the Axis powers and solidifying their military alliance to fight against France and Britain.

events.title: History's Most Powerful Earthquake Hits Chile
events.description: Chilean houses sit in a crumpled heap following the Valdivia earthquake.

events.title: Chandra Levy's Remains Are Found
events.description: Roughly a year after she vanished, the remains of 24-year-old federal intern Chandra Levy are discovered in a Washington, D.C. park. Her disappearance triggered a media frenzy when it came out that Levy was romantically involved with married Congressman Gary Condit, but another man was later convicted of the crime in 2010.

events.title: Captain Kidd Is Executed
events.description: Captain William Kidd is executed by hanging in London at age 56 after being found guilty of piracy and murder. Though Kidd had spent much of his career defending ships from pirates, he was later accused of becoming a pirate himself. At trial, Kidd was found guilty on all counts — but, to this day, some historians think his so-called crimes were overstated and that he deserves a pardon.

events.title: Blanche Monnier Is Discovered In Her Family's Attic
events.description: Blanche Monnier is discovered in her family's attic in Poitiers, France. Known as a beauty, Monnier was sought after by several suiters in the late 1800s. After Monnier told her mother that she wanted to marry a lawyer of low social status, her mother locked her in the attic to prevent the relationship from blossoming. Monnier would spend 25 years in that attic, emaciated and forced to live in her own filth. An anonymous letter to the police revealed Monnier's confinement, and she was soon rescued.

events.title: The Axeman Of New Orleans Strikes For The First Time
events.description: The Axeman of New Orleans strikes for the first time, killing Joseph Maggio and his wife, Catherine, in their home. The attacks would continue for another year and strike fear in the residents of New Orleans.

events.title: Bonnie And Clyde Are Killed
events.description: Embracing their notoriety, Bonnie and Clyde posed for this photo and then left the camera at a crime scene.

events.title: A Tsunami Hits Hawaii
events.description: USGSSurvivors of the tsunami look out at the devastation it caused.

events.title: Peter Sutcliffe Is Convicted Of The "Yorkshire Ripper" Murders
events.description: Peter Sutcliffe is convicted of murdering 13 women, earning a life sentence for each victim. Known as the "Yorkshire Ripper," Sutcliffe terrorized England throughout his blood-soaked reign between 1975 and 1980. A man on a self-proclaimed mission from God to kill sex workers, Sutcliffe not only murdered 13 victims, but also attempted to kill seven others. Along the way, police narrowly missed catching him nearly a dozen times while his own wife Sonia reportedly knew nothing of his vicious deeds.

events.title: Francys Arsentiev, The First Woman To Reach Mount Everest's Summit Without An Oxygen Mask, Dies
events.description: Francys Arsentiev becomes the first woman to reach Mount Everest's summit without an oxygen mask. Not long after achieving this feat, Arsentiev died while descending the mountain. The media would refer to her body as the "sleeping beauty" marker, largely in part of its waxy look. Years later, a fellow mountain climber and friend travelled to her body, providing her with a proper mountain burial and keeping her far away from where the cameras could easily find her.

events.title: Gabriel Fernandez Is Murdered By His Parents
events.description: Gabriel Fernandez is murdered by his parents in Los Angeles, California. After teachers noticed a multitude of injuries on the eight-year-old, they made repeated calls to social services. Fernandez often arrived at school with bruises, wounds from a BB gun, and cuts. Unfortunately, help would not come in time to save Fernandez.

events.title: Nicolaus Copernicus Dies
events.description: Nicolaus Copernicus dies in present-day Frombork, Poland, at the age of 70. The first modern European scientist to correctly propose that the Earth revolved around the Sun, the Polish astronomer also hypothesized that the Earth turns once daily on its own axis. His work Six Books Concerning the Revolutions of the Heavenly Orbs came out the year of his death, perhaps sparing him the wrath of the Catholic Church due to his "heretical" ideas.

events.title: Queen Victoria Is Born
events.description: A lithograph of Queen Victoria made in 1840, a few years after she became queen.

events.title: The Brooklyn Bridge Opens
events.description: The Brooklyn Bridge opens to great fanfare, connecting Brooklyn and Manhattan across the East River. The longest suspension bridge of its day, it took 14 years to complete. Its opening ceremony attracted thousands of New Yorkers as well as President Chester A. Arthur. A National Historic Landmark, the Brooklyn Bridge stands as a widely celebrated achievement of engineering nearly 150 years after its opening.

events.title: Josef Mengele Arrives At Auschwitz
events.description: Josef Mengele, center, at Auschwitz in 1944.

events.title: The English Restoration Begins
events.description: The English Restoration commences with the triumphant return of King Charles II from exile. Charles' father, Charles I, had been beheaded by Oliver Cromwell on January 30, 1649. But after Cromwell's death in 1658, Charles II was invited back to England, restoring the monarchy to power.

events.title: The U.S. Constitutional Convention Gets Underway
events.description: Some historians believe that if the delegates knew they were to draft an entirely new document and not simply amend the Articles of Confederation, that many of them wouldn't have shown up.

events.title: Oscar Wilde Is Sent To Prison For Sodomy
events.description: Oscar Wilde in 1889.

events.title: Marcel Petiot Is Executed
events.description: French serial killer Marcel Petiot is executed by guillotine in Paris, France. During World War II, Petiot, a doctor, offered to help Jewish refugees — but killed them instead and stole their valuables. He was finally caught after neighbors complained of a terrible smell coming from his house.

events.title: Etan Patz Is Kidnapped
events.description: Etan Patz at the age of six.

events.title: The Crash Of American Airlines Flight 191
events.description: Due to an issue with its left-wing engine, American Airlines Flight 191 spiraled during takeoff and fell to the ground in an explosion less than a mile from the runway. 273 people — every passenger and crew member on board — died as a result.

events.title: 'Hands Across America' Takes Place
events.description: Hands Across America, a charity event to fight poverty and homelessness in the United States, takes place when some five million people join hands and form a line — with some gaps — from the East Coast to the West Coast.

events.title: The Pequot Massacres Begin
events.description: English colonists slaughter the Pequots and destroy their fort near Stonington, Connecticut on May 26, 1637.

events.title: Nicholas II Is Crowned Czar
events.description: Nicholas II and his family, all of whom were eventually executed after the Russian Revolution.

events.title: Dracula Is Published
events.description: Bram Stroker's vampire novel Dracula goes on sale in London.

events.title: John Wayne Is Born
events.description: John Wayne with Jimmy Stewart in The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance (1962).

events.title: The Evacuation Of Dunkirk Begins
events.description: During World War II, the British launch the biggest evacuation in military history, extracting 338,000 soldiers from Dunkirk and across the English channel.

events.title: Mary Bell Is Born
events.description: Soon to be known as England's infamous ten-year-old murderer, Mary Bell is born in Corbridge, England. Unwanted and abused by her mother, Bell endured years of trauma before killing two young boys in Scotswood in 1968. She was given an indefinite sentence and released in 1980 at the age of 23.

events.title: Bassist Kristen Pfaff Is Born
events.description: Kristen Pfaff, best known as the bassist for the 1990s grunge band Hole, was born in Buffalo, New York. Pfaff went on to join the underground music scene in Minneapolis, starting the group Janitor Joe in 1991. In 1993, Pfaff joined Hole for their record Live Through This. Tragically, Pfaff would die at the age of 27 in 1994 of a drug overdose.

events.title: Broaddus Family Receives Their First Letter From The Watcher
events.description: The Broaddus Family receives their first letter from The Watcher at their 657 Boulevard home in Westfield, New Jersey. Before the family could move into their new home, they started receiving ominous letters from someone named "The Watcher." The letters contained disturbing comments about the children in the family.

events.title: St. Petersburg Is Founded
events.description: The city of St. Petersburg is established by Peter the Great. For over 200 years, from 1712 to 1918, it served as the capital of Russia. Though Bolsheviks made Moscow the new capital in 1918 following the Russian Revolution, St. Petersburg remains the second-largest city in Russia today.

events.title: "Wild Bill" Hickok Is Born
events.description: One of the few known photos of "Wild Bill" Hickok to survive to this day.

events.title: The Golden Gate Bridge Opens
events.description: Library of CongresThe Golden Gate Bridge while under construction in 1934.

events.title: The German Battleship Bismarck Sinks
events.description: The British navy sinks the German battleship Bismarck off the coast of France. The pride of the German fleet, the 823-foot vessel set out to intercept the British supply line. Instead, the British engaged the behemoth and sunk it after a short battle — killing almost its entire 2,221-man crew.

events.title: The Centralia Mine Fire Begins
events.description: Cole Young/FlickrSmoke rises from the road in Centralia, Pennsylvania.

events.title: Christopher Reeve Becomes Paralyzed
events.description: Actor Christopher Reeve, most famous for his role as Superman in the 1970s Superman film series, is paralyzed following an equestrian accident in Virginia.

events.title: The Indian Removal Act Is Signed Into Law
events.description: Following a vote by Congress, President Andrew Jackson signs the Indian Removal Act. The act took 25 million acres of land in Georgia, Florida, North Carolina, Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, and Arkansas from Native Americans to give to white settlers. Thus, the act also caused the forced relocation of as many as 60,000 Native Americans from their lands to present-day Oklahoma in a tragic episode that would become known as the Trail of Tears.

events.title: Volkswagen Is Founded
events.description: Nuremberg Museum of Industrial CultureA 1930s model of what would become the Volkswagen Beetle.

events.title: Amnesty International Is Founded
events.description: Amnesty International is founded by Peter Benenson, a British lawyer. The goal of the organization was to provide resources to people who had been imprisoned, tortured, or otherwise persecuted for their non-violent political, religious, or social beliefs and activities. Today, Amnesty International exposes human rights abuses around the world, lobbies governments, and provides education and training. The work of the organization has freed thousands from unjust imprisonment, led to the adoption of anti-torture legislation, and has inspired several countries to abolish the death penalty.

events.title: The Palestine Liberation Organization Is Founded
events.description: The Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) is founded. Organized by Palestinians displaced by the establishment of Israel in 1948, it sought both to provide a representative body for Palestinians and to oppose the state of Israel. Though the PLO initially engaged in extremism and terrorism, it's recognized today by the Arab League as the representative of the Palestinian people and is considered a "non-member observer state" by the United Nations.

events.title: Phil Hartman Is Murdered
events.description: Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic/Getty ImagesPhil and Brynn Hartman in 1998.

events.title: Constantinople Falls To The Ottoman Empire
events.description: The city of Constantinople falls to Sultan Mehmed II of the Ottoman Empire following a 55-day siege. The fall of the city marked the end of the Byzantine — and thus the Roman — Empire and opened up Europe to Ottoman expansion. It also heralded the beginning of the Renaissance, as many Greeks fled the city, bringing their knowledge and traditions to Italy.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Is Born
events.description: John F. Kennedy in the Oval Office in October 1962.

events.title: Edmund Hillary And Tenzing Norgay Summit Mount Everest
events.description: Keystone-France/Gamma-Keystone via Getty ImagesEdmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay after summiting Mount Everest.

events.title: Charles Harrelson Murders Judge John H. Wood Jr.
events.description: Mugshot of Charles Harrelson taken in 1960.

events.title: Jeff Buckley Dies
events.description: Musician Jeff Buckley, famous for his cover of the song "Hallelujah," drowns in the Mississippi River in Memphis, Tennessee at the age of just 30. While on the road, Buckley and one of his roadies stopped at the river. Buckley's roadie nervously watched as the singer waded into the water. After taking his eyes away from Buckley for only a minute, the roadie realized that Buckley had vanished. A month afterward, a riverboat passenger spotted his body and an autopsy later confirmed he had drowned.

events.title: Joan Of Arc Is Burned At The Stake
events.description: Convicted of heresy, Joan of Arc was made to stare at a crucifix as she was burned to death.

events.title: Christopher Marlowe Is Killed
events.description: A 16th-century portrait of a young man though to be Christopher Marlowe.

events.title: The First Balkan War Ends
events.description: The First Balkan War ends with the signing of a peace treaty in London. The conflict, which pitted the Balkan League countries of Bulgaria, Serbia, Greece, and Montenegro against the Ottoman Empire, had endured for seven months. It ended with a victory for the Balkan League, and the Ottoman Empire's loss of almost all its European territory.

events.title: Natalee Holloway Disappears
events.description: Mark Wilson/Getty ImagesNatalee Holloway's mother stands in front of a picture of her daughter, who has been missing since 2005.

events.title: The Infamous "Slender Man Stabbing"
events.description: 12-year-olds Morgan Geyser and Anissa Weier lure their friend Payton Leutner into the woods as a sacrifice for the Slender Man, an internet horror figure who had grown in popularity thanks to a Photoshop contest on the Something Awful forum.

events.title: Walt Whitman Is Born
events.description: Walt Whitman is born in West Hills, New York. A poet, essayist, and journalist, Whitman's "free verse" poetry revolutionized the art form. He's perhaps best known for his collection Leaves of Grass and for the poem, O Captain! My Captain!, inspired by the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.

events.title: Big Ben Rings For The First Time
events.description: Big Ben rings for the first time in London. The clock, perched atop the 320-foot Elizabeth Tower, was first proposed in 1834 after a fire destroyed much of the Palace of Westminster. The clock has stood proudly over London ever since, surviving the bombing of London during World War II, but has been largely silent since 2017 for much-needed renovations.

events.title: The Johnstown Flood Kills 2,000 People
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesThe remains of a house on Main and Union Streets that had a tree sent straight through it by the Johnstown Flood.

events.title: The RMS Titanic Leaves Its Dry Dock
events.description: Roughly a year before its catastrophic sinking, the RMS Titanic leaves its dry dock at the Harland and Wolff shipyard in Belfast, Ireland.

events.title: The Tulsa Race Massacre Begins
events.description: Smoke rises over "Black Wall Street" during the Tulsa Race Massacre.

events.title: Adolf Eichmann Is Hanged
events.description: Adolf Eichmann in 1942.

events.title: Benjamin Netanyahu Is Elected Prime Minister Of Israel
events.description: Benjamin Netanyahu is elected prime minister of Israel. The country's longest-serving prime minister, Netanyahu lost his seat in 1999 but returned to the prime ministership in 2009. He remained in power until 2021, when the COVID-19 pandemic, Israel's economic woes, and criminal charges against him led to the ascension of his successor, Naftali Bennett.

events.title: The Identity Of 'Deep Throat' Is Revealed
events.description: Deep Throat, a high-ranking source who leaked information about Watergate to Washington Post reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein, is revealed to be Mark Felt. In the 1970s, Felt was second-in-command at the F.B.I.

events.title: Millvina Dean, The Last Survivor Of The Titanic, Dies
events.description: Millvina Dean, the last living survivor of the Titanic disaster dies at 97 years old. Dean was only two months old when her family boarded the ill-fated ship.

events.title: The "Slender Man" Stabbing Nearly Kills Payton Leutner
events.description: Two 12-year-old girls, Anissa Weier and Morgan Geyser, lure their friend Payton Leutner into the woods in Waukesha, Wisconsin, and stab her 19 times. Allegedly inspired by the online "Slender Man" myth, Weier and Geyser hoped that their actions would prove their dedication to the fictional character. However, Leutner survived the so-called Slender Man stabbing, while Weier and Geyser were both committed to mental health institutions.

events.title: Anne Boleyn Is Crowned Queen Of England
events.description: Anne Boleyn is crowned queen of England. Her coronation came a decade after she first met King Henry VIII, who left his first wife, Catherine of Aragon, to be with her. But Anne's queenship was short-lived as Henry had her executed in 1536 after they were unable to produce a male heir.

events.title: Las Vegas Becomes A City
events.description: Las Vegas is declared a city and elects its first mayor.

events.title: Terra Nova Expedition Begins
events.description: The ill-fated Terra Nova Expedition to Antarctica begins.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe Is Born
events.description: Marilyn Monroe in her iconic white dress from The Seven Year Itch (1955).

events.title: Ronald Hunkeler, Inspiration For "The Exorcist," Is Born
events.description: Ronald Hunkeler, the boy who inspired the movie "The Exorcist," is born in Cottage City, Maryland. At just 14-years-old, Hunkeler began experiencing paranormal phenomena. His family reached out to religious institutions after medical services couldn't find anything wrong with him. While in St. Louis, Hunkeler underwent several exorcisms that his family reported were successful. He lived out the rest of his life as a NASA engineer and died at the age of 86. His exorcism story would inspire the blockbuster "The Exorcist."

events.title: News Of Nazi Death Camps First Becomes Public
events.description: The Liberty Brigade, a Warsaw-based underground newspaper, becomes the first outlet to publish stories about the existence of Nazi death camps. Six months earlier, the Wannsee Conference had made the extermination of European Jews an official policy of the Nazi regime, and it was now officially underway. And by the end of the war, an estimated 11 million people were killed in these camps.

events.title: Helen Keller Dies
events.description: Helen Keller in 1888 with her teacher, Anne Sullivan.

events.title: Nepalese Royal Massacre
events.description: During a party held at the royal palace, Crown Prince Dipendra of Nepal opened fire on his fellow members of the royal family. He shot nine people total and killed his mother and father - the Queen and King of Nepal - before shooting himself. Dipendra was King of Nepal for three days while in a coma before dying of his gunshot wound.

events.title: Harriet Tubman Frees 800 Enslaved People
events.description: Harriet Tubman frees 800 slaves during a raid on the Combahee River in South Carolina. Working with Union Colonel James Montgomery and 150 Black soldiers, she succeeded in ferrying hundreds of enslaved men, women, and children onto rowboats and then gunboats. Despite Tubman's participation in this raid, however, she was denied soldier's compensation.

events.title: Wallace Hartley Is Born
events.description: Wallace Hartley, the bandleader on the RMS Titanic who played as the ship sank, is born in Lancashire, England.

events.title: Albert Einstein Marries Elsa Einstein
events.description: Albert Einstein with his second wife, Elsa.

events.title: Babe Ruth Retires From Baseball
events.description: By the time he finished his 22nd and final season, Babe Ruth was easily the most celebrated baseball player to ever live.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth II Is Crowned
events.description: A coronation portrait of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip in June 1953.

events.title: Leonard Lake Is Arrested
events.description: Serial killer Leonard Lake is arrested in San Francisco, California.

events.title: The Duke Of Windsor Marries Wallis Simpson
events.description: National Media Museum/Wikimedia CommonsKing Edward VIII and Wallis Simpson in Yugoslavia in 1936.

events.title: The Zoot Suit Riots Begin
events.description: Victims of the Zoot Suit Riots, stripped and beaten in Los Angeles.

events.title: Valerie Solanas Shoots Andy Warhol
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesValerie Solanas being arrested after shooting Andy Warhol in 1968.

events.title: Lauren Spierer Disappears
events.description: FacebookLauren Spierer in an undated photograph shortly before her disappearance.

events.title: The Batavia Crashes On The Houtman Abrolhos
events.description: The Batavia, a merchant ship of the Dutch East India Company, crashed after being separated from its convoy. Although the ship's commander immediately set off to retrieve a rescue vessel, the remaining survivors were subjected to one of history's bloodiest mutinies when the de facto leader, Jeronimus Cornelisz, had more than 120 men, women, and children killed.

events.title: The First Public Demonstration Of The Hot Air Balloon Takes Place
events.description: Brothers Jacques-Étienne and Joseph-Michel Montgolfier display the first unmanned hot-air balloon before a crowd in Annonay, France. Their 500-pound balloon soared to 6,000 feet and remained aloft for 10 minutes. Other attempts quickly followed, including with animals and then humans.

events.title: Suffragist Emily Davison Dies
events.description: Hulton-Deutsch/Hulton-Deutsch Collection/Corbis via Getty ImagesEmily Davison was hit and killed by King George V's horse Anmer during the 1913 Epsom Derby.

events.title: The Tiananmen Square Massacre Unfolds In Beijing
events.description: Chip HIRES/Gamma-Rapho/Getty ImagesProtestors at Tiananmen Square.

events.title: Jodi Arias Kills Travis Alexander
events.description: Jodi Arias kills Travis Alexander in his home in Mesa, Arizona. After dating for a few months, Arias reportedly became infatuated with Alexander. The two would repeatedly fight, break up, then get back together.

events.title: Kyron Horman Disappears
events.description: Seven-year-old Kyron Horman disappears in Portland, Oregon. The second-grader arrived at school that morning with his stepmother, Terri Moulton Horman, who photographed him in front of the board he'd made for his science fair. But Kyron never returned home that afternoon and has been missing ever since.

events.title: Pat Garrett Is Born
events.description: Pat Garrett in 1907, the year before he was shot and killed by an unknown assassin.

events.title: Constantinople Burns
events.description: A vast swathe of the Ottoman city of Constantinople burns to the ground. The fire, caused by a girl who accidentally dropped a hot piece of charcoal out the window, ultimately killed 900 people and destroyed 3,000 homes.

events.title: The Lake Bodom Murders Take Place In Finland
events.description: The aftermath of the Lake Bodom murders.

events.title: Robert F. Kennedy Is Shot
events.description: Everett Collection HistoricalRobert Kennedy was shot three times, twice in the upper back and once in the head. Five other people were also struck by bullets.

events.title: The First Report On AIDS Is Published
events.description: The CDC publishes an article about Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia (PCP), a rare lung condition that was affecting five homosexual men in Los Angeles. Following the publication, other medical professionals contacted the organization about similar cases among homosexual men. The disease was called Gay-Related Immune Deficiency (GRID) before its name was changed to Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

events.title: Serial Killer Kelly Cochran Is Born
events.description: Kelly Cochran is born in Merrillville, Indiana. Cochran married her high school sweetheart immediately after graduation, promising that the two would never cheat on one another. If they did, someone would have to pay for it with their life.

events.title: "Tank Man" Is Photographed At Tiananmen Square
events.description: "Tank Man" makes his dramatic stand near Tiananmen Square.

events.title: The World's First University Museum Opens
events.description: The Ashmolean opens in Oxford, England. The world's first university museum, it featured the collection of English archaeologist Elias Ashmole, who donated his items to the school in 1677. Today, the Ashmolean Museum of Art and Archaeology displays both ancient and contemporary objects.

events.title: The YMCA Is Founded
events.description: The Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA) is founded in London by Sir George Williams. Hoping to create an alternative to brothels and taverns, the YMCA aimed to provide a place for young men to develop a healthy "body, mind, and spirit." Today, it has branches in 120 countries.

events.title: The Great Seattle Fire Devastates The City
events.description: The ruins of the Occidental Hotel following the Great Seattle Fire.

events.title: The D-Day Invasion Begins
events.description: Keystone/Getty ImagesU.S. troops storm the beaches of Normandy during D-Day in June 1944. The ambitious amphibious invasion of Nazi-occupied France led by the Allies helped turn the tide of World War II.

events.title: Robert F. Kennedy Dies
events.description: Robert F. Kennedy was fatally shot at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles, California.

events.title: Oil Tycoon J. Paul Getty Dies
events.description: 83-year-old oil tycoon J. Paul Getty dies of heart failure in Sutton Place.

events.title: An Earthquake Destroys Port Royal, Jamaica
events.description: A 7.5-magnitude earthquake strikes Port Royal, Jamaica. The quake caused the town to sink into its loose soil foundation and the subsequent tsunami submerged Port Royal in 40 feet of water. Some 2,000 people died immediately, with another 3,000 later succumbing to injury and disease.

events.title: Mahatma Gandhi Performs His First Act Of Civil Disobedience
events.description: Mohandas K. Gandhi is forcibly removed from a whites-only train car in Pietermaritzburg, South Africa. The incident inspired him to spend his life fighting for justice. "The hardship to which I was subjected was superficial – only a symptom of the deep disease of color prejudice," he wrote. "I should try, if possible, to root out the disease and suffer hardships in the process."

events.title: Hudson Stuck Summits Denali
events.description: Hudson Stuck circa 1914.

events.title: The Vatican Becomes A Sovereign State
events.description: The Vatican becomes a sovereign state. After Italy became a unified state, the Vatican shared Rome with the new government and began to feel politically threatened. In order to maintain the Vatican's influence and sovereignty, Pope Pius XI signed the Lateran Treaty with Benito Mussolini and secured the Vatican's independence. Today, the Vatican is the smallest country in the world (in both geographical size and population). It also has the smallest army in the world, with only 110 Swiss Guards to protect the pope and the country.

events.title: Jean Harlow Dies
events.description: Known as the "Blonde Bombshell," Jean Harlow was one of the most popular movie stars of the 1930s.

events.title: The Prophet Muhammad Dies
events.description: Prophet Muhammad dies in Medina, Saudi Arabia, at the age of 62. The founder of Islam and the man behind the religion's holy text, the Qurʾān, Muhammad is regarded by Muslims as God's final prophet. Today, almost 2 billion Muslims worldwide follow the path set forth by Muhammad.

events.title: Frank Lloyd Wright Is Born
events.description: Americasroof/Wikimedia CommonsA Frank Lloyd Wright house in Wisconsin.

events.title: Apache Chief Cochise Dies
events.description: Cochise dies on the Chiricahua Apache Reservation in present-day Arizona. An Apache chief, Cochise spent most of his life fighting the U.S. Army after he and others were accused of kidnapping a ranch hand's young son. After a decade of resistance, he negotiated a treaty and retired to a reservation.

events.title: George Mallory Is Seen Alive For The Last Time
events.description: British explorer George Mallory is seen alive for the last time as he and his climbing partner, Sandy Irvine, attempt to summit Mount Everest. Mallory's body was found in 1999; Irving's partial remains were discovered in 2024.

events.title: The "Napalm Girl" Photo Is Taken
events.description: AP/Nick UtThe so-called "Napalm Girl" photographed during the Vietnam War.

events.title: Anthony Wikimedia CommonsAnthony Bourdain was given a Peabody Award in 2013 for "expanding our palates and horizons in equal measure."Dies
events.description: Anthony Bourdain dies by suicide at a hotel in Kaysersberg-Vignoble, France, at the age of 61. A chef who became famous through his writing on the culinary "underworld," Bourdain also hosted the popular travel show Parts Unknown. All the while, he struggled with mental health issues that ultimately led to his tragic end.

events.title: The Roman Emperor Nero Dies
events.description: A bust of Nero, one of the most widely disparaged emperors in the history of Rome.

events.title: Jacques Cartier Sails Into The St. Lawrence River
events.description: Jacques Cartier sails into the St. Lawrence River for the first time. A French navigator, Cartier had been tasked by King Francis I of France to seek gold and spices in present-day Canada and to find a potential route to Asia. After his first voyage to the river, he erroneously believed that he had done so.

events.title: Handcart Pioneers Head To Salt Lake City
events.description: Some 500 Mormon pioneers embark on a 1,000-mile journey to Salt Lake City, Utah, from Iowa City, Iowa, carrying their belongings in handcarts. They were answering the call of Mormon leader Brigham Young, who had established Salt Lake City as the center of Mormonism. He declared: "Let them come on foot with handcarts or wheelbarrows; let them gird up their loins and walk through and nothing shall hinder or stay them."

events.title: The Horse Secretariat Wins The Triple Crown
events.description: Secretariat wins the Belmont Stakes — and, in the process, the Triple Crown. The three-year-old horse, who ran the one-and-a-half-mile race in a record two minutes and 24 seconds, was the first horse since 1948 to win the Kentucky Derby, the Preakness, and the Belmont Stakes. He raced six more times after that and "retired" in November 1973.

events.title: Maureen Kelly Disappears
events.description: Skamania County Sheriff's DepartmentMaureen Kelly has been missing since 2013.

events.title: Dee Dee Blanchard Is Murdered
events.description: Dee Dee Blanchard, the mother of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, is murdered in her Springfield, Missouri home by her daughter and her boyfriend. The 48-year-old had suffered from Munchausen by proxy, a mental disorder that causes a caretaker to fake illness of their dependent for attention.

events.title: The First Victim Of The Salem Witch Trials Is Put To Death
events.description: Everett Collection Inc/Alamy Stock PhotoSalem magistrates examine Rebecca Nurse, a woman accused of being a witch by Abigail Williams.

events.title: Benjamin Franklin Flies His Famous Kite
events.description: Benjamin Franklin flies a kite in a thunderstorm to explore the connection between lightning and electricity. Franklin found that there was, indeed, a connection, when he was able to draw an electrical charge into a Leyden jar.

events.title: Amelia Dyer Is Executed
events.description: Amelia Dyer is believed to have killed hundreds of infants.

events.title: The Villisca Axe Murders Take Place
events.description: Eight people are found bludgeoned to death in Villisca, Iowa. The victims, six members of the Moore family and two of their guests, had been killed with an axe. Though police considered several suspects, the so-called Villisca Axe Murders remain unsolved to this day.

events.title: 642 Civilians Are Massacred In Oradour-Sur-Glane
events.description: Davdavlhu/Wikimedia CommonsThe ruins of Oradour-sur-Glane are preserved as a memorial today.

events.title: King Henry VIII Marries Catherine Of Aragon
events.description: Catherine of Aragon, Henry VIII's first wife.

events.title: Polish Forces Triumph At The Battle Of Hodów
events.description: A Polish force of 400 soldiers, including 100 winged hussars, defeats a Crimean Khanate army that may have numbered between 25,000 and 70,000 men at the Battle of Hodów in Poland (present-day Ukraine).

events.title: James Cook "Discovers" The Great Barrier Reef
events.description: British Captain James Cook accidentally runs his ship, the HMS Endeavour, into the Great Barrier Reef off the coast of Australia. Tasked with exploring uncharted waters by King George III, Cook and his crew nearly wrecked upon the reef and spent several weeks repairing the vessel.

events.title: Henry Hill, Inspiration For Goodfellas Is Born
events.description: Henry Hill, the inspiration for the movie Goodfellas is born in Brooklyn, New York. At just 14, Hill dropped out of school to begin working for a crime family. Hill and his associate James Burke played major roles in orchestrating the Lufthansa heist, a robbery of the JFK airport, in 1978. Police would later arrest Henry Hill on drug charges, and while in custody, Hill confessed to his crimes in order to save his skin. Hollywood would eventually immortalize Hill's story in the film Goodfellas.

events.title: A Race Car Crashes Into Spectators At Le Mans
events.description: AFP via Getty ImagesPierre Levegh, and his car, in the aftermath of the Le Mans disaster.

events.title: Frank Morris, Clarence Anglin, And John Anglin Escape Alcatraz
events.description: Inmates Frank Morris, Clarence Anglin, and John Anglin escape from Alcatraz in the middle of the night. The trio devised a plan to escape via a ventilator in the prison's roof. Authorities believe they made it to San Francisco Bay, but no traces of them have ever been found.

events.title: Thich Quang Duc Burns Himself Alive
events.description: Vietnamese Buddhist monk Thich Quang Duc burns himself alive in Saigon. About a month earlier, South Vietnamese soldiers had opened fire on people displaying a Buddhist flag in violation of the Catholic government's policies. They killed nine, and so Duc took his own life in protest.

events.title: George Wallace Blocks The Entrance To The University Of Alabama
events.description: George Wallace, governor of Alabama, blocks the entrance to the University of Alabama in protest of two African American students attempting to enter. The event concludes with President JFK sending the National Guard to force Wallace to stand down.

events.title: Timothy McVeigh Is Executed
events.description: Timothy McVeigh, the domestic terrorist behind the Oklahoma City bombing, is executed at the age of 33.

events.title: Karl Von Drais Takes The World's First Bicycle Ride
events.description: Karl von Drais takes a ride on his invented "Laufmaschine" (running machine) or "dandy horse," thought to be the world's first bicycle. Little is known about von Drais or how he came up with his invention. But it was certainly a hit: today, there are over 1 billion bicycles in the world.

events.title: The Philippines Declares Independence
events.description: Filipino rebels led by Emilio Aguinaldo declare their independence from Spain during the Spanish-American war. Though they threw off 300 years of Spanish rule, their victory was short-lived. The United States annexed the Philippines after the conflict ended and controlled the islands until 1946.

events.title: Anne Frank Is Born
events.description: Anne Frank in 1940, two years before she began writing her famous diary.

events.title: Nicole Brown Simpson And Ron Goldman Are Murdered
events.description: The LIFE Picture Collection/Getty ImagesA policeman stands guard in front of Nicole Brown Simpson's house, where she and her friend Ron Goldman were killed.

events.title: Gunman Omar Mateen Attacks The Pulse Nightclub
events.description: Omar Mateen kills 49 people at Pulse in Orlando, Florida. Pulse, a gay nightclub, was hosting Latin Night when Mateen arrived at around 2 a.m. and suddenly opened fire. The American-born Mateen then called 911 and pledged allegiance to ISIS before police fatally shot him in a gun battle around 5 a.m.

events.title: Alexander The Great Dies
events.description: The death of Alexander the Great, based on the painting by German artist Karl Theodor von Piloty.

events.title: The Peasants' Revolt Enters London
events.description: A depiction of King Richard II meeting with English peasants during the Peasants' Revolt.

events.title: Miyamoto Mushashi Dies
events.description: Miyamoto Mushashi, famous Japanese swordsman and poet, dies in Higo Province.

events.title: The U.S. Supreme Court Establishes "Miranda Rights"
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court hands down its decision on Miranda v. Arizona, establishing that criminal suspects must be informed of their rights before interrogation. The decision came from the 1963 arrest of Ernesto Miranda, who gave a confession — which he later recanted — without knowing about his right to remain silent.

events.title: Three Die In The Oklahoma Girl Scout Murders
events.description: FacebookMichelle Guse, Lori Farmer, and Doris Milner.

events.title: Survivors Of The Mutiny Aboard The HMS Bounty Reach Timor
events.description: Seven weeks after his crew on the HMS Bounty mutinied, Captain William Bligh and 18 of his supporters make it to the island of Timor. Cast adrift in a small boat with water, bread, pork, rum, and wine by the mutineers, Bligh and the others miraculously survived the 3,600-mile journey to land.

events.title: Harriet Beecher Stowe Is Born
events.description: Harriet Beecher Stowe in 1852.

events.title: Dennis Martin Disappears
