events.description: Family Photo/Knoxville News Sentinel ArchiveDennis Martin disappeared shortly before his 7th birthday.

events.title: Hezbollah Hijacks TWA Flight 847
events.description: Hezbollah terrorists hijack TWA Flight 847 en route a from Athens to Rome. Rerouting the plane to Beirut, Lebanon, they demanded to know which passengers had "Jewish names," information that one fearless flight attendant named Uli Derickson refused to disclose. Some hostages were quickly released, but one was killed and others were held until June 30th.

events.title: Gangster Tony Spilotro Is Murdered
events.description: Las Vegas-based gangster Tony Spilotro goes missing with his brother in Chicago. On June 22, police found their bodies buried in a cornfield.

events.title: Canada And Denmark Agree To Share Hans Island
events.description: After decades of disputing over Hans Island, a small uninhabitable island about equidistant from Canada and Greenland, Denmark and Canada agree to share the territory, with Denmark getting 60 percent of the island, and Canada 40 percent.

events.title: King John Signs The Magna Carta
events.description: King John of England signs the Articles of the Barons, later called the Magna Carta. The document established certain rights for barons and put limits on the king's power. Though it changed little in the short term, the document established important ideas like the right to petition and due process that still exist in various forms around the world to this day.

events.title: Lisa Gherardini Is Born
events.description: Lisa Gherardini, the woman who posed for Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, is born in Florence, Italy.

events.title: Josiah Henson Is Born
events.description: Uncle Tom's Cabin Historic SiteJosiah Henson escaped slavery and later inspired Harriet Beecher Stowe.

events.title: The 'Pig War' Begins
events.description: An American farmer shoots a pig owned by a British man on San Juan Island, then a contested territory in present-day Washington state, leading to an ultimately bloodless conflict called the Pig War.

events.title: Marie Laveau Dies In New Orleans
events.description: Marie Laveau, the "Voodoo Queen" of New Orleans, dies at the age of 79. Today, her admirers leave offerings at her tomb in St. Louis Cemetery No.1 in New Orleans.

events.title: A Devastating Tsunami Strikes Japan
events.description: The 8.5-magnitude Sanriku earthquake triggers a tsunami in northern Japan. The deadly waves killed at least 22,000 people. Fishermen off the coast, however, weren't affected by the disaster and came home to find their communities in ruins.

events.title: New York Riverboat Fire Kills 1,000
events.description: A depiction of the fire that broke out on the General Slocum.

events.title: Jacob Stockdale Commits The Wife Swap Murders
events.description: Jacob Stockdale fatally shoots his mother and brother in Ohio. Years earlier, in 2008, the Stockdale family had participated in the reality show Wife Swap, where two families would "switch" wives for a short period of time. Just like on the show, the Stockdales were known to have been extremely tight-laced and focused on their faith and music. Jacob Stockdale's temporary "mother" on the show, Laurie Tonkovic, later suggested that his strict upbringing was exactly what caused him to "snap."

events.title: The Victoria Hall Theatre Disaster Kills 183 Children
events.description: Children attending a variety show at Victoria Hall in Sunderland, England, suddenly stampede toward the exits after being promised free toys. They came across a bolted, slightly ajar door, which resulted in hundreds of children being crushed under the others. In the end, 183 died and the disaster inspired emergency exits and "push bar" emergency doors.

events.title: Mollie Burkhart Dies
events.description: Mollie Burkhart, whose family was targeted during the Osage Indian Murders, dies at the age of 50 in Osage County, Oklahoma, following a long illness.

events.title: George Reeves Dies
events.description: ABC Photo Archives/ABC via Getty ImagesGeorge Reeves played Superman between 1952 and 1958.

events.title: Valentina Tereshkova Becomes The First Woman In Space
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman to go to space. An accomplished parachutist, she embarked on the historic voyage in a vessel called Vostok 6, which spent 71 hours in space and orbited Earth 48 times. Female astronauts didn't return to space until the 1980s.

events.title: Tupac Shakur Is Born
events.description: Tupac Shakur in 1991.

events.title: Hole Bassist Kristen Pfaff Dies
events.description: Kristen Pfaff, bassist in the band Hole, is found dead in the bathtub of her apartment. She died at the age of 27 of a drug overdose just two months after the suicide of her close friend, and bandmate Courtney Love's husband, Kurt Cobain. Pfaff had reportedly been in a drug recovery center earlier that year for her heroin use.

events.title: Caylee Anthony Goes Missing
events.description: Caylee Anthony, the two-year-old daughter of Casey Anthony, disappears in Orlando, Florida. Police soon became suspicious of Casey after witnesses reportedly last saw her driving off with Caylee. Additionally, Casey never reported her daughter missing. Authorities quickly arrested Casey after holes in her story became apparent.

events.title: Mumtaz Mahal Dies
events.description: A depiction of Mumtaz Mahal, whose tomb became the iconic Taj Mahal.

events.title: Anna Haining Bates And Martin Van Buren Bates Marry
events.description: Anna Haining Bates and Martin Van Buren Bates, the tallest married couple ever documented, get married in London.

events.title: The Statue Of Liberty Arrives In New York
events.description: The Statue of Liberty arrives in New York. The iconic 450,000-pound statue, a gift from France, arrived as 350 pieces packed into 200 containers. It was reassembled on Bedloe's Island in New York Harbor and officially dedicated by President Grover Cleveland on October 28, 1886.

events.title: The Kansas City Massacre
events.description: A shootout breaks out when Charles "Pretty Boy" Floyd, Vernon Miller, and Adam Richetti attempt to free Frank Nash from prison, resulting in four law enforcement officers and Nash dead.

events.title: Five Burglars Are Arrested At The Watergate Complex
events.description: Five men are arrested at the Watergate Complex in Washington, D.C. for breaking into the Democratic National Committee headquarters. The break-in proved to be just the tip of the iceberg — authorities soon found links to President Richard Nixon's reelection campaign and his White House. After a long, public investigation, Nixon resigned from office on August 8, 1974.

events.title: O.J. Simpson Leads Police On A Televised Car Chase
events.description: YouTubeO.J. Simpson's infamous white Ford Bronco during the chase.

events.title: Aaron Hernandez Murders Odin Lloyd
events.description: Odin Lloyd is shot and killed in North Attleborough, Massachusetts. Nine days later, police arrested NFL star Aaron Hernandez and charged him with Lloyd's murder. Hernandez was found guilty in April 2015 and died by suicide in prison two years later.

events.title: The War Of 1812 Begins
events.description: A depiction of the burning of Washington, D.C. during the War of 1812.

events.title: The Battle Of Waterloo Takes Place
events.description: The Battle of Waterloo, which pitted French troops led by Napoleon Bonaparte against soldiers led by Duke of Wellington of England and Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher of Prussia, takes place in present-day Belgium. During the pivotal battle, Napoleon was defeated — and subsequently exiled to the island of Saint Helena.

events.title: The "Great Whiskey Fire" Breaks Out In Dublin
events.description: A fire breaks out at Malone's malt house and a bonded storehouse on Chamber Street in Dublin, Ireland, which held approximately 5,000 barrels of whiskey. The blaze caused the burning whiskey to pour through the city's streets, where it was eagerly lapped up by locals. The so-called Dublin Whiskey Fire killed 13 people who drank too much of the burning booze.

events.title: Anastasia Romanov Is Born
events.description: World History Archive/UIG via Getty imagesAnastasia Romanov as a girl.

events.title: William Sidis Graduates From Harvard
events.description: William James Sidis, widely called the smartest man in history, graduates from Harvard. Born in 1898, William Sidis had an IQ roughly between 250 and 300. At just 18 months old, Sidis was able to read The New York Times. By the time he was six years old, he could speak several languages. Harvard University accepted Sidis' application when he was just nine years old, and he began attending classes at age 11. He graduated at 16 and began working random jobs around the country. By the time of his death at age 46, Sidis had largely lived his life in solitude.

events.title: Alan Berg Is Murdered
events.description: Alan Berg is gunned down in the driveway of his home in Denver, Colorado. An outspoken and confrontational radio host, Berg was killed by members of the white supremacist group The Order, who disliked his abrasive interview style and the fact that he was Jewish.

events.title: The First Official Baseball Game Is Played
events.description: The New York Nine play the Knickerbockers at New Jersey's Elysian Fields in the first baseball game ever officially recorded. The Mutuals won, 23-1, over the course of four innings. Baseball grew in popularity in the decades that followed, though the leagues we know today wouldn't take shape for another half-century and the first World Series would not be held until 1903.

events.title: The End Of Slavery Is Announced In Texas
events.description: A group of people attending a Juneteenth celebration in Texas in 1900.

events.title: Emperor Maximilian Of Mexico Is Executed
events.description: Emperor Maximilian of Mexico is executed by firing squad. Maximilian was an Austrian archduke who reigned as emperor of the Second Mexican Empire. While in power, Maximillian issued new laws concerning various aspects of government, including infrastructure and immigration. He also issued laws that granted all Mexicans the right to freedom of speech and created a public education system. However, growing republican forces eventually threatened Maximilian, and he was ultimately taken prisoner and sentenced to death.

events.title: King George V Changes The Royal Surname
events.description: King George V of Britain changes the royal surname from "Saxe-Coburg-Gotha" to "Windsor."

events.title: Julius And Ethel Rosenberg Are Executed
events.description: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg's trial captivated America during the early days of the Cold War.

events.title: James Gandolfini Dies
events.description: UPI/Alamy Stock PhotoWhile vacationing with his family in Rome on June 19, 2013, The Sopranos actor James Gandolfini died suddenly of a heart attack at the age of just 51.

events.title: Anton Yelchin Dies
events.description: Star Trek actor Anton Yelchin dies at the age of 27 after his SUV rolled down a hill and crushed him against a fence outside of his Los Angeles home.

events.title: Koko The Gorilla Dies
events.description: Koko.org/YouTubeKoko reading her alphabet book.

events.title: The French Royal Family Attempts To Flee
events.description: King Louis XVI of France, Queen Marie Antoinette, and their children attempt to escape Paris during the French Revolution. However, the royal family only made it as far as the town of Varennes before they were found out and sent back to the capital. The queen's hair allegedly turned white in the aftermath, a condition that's known today as "Marie Antoinette Syndrome." She was ultimately executed in October 1793, 10 months after her husband faced the same fate.

events.title: Lizzie Borden Is Found Not Guilty Of Murder
events.description: Lizzie Borden a few years before the murders of her father and stepmother.

events.title: The Boxer Rebellion Begins In China
events.description: The Boxer Rebellion, which aimed to drive foreigners out of China, begins. Led by the Society of the Righteous and Harmonious Fists, its participants were nicknamed "boxers" by Westerners who'd seen them doing boxing and other calisthenic rituals meant to make them invincible. Hundreds of foreigners and thousands of Chinese Christians were killed before an international coalition captured Beijing in August 1900.

events.title: Bugsy Siegel Is Assassinated
events.description: Gangster Bugsy Siegel is assassinated at his home in Beverley Hills, California.

events.title: Bob Woodward And 'Deep Throat' Meet
events.description: Washington Post reporter Bob Woodward and Mark Felt, a high-ranking FBI official known for decades only as "Deep Throat," meet for the first time to discuss the Watergate scandal.

events.title: Andrea Yates Drowns Her Children
events.description: Yates Family/Getty ImagesAndrea Yates with her husband and children.

events.title: Ryan Dunn Dies
events.description: Jackass star Ryan Dunn dies at the age of 34 after crashing his Porsche into a guardrail in West Goshen Township, Pennsylvania. According to police, the stunt performer had been driving at around 130 miles per hour at the time. The crash also killed his passenger, 30-year-old Zachary Hartwell.

events.title: Edward III Of England Dies
events.description: King Edward III dies in England. In power for 50 years, Edward oversaw historical events like the beginning of the Hundred Years' War — which he started in 1337 by claiming the French crown — and the arrival of the Black Death in England. His descendants eventually turned on each other in England's Wars of the Roses.

events.title: Oda Nobunaga Dies
events.description: Oda Nobunaga, Japan's first "Great Unifier" dies by ritual suicide, seppuku, after being betrayed by a general and attacked at Honnō-ji temple in Kyoto.

events.title: The U.S. Constitution Is Ratified
events.description: The signing of the Constitution on September 17, 1787. It was ratified a little under a year later in June 1788.

events.title: Twenty "Molly Maguires" Are Executed
events.description: Twenty men who allegedly belonged to an organization called the Molly Maguires are hanged in Pennsylvania. The Molly Maguires were Irish immigrants who organized secretly to fight unfair working conditions in coal mines. An unfair trial found 20 men affiliated with the group guilty of murder and sentenced them to die — an event known in Pennsylvania as "Black Thursday."

events.title: Mary Pickford And Douglas Fairbanks Are Mobbed In London
events.description: Mary Pickford and Douglas Fairbanks in 1920, the year of their wedding.

events.title: Ernest Burkhart Is Found Guilty
events.description: Ernest Burkhart is found guilty for his role in the Osage Indian Murders.

events.title: Cherish Perrywinkle Is Kidnapped
events.description: Eight-year-old Cherish Perrywinkle is kidnapped, raped, and murdered by a registered sex offender named Donald Smith. After offering to help Cherish's mother pay for clothing for her and her siblings, Smith lured the eight-year-old out of the store and into his van. Smith was found guilty of first-degree murder and other charges at trial and sentenced to death.

events.title: Richard II Of England Begins His Reign
events.description: Richard II ascended to the throne as a boy and was later forced to abdicate.

events.title: Mutineers Send Henry Hudson Adrift
events.description: English Captain Henry Hudson, his son, and seven of his supporters are set adrift by mutineers on Hudson's ship Discovery. Hudson and his crew had initially set out to discover a northwest passage to Asia but ended up trapped in ice in present-day Hudson Bay. Hudson, his son, and his supporters were never seen again. And back in England, his crew was arrested for the mutiny.

events.title: Galileo Galilei Is Forced To Recant His Support Of The Copernican Theory
events.description: The Roman Inquisition forces Galileo Galilei — who argued in his book The Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems that the Earth revolved around the Sun, and not the other way around — to recant. Galilei did so, though the astronomer allegedly also muttered: "And yet it moves." He was found guilty of heresy and sentenced to house arrest until he died in 1642.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Abdicates For The Second Time
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte abdicates for the second time and is exiled to the remote island of St. Helena, where he died in 1821.

events.title: Judy Garland Dies
events.description: Judy Garland's casket being placed inside a hearse.

events.title: Emanuela Orlandi Disappears
events.description: Fifteen-year-old Emanuela Orlandi disappears in Rome after attending a music lesson. The daughter of a Vatican official, her disappearance has prompted numerous theories that suggest she could have been taken by the Mafia, Turkish terrorists, or powerful figures within the Vatican. To date, neither Orlandi nor her remains have been found.

events.title: Anthony Senter Released On Parole
events.description: Anthony Senter, a former mobster and one of the Gemini Twins, is released from prison on parole, despite a life sentence.

events.title: Cleopatra Gives Birth To Caesar's Son
events.description: Cleopatra and Julius Caesar, who she allegedly seduced so that he would help her in a power struggle against her brother.

events.title: Oda Nobunaga Is Born
events.description: Oda Nobunaga, the Japanese samurai who conquered much of Japan and is considered the country's first "Great Unifier," is born in Owari Province.

events.title: Christopher Latham Sholes Receives A Patent For The Typewriter
events.description: Christopher Latham Sholes, alongside Carlos Glidden and Samuel W. Soulé, is granted a patent for the typewriter. Sholes had originally secured a patent with Soulé for a page-numbering machine, which Glidden suggested he modify so that it could print letters. Sholes later sold his patent to the Remington Arms Company, which produced the Remington Typewriter.

events.title: Antarctic Treaty Becomes Effective
events.description: The Antarctic Treaty signed by 12 countries becomes effective. This treaty designated Antarctica as a place of international cooperation, peace, and scientific discovery. The treaty prevents any nation from using Antarctica for military and nuclear purposes. Additionally, nations cannot lay claim to Antarctica. The treaty was meant to allow for freedom of scientific investigation in Antarctica for all nations. Today, 56 countries agree to abide by the rules of the Antarctic Treaty.

events.title: The Ice Box Murders Take Place In Houston
events.description: Houston Public LibraryThe ice box where Charles Rogers allegedly put his parents' remains.

events.title: Lorena Bobbitt Castrates Her Husband
events.description: Lorena Bobbitt cuts off the penis of her husband, John, and discards it in a field. In the ensuing trial, which captivated America, Lorena claimed that she'd attacked her husband because he'd abused her for years and because he'd raped her earlier that night. She was found not guilty by reason of temporary insanity and briefly placed in a psychiatric hospital; John's penis was later reattached.

events.title: Thai Soccer Team Gets Stuck In Tham Luang Cave
events.description: A youth Thai soccer team comprised of 12 players and their coach get stuck in Tham Laung cave in northern Thailand. Heavy rains flooded the cave, preventing the team from escaping and launching one of the biggest rescue operations in history.

events.title: Henry VIII Is Crowned King Of England
events.description: King Henry VIII circa 1509, when he ascended to the throne.

events.title: King Philip's War Begins
events.description: King Philip's War begins in colonial New England. So named for Wampanoag chief Metacomet, also called King Philip, the conflict endured for months and pitted various Native American tribes against English settlers (and some Indigenous allies). King Philip, and many other Native Americans, wanted to stop the English settlers' expansion on their lands, but the conflict ended in August 1676 with King Philip's death.

events.title: Modern Freemasonry Is Founded
events.description: The first Masonic Grand Lodge in the world is established in London, England. Then, four lodges gathered at the Goose and Gridiron Tavern to create the first "grand" lodge. This is considered the beginning of modern Freemasonry, though Freemason societies have long existed.

events.title: Butch Cassidy Robs His First Bank
events.description: Butch Cassidy's 1894 mugshot.

events.title: Chris Benoit Dies By Suicide After Murdering His Family
events.description: Chris Benoit shocks the professional wrestling world after he kills his family and commits suicide. A 22-time WWE champion, Benoit was a fan favorite known for his skill and charisma. Shortly after the murders, Benoit was scheduled to appear at a wrestling match. When he failed to show up, a concerned friend alerted authorities and sent them out to Benoit's house.

events.title: Maria Theresa Crowned Queen Of Hungary
events.description: Maria Theresa is crowned Queen of Hungary. The eldest daughter of Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI, Maria Theresa first ascended to power after his death in 1740. She later became the Holy Roman Empress.

events.title: The Battle Of Little Bighorn Begins
events.description: A depiction of the Battle of Little Bighorn.

events.title: The Korean War Begins
events.description: Some 75,000 soldiers from the North Korean People's Army march across the 38th parallel into South Korea, triggering the Korean War. The conflict killed some 5 million soldiers and civilians. The war came to a halt with an armistice in July 1953 but, without a peace treaty, never technically ended.

events.title: Serial Killer Charles Starkweather Is Executed
events.description: Charles Starkweather, the teenage serial killer who terrorized Heartland America throughout the mid-to-late 1950s, is executed via the electric chair.

events.title: Roy Sullivan Is Struck By Lightning For The Seventh Time
events.description: National Park ServiceRoy Sullivan shows how a lightning bolt struck his hat.

events.title: Michel Lotito, The Man With The Strangest Diet, Dies
events.description: Michel Lotito, a French performer, dies in Grenoble, France. Lotito rose to fame in the 1970s, 80s, and 90s for consuming inedible objects, including screws, bolts, and even a plane.

events.title: Michael Jackson Dies
events.description: Michael Jackson dies at the age of 50 in Los Angeles, California, from cardiac arrest triggered by an overdose of propofol and other drugs. One of America's most iconic pop stars, Jackson was a member of his family's band The Jackson 5 before he branched out as a solo artist with hits like "Beat It" and "Thriller." His legacy has been clouded in recent decades, however, by allegations of child molestation.

events.title: Francisco Pizarro Is Assassinated
events.description: Conquistador Francisco Pizarro in an 1835 painting.

events.title: A Gunpowder Factory Kills 300 In Luxembourg
events.description: Lightning strikes a gunpowder factory in Kirchberg, Luxembourg. The strike triggered an explosion that razed two blocks and killed more than 300 people. It's believed to be one of the deadliest lightning strikes in history.

events.title: The United Nations Charter Is Signed
events.description: The charter of the United Nations is signed in San Francisco, California, by delegates from 50 nations. The founding document of the organization, the charter sought to save "succeeding generations from the scourge of war" by maintaining peace, prompting progress, and encouraging the expansion of human rights. Today, the U.N. has 193 member states.

events.title: Israel Kamakawiwo'ole Dies
events.description: Universal MusicIsrael Kamakawiwo'ole was renowned for his rendition of "Somewhere Over the Rainbow" that was released in 1993.

events.title: Same-Sex Marriage Becomes Legal In The U.S.
events.description: The Supreme Court announces its decision in Obergefell v. Hodges, declaring that bans on same-sex marriages and bans on recognizing same-sex marriages were unconstitutional. The case originated with a gay couple named Jim Obergefell and John Arthur, whose marriage was recognized in Maryland but not in Ohio. The Supreme Court decision effectively made same-sex marriage legal in all 50 states.

events.title: James Smithson Dies
events.description: James Smithson dies in Genoa, Italy, at the age of 64. One of Europe's leading scientists, Smithson inherited a fortune from his mother. In his will, he decreed that if his nephew died without heirs, his estate would go to "the United States of America, to found at Washington, under the name of the Smithsonian Institution, an Establishment for the increase and diffusion of knowledge." And since his nephew did die without heirs, the now-famous Smithsonian Institution was born.

events.title: Joseph Smith Is Killed
events.description: Joseph Smith, the founder of Mormonism, in a painting from circa 1842.

events.title: The First Newbery Medal Is Awarded
events.description: The first Newbery Medal for children's literature is awarded to Hendrik Willem van Loon for his book The Story of Mankind. The award, given by the American Library Association, sought to encourage originality and excellence. Other winners include The Giver by Lois Lowry, Sarah, Plain and Tall by Patricia MacLachlan, and A Wrinkle in Time by Madeleine L'Engle.

events.title: The BTK Killer Pleads Guilty To Murder
events.description: Larry W. Smith/AFP/Getty ImagesDennis Rader being escorted into the El Dorado Correctional Facility in Kansas. August 19, 2005.

events.title: Marcus Wesson Is Sentenced To Death
events.description: Marcus Wesson, the infamous leader of the incestuous "Wesson Clan," is sentenced to death in California. One year earlier, Wesson had brutally murdered nine of his children at his home in Fresno. Authorities later discovered that seven of the children had been born out of incest, as Wesson had raped two of his daughters and three of his nieces.

events.title: Charles I Becomes The Holy Roman Emperor
events.description: Charles I of Spain is elected Holy Roman Emperor. The grandson of Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I, Charles was selected in lieu of other heads of state, including Henry VIII of England and Francis I of France. He then ruled as Emperor Charles V until 1556 — when he abdicated the throne and retired to the Monastery of Yuste.

events.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau Is Born
events.description: Jean-Jacques Rousseau is born in Geneva, Switzerland. Today, Rousseau is known as one of the most influential Enlightenment thinkers. His works include The Social Contract, Discourse on the Origin and Basis of Inequality Among Men, and On Education. His philosophy emphasized the natural goodness of man, promoted democracy, and critiqued the social systems that created inequality. His works would have a great impact on both the American Revolution and French Revolution.

events.title: Archduke Franz Ferdinand Is Assassinated
events.description: Franz Ferdinand's blood-stained uniform.

events.title: The Stonewall Riots Begin In New York City
events.description: The crowd attempts to impede police arrests during the raid on the Stonewall Inn nightclub, June 28, 1969.

events.title: Mike Tyson Bites Evander Holyfield's Ear
events.description: YouTubeMike Tyson's infamous ear bite in 1997.

events.title: The Globe Theatre Burns Down
events.description: Tohma/Wikimedia CommonsThe modern-day Globe Theatre was constructed in the 1990s.

events.title: Canada's Worst Rail Disaster Kills 99
events.description: A train carrying hundreds of passengers drops through the gap of a swing bridge over the Richelieu River in Quebec. Though a red light had signaled for the train to stop, neither the conductor nor the engineer apparently saw it. Ninety-nine people, mostly German and Polish immigrants, died in the so-called St. Hilaire train disaster, which is still considered the worst rail disaster in Canadian history.

events.title: Jayne Mansfield Dies
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJayne Mansfield and the two men with her in the front seat died instantly when they collided with a trailer truck.

events.title: Furman v Georgia Puts A Moratorium On Capital Punishment
events.description: The Supreme Court case Furman v Georgia declared the death penalty unconstitutional, commuting death row inmates' sentences to life in prison instead.

events.title: Bob Crane Is Found Murdered
events.description: Bob Crane, the Hogan's Heroes star, is bludgeoned to death in his apartment in Scottsdale, Arizona. The murder remains officially unsolved to this day, but many believe that John Carpenter, a close friend of Crane's, was the one who killed him. Carpenter, a regional Sony sales manager, had provided Crane with photo and video equipment to document his sex life. In return, Crane had used his celebrity to help Carpenter meet women. However, when Crane tried to end his friendship with Carpenter, he reportedly became enraged. But although Carpenter was eventually tried for the murder, he was ultimately acquitted.

events.title: The "Ken And Barbie Killers" Wed
events.description: Paul Bernardo and Karla Homolka, known as the Ken and Barbie Killers, get married. By then, Bernardo had abducted and raped a number of women, and Homolka had even helped him to rape and murder her own sister. They continued to rape and murder together before DNA evidence led police to Bernardo's door, leading to the couple's arrest in 1993. Bernardo was ultimately sentenced to life in prison for his crimes, but Homolka served just 12 years in exchange for her cooperation with authorities.

events.title: Hernán Cortés Retreats
events.description: Spanish forces led by Hernán Cortés retreat from the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan in present-day Mexico City. Though some Spanish soldiers successfully escaped the Aztec revolt against their rule, others died during the withdrawal because they'd filled their boats with too much treasure, causing the vessels to sink. But despite this brief setback, Cortés returned to Tenochtitlan less than a year later and conquered the capital, marking the end of the Aztec empire.

events.title: 14-Year-Old Jeanne Boulet Is Killed By The Beast Of Gévaudan
events.description: While watching over her family's livestock, a young girl named Jeanne Boulet is attacked by the mysterious Beast of Gévaudan, a monster that terrorized 18th-century France.

events.title: Charles Blondin Crosses Niagara Falls On A Tightrope
events.description: Charles Blondin crossing over Niagara Falls in 1859.

events.title: A Mysterious Explosion Occurs Near Siberia's Podkamennaya Tunguska River
events.description: Sovfoto/UIG/Getty ImagesA small portion of the Siberian forest that was flattened by the Tunguska explosion.

events.title: The "Night Of The Long Knives" Takes Place In Nazi Germany
events.description: SA chief Ernst Röhm, who Adolf Hitler had killed as part of the Night of the Long Knives.

events.title: Marcus Wayne Chenault Fatally Shoots Alberta King
events.description: Marcus Wayne Chenault shoots and kills Alberta Williams King, the mother of Martin Luther King Jr., at Ebenezer Baptist Church in Atlanta, Georgia.

events.title: Stephen McDaniel Is Interviewed About The Disappearance Of Lauren Giddings
events.description: Stephen McDaniel is interviewed by a local news outlet in Georgia about the disappearance of his downstairs neighbor Lauren Giddings. McDaniel acted distraught on camera — but he was actually the one who had murdered her. By the time of the interview, McDaniel was already a person of interest, and he was arrested shortly thereafter. He eventually pleaded guilty to the crime and was later sentenced to life in prison.

events.title: The Battle Of Gettysburg Begins
events.description: Union soldiers lie dead after the Battle of Gettysburg. Circa July 4 - July 7, 1863.

events.title: Canada Becomes A Country
events.description: The British North America Act goes into effect, creating the nation of Canada. The act brought together the territories of Upper and Lower Canada, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick, and opened the door for other provinces to join. This date is celebrated as "Canada Day" in Canada.

events.title: Theodore Roosevelt Charges Up San Juan Hill
events.description: Future president Theodore Roosevelt becomes a national hero after leading a charge up San Juan Hill in Cuba during the Spanish-American War, in what Roosevelt later called "the greatest day" of his life.

events.title: Operation Crossroads Begin
events.description: Operation Crossroads, a series of American nuclear tests, begins at Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands.

events.title: Princess Diana Is Born
events.description: Princess Diana and actor John Travolta at the White House in 1985.

events.title: Anneliese Michel Dies After Her Exorcism
events.description: Anneliese Michel dies after her exorcism in Germany. Diagnosed with epilepsy, Michel experienced frequent symptoms like seizures, trances, and memory loss.

events.title: The Wonderland Murders Shock Los Angeles
events.description: The so-called 'Wonderland Murders' take place at 8763 Wonderland Avenue, a known drug house, in Los Angeles, California.

events.title: The Revolt On The Amistad Begins
events.description: Fifty-three enslaved people abducted from Africa revolt and kill the captain of the Amistad. The mutineers then commanded the navigator to bring them home to Sierra Leone, but he steered the ship north, where it was captured by the U.S. Navy. Following a protracted public debate and a Supreme Court case, the mutineers were released and returned to Sierra Leone.

events.title: U.S. President James Garfield Is Shot
events.description: A depiction of Charles Guiteau's attack on James Garfield.

events.title: Peter Kürten Is Executed
events.description: Peter Kürten, a German serial killer dubbed the "Düsseldorf Vampire" is executed by guillotine.

events.title: Amelia Earhart Disappears
events.description: Amelia Earhart sitting in a plane in 1936, the year before she disappeared.

events.title: Larry Walters Takes Flight In A Lawnchair Attached To Balloons
events.description: Larry Walters ties 43 eight-foot weather balloons to a lawn chair and takes flight. Walters stayed aloft for 45 minutes until he shot a number of the balloons and slowly drifted back to earth, where he collided with a power line. Though Walters was unharmed, he died of suicide 11 years later in 1993.

events.title: William I Becomes Duke Of Normandy
events.description: William I, known as William the Conqueror, becomes Duke of Normandy at the age of eight following the death of his father, Robert I. He successfully defended his right to the English throne during the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and later expanded his kingdom by conquering Scotland and Wales.

events.title: George Washington Takes Command Of The Continental Army
events.description: George Washington in 1776, when he was the commander of the Continental Army.

events.title: Pickett's Charge Takes Place During The Battle Of Gettysburg
events.description: Pickett's Charge, a doomed Confederate assault on Union lines during the Battle of Gettysburg, takes place. Some 6,000 Confederate soldiers died within an hour of fighting, and Confederate General Robert E. Lee withdrew his troops from the battlefield the next day, handing the Union a victory.

events.title: Franz Kafka Is Born
events.description: Franz Kafka is born in Prague, then a part of Austria-Hungary. During his life, Kafka penned startling and penetrating works of fiction like The Metamorphosis. He died in 1924 at the age of 40 of tuberculosis.

events.title: Jim Morrison Dies
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesJim Morrison at a performance in Germany in 1968.

events.title: Operation Entebbe Rescues 102 Hostages In Uganda
events.description: Israeli commandos launch Operation Entebbe, a daring rescue mission designed to save more than 100 hostages in Uganda who were taken captive after their plane was hijacked by the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP).

events.title: A Stampede In Mecca Kills 1,400
events.description: Pilgrims visiting Mecca during the Hajj are caught in a stampede in a tunnel. Some 1,400 people died from suffocation and getting trampled to death. It was the deadliest disaster during the Hajj until 2015 when 2,000 pilgrims were crushed to death in the Mina stampede.

events.title: Brendon Grimshaw Dies
events.description: Brendon Grimshaw, known for restoring Moyenne Island in Seychelles, dies. A working journalist, he bought the island in the 1960s, and spent the rest of his life dedicated to reintroducing native plants and animals to Moyenne. The island is now part of a national park and can be visited on organized tours.

events.title: The Declaration Of Independence Is Adopted
events.description: Some, like John Adams, thought that the country would celebrate July 2nd as Independence Day, since that's when delegates formally approved the motion to declare independence.

events.title: Thomas Jefferson And John Adams Die
events.description: Founding Fathers Thomas Jefferson and John Adams die within hours of each other. Adams, the United States' second president, and Jefferson, the nation's third, had each played a crucial role in the country's path to independence. Though they'd had a political falling out, the two men reconciled after their respective presidencies, and Adams' last words were, "Thomas Jefferson still survives!" though, unbeknownst to him, Jefferson had already passed away.

events.title: James Monroe Dies
events.description: Five years after Thomas Jefferson and John Adams's death, their fellow Founding father and former president James Monroe dies at the age of 73.

events.title: The Dead Rabbits And Bowery Boys Riot In Lower Manhattan
events.description: A depiction of a stereotypical Bowery Boy.

events.title: France Gifts The Statue Of Liberty To The United States
events.description: France gifts the Statue of Liberty to the United States to commemorate the American-French alliance during the American Revolution. In 1865, Edouard de Laboulaye proposed the creation of the statue to honor ideas of freedom and liberty. Sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi drafted an idea for the statue in 1870.

events.title: Katherine Bowes-Lyon Is Born
events.description: Katherine Bowes-Lyon, the cousin of Queen Elizabeth II, is born. The British public was shocked after news broke in the 1980s that Bowes-Lyon, alongside her sister Nerissa, were institutionalized and declared dead in their youth despite being alive.

events.title: Michael Mageau And Darlene Elizabeth Are Attacked
events.description: The Zodiac killer strikes once again, this time killing two young people named Michael Mageau and Darlene Elizabeth.

events.title: Bob Ross Dies
events.description: YouTubeBob Ross was suffering from lymphoma during his final televised appearance.

events.title: P.T. Barnum Is Born
events.description: Phineas Taylor Barnum, later known as P.T. Barnum, is born in Bethel, Connecticut. A showman, Barnum acquired New York's American Museum and filled it with "curiosities" like conjoined twins. He later joined with James A. Bailey to create Barnum and Bailey's Circus, which operated until 2017.

events.title: The U.S. Secret Service Is Founded
events.description: Secret Service members protecting President Theodore Roosevelt.

events.title: Boise City 'Bombing Raid' Takes Place
events.description: Pilots at the Dalhart Army Air Base in Texas accidentally drop six dummy bombs on the town of Boise City, Oklahoma, during a practice flight. The so-called Boise City Bombing Raid lasted just 30 minutes and, miraculously, didn't inflict any damage on the town or its residents. Boise City even erected a bronze plaque to commemorate the bombing in 1993.

events.title: The 26th Amendment Of The U.S. Constitution Grants Suffrage To All Citizens Over 18
events.description: The 26th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution grants suffrage to all citizens over the age of 18. Prior to this amendment, states were able to determine their own minimum voting age, and only four had a minimum voting age below 21. American men were strong proponents of lowering the voting age to 18, as many of them had been drafted into the Vietnam War without the ability to vote. The amendment was ratified in four months — the fastest ratification of an amendment in U.S. history.

events.title: Dolly The Cloned Sheep Is Born
events.description: Jeroen Kransen/FlickrDolly the Sheep's preserved body at the National Museum of Scotland.

events.title: First Lilith Fair Show
events.description: The first show of the touring festival Lilith Fair took place at the Gorge in Washington State. The show marked the beginning of a very successful first year for the festival, which featured a line-up of exclusively women artists and performers. The festival would tour for another two years before stopping for a decade-long hiatus. Lilith Fair creator Sarah McLachlan put together one last Lilith Fair in 2010 before retiring the festival.

events.title: Richard III Becomes King Of England
events.description: Richard III becomes the king of England after declaring the sons of his late brother, King Edward IV, illegitimate. Having locked up — and perhaps murdered — his nephews, Richard reigned for two years. He was killed in 1485 during an uprising led by Henry Tudor, who became King Henry VII.

events.title: Sir Thomas More Is Executed
events.description: Thomas More in a 1527 portrait by Hans Holbein the Younger.

events.title: John Paul Jones Is Born
events.description: John Paul Jones is born in Arbigland, Kirkcudbrightshire, Scotland. A sailor, he became a naval hero during the Revolutionary War by leading American troops against the British. Jones later served in the Imperial Russian Navy before he died in Paris of interstitial nephritis in 1792.

events.title: Louis Pasteur Gives The First Rabies Shot
events.description: Louis Pasteur gives the first rabies inoculation to nine-year-old Joseph Meister, who'd been bitten by a rabid dog. Meister — who would have likely died — soon recovered, and Pasteur's inoculation technique quickly spread.

events.title: The Homestead Strike Ends
events.description: Striking workers from Carnegie Steel defeat the Pinkerton Detective Agency in Pittsburgh's Homestead, prompting the governor to deploy the National Guard to protect strikebreakers. In the end, the union strikers were defeated, dealing a major blow to their efforts to help steelworkers unionize.

events.title: Anne Frank Goes Into Hiding
events.description: Anne Frank in 1940.

events.title: Judy Warren, The Only Child Of Ed And Lorraine Warren, Is Born
events.description: Judy Warren, the daughter of famous paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren, is born. She went on to marry a former cop named Tony Spera, who now maintains the Warrens' business.

events.title: Tammy Lynn Leppert Disappears From Cocoa Beach, Florida
events.description: Scarface actress Tammy Lynn Leppert disappears from Cocoa Beach, Florida after exhibiting months of increasingly paranoid behavior.

events.title: Skylar Neese Is Murdered
events.description: Sixteen-year-old Skylar Neese is murdered by two of her close friends, Shelia Eddy and Rachel Shoaf. After deciding that they "didn't like" Neese, Eddy and Shoaf lured her into the woods and stabbed her to death. Neese's death inspired "Skylar's Law," which mandates that Amber Alerts are issued for all missing children — not just those believed to be kidnapped.

events.title: Mary Surratt Is Executed
events.description: Four people, including Mary Surratt, are hanged for their role in the assassination of President Abraham Lincoln.

events.title: Ringo Starr Is Born
events.description: Richard Starkey, later known as Ringo Starr, is born in Liverpool, England. A drummer, Starr rose to fame as a member of the Beatles, where he played the drums and sang some of the band's most iconic songs, like "Yellow Submarine." Today, he's considered one of the greatest drummers of all time.

events.title: Howard Hughes' Plane Crash In Los Angeles
events.description: World-famous aviator Howard Hughes is piloting an experimental spy plane he recently built when the hydraulics suddenly give out and he crashes into a series of Beverly Hills mansions, narrowly escaping with his life. Miraculously, no one was killed when the plane went down, even though the right wing tore through one couple's bedroom and one of the engines went flying more than 60 feet through another home.

events.title: The Roswell UFO Incident
events.description: History's most infamous alien conspiracy gets underway when a rancher near Roswell, New Mexico, brings pieces of a supposed flying saucer he'd found to the local sheriff's office. At first, the Air Force claimed that they had recovered the wreckage of a "flying disc" from Foster Ranch.

events.title: Bumpy Johnson Dies
events.description: Records of the Bureau of Prisons/Wikimedia CommonsA mugshot of Bumpy Johnson, the notorious Harlem crime boss, from 1954.

events.title: The '7/7' London Bombings Take Place
events.description: Four suicide bombers detonate explosives on public transport in London, England. The so-called 7/7 attacks, perpetrated by Islamist terrorists, killed 52 people, including the bombers themselves. An additional 700 people were injured in the attack, which is considered one of the worst in British history.

events.title: Percy Bysshe Shelley Dies
events.description: Percy Bysshe Shelley drowns off the coast of Italy during a severe storm. A writer and the husband of Frankenstein author Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley, Percy wrote poetry, prose, and essays. Though he was not well known during his life, pieces like Prometheus Unbound brought him posthumous fame.

events.title: Cora Pearl Dies
events.description: adoc-photos/Corbis via Getty ImagesCora Pearl sitting with her friend Amie Beresford.

events.title: The Steamship Milwaukee Sinks Into Lake Michigan
events.description: After its captain — and the captain of the C. Hickox — failed to follow proper procedures, the steamship Milwaukee and the Hickox collide, destroying the Milwaukee and sinking it to the bottom of Lake Michigan.

events.title: The Crew Of The Potemkin Surrenders
events.description: The crew of the Russian battleship Potemkin surrenders in Costanza, Romania, in exchange for asylum. On June 27, the men had mutinied and commandeered the vessel (radicals on the ship had long planned the uprising, but the revolt was ultimately triggered by maggoty beef). Though most went on to live in obscurity, the mutineers were seen as heroes after the 1917 Russian Revolution.

events.title: Charles Schmid Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/GettyCharles Schmid killed at least three teenagers before he was caught.

events.title: Lars Mittank Goes Missing
events.description: Lars Mittank goes missing from the airport in Bulgaria. While spending time on a vacation with his friends in Bulgaria, the 28-year-old Berlin native got into a fight with some local men and sustained serious head injuries.

events.title: Catherine The Great Becomes Empress
events.description: Catherine II is proclaimed Empress of Russia after convincing the army to support her over her husband, Emperor Peter III. Later known as Catherine the Great, the monarch ruled over Russia for the next 34 years and was the country's longest-ruling female leader.

events.title: President Zachary Taylor Dies
events.description: Zachary Taylor was president for just four months before he died suddenly in 1850.

events.title: Nikola Tesla Is Born
events.description: Famed scientist and inventor Nikola Tesla is born in Croatia. Tesla studied engineering and mathematics before emigrating to the United States in 1884. Tesla set up laboratories in New York City where he worked on various electrical and mechanical contraptions, one of which earned him a substantial amount of money. He was particularly interested in developing wireless power sources. Though Tesla died in poverty and anonymity in 1943, today he is known as an historic inventor who was decades ahead of his time.

events.title: The First Wimbledon Tournament Takes Place
events.description: The first Wimbledon Tournament is held on a croquet lawn at the All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club in London. Since then, the annual tennis tournament has occurred every summer.

events.title: Garry Hoy Accidentally Jumps To His Death
events.description: The tower in Toronto from which Garry Hoy plummeted to his death in 1993.

events.title: Emperor Hadrian Dies
events.description: Roman Emperor Hadrian dies in Baiae in present-day Italy at the age of 62. In power for a little over two decades, Hadrian is perhaps best remembered for his architectural accomplishments. He ordered the building of Hadrian's Wall to demarcate the northern limit of Roman control in Britannia and the reconstruction of the Pantheon.

events.title: The 'Great' Fire Burns Across London
events.description: The Great Fire Of London 1212, also called the Great Fire of Southwark, burns through London. It started south of the Thames before spreading across the city, including the London Bridge, which then included wooden houses and shops.

events.title: Lady Jane Grey Becomes Queen Of England
events.description: Lady Jane Grey was queen for just nine days before Princess Mary, the daughter of Henry VIII, took power and had Jane executed.

events.title: Frank Leslie Murders 'Blondie Mollie' Williams
events.description: Frank "Buckskin" Leslie murders "Blonde Mollie" Williams, a sex worker and his lover, in Tombstone, Arizona. According to the Tombstone Daily Epitaph, Leslie came home drunk and found Williams speaking to a man. Filled with jealousy, he shot them both and killed her, and later plead guilty to murder.

events.title: The NKVD, The Soviet Secret Police, Is Founded
events.description: Under the regime of Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, the NKVD, or the The People's Commissariat for Internal Affairs, is founded. The NKVD would later be instrumental in carrying out Stalin's Great Purge.

events.title: John Paul Getty III Is Kidnapped
events.description: Vittoriano Rastelli/Corbis/Getty ImagesJohn Paul Getty III shortly after his kidnappers released him in December 1973.

events.title: Ken McElroy Is Killed
events.description: Ken McElroy — the "town bully" of Skidmore, Missouri — is shot and killed in broad daylight. McElroy had terrorized the town for years and had nearly killed the town grocer.

events.title: The First Quakers Arrive In The Colonies
events.description: Englishwomen Ann Austin and Mary Fisher become the first Quakers to arrive in the American colonies. Coming from Barbados, where Quakers had an established missionary, Austin and Fisher landed in Boston. Local Puritans frowned on their teachings, however, and they were both jailed for five years before they were deported back to Barbados.

events.title: Alexander Hamilton Is Killed In A Duel
events.description: Alexander Hamilton, left, and Aaron Burr, right, infamously dueled in Weehawken, New Jersey, resulting in Hamilton's death.

events.title: The Conjoined McCoy Twins Are Born
events.description: Millie and Christine McCoy, a pair of conjoined twins, are born in Welches Creek, North Carolina. The daughters of an enslaved couple, they were taken from their parents and sold in order to be exhibited as "The Carolina Twins." They later worked in circuses across the world on their own terms and wrote a book about their lives.

events.title: The Cicero Race Riots Begin
events.description: Four thousand white residents of Cicero, Illinois, riot after a Black family moves into an apartment building in town. The riot lasted several days and caused some $20,000 in damage.

events.title: To Kill A Mockingbird Is Published
events.description: To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee is published. The iconic coming-of-age story about racial injustice in a small Southern town won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1961. Lee's story was also adapted into a film the next year, for which Gregory Peck won an Oscar for his portrayal of Atticus Finch.

events.title: Skylab Crashes To Earth
events.description: Skylab as seen from space in 1974.

events.title: Julius Caesar Is Born
events.description: Metropolitan Museum of ArtJulius Caesar is known today for his assassination and his romance with Cleopatra.

events.title: Geoffrey Chaucer Becomes Chief Clerk Of The King's Works
events.description: King Richard II appoints Geoffrey Chaucer as chief clerk of the king's works. Chaucer, a poet, had previously produced a number of works including The Parlement of Foules and Troilus and Criseyde. In the late 1380s and early 1390s, he began the work for which he is best known, Canterbury Tales.

events.title: King Henry VIII Marries Catherine Parr
events.description: King Henry VIII of England marries Catherine Parr. His sixth and final wife, Parr outlived the king, who died in 1547. Her five predecessors — except for Henry's third wife Jane — had been divorced or executed by Henry.

events.title: Abigail Williams Is Born
events.description: Abigail Williams, one of the first girls to accuse people of witchcraft during the Salem Witch Trials in 1692, is born.

events.title: Alexander Hamilton Dies In A Duel With Aaron Burr
events.description: Alexander Hamilton dies after a duel with Aaron Burr. Burr shot Hamilton in the abdomen, and the founding father later passed away with his family at his bedside.

events.title: Henry David Thoreau Is Born
events.description: Henry David Thoreau near the end of his life.

events.title: Lyudmila Pavlichenko Is Born
events.description: Lyudmila Pavlichenko, the best female sniper in history, is born in Bila Tserkva, Ukraine.

events.title: Carmine Galante Is Killed
events.description: Mob boss Carmine Galante is shot and killed in Brooklyn, New York, at the age of 69. The acting boss of the Bonanno crime family, Galante oversaw the family's heroin operations. He was assassinated at a restaurant in Bushwick, likely at the behest of other mafia families.

events.title: Disco Demolition Night Results In A Riot
events.description: A drunk crowd swarms the baseball field at Comiskey Park in Chicago and starts an anti-disco riot in what would later be called Disco Demolition Night.

events.title: The Carabinieri Is Established
events.description: Victor Emmanuel I of Savoy establishes the Carabinieri. An Italian branch of law enforcement, they were tasked with "[contributing] to the necessary happiness of the State, which cannot be separated from protection and defense of all good subjects." The Carabinieri continue to operate to this day.

events.title: John Jacob Astor IV Is Born
events.description: John Jacob Astor IV is born in Rhinebeck, New York. A member of the prominent Astor family, Astor was the wealthiest passenger aboard the RMS Titanic, and perished when the ship sank on April 15, 1912.

events.title: Johnny Ringo Is Killed
events.description: Johnny Ringo's death was officially ruled a suicide, but frontier icons like Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday have claimed they shot him.

events.title: The First World Cup Matches Are Played
events.description: The first World Cup games are played in Montevideo, Uruguay. In those games, France defeated Mexico 4-1 and the United States won over Belgium 3-0. The first World Cup final, held on July 30, pitted Uruguay against Argentina and resulted in a 4-2 victory for Uruguay.

events.title: Frida Kahlo Dies
events.description: Frida Kahlo posing with her self-portraits.

events.title: Ruth Ellis Is Executed
events.description: Ruth Ellis, a Welsh nightclub hostess, is hanged after murdering her former lover. She was the last woman to be executed in the United Kingdom.

events.title: Conrad Roy Dies By Suicide
events.description: Conrad Roy dies by suicide, poisoning himself with carbon monoxide fumes in his truck in Fairhaven, Massachusetts. In the aftermath, his girlfriend Michelle Carter was accused of encouraging him to commit suicide with a series of text messages. She was convicted of involuntary manslaughter and spent 11 months in prison.

events.title: The Dancing Plague Breaks Out In Strasbourg
events.description: The "dancing plague" begins in Strasbourg, France. It started with one woman who compulsively danced until she collapsed from exhaustion and soon spread throughout the city.

events.title: Parisians Storm The Bastille Prison
events.description: A depiction of the storming of the Bastille, one of the most important dates in French history.

events.title: Gustav Klimt Is Born
events.description: Gustav Klimt, the painter most famous for his work The Kiss, is born in Vienna, Austria. Klimt is most known for his paintings depicting the female body and his unorthodox artistic choices. Klimt belonged to the Vienna Secession movement, an artistic movement that gave unconventional artists the ability to show their work in exhibitions.

events.title: Billy The Kid Is Killed By Pat Garrett
events.description: Billy the Kid is shot and killed by Sheriff Pat Garrett in New Mexico Territory.

events.title: The Great Railroad Strike Begins
events.description: Railroad workers begin striking in Martinsburg, West Virginia to stop the increasingly common pay cuts by railroad companies. The strike halted all trains in the area. The strike eventually spread throughout the country, growing to over 100,000 strong. By the time the strike ended in August of 1877, over 100 people had been killed during the unrest across the country.

events.title: Richard Speck Murders Eight Nursing Students
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesRichard Speck murdered eight female nurses in Chicago, shocking the nation.

events.title: Bobby Kent Is Murdered By His Friends
events.description: Bobby Kent was killed by seven of his peers. One of his killers included Marty Puccio, Kent's best friend. However, Kent was both physically and emotionally abusive toward Puccio for years. Additionally, he was abusive to his ex-girlfriend Alice Wallis. Eventually, Puccio girlfriend and Wallis' friend, Lisa Connelly got fed-up with Kent's treatment of her boyfriend. So, a group was formed to take out Kent permanently. Kent's murder went on to inspire the 2001 film Bully.

events.title: Jerusalem Is Captured By Christians
events.description: Jerusalem is captured by Christian knights during the First Crusade. Once they breached the city walls, the soldiers slaughtered tens of thousands of Muslims and Jews living there. Though Egyptian soldiers subsequently marched on the city, Christian forces were able to repel them.

events.title: The Pike Expedition Sets Out
events.description: Zebulon Pike led an expedition to explore the American southwest.

events.title: Charles Stratton Dies
events.description: Charles Stratton, a famous sideshow performer known as "General Tom Thumb," dies at the age of 45 in Bridgeport, Connecticut, after suffering from a stroke.

events.title: Robert Wadlow Dies
events.description: Robert Wadlow, the tallest man in the world at eight feet 11 inches, dies at the age of 22.

events.title: John Christie Is Executed
events.description: John Christie is executed in London by hanging. Between 1943 and 1953 he killed six women, including his own wife. He was finally caught after he moved out of his apartment and the bodies of several of his victims were found under the floorboard.

events.title: Gianni Versace Is Murdered
events.description: The aftermath of Gianni Versace's death in Miami.

events.title: Barbara Rogers Murders Her Boyfriend Over Sherry Shriner's Alien Cult
events.description: Barbara Rogers murders her boyfriend, Steven Mineo, over the alien cult started by a YouTube personality named Sherry Shriner. Shriner began publishing content about reptilian aliens in the 2000s, eventually amassing a following of 20,000 people on YouTube alone. Two of Shriner's followers, Rogers and Mineo, believed in Shriner's ideology, but they were shunned from the group after posting content that Shriner disliked.

events.title: The First Catholic Mission Is Founded In California
events.description: The first Catholic mission is founded in present-day San Diego. Called Mission San Diego de Alcalá, it was created by a Franciscan priest named Father Junipero Serra. He went on to found eight more missions across present-day California.

events.title: Ida B. Wells Is Born
events.description: Ida B. Wells circa 1895.

events.title: The World's First Atomic Bomb Is Tested
events.description: The world's first atomic bomb is tested in Alamogordo, New Mexico. A product of the Manhattan Project, the bomb was finished as World War II began drawing to a close. It was soon deployed twice before war's end when American forces dropped it on the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

events.title: Saddam Hussein Becomes President Of Iraq
events.description: Saddam Hussein becomes the president of Iraq. After assuming the presidency, Hussein used his power to gain a tight grip over Iraq. He used an extensive secret service network to suppress opposition, build up the armed forces, and build a cult of personality in Iraq. Until the U.S. invasion of Iraq in 2003, Hussein maintained power in the country. In 2006, Hussein was executed for crimes against humanity after a court found him guilty of murder and torture.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Jr. Dies
events.description: Brownie Harris/Corbis via Getty ImagesJohn F. Kennedy Jr. was 38 years old when he fatally crashed his plane.

events.title: John Jacob Astor Is Born
events.description: John Jacob Astor is born in Waldorf, Germany. One of the wealthiest people of his era, Astor later emigrated from Germany to the United States, where he made his fortune in the fur trade. He left $400,000 — about $13 million today — upon his death to build the Astor Library in New York City, which was later consolidated with other libraries into New York Public Library.

events.title: The Romanov Family Is Executed
events.description: The Romanov family in 1913, five years before they were executed.

events.title: Disneyland Opens In California
events.description: Disneyland opens in Anaheim, California. The brainchild of Walt Disney, the amusement park opened to great fanfare, with thousands of people descending to explore it on opening day. Since then, Disneyland has become a popular destination, with an estimated 18 million visitors a year.

events.title: The Iconic 'Kiss Of Life' Photo Is Taken
events.description: Rocco Morabito/Jacksonville JournalThe famous "Kiss of Life" photo shows a daring, in-air rescue.

events.title: Cannibal Killer Issei Sagawa Is Arrested
events.description: Issei Sagawa is arrested for the murder of Renée Hartevelt in Paris. After inviting the young woman to his place to study, Issei shot her in the head. Then, he proceeded to cut up her body and eat her. He later placed her body parts in suitcases and abandoned them around Paris.

events.title: The Great Fire Of Rome Ignites
events.description: A fire burns through the city of Rome. The blaze, which started in the slums near Palatine Hill, destroyed three of Rome's 14 districts and killed hundreds. Despite the common refrain, however, then-emperor Nero didn't "fiddle" during the fire — he wasn't even in the city.

events.title: Virgil Earp Is Born In Kentucky
events.description: Lawman Virgil Earp is born in Hartford, Kentucky. Earp, alongside his brothers, would play a large role in the gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona.

events.title: The "Unsinkable" Molly Brown Is Born
events.description: Molly Brown hands an award to Sir Arthur Henry Rostron, the captain of the ship RMS Carpathia that rescued hundreds of Titanic passengers.

events.title: The Newsboys Strike Begins
events.description: The newsboy strike begins in New York City. Then, so-called "newsies" — some as young as seven — went head to head with newspaper moguls like William Randolph Hearst and Joseph Pulitzer over the price of a newspaper bundle. Though the young strikers were initially dismissed, they caused enough havoc to convince Heart and Pulitzer to change their policies.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Publishes Mein Kampf
events.description: The first of two volumes of Mein Kampf by Adolf Hitler is published. The book — which Hitler wrote while imprisoned for his role in the Beer Hall Putsch — discussed the problems he believed faced Germany, including the loss of "racial purity." Sales were modest until 1933, when Hitler became Germany's chancellor and put the country on the path toward World War II.

events.title: George "Machine Gun" Kelly Dies
events.description: George "Machine Gun" Kelly dies of a heart attack at Federal Penitentiary in Leavenworth, Kansas. Kelly was a notorious gangster during the Great Depression Era who made headlines for abducting an oil tycoon for ransom.

events.title: The 'Chappaquiddick Incident' Takes Places
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesTed Kennedy's black Oldsmobile following the fatal car crash.

events.title: Rebecca Schaeffer Is Murdered
events.description: Rebecca Schaeffer is shot and killed by her stalker Robert John Bardo in Los Angeles. The 21-year-old actress had risen to fame through her character on My Sister Sam and had hoped to expand into film roles. In the aftermath of her murder, Schaeffer's death helped inspire anti-stalking legislation.

events.title: Lady Jane Grey Is Deposed As Queen
events.description: Lady Jane Grey is deposed as Queen of England after just nine days on the throne. Dubbed the "Nine Days' Queen," Grey rose to power upon the command of her late cousin, King Edward VI, who preferred her succession over that of his half-sisters, Mary and Elizabeth. But Mary's supporters rallied to her side, leading to Grey's imprisonment and later execution.

events.title: The Rosetta Stone Is Discovered
events.description: Steven Zucker, Smarthistory co-founder/FlickrThe Rosetta Stone provided the key to translating the "lost" language of Egyptian hieroglyphics.

events.title: Doc Holliday Kills For The First Time
events.description: John Henry "Doc" Holliday kills Mike Gordon, marking the first — but not last — time that the Wild West icon would take a life. Holliday, a former dentist, crossed paths with Gordon at Holliday's saloon in Las Vegas, New Mexico. When Gordon started firing in the saloon after a girl refused to run away with him, Holliday shot and killed Gordon with a single shot.

events.title: Enjar Mikkelsen Is Rescued From The Arctic
events.description: Arktisk Institut/Public DomainEjnar Mikkelsen, shortly before his rescue in 1912.

events.title: Desiree Washington Accuses Mike Tyson Of Rape
events.description: Pageant queen Desiree Washington accuses boxer Mike Tyson of rape. In one of the biggest scandals of the 1990s, Washington claimed that Tyson raped her inside his hotel room at the Canterbury Hotel in Indianapolis, Indiana.

events.title: The Annabelle Doll Is Introduced To The World For The First Time In The Conjuring
events.description: The Annabelle Doll is introduced in the film The Conjuring, becoming an instant sensation. Although the movie differs from the true story of Annabelle, both versions are equally unnerving.

events.title: Francesco Petrarca Is Born
events.description: Francesco Petrarca is born in Arezzo, Italy. Considered the "Father of Humanism," Petrarca, also called Petrarch, is especially known for his poems of longing for a woman called "Laura." Some scholars believe that his interest in the classics helped spark the Italian Renaissance.

events.title: Sitting Bull Surrenders
events.description: Sitting Bull's name was a nod to the buffalo, who Native Americans saw as fearless, strong, and stubborn.

events.title: The July Plot To Assassinate Hitler Fails
events.description: The "July Plot," a plan to assassinate Hitler fails. Claus von Stauffenberg and other conspirators wanted to kill Hitler, end Nazi rule in Germany, and make peace with Allied forces to bring an end to World War II. The plan involved Stauffenberg bringing a briefcase with a bomb to one of Hitler's conferences. During the conference, Stauffenberg laid the briefcase under the conference table and left the room to take a call. Then, the bomb exploded, killing three and injuring 20 others. Hitler, however, did not die in the blast. Following the incident, more than 7,000 people were arrested and 4,980 were executed.

events.title: The Moon Landing
events.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin land on the moon, becoming the first people in history to ever do so. As they stepped onto the lunar surface, Armstrong uttered his now famous quote: "That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind." Six more missions went to the moon between 1969 and 1972.

events.title: Bruce Lee Dies
events.description: Bruce Lee's death shocked the world and remains mysterious to this day.

events.title: Michael Romanov Is Crowned Tsar, Beginning The Romanov Dynasty In Russia
events.description: Michael Romanov is crowned tsar of Russia, beginning the Romanov Dynasty. After the Tsardom parliament elected Michael Romanov, he began what would be his 49-year rule over Russia. During Michael Romanov's reign, Russia conquered much of Siberia and ended the Time of Troubles, a period of succession crisis. During his lifetime, Michael Romanov had ten children, including the future tsar, Alexei I.

events.title: Alexandria Is Hit By A Tsunami
events.description: A devastating tsunami strikes the Egyptian city of Alexandria. Triggered by an estimated 8.0 earthquake off the coast of Greece, the tsunami killed 5,000 within Alexandria and as many as 45,000 in surrounding areas. It also left some striking artifacts, like the sunken Roman city of Neapolis.

events.title: 'Wild' Bill Hickok Fights In The First Known Western Showdown
events.description: The Hickok-Tutt shootout, as depicted in Harper's New Monthly Magazine in February 1867.

events.title: Ernest Hemingway Is Born
events.description: Ernest Hemingway is born in Oak Park, Illinois. Considered one of the finest novelists of the 20th century for his sparse, direct prose, he produced iconic works like The Sun Also Rises (1926), For Whom The Bell Tolls (1940), and The Old Man And The Sea (1952). Hemingway died of suicide in 1961 at the age of 61.

events.title: The Scopes Monkey Trial Ends
events.description: John Scopes, the Dayton, Tennessee, teacher at the center of the Scopes Monkey Trial.

events.title: William Wallace Is Defeated At The Battle Of Falkirk
events.description: King Edward I of England soundly defeats Scottish resistance forces led by William Wallace at the Battle of Falkirk. Wallace went on the run as Edward pursued him north. The English finally captured the Scottish leader in 1305 and infamously hanged, drawn, and quartered him that year for treason in a grisly public execution.

events.title: John Dillinger Is Killed
events.description: John Dillinger posing with his Tommy gun shortly before his death in 1934.

events.title: The Special Operations Executive Is Formed
events.description: Dismayed by the fall of France in 1940, Winston Churchill devises a plan to take the fight directly to the enemy via a new specialized tactical group, the Special Operations Executive.

events.title: Pablo Escobar Escapes Police Custody
events.description: Pablo Escobar escapes police custody by breaking out of jail. Escobar was one of the most prolific drug kingpins in the world. Based out of Colombia, Escobar operated one of the largest cocaine distribution organizations in the world. Prior to his imprisonment, Escobar made a deal with the Colombian government to avoid extradition to the United States. As part of this agreement, Escobar was imprisoned at a luxurious private prison. Once Escobar heard that the government was going to move him to a state-owned prison, he fled. Escobar was on the run until his death at the hands of Colombian police in 1993.

events.title: Norwegian Domestic Terror Attacks Occur In Oslo And Utøya island
events.description: Anders Behring Breivik commits his attack in Oslo and Utøya island in Norway. Breivik was a neo-Nazi who spouted anti-Islamic rhetoric and believed that Europe was being overtaken by a wave of cultural Marxism. He decided to commit acts of domestic terrorism by planting a car bomb near Regjeringskvartalet, the governmental district of Norway, and fatally shooting 67 people who were attending a Norwegian Labour Party summer camp on Utøya island. In total, 77 people lost their lives in the attack, and over 300 people were injured. Breivik was sentenced to 21 years in prison, the maximum sentence in Norway.

events.title: England's Prince George Is Born
events.description: Christopher Neve/FlickrKate Middleton, Prince William, and Prince George on the day after George's birth.

events.title: Henry VIII's Illegitimate Son Dies
events.description: Henry Fitzroy, the illegitimate son of England's King Henry VIII, dies at the age of 17 at St. James Palace in London. Fitzroy, whose mother Elizabeth Blount was a lady-in-waiting to Queen Catherine of Aragon, was openly acknowledged by his father. The king was desperate for a son and may have even legitimized Fitzroy as his heir if Fitzroy hadn't died so young.

events.title: Lawman Seth Bullock Is Born
events.description: Canadian-American lawman Seth Bullock is born in Canada. Bullock would go on to become a sheriff in Deadwood, South Dakota and rub shoulders with Theodore Roosevelt.

events.title: Ford Sells Its First Car
events.description: Sicnag/FlickrA Ford Model A at the Gilmore Museum in Michigan.

events.title: The Detroit Riots Begin
events.description: The Detriot Riots begin in Detroit, Michigan. Triggered by an early morning police raid and exacerbated by racial tensions and the worsening economy, the riots endured for five days. By the time the U.S. Army and the National Guard quelled the riots, some 43 people had been killed while 1,400 buildings burned or looted.

events.title: Vic Morrow Dies On The Set Of Twilight Zone: The Movie
events.description: Actor Vic Morrow dies while filming Twilight Zone: The Movie. The film featured a helicopter chase sequence with Morrow and two child actors. When the helicopter malfunctioned, it barreled into the actors and killed them instantly.

events.title: Amy Winehouse Dies
events.description: Flickr/Fionn KidneyAmy Winehouse seemed destined for greatness but struggled with substance abuse.

events.title: Sally Ride Dies
events.description: Sally Ride, the first American woman in space, dies. Ride joined NASA in 1978, and by 1983, she became the first female American astronaut in space while participating in the Space Shuttle Challenger mission. After her time at NASA, Ride became a professor at top universities in the United States, teaching physics. In her spare time, she led outreach programs for NASA and continued spreading her love for space to the American public.

events.title: Mary, Queen Of Scots Is Deposed
events.description: Mary, Queen of Scots, is removed from power. She was forced from the throne following her marriage to James Hepburn, 4th Earl of Bothwell, who many suspected had orchestrated the death of her second husband, Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley. As a result, power was handed to Mary's one-year-old son, James, and the former monarch spent the rest of her life under virtual house arrest in England before Queen Elizabeth I had Mary executed in 1587.

events.title: Simón Bolívar Is Born
events.description: Simón Bolívar is known as the El Libertador.

events.title: Mormon Settlers Arrive In Salt Lake Valley
events.description: One hundred and forty-eight Mormon pioneers, led by Brigham Young, arrive in Utah's Great Salt Lake Valley. The pioneers had set out more than a year earlier, hoping to establish a settlement after the assassination of their leader, Joseph Smith, in Illinois. Young declared that the Great Salt Lake Valley was "the place," and Mormons celebrate July 24 as Pioneer Day.

events.title: Hiram Bingham Arrives At Machu Picchu
events.description: Zielonamapa.pl/FlickrNow a popular tourist destination, Machu Picchu was likely once a retreat for Incan leaders.

events.title: Buck And Blanche Barrow Are Arrested
events.description: Buck and Blanche Barrow are arrested in Iowa. Accomplices of Bonnie and Clyde (Buck was Clyde's brother), Buck and Blanche accompanied the infamous duo on their 1930s crime spree. Though Blanche survived their arrest, Buck later succumbed to his injuries.

events.title: Missionaries Are Banished From Japan
events.description: Concerned that too many lords were converting, Japanese leader Toyotomi Hideyoshi issues an edict that bans Christian missionaries from Japan. Many continued to operate in secret, however, which led to the crucifixion of 26 Christians in Nagasaki in 1597. Christianity was largely banned in Japan in 1614, a ban that remained in place until 1873.

events.title: The First Railroad Accident Takes Place In The U.S.
events.description: America's first railroad accident takes place near Quincy, Massachusetts. Then, four people standing atop a vacant car were thrown off after a cable snapped. They fell off the train and down a 34-foot drop, where three were injured and one died.

events.title: Emmett Till Is Born
events.description: Emmett Till and his mother Mamie, circa 1950.

events.title: The Test Baker Nuclear Test Takes Place
events.description: The American military conducts Test Baker, exploding a nuclear bomb 90 feet beneath the waters near Bikini Atoll. The blast created a towering "spray dome" as well as a tsunami with waves nearly 100 feet high.

events.title: The Tuskegee Experiment Is Revealed
events.description: The U.S. public learns about the Tuskegee experiment for the first time. The experiment, which endured from 1932 until 1972, studied the progression of untreated syphilis in poor Black men. But the men didn't know about the experiment, and some of them unknowingly passed it on to their families.

events.title: Judith Barsi Is Murdered
events.description: YouTubeJudith Barsi in Slam Dance.

events.title: Phoolan Devi, The "Bandit Queen," Is Assassinated
events.description: Phoolan Devi, also known as the "Bandit Queen", was killed outside of her home on the afternoon of July 25, 2001. She was a member of India's parliament at the time, but was previously the leader of a gang. She was 37 years old when she died.

events.title: Inca Emperor Atahualpa Is Executed
events.description: Inca Emperor Atahualpa is executed via garrote by the Spanish after spending almost a year in captivity.

events.title: Liberia Proclaims Its Independence
events.description: The Republic of Liberia proclaims its independence. Formerly a colony of the American Colonization Society, an organization created to return enslaved people to Africa, Liberia swiftly called upon the international community to recognize its sovereignty. Britain became the first nation to do so, but the United States didn't recognize Liberian independence until 1862.

events.title: Outlaw Black Bart "The Gentleman Bandit" Commits First Robbery
