events.description: Outlaw Black Bart, otherwise known as Charles E. Boles, commits his first stagecoach robbery in California.

events.title: The FBI Is Founded
events.description: Charles Bonaparte, a grandnephew of the French emperor, founded the FBI.

events.title: Helen Mirren Is Born
events.description: Helen Mirren during the filming of 1969's Age of Consent, which was her breakthrough movie role.

events.title: Ed Gein Dies
events.description: JOHN CROFT/Star Tribune via Getty ImagesEd Gein admitted that he killed two women, and police found human skin, bone, and other remains in his Plainfield, Wisconsin home.

events.title: Diane Schuler Crashes On The Taconic Parkway
events.description: Diane Schuler crashes while driving the wrong way on New York's Taconic Parkway, killing all but one passenger. After going on a weekend camping trip with her children and nieces, Diane packed up her minivan and prepared to make the trip back home. A few hours into the trip, witnesses reported seeing a minivan driving aggressively and another reported seeing a woman vomiting next to her minivan on the side of the road.

events.title: Maximilien Robespierre Is Overthrown
events.description: Maximilien Robespierre is overthrown and arrested in Paris during the French Revolution. A revolutionary himself, Robespierre rose to power by speaking out against the monarchy and advocating for democratic reforms. But his embrace of violence during the infamous Reign of Terror made Robespierre unpopular, leading to his arrest and execution a day later by guillotine.

events.title: Vincent van Gogh Shoots Himself
events.description: Vincent van Gogh's "Self-Portrait," painted in 1887.

events.title: Scientists Isolate Insulin
events.description: Frederick Banting and Charles Best isolate insulin for the first time. Banting, a Canadian surgeon, and Best, a University of Toronto medical student, made the discovery by experimenting with dogs. Their discovery turned diabetes from a fatal disease into a manageable one.

events.title: The Summer Olympics Are Bombed In Atlanta
events.description: A nail-filled pipe bomb explodes in Centennial Olympic Park in Atlanta, Georgia, killing one and injuring more than 100. Though suspicion initially fell on security guard Richard Jewell, a number of other bombs were subsequently detonated at locations like abortion clinics and gay clubs. Evidence finally led authorities to a carpenter named Eric Rudolph, who they captured in 2003 after a long manhunt.

events.title: Adam Walsh Is Kidnapped
events.description: TwitterAdam Walsh was just six years old when he was kidnapped and killed in Florida.

events.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard Is Born
events.description: Gypsy Rose Blanchard is born in Golden Meadow, Louisiana. She would later make headlines for orchestrating the murder of her mother, Dee Dee Blanchard, after suffering from a lifetime of abuse stemming from her mother's Munchausen by proxy syndrome.

events.title: Henry VIII Marries Catherine Howard
events.description: King Henry VIII weds Catherine Howard at Oatlands Palace in Surrey. The marriage, Henry's fifth, didn't last. Less than two years after their wedding, Henry had her beheaded after allegations of Catherine's sexual past came to light.

events.title: Johann Sebastian Bach Dies
events.description: Johann Sebastian Bach is one of the most well-known classic composers in history.

events.title: A Plane Crashes Into The Empire State Building
events.description: A B-25 Mitchell bomber with two pilots and one passenger crashes into the Empire State Building. The crash, caused by heavy fog, triggered a massive explosion between the 75th and 79th floors. Fourteen people died, and the impact caused the modern equivalent of $10.5 million in damages.

events.title: The Great Tangshan Earthquake Hits
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesThe aftermath of the Tangshan Earthquake.

events.title: The First Victims Of The Atlanta Child Killer Are Found
events.description: The bodies of 14-year-old Edward Hope Smith and 13-year-old Alfred Evans are discovered in southwest Atlanta, days after both boys went missing. The first victims of the so-called Atlanta Child Killer, their deaths were followed by at least 26 other murders. In 1981, police arrested Wayne Williams, who was found guilty of two of the murders and sentenced to life in prison.

events.title: The Spanish Armada Is Defeated
events.description: The Spanish Armada is defeated by the English during a battle off the coast of Gravelines, France. The Spanish, who hoped to conquer England and bring the country back under Catholic rule, were forced into a retreat after eight hours of fighting. During their return journey, half of Spain's fleet perished from shipwrecks, storms, and a lack of supplies.

events.title: King Umberto I Of Italy Is Assassinated
events.description: King Umberto I of Italy circa 1882.

events.title: Clara Bow, The Original Flapper, Is Born
events.description: Clara Bow, the original flapper and the "it girl" of the 1920s, is born in Brooklyn, New York.

events.title: The Lord Of The Rings Is Published
events.description: The Lord of the Rings is first published in the United Kingdom. The book's author, J. R. R. Tolkien, decided to write the series after the success of his children's book The Hobbit. The Lord of the Rings is considered one of the greatest fantasy books ever written and has left a significant mark on popular culture. It is one of the best-selling books in history, with over 150 million copies sold.

events.title: NASA Is Founded
events.description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is established by the U.S. Congress. Less than a year earlier, the Soviet Union had taken the first leap in the "Space Race" by sending a satellite called Sputnik I into outer space. NASA, tasked with building out America's space program, made history about a decade later by putting a man on the moon on July 20, 1969.

events.title: Mama Cass Elliot Dies
events.description: Donaldson Collection/Getty ImagesMama Cass Elliot circa 1970.

events.title: Mickey Cohen Dies
events.description: Mickey Cohen, the mob boss who controlled 1950s Los Angeles, dies of stomach cancer. In the 1940s, Cohen was Bugsy Siegel's right hand man. In the 1950s, he would led the LA-based Cohen crime family.

events.title: Baghdad Is Founded
events.description: The city of Baghdad is founded by Abbasid caliph al-Mansur as the capital of the Abbasid dynasty. For hundreds of years, the intricately designed city reigned as one of the most important in the region — until the Mongols conquered it in the 13th century. Today, Baghdad is the capital of Iraq.

events.title: Miguel Hidalgo Is Executed
events.description: Miguel Hidalgo portrayed as the father of Mexico in a 1905 painting.

events.title: Emily Brontë Is Born
events.description: Emily Brontë is born in Yorkshire, England. A writer, Brontë produced just one novel in her life, Wuthering Heights (1847). But her haunting tale of love and revenge on the English moors is considered a masterpiece today.

events.title: Otto von Bismarck Dies
events.description: Otto von Bismarck, a Prussian-born statesman and the first chancellor of the German Empire, dies a the age of 83. Bismarck is one of the most influential figures in German history. As a statesman, Bismarck oversaw the unification of Germany and gained a reputation in Europe as a master diplomat and peacemaker. Under his leadership, modern Germany began to take shape.

events.title: The USS Indianapolis Is Sunk By Japanese Torpedoes
events.description: The USS Indianapolis is sunk by a Japanese submarine in the Philippine Sea, plunging 900 men into the shark-infested waters. As many as 150 were killed by sharks, and only 316 men survived.

events.title: Jimmy Hoffa Disappears
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJimmy Hoffa bolstered the power of unions before he mysteriously disappeared, possibly after being abducted and murdered by the mob.

events.title: Daniel Defoe Is Placed In A Pillory
events.description: A depiction of Daniel Defoe in the pillory, and the flowers people threw at his feet.

events.title: A Hurricane Sinks Spanish Treasure Ships
events.description: A hurricane sinks 10 Spanish ships full of gold and silver off the coast of present-day Florida. The ships, en route home from Cuba, sank swiftly in the storm, killing around 1,000 people. Though Spain recovered much of the lost treasure the next year, it took until the 1960s to recover it all.

events.title: Andrew Johnson Dies
events.description: Andrew Johnson in 1875, the year that he died.

events.title: An F4 Tornado Hits Edmonton, Canada
events.description: A tornado tears through Edmonton, Canada. The powerful storm, which raged for an hour, killed 27 people, injured more than 300, and destroyed more than 300 homes. It's considered one of the worst natural disasters in Canadian history.

events.title: Further Events That Happened On This Day In History
events.description: 1774: English scientist Joseph Priestley discovers oxygen.

events.title: Henry III Of France Is Assassinated
events.description: Henry III was only 35 when he was assassinated in 1589.

events.title: Queen Anne Of England Dies
events.description: Queen Anne pictured with her son William, Duke of Gloucester, who died at age 11.

events.title: Francis Scott Key Is Born
events.description: Francis Scott Key portrait by Joseph Wood, circa 1825.

events.title: Seth Bullock Arrives In Deadwood
events.description: Seth Bullock, a former lawman, arrives in Deadwood, South Dakota, and soon succeeds in "taming" the rambunctious Wild West town.

events.title: Anne Frank Writes Her Final Diary Entry
events.description: Anne Frank makes a final entry in her diary three days before the Gestapo capture her and her family. The 15-year-old girl wrote, "I... keep trying to find a way to become what I'd like to be and what I could be if... if only there were no other people in the world." After her capture, Frank was sent to the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, where she died in February or March 1945.

events.title: The Warsaw Uprising Begins
events.description: The Warsaw Uprising, a failed attempt to liberate Warsaw from German control, begins in Poland.

events.title: The First Zodiac Letter Arrives At The San Fransisco Chronicle Office
events.description: Following a string of killings, the Zodiac killer pens a letter to multiple newspapers in northern California, including the San Fransisco Chronicle.

events.title: George R.R. Martin's A Game Of Thrones Is Published
events.description: A Game of Thrones, the first novel in George R.R. Martin's epic fantasy saga is released. Martin would go on to write a total of five books for his "A Song of Ice and Fire" series, which was later adapted into the HBO hit show Game of Thrones. The author has said he intends to release two more books to finish the series.

events.title: Henry Hudson Sails Into What Is Now Hudson Bay
events.description: A depiction of Henry Hudson's ship from his 1609 voyage, the Half Moon, in what would become known as the Hudson River.

events.title: The First U.S. Census Is Conducted
events.description: The first U.S. census take place, counting almost 4 million free citizens and almost 700,000 enslaved people. The most populous state was Virginia, with 747,610 residents. The least populated state was Delaware, with 59,094 residents. At the completion of the first census, many expressed skepticism over the results, given the considerable amount of people living in rural areas and the lack of infrastructure to reach them. Today, the census occurs ever 10 years in the United States and requires mandatory participation.

events.title: The First Cable Car Begins Operating In San Francisco
events.description: The Clay Street Hill Railroad company tests its first cable car on San Francisco's Clay Street at 4 a.m. They had begun building a cable line on the street in May 1873, and the line opened to the public a month after its initial test was conducted. Today, San Francisco's cable cars are a National Historic Landmark and an iconic part of the city's very identity.

events.title: Wild Bill Hickok Dies
events.description: A cabinet card of Wild Bill Hickok. 1873.

events.title: U.S. President Warren G. Harding Dies In Office
events.description: Warren G. Harding was the 29th President of the United States.

events.title: The Gulf War Begins
events.description: Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein invades Kuwait, marking the start of the Gulf War.

events.title: William Wallace Is Captured
events.description: William Wallace riding into battle.

events.title: Christopher Columbus Sets Sail For The New World
events.description: Christopher Columbus sets off on what would become his famous journey to the New World. The Nina, the Pinta, and the Santa Maria set sail from Palos de la Frontera, Spain under the sponsorship of monarchs Ferdinand II and Isabella I. Columbus was seeking a western route to the Far East, but he didn't expect the American continents to be in his way.

events.title: Germany And France Declare War On Each Other
events.description: Germany and France declare war on each other, intensifying Europe's march toward World War I.

events.title: Sir Roger Casement Is Hanged For Treason
events.description: Diplomat and Irish nationalist Sir Roger Casement is executed for treason after seeking German military aid for Easter Rising, the 1916 insurrection for Irish independence from British rule. During World War I, Casement sought German aid hoping that the Germans would want to assist Ireland's cause as an additional blow against Britain. Because of his execution, Casement became one of the most famous martyrs in the fight for Irish independence.

events.title: Jesse Owens Wins His First Gold Medal At The Berlin Olympics
events.description: Associated PressJesse Owens salutes during the presentation of the gold medal for the long jump event at the Berlin Olympics.

events.title: The U.S.S. Nautilus Travels Under The North Pole
events.description: The USS Nautilus was the world's first nuclear submarine.

events.title: Dom Pérignon Invents Champagne
events.description: Benedictine monk Dom Pierre Pérignon invents Champagne at his abbey in Hautvillers, France. According to legend, Pérignon supposedly called out, "Come quickly, I am drinking the stars!" when he first took a sip of his creation. Despite such mythology, the historical record shows that modern Champagne wasn't invented until the mid-19th century, long after Pérignon's death.

events.title: The Ax Murders Of Andrew and Abby Borden
events.description: The Fall River house where Andrew and Abby Borden were killed.

events.title: Anne Frank Is Captured By The Gestapo
events.description: Anne Frank attends school in Amsterdam in 1940, two years before she went into hiding along with her family.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe Dies
events.description: E. Murray/Fox Photos/Getty ImagesThe room where Marilyn Monroe died.

events.title: Carlina White Goes Missing
events.description: Carlina White goes missing from a Harlem hospital. After baby Carlina showed signs of an infection, her parents Joy White and Carl Tyson rushed her to the hospital. Hours later, a woman entered Carlina's room and abducted her. Joy White and Carl Tyson would not see their child again for 23 years.

events.title: Henry I Becomes King Of England
events.description: Henry I, the youngest son of William the Conqueror, is crowned king of England after his brother dies in a hunting accident. Henry brought peace to England and in 1106, bested his eldest brother to become the Duke of Normandy. Ultimately, he was succeeded by his nephew, Stephen of Blois, although he had planned for his daughter Matilda to take the throne, which resulted in a period of civil war called the Anarchy.

events.title: The Mayflower Makes Its Failed First Attempt To Depart England
events.description: Mayflower in Plymouth Harbor by William Halsall. 1882.

events.title: Anna Haining Bates Dies
events.description: Anna Haining Bates, one half of the tallest married couple ever, dies in Seville, Ohio, at the age of 41.

events.title: Neil Armstrong Is Born
events.description: NASANeil Armstrong was commander of the Apollo 11 mission that landed humans on the Moon for the first time.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe's Body Is Discovered
events.description: Keystone/Getty ImagesMedical attendants remove the body of Marilyn Monroe from her home.

events.title: Dalia Dippolito Is Arrested For Trying To Have Her Husband Killed
events.description: Police call Dalia Dippolito and inform her that her husband Mike has been murdered — but it was all a set-up. Dalia broke down when police told her of her husband's death, but in reality she had hired a hitman to have him killed. That hitman turned out to be an undercover cop, who led officers in a sting operation against her. Meanwhile, her husband Mike Dippolito was alive and well. In the end, Dalia Dippolito was sentenced to 16 years in prison.

events.title: Anna Haining Bates, One Of The Tallest Women In The World, Is Born
events.description: Anna Haining Bates, a woman who stood at 7 feet 11 inches tall, is born in Canada.

events.title: The First Execution By Electric Chair Takes Place
events.description: The electric chair in which William Kemmler was executed.

events.title: Andy Warhol Is Born
events.description: Famed American artist Andy Warhol is born Andrew Warhola in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Warhol was a leading figure in the pop art movement of the 1960s, and his best-known works include the Campbell's Soup Cans and Marilyn Diptych silkscreen paintings. He was also a filmmaker, creating underground films such as Chelsea Girls. Warhol died in 1987 after gallbladder surgery and dictated that his estate be used to create the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts.

events.title: The Atomic Bomb Is Dropped On Hiroshima
events.description: U.S. Department of Defense Aerial views of Hiroshima before and after the bombing.

events.title: The Alpha Dog Abduction Occurs
events.description: The Alpha Dog kidnapping is committed in Santa Barbara, California. Benjamin Markowitz hung out with the "wrong crowd," and his half-brother, Nicholas, would pay for it. Local gang leader Jesse James Hollywood worked with Benjamin to sell drugs in the area. After Benjamin backed out, Hollywood wanted revenge.

events.title: Cyntoia Brown Murders Johnny Allen
events.description: Cyntoia Brown, a 16-year-old victim of child sex trafficking, shoots and kills 43-year-old Johnny Allen, who she claimed offered her $150 to have sex with him. After meeting Allen in the parking lot of a Sonic Drive-In, she returned with him to his house. They never engaged in sexual intercourse, but Brown shot him in the back of the head, stole his money and two guns, and fled in his truck.

events.title: Elizabeth Báthory Is Born
events.description: Elizabeth Báthory, a Hungarian noblewoman and alleged serial killer, is born. Báthory was accused of torturing and murdering hundreds of women and young girls between 1590 and 1610. More than 300 individuals described seeing evidence of these crimes, but others believe the accusations were fabricated to destroy her family's influence in the region. Nevertheless, Báthory was imprisoned in the Castle of Csejte in 1610, where she died four years later.

events.title: George Washington Creates The Purple Heart Award
events.description: While commander-in-chief of the Continental Army during the American Revolution, George Washington establishes the Badge of Military Merit, a purple cloth heart that will later become the modern Purple Heart award. The badge was to be given to a soldier "whenever any singularly meritorious action is performed."

events.title: Mata Hari Is Born
events.description: Mata Hari was famed for her revealing costumes.

events.title: Thor Heyerdahl Completes His Voyage Across The Pacific Ocean In A Raft
events.description: Keystone/Getty ImagesThor Heyerdahl aboard his Kon-Tiki raft in 1947.

events.title: The Winchester Mystery House Becomes A Historical Landmark
events.description: The Winchester Mystery House at the time Sarah Winchester resided there.

events.title: The White House Farm Murders
events.description: PA Images via Getty ImagesThe Essex farmhouse at Tolleshunt D'Arcy near Maldon where Jeremy Bamber shot his family.

events.title: Brigham Young Is Chosen To Lead The Mormon Church
events.description: Brigham Young becomes the leader of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints after founder Joseph Smith is murdered by an angry mob. During his time as the Church's leader, Young led 148 Mormon pioneers from Illinois to the Salt Lake Valley, where he founded Salt Lake City. He then established what is now known as Brigham Young University.

events.title: Emiliano Zapata Is Born
events.description: Emiliano Zapata in 1914.

events.title: The Endurance Departs From Plymouth, England
events.description: Famed explorer Ernest Shackleton and the crew of the Endurance set sail for Antarctica, marking the beginning of a perilous journey that would leave them stranded and fighting for their lives.

events.title: England's "Great Train Robbery"
events.description: The "South West Gang" pulls off the largest train robbery in British history, stealing 2.6 million pounds sterling — the equivalent of over $70 million in today's dollars. Bruce Reynolds, Gordon Goody, Ronald Edwards, and Charlie Wilson joined forces with a dozen other criminals known as the "South Coast Raiders" to board the train, beat the conductor, and get away with the massive loot in what would be one of the biggest heists in history.

events.title: Richard Nixon Resigns
events.description: FlickrRichard Nixon leaves the White House after his resignation.

events.title: Serial Killer Shelly Knotek Is Arrested
events.description: Serial killer and mom Shelly Knotek is arrested in Washington. Known as a selfless family, the Knoteks would always open their home to strangers. Unfortunately, those that stayed in the Knotek home rarely made it out.

events.title: Construction Begins On The Leaning Tower Of Pisa
events.description: PicrylThe tower's tilt reached its height in 1990, before restoration work helped lessen its trademark lean.

events.title: Henry David Thoreau Publishes Walden
events.description: Henry David Thoreau's famous book Walden, or, A Life In The Woods, is published. At the age of 27, Thoreau moved to Walden Pond in Concord, Massachusetts, and built a small cabin in order to live off the land and document his views on politics, philosophy, and nature. The result was Walden, a series of essays about his time of experimental simple living.

events.title: The Pawpaw Tree Incident Takes Places
events.description: The Pawpaw Tree Incident takes place in Kentucky when three members of the McCoy family, Tolbert, Pharmer, and Randolph Jr., are tied to pawpaw bushes and killed by members of the Hatfield family in retribution for the murder of Ellison Hatfield.

events.title: Jesse Owens Wins His Fourth Gold Medal
events.description: Black American track and field athlete Jesse Owens wins a gold medal in the 4 × 100 m sprint relay at the 1936 Olympic Games in Berlin, Germany. It was Owens' fourth gold of the competition, and outraged prominent Nazis like Joseph Goebbels.

events.title: The Bombing Of Nagasaki
events.description: An atomic cloud rises over the city of Nagasaki after the bombing on August 9, 1945.

events.title: The Manson Family Murders Begin
events.description: FlickrOn August 9, 1969, the Manson Family killed five people inside this house at 10050 Cielo Drive.

events.title: Warren Jeffs Is Sentenced To Life In Prison
events.description: Warren Jeffs, president of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, is sentenced to life in prison plus 20 years for two counts of felony child sexual assault.

events.title: The Warship Vasa Sinks
events.description: The Swedish warship Vasa sinks less than a mile into her maiden voyage. Heralded as a paragon of modern engineering, the 226-foot ship had the capacity to carry 64 heavy cannons. However, within 20 minutes of launching, the overburdened ship tipped and sank in front of the thousands of spectators who had gathered to watch her depart from Stockholm.

events.title: The Louvre Opens In Paris
events.description: The Louvre Museum in Paris, France.

events.title: The Smithsonian Institution Is Established
events.description: An Act of Congress establishes the Smithsonian Institution, the world's largest museum and research complex. The initial funds for the museum came from the estate of British scientist James Smithson, who left his money to the U.S. government for the purpose of "an establishment for the increase and diffusion of knowledge."

events.title: Jim Morrison's Indecent Exposure Trial Begins
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesJim Morrison performing in Germany in 1968.

events.title: The "Son of Sam" Is Arrested
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesDavid Berkowitz, a.k.a. "Son of Sam," poses for a mugshot following his arrest on August 11, 1977.

events.title: Journalist Kim Wall Goes Missing After Boarding Peter Madsen's Submarine
events.description: Swedish journalist Kim Wall was a highly respected freelancer, working on a story about the Danish billionaire inventor Peter Madsen. Madsen invited Wall to an interview on his new miniature submarine, the Nautilus, from which he later had to be rescued as it began to sink into the ocean. Wall's torso was later found on a beach, and in a 2020 documentary, Madsen admitted to killing Wall on board the submarine before intentionally sinking it.

events.title: Robert Ingersoll Is Born
events.description: "The Great Agnostic" Robert G. Ingersoll is born in Dresden, New York. The lawyer, politician, and orator earned his nickname by campaigning in defense of agnosticism during the Golden Age of Free Thought in the mid-19th century, when he popularized scientific rationalism and criticism of the Bible. Ingersoll became a successful attorney general for the state of Illinois, but his religious views kept the Republican Party from appointing him to higher posts.

events.title: The First Civilian Prisoners Arrive At Alcatraz
events.description: National Park ServiceA guard stands watch as prisoners enter Alcatraz's mess hall for a meal in 1955.

events.title: The Watts Rebellion Begins
events.description: The Watts Rebellion was the most destructive uprising of its kind in the city's history until the Rodney King riots of 1992.

events.title: Poughkeepsie Killer Kendall Francois Is Sentenced To Life In Prison
events.description: The Poughkeepsie Killer Kendall Francois is sentenced to life in prison for the murders of eight women. Known by his nickname "Stinky," Francois was noted by his coworkers and family as always emanating a horrendous stench. Police would later realize that the stench came from the multiple bodies that Francois had stashed inside his New York home.

events.title: Robin Williams Dies
events.description: Peter Kramer/Getty ImagesRobin Williams in 2006.

events.title: Cleopatra Dies By Suicide
events.description: The Death of Cleopatra by Reginald Arthur. 1892.

events.title: Minnie Dean Is Executed
events.description: New Zealand serial killer Minnie Dean is hanged after being convicted of infanticide. Earlier that year, she was seen boarding a train with a baby and a hatbox, then leaving the train without the baby and a suspiciously heavy hatbox, according to railroad porters. Police soon dug up her garden and found the bodies of three children. Dean is the only woman to be executed in the history of New Zealand.

events.title: The Wizard Of Oz Premieres
events.description: MGMThough it struggled to break even during its theatrical run, the film has since become one of the most enduring classics in the history of American cinema.

events.title: Joseph P. Kennedy Jr. Is Killed
events.description: Joseph P. Kennedy Jr., the older brother of John F. Kennedy, is killed during a World War II mission known as Operation Aphrodite.

events.title: Buford Pusser's Wife Is Murdered
events.description: Buford Pusser's wife, Pauline, is murdered while investigating a disturbance out of town. Buford Pusser was a sheriff in Tennessee known for his crackdowns on crime and corruption. After his wife was fatally shot while tagging along on her husband's work call, Pusser became hell-bent on getting revenge.

events.title: History's Most Complete Tyrannosaurus Rex Fossil Is Discovered
events.description: "Sue" the Tyrannosaurus rex in the Field Museum of Natural History in Chicago, Illinois.

events.title: The Aztec Capital Falls To Hernán Cortés
events.description: A portrait of Hernán Cortés.

events.title: King Louis XVI Of France Is Arrested
events.description: King Louis XVI of France is arrested for treason and declared an enemy of the people. The French Revolution was in full swing, and the country's lower classes were fighting back against the country's vast social inequality and absolute monarchy. Louis and his wife, Queen Marie Antoinette, had been forced to flee Versailles and accept a new constitution that reduced them to mere figureheads with no real power.

events.title: Annie Oakley Is Born
events.description: Annie Oakley in 1889.

events.title: Construction Begins On The Berlin Wall
events.description: The Berlin Wall as seen in 1986, just three years before it finally fell.

events.title: Julia Child Dies At The Age Of 91
events.description: Julia Child dies at the age of 91 in Montecito, California. A beloved American chef and television personality, Julia Child did not always know that she was destined to be a culinary icon. During World War II, Julia Child worked as a spy for the CIA. It was during this time that she uncovered her love for recipes and cooking, while also developing a shark repellant recipe for the CIA.

events.title: Mary Blandy Poisons Her Father
events.description: Wellcome Library, LondonA depiction of Mary Blandy's execution.

events.title: Russians Settle Alaska
events.description: Russian explorer Grigory Shelekhov finds Russia's first permanent settlement in Alaska at Three Saints Bay.

events.title: Doc Holliday Is Born
events.description: Doc Holliday in Tombstone, Arizona circa 1882.

events.title: Construction Is Completed On The Cologne Cathedral
events.description: After more than 600 years of construction, Germany's Cologne Cathedral is finally completed. The 515-foot building is the tallest twin-spired church in the world as well as the largest Gothic church in Northern Europe.

events.title: The Boxer Rebellion Is Crushed
events.description: European, American, and Japanese forces seize Beijing to crush the Boxer Rebellion. The Boxer Rebellion was an anti-foreigner rebellion fought by the "boxers," or Chinese villagers, many of whom had martial arts experience. At the time, Western missionaries were prevalent in China, spreading Christianity. China had lost the Sino-Japanese War five years earlier, and ordinary Chinese people worried that foreign interference would eventually take over the Qing government.

events.title: World War II Comes To An End
events.description: The iconic "V-J Day in Times Square" photo captured by Alfred Eisenstaedt.

events.title: Napoleon Is Born
events.description: A portrait of Napoleon Bonaparte by Jacques-Louis David. 1812.

events.title: The Opening Of The Panama Canal
events.description: After 10 years of construction, the Panama Canal opens to boat traffic. The canal made it easier than ever before for ships to travel from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean, as they no longer had to navigate around South America. The French initially attempted to build the canal starting in 1881, but they were forced to stop due to engineering problems and a high mortality rate among workers. The United States took over in 1904, completing the 51-mile-long canal.

events.title: India Gains Independence
events.description: The Indian Independence Bill takes effect, creating the independent countries of India and Pakistan and bringing an end to British rule in the region. The British had controlled India since 1757, but after World War II, Mahatma Gandhi and other leaders organized the "Quit India" campaign, which led to their arrest by British authorities. Though Britain did eventually grant India's independence, it led to a period of religious turmoil between Muslims and Hindus. This strife would soon inspire one extremist to assassinate Gandhi within months of India winning its independence.

events.title: Konrad Schumann Leaps Into Freedom
events.description: Taken by Peter Leibing on August 15, 1961, Konrad Schumann abandons his post guarding the new Berlin Wall, defecting to West Germany.

events.title: Woodstock Begins
events.description: A small portion of the crowd at Woodstock, which ultimately welcomed more than eight times the amount of attendees that they had planned for.

events.title: The First Transatlantic Telegraph Is Sent
events.description: Queen Victoria sends the world's first transatlantic telegraph, congratulating United States President James Buchanan on the success of Britain and the U.S. at building the new telegraph cable. The new ability to quickly send and receive information across the Atlantic Ocean would be revolutionary for news, business, and trade. Unfortunately, the new cable stopped working after just a few weeks, and it would be eight years before there was consistent overseas communication via telegraph.

events.title: Gold Is Discovered In The Yukon Territory
events.description: U.S. National Park ServiceMen line up to cross Chilkoot Pass on their way to the Klondike.

events.title: Madonna Is Born
events.description: Madonna, the "Queen of Pop," is born Madonna Louise Ciccone in Bay City, Michigan. The singer dropped out of college and moved to New York City to pursue a career in dance, and five years later she released her debut album, skyrocketing her to fame. Today, Madonna is the best-selling female music artist of all time with more than 300 million records sold around the world. She's also the highest-grossing solo touring artist of all time.

events.title: Elvis Presley Dies
events.description: Elvis Presley was just 42 years old when he died suddenly, leaving his fans around the world stunned.

events.title: Aretha Franklin Dies
events.description: Aretha Franklin, the "Queen of Soul," dies in Detroit, Michigan. Franklin remains beloved around the world to this day, known for her hit songs like "Respect" and "(You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman." Three days before Franklin's death, the media caught wind that she was seriously ill. Other artists like Stevie Wonder and Jesse Jackson all visited her while she rested at home before passing away at the age of 76 from pancreatic cancer. Rolling Stone has called her "the greatest singer of her generation."

events.title: Davy Crockett Is Born
events.description: A portrait of Davy Crockett by John Gadsby Chapman. Unknown date.

events.title: Billy The Kid Kills His First Man
events.description: One of the only authenticated photos of Billy the Kid. Circa 1879-1880.

events.title: James Jameson Dies
events.description: A 19th-century explorer and heir to the Jameson Irish Whiskey fortune, James Jameson dies of a fever, shortly after he's implicated in a gruesome incident of cannibalism involving a young enslaved girl.

events.title: Mark Felt Is Born
events.description: Mark Felt, better known as the anonymous source "Deep Throat" from the Watergate scandal, is born in Twin Falls, Idaho.

events.title: David Koresh Is Born
events.description: Vernon Howell, later known as Branch Davidian leader David Koresh, is born in Houston, Texas.

events.title: Peter Fechter Is Killed While Trying To Cross The Berlin Wall
events.description: Peter Fechter, a German bricklayer, is shot by East German border guards while trying to cross the Berlin Wall into West Berlin. The 18-year-old and his friend Helmut Kulbeik plotted their daring escape attempt carefully, and Kulbeik actually made it across the wall safely. Fechter, however, was shot in the pelvis while climbing the wall, and East German guards refused to let anyone provide medical attention. He bled out in front of hundreds of onlookers, and the guards who shot him were found guilty of manslaughter decades later in 1997.

events.title: The Stanford Experiment Begins
events.description: The Stanford Prison Experiment, meant to study the dynamics between prison guards and inmates, begins. The experiment was meant to last for two weeks but was canceled after just six days because of the guards' cruelty.

events.title: First Transatlantic Balloon Flight Takes Place
events.description: Ben Abruzzo, Maxie Anderson, and Larry Newman become the first people to cross the Atlantic Ocean in a helium-filled balloon. The three adventurers had boarded a balloon named the Double Eagle II in Presque Isle, Maine. Just over 137 hours later, they safely landed in Miserey, France, about 50 miles from Paris. This was the 14th known attempt to cross the Atlantic in a balloon.

events.title: Azaria Chamberlain Disappears
events.description: Nine-week-old Azaria Chamberlain vanishes while camping with her family in Australia. Her mother Lindy's claim that she was taken by a "dingo" was met with mockery and distrust — and Lindy was jailed for murder — but investigators proved six years later that dingoes, had, in fact, taken the baby.

events.title: Genghis Khan Dies
events.description: Genghis Khan, as portrayed in a 14th-century Yuan-era album.

events.title: Roanoke Colony Is Found Deserted
events.description: The Lost Colony, design by William Ludwell Sheppard, engraving by William James Linton.

events.title: Butch Cassidy Tries To Organize A Train Robbers' Syndicate
events.description: Wild West outlaw Butch Cassidy allegedly attempts to form a Train Robbers' Syndicate of over 200 outlaws. Instead, many of these outlaws split into their own groups, the most infamous of which was Cassidy's Wild Bunch. Today, the Wild Bunch is remembered as the most successful train-robbing gang in history.

events.title: Women Win The Right To Vote In The United States
events.description: The 19th Amendment to the United States Constitution is ratified, legally guaranteeing women the right to vote in America. Suffragists had protested for the right for decades and the amendment was first introduced to Congress in 1878. Some states had already passed laws giving women the right to vote, but it wasn't until Tennessee ratified the amendment on August 18, 1920, that it obtained the support of three-fourths of the states needed to make it a right across America.

events.title: Yangtze River Peaks In A Catastrophic Flood
events.description: After weeks of heavy rainfall in China, the Yangtze River peaks at 53 feet above its average levels. The flood spread over a 500-square-mile area and killed about 3.7 million people, making it one of the worst natural disasters of the 20th century.

events.title: Sally Horner, The "Real Life Lolita," Dies
events.description: Sally Horner, who's kidnapping is believed to have been part of the inspiration behind the book Lolita, dies in a car accident at 15 years old. She was kidnapped four years earlier by Frank La Salle, a convicted rapist, and had been rescued just two years before her death.

events.title: Emperor Augustus Dies
events.description: A bust of Emperor Augustus. Circa 30 B.C.E.

events.title: George Burroughs Is Hanged During The Salem Witch Trials
events.description: George Burroughs and four other victims of the Salem Witch Trials are hanged for witchcraft in one of the town's many rounds of executions.

events.title: The French Academy Of Sciences Debuts The Daguerreotype
events.description: Two years after Louis Daguerre creates the daguerreotype process, the French government awards him a lifetime pension and releases the details of the process to the world for free.

events.title: Orville Wright Is Born
events.description: Orville Wright in 1905.

events.title: The Great Purge Begins In The Soviet Union
events.description: The Great Purge begins as an effort to rid the Soviet Union of Joseph Stalin's political rivals' influence. The purge saw the executions of old Communist Party leadership and government officials before expanding to certain ethnic minorities, peasants, intellectuals, and ordinary citizens who were in the wrong place at the wrong time. This period lasted about two years, during which an estimated 700,000 to 1.2 million people died.

events.title: Otto Frank Dies
events.description: Otto Frank, the father of Anne Frank who later published her diaries, dies in Birsfelden, Switzerland, at the age of 91

events.title: Don Lewis Is Reported Missing
events.description: Don Lewis, the millionaire husband of big cat enthusiast Carole Baskin, is reported missing from his Tampa, Florida home and wildlife sanctuary.

events.title: Jared Fogle Is Arrested On Child Pornography Charges
events.description: The U.S. Attorney's Office announces that Jared Fogle, the Subway spokesperson commonly known as "Jared from Subway," has been arrested for possession of child pornography and traveling across state lines to engage in commercial sex with minors. When the executive director of Fogle's non-profit, Russell Taylor, was arrested in early 2015, authorities discovered that Taylor had been sending child porn to Fogle directly and arrested him.

events.title: The First Enslaved Africans Arrive In Jamestown Colony
events.description: Around 20 enslaved Africans who had been captured by Portuguese forces in Angola arrive in Jamestown. They disembarked from the White Lion ship at Point Comfort, near what is today Hampton, Virginia. Though they were not the first enslaved Africans to set foot in what would become the United States, their arrival marked a turning point for slavery in North America — as it helped introduce the transatlantic slave trade to Jamestown and other settlements.

events.title: John Milton Publishes Paradise Lost
events.description: Paradise Lost, John Milton's epic poem about the biblical Fall of Mankind, is released. The work is considered to be Milton's masterpiece, and it is mostly because of Paradise Lost that he is today known as one of the greatest English writers of all time. Milton wrote the poem between 1658 and 1663 — dictating it to others, as he'd gone blind in 1652.

events.title: Leon Trotsky Is Killed In Mexico
events.description: Leon Trotsky in the early 1920s.

events.title: Czechoslovakia's Prague Spring Ends With Soviet Invasion
events.description: Czechoslovakia's Prague Spring ends as a result of a Soviet invasion. For about seven months, Czechoslovakians enjoyed a brief period of liberal reforms in politics and economics. Alexander Dubček, a Czechoslovakian leader, became the figurehead of the liberalizing movement, dubbed the Prague Spring. However, Moscow was deeply unhappy with the reforms and expressed to Dubček that there would be consequences if the country continued to pursue liberalization. By August, the Soviet Union launched an invasion, putting an end to the Prague Spring.

events.title: The Menendez Brothers Kill Their Parents
events.description: Ted Soqui/Sygma/Getty ImagesLyle and Erik Menendez were sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

events.title: Nat Turner Launches A Rebellion Of Enslaved People
events.description: Nat Turner leads a rebellion of around 75 enslaved Africans against their enslavers in Southampton County, Virginia. They killed about 55 white people in the area, making it the deadliest slave revolt in the history of the United States. The rebellion was suppressed after a few days, and Turner was tracked down and executed about six weeks later.

events.title: The Mona Lisa Is Stolen
events.description: The Mona Lisa is returned to the Louvre after being stolen.

events.title: The Kelly-Hopkinsville UFO Incident Takes Place
events.description: The Sutton family from Kelly, Kentucky rushes into the police station in nearby Hopkinsville and claims a UFO landed on their farm. Multiple family members swore they saw aliens disembark and peep into their windows.

events.title: Hawaii Becomes The 50th U.S. State
events.description: Hawaii becomes the 50th state of the United States. Back in the 19th century, Hawaii was ruled by a monarchy and was deeply economically tied to the United States. But in 1887, a group of non-native businessmen and lawyers forced Hawaiian King Kalākaua to sign a constitution that stripped power from the monarchy and prevented most Native Hawaiians from voting.

events.title: Carbon Dioxide Erupts From Lake Nyos In Cameroon
events.description: Lake Nyos, eight days after the eruption.

events.title: The Ruby Ridge Siege Begins
events.description: The Ruby Ridge siege begins near Ruby Ridge in Idaho when federal agents preparing to arrest white separatist Randy Weaver come across his son and dog in the woods, resulting in a shootout that leaves Deputy U.S. Marshal William F. Degan, 14-year-old Sammy Weaver, and the dog, Striker, dead.

events.title: Battle Of Bosworth Field Takes Place
events.description: Richard III and Henry Tudor fight in the center of Bosworth Field, as painted by Abraham Cooper in 1825.

events.title: "Night Of Fire" Sets Off The Haitian Revolution
events.description: The Haitian War of Independence begins with the "Night of Fire," with more than 100,000 enslaved men and women rising up against French control. They burned plantations and executed as many French people as they could find. Toussaint Louverture quickly became a leader of the revolution, which succeeded in achieving Haitian independence in 1804.

events.title: Michael Collins Is Assassinated
events.description: Michael Collins, an Irish revolutionary and member of Sinn Fein, is assassinated in County Cork, Ireland. The previous year, he agreed to the Anglo-Irish Treaty, which partitioned Ireland into the independent Irish Free State (now the Republic of Ireland) and Northern Ireland, which remained under the control of the United Kingdom. Collins was shot to death by anti-treaty forces who wanted revenge for his role in it.

events.title: "Devil's Island" Penal Colony Closes
events.description: Antoine Hubert/FlickrDevil's Island, also called Île du Diable, is one of French Guiana's Îles du Salut, or Salvation Islands.

events.title: "Mr Cruel" Begins His Crime Spree In Australia
events.description: The yet-unidentified child rapist known only as "Mr Cruel" begins his attacks against girls in Melbourne, Australia. Dressed in a ski mask, he broke into a home in the quiet neighborhood of Lower Plenty. He bound the parents and son, then sexually assaulted the 11-year-old daughter. This brutal attack would cause massive panic in Melbourne.

events.title: William Wallace Is Executed
events.description: The trial of William Wallace at Westminster.

events.title: Bobby Dunbar Goes Missing
events.description: The boy raised as Bobby Dunbar (left) posing alongside his family.

events.title: Nicola Sacco And Bartolomeo Vanzetti Are Executed
events.description: Bartolomeo Vanzetti and Nicola Sacco at their trial in 1923.

events.title: Henry Lee Lucas Is Born
events.description: Henry Lee Lucas, the "Confession Killer," is born in Blacksburg, Virginia. In the 1970s, Lucas and his companion Ottis Toole murdered, raped, and cannibalized hundreds of victims. At least, that's what they claimed.

events.title: JFK And Jackie Lose Their First Child
events.description: John F. Kennedy and Jackie Kennedy lose their first child, Arabella. Jackie Kennedy gave birth to a stillborn infant and nicknamed her Arabella.

events.title: John Lennon And Cynthia Powell Get Married
events.description: Beatles star John Lennon marries Cynthia Powell after discovering they were expecting a child. Their relationship was turbulent and marked with abuse.

events.title: The World Wide Web Opens To The Public
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, launches the first web page available to the general public. A British computer scientist, Berners-Lee developed the website while working at CERN in Switzerland and opened it to the public on what is now known as Internaut Day. The site contained information about the World Wide Web, such as frequently asked questions and an executive summary of the project.

events.title: Mount Vesuvius Erupts
events.description: The Last Day of Pompeii by Karl Bryullov.

events.title: Rome Is Sacked By Visigoths
events.description: Rome is sacked for the first time in 800 years by Visigoths led by King Alaric I. Though the Roman Empire survived for several more decades afterward, the attack on Rome helped lead to its fall in 476 C.E.

events.title: The St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre Begins
events.description: The St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre, which was said to be instigated by Catherine de' Medici, takes place in Paris, France. In the early hours of August 24, a group of Catholic nobles and citizens attacked Protestant French Huguenots who were in town for the wedding of Catherine's daughter — who was marrying a Huguenot. The massacre, sparked by religious rivalries, spread throughout the city and beyond for the next several weeks, leaving up to 30,000 people dead.

events.title: British Forces Burn The White House
events.description: The British invade Washington, D.C., setting fire to the White House and other government buildings. As part of a campaign during the War of 1812, the attack was partially in retaliation for Americans targeting York in Ontario, Canada the previous year. President James Madison had already been evacuated from the White House, and his wife Dolley famously had George Washington's portrait saved from the flames. The building was later reconstructed, though it took three years.

events.title: Notorious Mobster Carlo Gambino Is Born
events.description: Carlo Gambino, the most powerful mob boss in history, is born in Palermo, Sicily. 19 years later, Gambino would emigrate from Sicily to New York, where he would rise through the ranks and control one of the most dangerous mob families in history.

events.title: Amelia Earhart Takes Off On Her Non-Stop Flight Across The United States
events.description: Amelia Earhart takes off on her non-stop flight across the United States, becoming the first woman to do so. Earhart piloted a Lockheed Vega 5B from Los Angeles to Newark in 19 hours and five minutes. Earhart flew 128 miles an hour and flew at an altitude of 10,000 feet. Less than a year later, Earhart broke her own record after completing the same flight about two hours faster. Ultimately, however, Earhart died near Howland Island in the Pacific while trying to circumnavigate the globe in July 1937.

events.title: The First "Gainesville Ripper" Murders Occur
events.description: Public record via Jacksonville.comDanny Rolling a.k.a. the "Gainesville Ripper" on trial for murder.

events.title: Ivan The Terrible Is Born
events.description: Portrait of Ivan the Terrible, by Viktor Vasnetsov.

events.title: "The Great Moon Hoax" Is Published In The New York Sun
events.description: The first of a series of six articles later dubbed "The Great Moon Hoax" is published in the newspaper New York Sun. The articles detailed the discovery of civilization and life on the moon, including winged humanoids and unicorns. The stories were likely written by reporter Richard Adams Locke and intended as satire, but readers were so convinced that the paper later had to admit to the hoax.

events.title: Matthew Webb Becomes The First Person To Swim The English Channel
events.description: English Captain Matthew Webb becomes the first person to swim across the English Channel with no artificial aids. He was inspired to attempt the feat when he read about the failed efforts of others. Webb began in Dover, England on August 24th and swam the equivalent of about 40 miles to Calais, France in less than 22 hours. The accomplishment brought Webb renown, but it also inspired him to try more dangerous stunts, and he later died while trying to swim across the Niagara River downriver from Niagara Falls.

events.title: Samantha Smith Dies In A Plane Crash
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesSamantha Smith holds up the letter she received from Soviet leader Yuri Andropov. April 1983.

events.title: Captain James Cook Sets Sail On The HMS Endeavour
events.description: Captain James Cook sets off from Plymouth, England on the first of three Pacific Ocean exploration voyages. He initially believed that the sole purpose of the trip was to travel to Tahiti to observe the transit of Venus. But after setting sail, he opened his sealed orders to discover he was also tasked with finding evidence of the hypothetical continent "Terra Australis." Cook and his crew would later become the first Europeans to visit Australia's eastern coastline in April 1770.

events.title: Mother Teresa Is Born
events.description: Mother Teresa in 1995.

events.title: The U.S. Navy Approves Operation HIGHJUMP
events.description: The U.S. Navy approves Operation HIHGJUMP, an Antarctic expedition. The operation was designed to test military capabilities in frigid conditions and establish an American base in Antarctica.

events.title: "Preppy Killer" Robert Chambers Kills Jennifer Levin
events.description: Dan Godfrey/NY Daily News Archive via Getty ImagesDetectives investigate the crime scene in Central Park where Jennifer Levin was found dead.

events.title: Jaycee Dugard Is Discovered Alive After 18 Years In Captivity
events.description: Jaycee Lee Dugard is discovered alive after she was kidnapped by Phillip Garrido while walking to her school bus in California 18 years earlier — when she was 11 years old. During Dugard's time in captivity, she was raped repeatedly by Garrido and she eventually gave birth to two of his children. One day, Garrido, already a registered sex offender, showed up for a visit with his parole officer with Dugard and their two daughters, who he had once tried to pass off as younger siblings of Dugard. Police separated Dugard and the girls from Garrido for questioning and finally uncovered the truth.

events.title: Alison Parker Is Fatally Shot By Her Former Coworker On Camera
events.description: Journalist Alison Parker is fatally shot by her former coworker on camera. Parker was a promising reporter for WDBJ7, a local news station in Roanoke, Virginia. While interviewing an executive director of the Chamber of Commerce, Parker and her cameraman, Adam Ward, were murdered by their former coworker, Vester Lee Flanagan. Flanagan once worked for WDBJ7, until he was fired for making people uncomfortable.

events.title: Visigoths Sack Rome
events.description: Visigoths from Eastern Europe end a three-day sack of Rome, becoming the first foreign enemy to take the city in over 800 years. Led by Alaric, the Germanic people looted much of Rome, though they protected many of the treasures in St. Peter's Basilica. The sack was a major event in the fall of the Western Roman Empire. St. Jerome later wrote: "The City which had taken the whole world was itself taken."

events.title: Krakatoa Erupts
events.description: An 1888 lithograph of Krakatoa's eruption.

events.title: The Anglo-Zanzibar War Begins And Ends
events.description: The shortest war in history, the Anglo-Zanzibar War is fought between the British Empire and the East African island sultanate of Zanzibar. The war, which was fought over the succession of the next sultan, lasted between 38 and 45 minutes. A Zanzibari prince who was angry about Britain's choice for the successor took over his palace, so the British bombarded it. Only one British soldier was wounded, while the prince's Zanzibari fighters suffered 500 casualties.

events.title: The Guinness Book Of Records Debuts
events.description: The first edition of the Guinness Book of Records, the predecessor to the Guinness World Records book, is published in Great Britain and quickly becomes a hit. The book is released annually, documenting the feats of humans and animals around the world. It was inspired by a debate among Sir Hugh Beaver and his friends about whether or not the golden plover was the fastest game bird in Europe.

events.title: Edmund Kemper Commits His First Murder
events.description: Ed Kemper's 1973 mugshot.

events.title: Brian Epstein Dies
events.description: Brian Epstein, the man who discovered the Beatles and became the band's first manager, dies at the age of 32 of an accidental drug overdose.

events.title: St. Elizabeth Is Born
events.description: Elizabeth Ann Seton (née Bayley), who will later become canonized as a saint, is born in New York City. She was the first American-born person beatified by the Roman Catholic Church. Elizabeth was raised Episcopalian, but she joined the Catholic Church in 1805 and took her vow of chastity in 1809. Elizabeth later founded the Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph and dedicated the latter part of her life to establishing Catholic institutions in the United States.

events.title: Zulu King Cetshwayo Is Captured
events.description: The last great ruler of Zululand in Southern Africa, King Cetshwayo, is captured by the British after his forces are defeated in the British-Zulu War. It was his resistance to British rule in Africa that led Britain to invade earlier that year, as he refused to disband his troops when ordered. After thousands of casualties on both sides, the British captured King Cetshwayo and sent him into exile, where he would die in 1884.

events.title: Emmett Till Is Lynched
events.description: Emmett Till on Christmas Day, 1954.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Gives His Famous "I Have A Dream" Speech
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. gives his "I Have A Dream" speech in Washington, D.C.

events.title: Elisabeth Fritzl "Goes Missing" From Her Home In Austria
events.description: Eighteen-year-old Elisabeth Fritzl "goes missing" from her home in Austria. The truth of her whereabouts was much darker. After building a secret chamber in his basement, Elisabeth's father, Josef, locked her in. She would spend the next 24 years there, subjected to horrendous sexual abuse and forced to carry her father's children.

events.title: Brian Wells Enters A PNC Bank In Erie, PA With A Bomb Strapped To His Chest
events.description: Brian Wells, also known as the "Pizza Bomber," robs a PNC bank in Erie, Pennsylvania with a bomb strapped to his chest. Although Wells died surrounded by police that day, the robbery kicked off a much larger investigation into who masterminded the robbery and why, setting the stage for the Netflix docu-series Evil Genius.

events.title: The Last Inca Emperor Is Executed
events.description: Atahuallpa, the last emperor of the Inca, is executed by conquistador Francisco Pizarro. The leader was known for being brave and ambitious, and he had recently led his forces to victory in a civil war against his half-brother over control of the empire. But in November 1532, he accepted an invitation to dine with Pizarro, who had him captured. Pizarro held Atahuallpa for nine months, accepting his ransom of 24 tons of gold and silver before killing him.

events.title: The Last Surviving Member Of The Yahi Tribe Emerges In California
events.description: Ishi, the last known member of the Indigenous Yahi people, emerges from the wilderness in Oroville, California. He had lived in isolation for years after his tribe was destroyed by genocide. Ishi means "man" in the Yahi language, and he was given this name because his people's tradition demanded that he could not speak his own name until introduced by another Yahi. Since he was the last remaining tribe member, however, he died without ever revealing his true name.

events.title: The Louvre Begins Moving Art Out Of The Museum
events.description: The Louvre Museum in Paris, France begins moving art pieces out of the museum to keep incoming Nazi forces from taking or destroying them. Supported by the Monuments Men, a Allied civilian art rescue operation, the Louvre successfully prevented Nazis from getting their hands on some of the world's most priceless art.

events.title: GG Allin Is Born
events.description: Punk rock legend GG Allin is born in New Hampshire. Known for his intense music and performances, GG Allin is one of the most shocking hardcore punk artists of all time. After growing up in a strict and abusive religious home, Allin sought to rebel. He initially looked to cross-dressing, music, and drugs to fulfill this need.

events.title: Michael Jackson Is Born
events.description: The "King of Pop," Michael Jackson, is born in Gary, Indiana. From a young age, Jackson was thrust into the music industry, performing in the Jackson 5 with his siblings when he was just six years old. He went on to become one of the most famous and successful musical artists in history. Jackson's later life was marked by numerous controversies, including accusations of sexually abusing children, and he died in 2009 after suffering from cardiac arrest, which was caused by a lethal combination of drugs.

events.title: Hurricane Katrina Hits New Orleans
events.description: Trinity CollegeThe flooded streets of New Orleans in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina.

events.title: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley Is Born
events.description: A portrait of Mary Shelley by Richard Rothwell.

events.title: Vladimir Lenin Is Shot
events.description: Fanny Kaplan, a Ukrainian Jewish woman and a member of the Socialist Revolutionary Party, shoots Vladimir Lenin in an assassination attempt. Lenin had just given a speech at the Hammer and Sickle, a factory in Moscow, and after he left the building, Kaplan shot at him three times. Two of the bullets struck him, one in the neck and one in the left shoulder. The Russian leader survived, but his health was never the same, and it's been suggested that the shooting contributed to the later strokes that took his life.

events.title: Hotline Opens Between Moscow And Washington, D.C.
events.description: A direct hotline opens between the White House and the Kremlin in Moscow in an effort to facilitate communication between U.S. and Soviet leaders. After the Cuban Missile Crisis, President John F. Kennedy wanted a way to quickly exchange messages with the Kremlin to prevent future misunderstandings and reduce the risk of nuclear war. The line was to be used only for emergencies rather than for everyday communication, and it was first utilized three months later when Kennedy was assassinated.

events.title: Bryce Laspisa Disappears
events.description: FIND BRYCE LASPISA/FacebookBryce Laspisa with his parents.

events.title: The United States Leaves Afghanistan
events.description: The United States leaves Afghanistan after 20 years. Newly elected President Biden declared that he would end the war in Afghanistan and bring American troops home. Various agreements with the Taliban essentially forced the U.S. to withdraw all forces by 2021. Prior to pulling troops out of Afghanistan, the U.S. government warned American citizens to exit the country as quickly as possible. Immediately following the evacuation of U.S. troops, Afghanistan fell into Taliban hands, sparking a refugee crisis. The evacuation caused condemnation among many who believed it was poorly managed.

events.title: Henry V Of England Dies
events.description: After contracting dysentery during battle, King Henry V of England dies at the Château de Vincennes near Paris, France. He was just 35 years old and had been king for only nine years. His heir, Henry VI, was a mere nine months old when he ascended to the English throne. And a few months later, when the infant monarch's grandfather Charles VI died, he became the king of France as well.

events.title: Jack The Ripper Claims His First Victim
events.description: Mary Ann Nichols' body was found in London's Whitechapel district.

events.title: Mad Gasser Of Mattoon Strikes For The First Time
events.description: The attacks from the Mad Gasser of Mattoon, Illinois begin. Over the course of a few months, residents of Mattoon reported acute physical symptoms, including paralysis and vomiting, after smelling bizarre odors in their homes. Today, some believe the gas attacks were the work of a crazed individual, but others think it is a clear cut case of mass hysteria.

events.title: "Night Stalker" Richard Ramirez Is Attacked By A Mob And Arrested
events.description: After murdering at least 13 people, Richard Ramirez is chased by a group of angry Los Angeles residents after he is spotted and recognized as the notorious "Night Stalker" serial killer. Ramirez was unaware that a photo of his face had been published in newspapers and on TV while he was going about his day as usual. When the citizens caught Ramirez, they held him down and viciously beat him until police arrived to arrest him.

events.title: The Ruby Ridge Standoff Ends
events.description: The Ruby Ridge standoff ends in Idaho. U.S. marshals arrived at the home of self-proclaimed "white separatist" Randy Weaver in Boundary County, Idaho to arrest him for failing to appear in court for a weapons charge. The marshals surrounded the property to conduct a surveillance operation. Then, Randy's 14-year-old son, Sammy, exchanged gunfire with the surveillance team after an officer shot and killed his dog. The situation escalated to an 11-day standoff that left two of the Weavers, including Sammy, dead.

events.title: Princess Diana Dies
events.description: Jacques Langevin/Sygma via Getty ImagesOne of the last photos of Princess Diana alive.

events.title: James Callender Reveals Thomas Jefferson And Sally Hemings' Relationship
events.description: James Callender publishes an explosive exposé accusing President Thomas Jefferson of having several children with an enslaved woman named Sally Hemings. His accusation would be proven almost 200 years later when a DNA test linked Hemings' descendents to Jefferson.

events.title: Aaron Burr Is Acquitted Of Treason
events.description: National Endowment for the HumanitiesThe courtroom during Aaron Burr's trial.

events.title: Germany Invades Poland, Triggering The Outbreak Of World War II In Europe
events.description: Nazi Germany invades Poland, justifying the action by claiming Poland was persecuting ethnic Germans living in the country and that Poland was collaborating with Britain and France to invade Germany. The SS staged a false flag attack against a German radio station on the border and Nazi forces attacked Poland in "retaliation."

events.title: The Berkshire UFO Incident Occurs
events.description: The Berkshire UFO Incident occurs in Berkshire County, Massachusetts. About 40 people reported seeing bizarre lights in the sky, and at least one person reported being abducted by aliens.

events.title: Bobby Fischer Wins The World Chess Championship
events.description: Bobby Fischer faces off against Boris Spassky at the World Chess Championship in Reykjavik, Iceland.

events.title: The Wreckage Of The Titanic Is Discovered
events.description: The bow of the RMS Titanic.

events.title: The Beslan School Massacre Begins
events.description: The Beslan school massacre begins in Beslan, Russia. A group of armed Chechen terrorists took more than 1,100 people hostage at a local school. The terrorist group managed to herd the hostages into the school's gym where they remained for the next three days. Eventually, the Russian government received word that a terrorist attack was underway and deployed troops to end the conflict. On the third day of the standoff, Russian forces stormed the building. In the storming, the school caught on fire and hundreds were killed or injured. In total, 333 people died in the siege, making it the deadliest school shooting in history.

events.title: Picher, Oklahoma Is Unincorporated And Evacuated
events.description: Picher, Oklahoma, America's most toxic ghost town, is unincorporated and evacuated given evidence of serious health concerns.

events.title: Octavian Defeats Mark Antony
events.description: Off the west coast of Greece, Octavian defeats Mark Antony at the Battle of Actium, solidifying his control over the Roman Empire. The heir of Julius Caesar, Octavian saw Antony, Cleopatra, and the supposed son of Cleopatra and Caesar, Caesarion, as threats to his power. After his victory, Octavian followed Antony and Cleopatra to Alexandria, where both died by suicide.

events.title: The Great Fire Of London Breaks Out
events.description: A depiction of the Great Fire of London, which destroyed almost the entire city in 1666.

events.title: Queen Liliuokalani Is Born
events.description: Unknown/Hawaii State ArchivesQueen Liliuokalani when she was a princess in the 1870s.

events.title: The Chichijima Incident Takes Place
events.description: George Bush Presidential Library and MuseumGeorge H.W. Bush was a 20-year-old pilot when the Chichijima incident occured.

events.title: Divers Discover Bimini Road
events.description: Divers Joseph Manson Valentine, Robert Angove, and Jacques Mayol find an odd pattern of limestone rocks in the waters of the Bahamas. Dubbed Bimini Road, the pattern becomes the focus of numerous studies from people convinced it could be a road to Atlantis.

events.title: Ho Chi Minh Dies
events.description: Ho Chi Minh dies at the age of 79 in Hanoi, Vietnam. The head of the Vietnamese nationalist movement, Ho Chi Minh fought the Japanese, the French, and the Americans in the name of Vietnamese independence. He served as the first president of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam and Saigon, the former capital of South Vietnam, was renamed Ho Chi Minh City in his honor.

events.title: Richard The Lionheart Is Crowned King
events.description: Richard the Lionheart was king for 10 years.

events.title: Captain James Cook Becomes First European To Make Contact With Remote Asmat Tribe
events.description: Captain James Cook and his crew land on the shores of New Guinea, the territory of the remote Asmat tribe who would later be connected to the disappearance of Michael Rockefeller in the 1960s.

events.title: The Treaty Of Paris Is Signed
events.description: The United States, Great Britain, Spain, and France sign the Treaty of Paris in Paris, France. The treaty ended the American Revolution, which had begun eight years earlier in 1775. It established the United States as a sovereign nation and set the borders of the new country.

events.title: Frederick Douglass Escapes Slavery
events.description: Frederick Douglass in the 1840s.

events.title: Griselda Blanco, "Queen of Cocaine," dies
events.description: Grisdela Blanco, the "Queen of Cocaine," dies in Medellín, Columbia. Known as "La Madrina," Blanco was a prolific Colombian drug lord in the 1980s. She is believed to have killed anywhere from 200 to 2,000 people to protect her drug empire. After serving time in prison, Blanco was sent back to Colombia in 2004. There, unidentified assailants would assassinate her outside a butcher shop.

events.title: Ariel Castro Commits Suicide
events.description: Angelo Merendino/Getty ImagesAriel Castro pleads during his sentencing on August 1, 2013, in Cleveland, Ohio. Castro was sentenced to life without parole plus 1,000 years for abducting three women between 2002 and 2004.

events.title: The Western Roman Empire Falls
events.description: The Western Roman Empire falls to barbarians. Odoacer, a Germanic mercenary leader in the Roman imperial army, deposed Romulus Augustus, the boy emperor of Rome. Odoacer declared himself King of Italy, effectively ending the Western Roman Empire, though it continued in the East.

events.title: Athelstan Is Crowned King Of England
events.description: Athelstan, son of Edward the Elder, is crowned king. He is considered to be the first king of all of England.

events.title: Apache Leader Geronimo Surrenders
events.description: Geronimo, pictured here in 1887, spent decades resisting the encroachment of settlers before surrendering to federal troops.

events.title: The Little Rock Nine Enter An Integrated School
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesOn the first day of school at Little Rock Central High School, students heckle Elizabeth Eckford.

events.title: Dorothy Counts Integrates Harry Harding High School
events.description: Dorothy Counts, 15, becomes the first Black student to attend Harry Harding High School In Charlotte, North Carolina.

events.title: Google Is Founded
events.description: Computer scientists Larry Page and Sergey Brin found Google while enrolled as PhD students at Stanford University. Google, the world's most popular search engine, would later expand into a massive variety of tech products, and in 2015, a restructuring of Google would lead to the creation of Alphabet, Inc., the parent company of Google and its subsidiaries. Alphabet, Inc. is considered one of the Big Five tech companies alongside Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft.

events.title: Lloyd Avery II Is Murdered By His Cellmate
events.description: Lloyd Avery II, an actor in the 1991 film Boyz N The Hood, is murdered by his cellmate Kevin Roby. Roby was a proclaimed Satanist who strangled Avery to death after the two argued about religion.

events.title: Steve Irwin Dies
events.description: Paul Drinkwater/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images/span>Steve Irwin appears on the Jay Leno Show in 2002 with a live alligator.

events.title: Mother Teresa Is Canonized
events.description: Mother Teresa is canonized by Pope Francis. Mother Teresa was a Catholic missionary who worked primarily in hospitals in India. She gained an international reputation as a selfless humanitarian dedicated to spreading her faith. In recent times, disturbing facts about Mother Teresa's Catholic organizations have come to light, sparking debate about who Mother Teresa really was.

events.title: King Louis XIV Is Born
events.description: Louis XIV is born in Saint-Germain-en-Laye, France, to Louis XIII and Anne of Austria.

events.title: Construction Of Neuschwanstein Castle Begins
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesNeuschwanstein Castle later inspired Walt Disney as he worked on Sleeping Beauty.

events.title: Crazy Horse Dies
events.description: Crazy Horse dies at Fort Robinson, Nebraska, following an altercation with a guard who stabbed him with a bayonet. A Lakota leader, Crazy Horse had long resisted the encroachment of American settlement on indigenous land and fought in the Battle of Little Bighorn in 1876. After a harsh winter devastated his tribe, however, Crazy Horse agreed to surrender in 1877.

events.title: Freddie Mercury Is Born
events.description: Hulton-Deutsch/Hulton-Deutsch Collection/Corbis via Getty ImagesFreddie Mercury dazzled with his fashion sense, vocal prowess, and lyrics.

events.title: Lynette Fromme Attempts To Assassinate President Gerald Ford
events.description: Lynette "Squeaky" Fromme attempts to assassinate President Gerald Ford in San Francisco. A former member of the infamous Manson Family, Fromme claimed she wanted to kill the president because Ford had relaxed provisions in the Clean Air Act. But Fromme had forgotten to load the chamber of her .45 caliber pistol, and the gun didn't go off when she fired it.

events.title: Terrorists Hijack Pam Am Flight 73
events.description: Four Palestinian terrorists hijack Pan Am Flight 73 while the plane stopped in Karachi, Pakistan.

events.title: Ferdinand Magellan's Ship Becomes The First To Circumnavigates The Globe
events.description: The Victoria arrives at Sanlúcar de Barrameda in Spain, becoming the first vessel to circumnavigate the globe. Three years earlier, Ferdinand Magellan had set out from Spain with the Victoria and four other ships in hopes of finding a western route to Indonesia. But though the Victoria made it back to Spain, Magellan didn't — he was killed in battle in the Philippines in April 1521.

events.title: President William McKinley Is Shot
events.description: A depiction of William McKinley's assassination in Buffalo, New York.

events.title: Howard Unruh Commits America's First Mass Shooting
events.description: Howard Unruh kills 13 people in Camden, New Jersey. Considered America's first mass shooting, the violence unfolded over just 12 minutes as Unruh went on a "Walk of Death." He allegedly set out on the rampage after squabbling with his neighbors, and later told a psychologist that he would have killed "a thousand" if he'd had enough bullets.

events.title: William S. Burroughs Kills Joan Vollmer
events.description: Allen Ginsberg EstateJoan Vollmer in New York City in 1944.

events.title: Chris McCandless's Body Is Discovered
events.description: Chris McCandless took many self-portraits, including this one in front of the abandoned bus that served as his shelter.

events.title: Richard The Lionheart Breaks Through The Muslim Army On The Way To Jerusalem
events.description: Battle of Arsuf painted by Eloi Firmin Feron (1802-1876).

events.title: Queen Elizabeth I Is Born
events.description: Elizabeth I is born at Greenwich Palace in London, England. The daughter of Anne Boleyn and King Henry VIII, her birth was a bitter disappointment to her father, who had hoped for a son. Elizabeth nevertheless rose to power in 1558 after the death of her older sister, Mary, and ruled England for 45 years.

events.title: Henry Every Raids The Mughal Ship Ganj-i-Sawai
events.description: English pirate Henry Every raids the Mughal ship Ganj-i-Sawai in the Indian Ocean. Referred to as the most profitable raid in piracy history, the attack earned Every the equivalent of £115 million today.

events.title: Buddy Holly Is Born
events.description: Buddy Holly had a handful of hits before he died at the age of 22.

events.title: The Battle Of Wizna Begins
events.description: The Battle of Wizna, in which 720 Polish soldiers held back an army of 42,000 Germans for three days, begins near the Polish village of Wizna at the dawn of World War II.

events.title: The Blitz Begins Over Great Britain
events.description: Winston Churchill tours Coventry Cathedral after it was bombed and mostly destroyed in November 1940.

events.title: Carlos Lehder Is Born
events.description: Colombian drug kingpin Carlos Lehder is born in Armenia, Colombia.

events.title: Tupac Shakur Is Shot
events.description: Tupac Shakur in 1991, five years before he died.

events.title: Joan Of Arc Attacks Paris
events.description: Joan of Arc attacks Paris during the Hundred Years' War. The war stemmed from the issue of French succession. Two royal houses, the English House of Plantagenet and the French House of Valois, claimed to be the rightful heirs to the throne. This conflict sparked widespread violence across France. Joan of Arc, a young peasant woman, claimed to have visions from God directing her to defend France from English rule. Charles VII, the future King of France, believed in her divinity, and sent Joan of Arc to battles across the country. Joan of Arc eventually led an unsuccessful campaign to capture Paris after English and rival French forces took the city. This siege was unsuccessful, and Joan of Arc was later captured a year later.

events.title: New Amsterdam Becomes New York
events.description: New Amsterdam becomes New York after Dutch Governor Peter Stuyvesant surrenders to the British.
