Stuyvesant had hoped to put up more of a fight over the capital of New Netherland but failed to rally his subjects. New Amsterdam was renamed after the Duke of York, who had led the British attack.

events.title: Jack The Ripper Kills His Second Victim
events.description: Annie Chapman's mortuary photo.

events.title: A Hurricane Levels Galveston, Texas
events.description: A Category 4 hurricane devastates Galveston, Texas. The Galveston hurricane, one of the worst natural disasters in American history, killed between 6,000 and 8,000 people.

events.title: The Delano Grape Strike Begins
events.description: The Phillip & Sala Burton Center for Human Rights/Farmworker Movement Documentation ProjectDolores Huerta working the picket line during the Delano Grape strike. 1966.

events.title: William The Conqueror Dies
events.description: William the Conqueror dies around the age of 59. Weeks earlier, his horse had reared up during a battle in France, pushing the king's saddle pommel into his abdomen. It caused an infection that proved fatal, and after he was placed in a tomb too small for his body, his corpse exploded during his funeral.

events.title: Colonel Sanders Is Born
events.description: Fred Ross/Toronto Star via Getty ImagesHarland Sanders, known popularly as Colonel Sanders.

events.title: Virginia Rappe Dies After Attending A Hollywood Party
events.description: Actress Virginia Rappe dies from peritonitis three days after attending a Hollywood party with Roscoe "Fatty" Arbuckle. The death scandalized 1920s Hollywood and led to the end of Arbuckle's acting career.

events.title: American Gangster Frank Lucas Is Born
events.description: American gangster Frank Lucas is born in North Carolina. Lucas would earn the nickname "Superfly" as he operated a heroin empire in Harlem, New York. His modus operandi, as he states, included smuggling heroin into the United States through Vietnam, packing coffins of deceased American soldiers with his own brand of "Blue Magic," a potent and destructive type of heroin.

events.title: The Attica Prison Riot Begins
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesInmates raise their fists during the Attica Prison Riot.

events.title: Mao Zedong Dies
events.description: Mao Zedong dies at the age of 82 in Bejing, China, following three heart attacks and ongoing struggles with Parkinson's disease. The leader of the Chinese Communist Party, Mao rose to power in 1949 and set out to develop China as a communist country and an economic powerhouse. Though some of his policies, like the Great Leap Forward, killed millions, Mao is largely viewed favorably in China today.

events.title: John Smith Is Elected To Lead Jamestown
events.description: John Smith is elected council president of Jamestown, Virginia. The 27-year-old Englishman had proven himself to his fellow colonists during the winter of 1607-1608, when the English settlement struggled with disease, starvation, cannibalism, and attacks from Native Americans. Smith is perhaps known for his capture by Powhatan warriors and alleged rescue by the chief's young daughter, Pocahontas.

events.title: Marie Laveau Is Born
events.description: Marie Laveau was known as New Orleans' "Voodoo Queen."

events.title: The World's First Drunk Driving Arrest Takes Place
events.description: A London taxi driver named George Smith becomes the first person to ever be arrested for drunk driving. The 25-year-old had driven his cab into a building, prompting his arrest. He was fined 25 shillings after pleading guilty.

events.title: The Last Person Is Executed By Guillotine In France
events.description: GERARD FOUET/AFP via Getty ImagesHamida Djandoubi arriving at his trial in February 1977.

events.title: The Large Hadron Collider Is Turned On
events.description: Scientists turn on the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) lab in Geneva, Switzerland. The largest particle accelerator in history, the LHC allowed scientists to study subatomic particles like never before. Though the lab was shut down during the COVID-19 pandemic, the LHC was restarted in April 2022.

events.title: The Hope Diamond Is Stolen
events.description: The Hope Diamond, then called the French Blue, is stolen among other crown jewels during the French Revolution. It reappeared in London 20 years later, where the jewel was called the "Hope Diamond" for the first time. Some believe that the Hope Diamond is cursed, as many of its owners, including King Louis XVI, died gruesome deaths.

events.title: The Mountain Meadows Massacre Ends
events.description: An 1873 depiction of the Mountain Meadows Massacre.

events.title: Fatty Arbuckle Is Arrested
events.description: Silent film star Roscoe Conkling "Fatty" Arbuckle is arrested following the death of actress Virginia Rappe.

events.title: Pinochet Leads A Successful Coup In Chile
events.description: Augusto Pinochet leads a successful coup in Chile. In the early 1970s, Pinochet rose through the ranks of the Chilean military before launching a coup against Chilean president Salvador Allende. With support from the United States, Pinochet became the de facto dictator of Chile. While in power, Pinochet violently suppressed any opposition, resulting in the execution of 1,200 to 3,200 people, the imprisonment of 80,000 people, and the torture of thousands. Pinochet left office in 1990 but continued to work in Chilean government until his arrest for human rights violations. He died in 2006 while under house arrest.

events.title: The 9/11 Attacks Take Place
events.description: Andrew Lichtenstein/Corbis via Getty ImagesA woman looks in disbelief as smoke billows from the World Trade Center in New York City.

events.title: The Battle Of Vienna Ends Ottoman Domination In Eastern Europe
events.description: Forces loyal to the Holy Roman Empire defeat an Ottoman Empire army at Kahlenberg Mountain near Vienna, a victory which ushered in the beginning of the end of Ottoman domination in eastern Europe.

events.title: HMS Terror Gets Trapped In Ice
events.description: An engraving of the HMS Terror, one of the two ships lost during the Franklin expedition.

events.title: The SS Central America Sinks
events.description: The SS Central America sinks during a hurricane off the coast of North Carolina. The vessel carried over 500 passengers and 30,000 pounds of gold at the time, sparking a century-long search for the wreckage. Finally, in 1988, she was found.

events.title: Jesse Owens Is Born
events.description: Black American track and field athlete James Cleveland "Jesse" Owens is born in Oakville, Alabama. Owens would go on to win four gold medals at the 1936 Olympic games in Berlin, where his victories flew in the face of hateful Nazi racial policies.

events.title: The Lascaux Cave Paintings Are Discovered
events.description: An image painted on the walls of the Lascaux Cave in France.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Weds Jacqueline Lee Bouvier
events.description: John F. Kennedy marries Jacqueline Lee Bouvier in St. Mary's Roman Catholic Church in Newport, Rhode Island. From the outside, the dashing future president and his glamorous wife seemed to have a charmed relationship, though it was strained by Kennedy's constant infidelity. John F. Kennedy was assassinated in 1963 when he was president and Jacqueline later married Greek shipping magnate Aristotle Onassis.

events.title: Soviet Union Launches Luna 2, The First Space Probe To Reach The Moon
events.description: The Soviet Union launches Luna 2, the first space probe to reach the moon. Its predecessor, Luna 1, also launched in the direction of the moon but failed to land. Luna 2 was similar to Luna 1 in appearance, with long antennas and a spherical base. As it approached the moon, Luna 2 released a cloud of sodium as part of an experiment to analyze the behavior of gas in space. Then, Luna 2 made contact with the moon's surface. This launch proved that the moon did not have a magnetic field or a radiation belt.

events.title: Johnny Cash Dies
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesJohnny Cash poses for a moody portrait in Memphis, Tennessee, in 1957.

events.title: Michelangelo Begins His 'David' Statue
events.description: Michelangelo Buonarroti begins to carve the statue that becomes the iconic "David." His carving, commissioned by the Opera del Duomo for the Cathedral of Florence, took three years to complete and depicts the Biblical hero David who vanquished the giant Goliath with a slingshot.

events.title: Phineas Gage Is Impaled By A Metal Pole
events.description: Phineas Gage with the tamping iron that impaled him in 1848.

events.title: Milton Hershey Is Born
events.description: Milton Hershey is born in Derry Township, Pennsylvania. The founder of the Hershey Chocolate Company, Hershey introduced iconic candies like the Hershey Kiss. He was also known for his philanthropy and opened up the Milton Hershey School to educate orphans in 1909.

events.title: Alberta King Is Born
events.description: Alberta King, mother of Martin Luther King, Jr., is born in Atlanta, Georgia.

events.title: Rosemary Kennedy Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesRosemary Kennedy with her father, Joseph, in 1938.

events.title: Rodney Alcala Appears On 'The Dating Game'
events.description: YouTubeRodney Alcala and Jed Mills on The Dating Game.

events.title: Super Mario Bros. Is Released
events.description: The first Super Mario Bros. was released in Japan and the United States in 1985.

events.title: Gina Grant Is Arrested For The Murder Of Her Mother
events.description: Gina Grant is arrested after her mother was found murdered in their home. Grant pleaded no contest to the charge and served a year behind bars. Her decision to apply to Harvard would kickstart a national debate regarding privacy laws and criminal rehabilitation.

events.title: Dante Alighieri Dies
events.description: Dante Alighieri dies in Ravenna, Italy, at the age of 56 from malaria. A poet, writer, and philosopher who famously wrote the Divine Comedy, Dante passed away just hours after finishing the final part, Paradiso.

events.title: Francis Scott Key Writes The Star-Spangled Banner
events.description: A depiction of the bombardment of Fort McHenry, which inspired Francis Scott Key to write The Star-Spangled Banner.

events.title: Aaron Burr Dies
events.description: Aaron Burr, who infamously killed Alexander Hamilton during their 1804 duel, dies at the age of 80 after suffering from a stroke.

events.title: Elizabeth Ann Seton Is Canonized
events.description: Elizabeth Ann Seton is canonized by Pope Paul VI. One of the first American-born saints, Seton dedicated much of her life to charity and founded the Society for the Relief of Poor Widows with Small Children in 1797. After her husband's death, she converted to Catholicism and established the first American religious order, the Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph, in 1809.

events.title: Manacled Mormon Case Begins
events.description: Manacled Mormon case begins in Devon, England. A call to the Devon police from a anxious young man came in. The man was a Mormon missionary named Kirk Anderson. He claimed that a woman named Joyce McKinney had imprisoned him and repeatedly raped him over a period of three days. Anderson claimed he only escaped after he promised to marry McKinney. During an interview with police, McKinney stated that she had not raped Anderson, and that the two of them were in love. The story of the "manacled Mormon" made international headlines and became a "perfect tabloid story" of religion, love, and crime.

events.title: Grace Kelly Dies
events.description: Archive Photos/Getty ImagesAmerican actress Grace Kelly circa 1955.

events.title: Gemini Twins Anthony Senter And Joey Testa Are Sentenced To Life In Prison
events.description: Mobsters Anthony Senter and Joey Testa, better known as the Gemini Twins, are each dealt life sentences for their involvement in multiple murders.

events.title: Marco Polo Is Born
events.description: Marco Polo, the Venetian explorer who traveled through Asia in the 13th century, is born in Venice, Italy.

events.title: Charles Darwin Arrives In The Galapagos Islands
events.description: English naturalist Charles Darwin arrives in the Galapagos Islands aboard the HMS Beagle.

events.title: Agatha Christie Is Born
events.description: Agatha Christie as a young woman in the 1910s.

events.title: Lea Papin, The Youngest Papin Sister, Is Born
events.description: Lea Papin, the youngest Papin sister, is born in France. Lea Papin, along with her older sister Christine, worked as live-in maids for the Lancelin family in Le Mans, France. On February 2, 1933, Lea and Christine killed two members of the Lancelin family during a scuffle. Other family members would eventually find their badly beaten and mutilated bodies in the entryway to the house. Police soon arrested the two sisters for the crime. Immediately, the two girls confessed to the murders, but claimed that they were done in self defense. Their case would divide 1930s France along class lines.

events.title: The Nuremberg Race Laws Pass In Nazi Germany
events.description: The German parliament passes the Nuremberg Race Laws, two pieces of legislation that provided the legal framework for the Nazi's persecution of Jewish people. The laws were designed by Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party, and they stripped Jewish men, women, and children of German citizenship and forbade marriage between Jewish and German citizens. The Nuremberg Race Laws did not define a "Jew" as someone who practiced the Jewish religion but rather as someone who had three to four Jewish grandparents.

events.title: The Birmingham Church Bombing
events.description: FBIThe aftermath of the Birmingham church bombing.

events.title: The Mayflower Departs England
events.description: After a failed attempt the previous month, the Mayflower leaves Plymouth, England, and sets sail for the New World with 102 passengers on board. Some of the colonists were entrepreneurs seeking wealth in the New World, but 35 of them were Pilgrims looking for a place to practice their religion free from the Church of England. The ship would reach present-day Massachusetts two months later.

events.title: The Mexican War Of Independence Begins
events.description: Catholic priest Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla publicly reads his tract Grito de Dolores (The Cry of Dolores), calling for the end of Spanish rule in Mexico and sparking the Mexican War of Independence. Hidalgo also called for racial equality and land redistribution, and soon thousands of Indigenous locals and mestizos gathered to march on Mexico City. Hidalgo, the "father of Mexican independence," was captured just four months later and later executed by firing squad.

events.title: The Wall Street Bombing
events.description: The aftermath of the Wall Street bombing.

events.title: Peg Entwistle Dies By Suicide
events.description: Peg Entwistle in 1929.

events.title: King Of Jordan Declares Martial Law
events.description: The King of Jordan declares martial law during the Jordanian Civil War. The conflict in Jordan began with violence between the Jordanian Armed Forces (JAF), under the leadership of King Hussein, and Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO). The PLO openly called for the overthrow of the Jordanian monarchy and launched a series of plane hijackings. The hijackings ended with PLO forces blowing up the empty planes in Zarqa, Jordan in front of journalists. King Hussein viewed this act as intolerable and declared martial law in Jordan. Under his leadership, King Hussein drove the PLO out of Jordan, primarily to Lebanon and Syria. King Hussein terminated martial law in 1992, more than 20 years later.

events.title: The Ariel School Phenomenon Occurs
events.description: The Ariel School Phenomenon occurs at a school in Zimbabwe. A group of school children claimed to have witnessed a UFO during recess.

events.title: The Constitution Is Signed
events.description: The Constitution is signed by 39 delegates at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia. It was then sent to Congress in New York City, and then to the states for ratification.

events.title: Harriet Tubman Escapes From Slavery
events.description: Harriet Tubman in 1895.

events.title: The Battle Of Antietam Begins
events.description: In the early morning hours, Union and Confederate troops begin fighting near Antietam Creek in Maryland, beginning the single bloodiest day in American combat history.

events.title: Frida Kahlo Is Injured In A Bus Accident
events.description: Frida Kahlo is injured in a bus accident in Mexico City. At 18-years-old, Kahlo was studying to become a doctor at the National Preparatory School in Mexico City. On the day of the accident, Kahlo and her friend Alejandro Gomez Arias boarded a bus heading to Kahlo's hometown of Coyoacan. Not long after the duo boarded, the bus slammed into a trolley at full speed, resulting in a metal rod flying across the bus and impaling Kahlo in the abdomen. While recovering from her injuries in bed, Kahlo began painting her pain. Today, Kahlo is famous for her brutal and raw depictions of pain and heartbreak.

events.title: Operation Market Garden Begins
events.description: Operation Market Garden, an Allied initiative during World War II to push into German territory, begins. Though the operation would free several Dutch cities, it ultimately failed to make significant gains into Germany.

events.title: NASA Unveils The First Space Shuttle
events.description: NASA publicly unveils the Enterprise, the agency's first space shuttle. It took nearly 10 years to develop the shuttle and it cost almost $10 billion to construct. The Enterprise was used for atmospheric test flights and was not capable of traveling in outer space. Today, the shuttle can be seen at the Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum in New York City.

events.title: Occupy Wall Street Begins
events.description: The Occupy Wall Street movement protested wealth inequality, among other issues.

events.title: Anne Hutchinson Arrives In The New World
events.description: Englishwoman Anne Hutchinson arrives in the Massachusetts Bay Colony, from which she will be banished just four years later. Hutchinson was controversial for her religious views that salvation could be achieved by faith alone.

events.title: Samuel Johnson Is Born
events.description: English poet and literary critic Samuel Johnson is born in Lichfield, England. He is perhaps best known for writing A Dictionary of the English Language, the preeminent dictionary for nearly 200 years until the Oxford English Dictionary was published in the late 19th century. Johnson single-handedly completed the dictionary over the course of eight years in "one of the greatest single achievements of scholarship."

events.title: "Lonely Hearts Killer" Harvey Glatman Is Executed
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesHarvey Glatman in jail in 1958.

events.title: Jimi Hendrix Dies
events.description: American guitarist Jimi Hendrix dies at the age of 27 after asphyxiating on his own vomit while intoxicated with barbiturates.

events.title: Patty Hearst Is Arrested For Armed Robbery
events.description: San Mateo County Sheriff's Office/Wikimedia CommonsPatty Hearst's booking photo following her arrest in San Francisco.

events.title: Giles Corey Is Executed In The Salem Witch Trials
events.description: Giles Corey was crushed to death after refusing to cooperate during his trial.

events.title: President James Garfield Dies
events.description: U.S. President James Garfield dies after only six months in office. He'd been shot by Charles Guiteau in an assassination attempt nearly three months earlier, and one of the bullets had lodged in his abdomen.

events.title: Frances Farmer Is Born
events.description: American actress and TV host Frances Farmery is born in Seattle, Washington. Though she had a successful acting career, Farmer was also known for her tumultuous personal life. In 1942, she was arrested for drunk driving and later sentenced to 180 days in jail.

events.title: Lesley Hornby, "Twiggy," Is Born
events.description: The 1960s fashion icon Twiggy is born in London. Her likeness would become synonymous with the culture of 1960s youth.

events.title: Betty And Barney Hill Are Allegedly Abducted By Aliens
events.description: Betty and Barney Hill claim they are abducted by aliens while driving through New Hampshire. Under hypnosis two years later, they described encountering little gray men who probed them aboard a UFO.

events.title: Jeannette DePalma's Body Is Found
events.description: The body of missing teenager Jeannette DePalma is discovered in Houdaille Quarry in New Jersey after a dog brings her decomposing arm to its owner. DePalma had vanished six weeks prior after telling her parents she was taking the train to her friend's house. Investigators could not determine a cause of death, but witnesses who saw her body claim that she was surrounded by occult items, leading to suspicions that she was a victim of human sacrifice.

events.title: Ötzi The Iceman Is Discovered
events.description: Ötzi before he was removed from the glacier.

events.title: The First National Negro Convention Convenes In Philadelphia
events.description: A total of 40 delegates from seven states meet in the historic Mother Bethel church in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, to discuss the issues of slavery and racial hostility in America. Leaders ultimately pledged to work to improve the lives of Black men, women, and children living in the United States and help those who were able to flee to Canada. The convention sparked a movement of similar meetings across the country, and a strong, collective Black voice soon emerged.

events.title: Upton Sinclair Is Born
events.description: American writer and muckraker Upton Sinclair is born in Baltimore, Maryland. He spent much of his life fighting for workers' rights, and many of his novels criticized the social and economic conditions of the 20th century.

events.title: The First Cannes Film Festival
events.description: AFP/Getty ImagesStars parading in the streets of Cannes for the first festival in 1946.

events.title: Tara Calico Disappears
events.description: YouTubeA mysterious Polaroid found in 1989 that's believed to show Tara Calico.

events.title: "Don't Ask Don't Tell" Is Repealed
events.description: The U.S. military policy "Don't Ask Don't Tell" (DADT) is repealed during the Obama Administration. The DADT policy prevented openly gay, lesbian and bisexual Americans from serving in the U.S. Army Forces while simultaneously preventing the discrimination of closeted homosexual or bisexual servicemen and servicewomen. The act prohibited gay or bisexual members of the military from speaking about their sexual orientation. It also prevented superiors from opening an investigation into the sexual orientation of their subordinates without probable cause. The act was active from 1993 to 2011.

events.title: Storm Area 51: They Can't Stop Us All
events.description: On September 20, 2019 about 150 people camped outside of the gates to the restricted government facility known as Area 51 in the Nevada desert. The event was the culmination of a viral online joke made earlier that same summer from a Facebook user who created a event called "Storm Area 51, They Can't Stop Us All". Of the two million people who RSVP'd, about 150 showed up to the entrance of the facility, and an additional 1,500 attended music festivals in nearby desert towns.

events.title: Virgil Dies
events.description: Virgil, author of the Latin epic poem The Aeneid, dies after contracting a fever on a trip to Greece. He'd traveled to Achaea to revise his famous work and later met with the emperor Augustus, who had commissioned The Aeneid, before falling ill. Virgil died on a ship in the harbor of Brundisium on his way back to Italy, and though he'd ordered his poem to be burned if he died before it was finished, Augustus refused and had it published instead.

events.title: Benedict Arnold Commits Treason
events.description: American General Benedict Arnold meets with John Andre, a British major, and discusses exchanging West Point for a large amount of money and a position in the British army.

events.title: Joseph Smith Claims To Receive A Visit From The Angel Moroni
events.description: Church of Latter-Day Saints founder, Joseph Smith, claims to have received a visit from the angel Moroni. According to Smith, Moroni was the guardian of the golden plates, the source of information that would later be used to write the Book of Mormon. According to Smith, Moroni appeared to him so that he could translate the golden plates and create God's true religion on Earth. After Smith translated the plates, Moroni confiscated them and they were never seen again.

events.title: Nez Perce Chief Joseph Dies Of A "Broken Heart"
events.description: Chief Joseph in 1901.

events.title: The Great New England Hurricane Makes Landfall
events.description: weather.govThe aftermath of the Great New England Hurricane of 1938.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Jr. Weds Carolyn Bessette
events.description: John F. Kennedy Jr. and Carolyn Bessette get married at a secret ceremony on Cumberland Island in Georgia. Sadly, Carolyn and JFK Jr. died in 1999 after he crashed his plane off Martha's Vineyard.

events.title: Shaka Zulu Is Assassinated
events.description: A rendering of Shaka, the founder of the Zulu empire.

events.title: Ilse Koch Is Born
events.description: Concentration camp guard and Nazi war criminal Ilse Koch is born in Dresden, Germany. During World War II, Koch was known as the "Witch of Buchenwald" due to her especially cruel treatment of prisoners. She was even accused of taking the tattooed skin of murdered inmates as a souvenir. After the war, Koch was sentenced to life in prison at a hard labor camp, where she eventually took her own life in 1967.

events.title: Sara Jane Moore Attempts To Assassinate President Gerald Ford
events.description: Janet Fries/Getty ImagesSara Jane Moore in custody after her attempt to kill President Ford.

events.title: Polish Solidarity Movement Begins
events.description: The Polish Solidarity movement begins with the meeting of 36 delegates from regional trade unions in Gdańsk, Poland. Solidarity began as a worker's movement in the 1970s that specifically fought against years of wage stagnation and unfair work practices. In the 1980s, it started to become an anti-communist social movement that attracted major popularity in Poland. After years of harsh suppression by the Polish government, Solidarity finally led to the removal of Soviet influence and opened up the country to semi-free elections.

events.title: Cassie Jo Stoddart Is Killed In The "Scream Murder"
events.description: High school student Cassie Jo Stoddart is stabbed to death by her classmates Brian Draper and Torey Adamcik in their small Idaho town. Stoddart was house sitting for her aunt and uncle when the two 16-year-old boys suddenly entered the home and stabbed her to death — while filming their vicious crime.

events.title: Kublai Khan Is Born
events.description: A post-mortem illustration of Kublai Khan drawn shortly after his death in 1294.

events.title: The Merchant Royal Sinks Into The Atlantic
events.description: The Merchant Royal, an English merchant ship, sinks off the coast of England with over 100,000 pounds of gold onboard. The ship was on its way from Cádiz, Spain back to its home port in London when it began leaking badly.

events.title: Emily Roebling Is Born
events.description: A portrait of Emily Roebling from 1896.

events.title: Planet Neptune Is Observed For The First Time
events.description: Johann Gottfried Galle observes Neptune, the eighth planet in our solar system, for the first time. Urbain Le Verrier, a French astronomer, calculated Neptune's most likely position using Uranus' orbit. Johann Galle used these calculations to observe the planet through a telescope. Researchers believe earlier astronomers, including Galileo, also observed Neptune but did not realize it was a planet. Only 17 days after Neptune's discovery, astronomer William Lassell discovered one of the planet's moons using a homemade telescope.

events.title: Seth Bullock Dies
events.description: Seth Bullock, the sheriff who tamed the Wild West outpost of Deadwood, South Dakota, dies at the age of 70.

events.title: Mickey Rooney Is Born
events.description: Mickey Rooney in 1945.

events.title: First Victim Of The Hydrogen Bomb Dies
events.description: Aikichi Kuboyama, a Japanese fisherman whose ship was caught in the fallout of the Castle Bravo nuclear test, dies at age 40 of radiation sickness. He's considered the first person to die from the hydrogen bomb.

events.title: Mel Ignatow Kills His Girlfriend Brenda Schaefer
events.description: YouTubeMel Ignatow and Brenda Schaefer.

events.title: The U.S. Supreme Court Is Established
events.description: President George Washington signs the Judiciary Act, establishing the federal court system, including the Supreme Court. According to Article Three of the U.S. Constitution, the Supreme Court has ultimate jurisdiction over all laws, particularly when there is a question of constitutionality. When it was first formed, the court was to have six justices, with Washington appointing John Jay as the first chief justice. It wasn't until 1869 that the court was expanded to have nine justices, which remains in place to this day.

events.title: Saigō Takamori Dies
events.description: A depiction of the Battle of Shiroyama, in which Saigō Takamori was killed.

events.title: F. Scott Fitzgerald Is Born
events.description: Princeton University LibraryF. Scott Fitzgerald in 1930.

events.title: President Eisenhower Uses Federal Troops To Enforce Integration In Arkansas
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesSoldiers escort the first African-American students to integrate Little Rock, Arkansas' Central High School on September 24, 1957.

events.title: Nirvana Releases Nevermind, One Of The Most Popular Grunge Albums Of All Time
events.description: The Aberdeen, Washington rock band Nirvana was formed in 1987 by Kurt Kobain and Krist Novoselic. A few years later, Nirvana became a hit in the Seattle grunge scene. In 1991, the band became an international name after the release of the song "Smells Like Teen Spirit" from their second album Nevermind. By the end of 1991, the album was selling 400,000 copies a week in the United States. In total, the album sold more than seven million copies in the United States and over 30 million worldwide.

events.title: Vasco Núñez De Balboa Spots The Pacific Ocean
events.description: A 19th-century portrait of Vasco Núñez de Balboa.

events.title: British Forces Occupy Philadelphia
events.description: British forces occupy Philadelphia during the American Revolution. At the time, Philadelphia was the American capital and a Loyalist hotspot. By taking the city, British forces hoped to draw George Washington into battle with Loyalist support and crush the Continental Army once and for all. Under British occupation, Philadelphia faced massive shortages and the city's citizens often endured cruel treatment by the soldiers. British forces left the city in June 1778 as there had been no strategic advantage to taking the city.

events.title: William Faulkner Is Born
events.description: Prolific writer William Faulkner is born in New Albany, Mississippi. To this day, Faulkner remains one of the most celebrated authors in all of American literature. He won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his novels A Fable and The Reivers, though he's perhaps best known for his book The Sound and the Fury. In all, he wrote 19 novels, 125 short stories, 20 screenplays, and six collections of poetry throughout his 43-year career before dying in 1962.

events.title: Emily Post Dies
events.description: Famed etiquette expert Emily Post dies in her New York City apartment at the age of 87. Post came from a wealthy Baltimore family before attending finishing school in New York as a teenager.

events.title: Joe Valachi Becomes The First Mobster To Publicly Acknowledge The Mafia's Existence
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJoe Valachi was the first Mafioso to break the Mafia's code of silence and publicly admit to its existence.

events.title: John Bonham Dies
events.description: John Bonham, the drummer for Led Zeppelin, dies at the age of 32 by choking on vomit in his sleep following a day of binge drinking.

events.title: Sir Francis Drake Completes His Trip Around The World
events.description: Sir Francis Drake's historic circumnavigation of the globe took nearly three years to complete.

events.title: Johnny Appleseed Is Born
events.description: John Chapman, better known as the folk hero Johnny Appleseed, is born in Leominster, Massachusetts.

events.title: Fire Devastates Deadwood, South Dakota
events.description: A fire burns through the mining wild west town of Deadwood, South Dakota, destroying over 300 buildings. The disaster left hundreds of people homeless, with many people who lost everything leaving town.

events.title: George Gershwin Is Born
events.description: American composer and pianist George Gershwin is born in Brooklyn, New York. He began studying music at age 11, and by his teens he was known as one of the most talented pianists in New York. Some of Gershwin's most famous works include "Rhapsody in Blue" and the opera Porgy and Bess, and he composed 48 shows in total for musical theater and Broadway over the course of his prolific career. Though he died of a brain tumor at just 38 in 1937, his compositions remain an essential part of the American songbook to this day.

events.title: The Brady Bunch Premieres On Television
events.description: The Brady Bunch premieres on television. The beloved American television show revolved around a large blended family, the Bradys, and their adventures. Although it was never a big hit during its time on the air, the show became a cultural icon in the years following its cancellation in 1974. The show eventually featured several spin-offs, including films and Christmas albums. Even today, the show's theme song is easily identified television theme songs in pop culture history.

events.title: Stanislav Petrov Prevents The Outbreak Of Nuclear War
events.description: Scott Peterson/Getty ImagesStanislav Petrov in 2004.

events.title: Actor Johnny Lewis Falls To His Death After Killing His Landlady
events.description: Suffering from severe mental health issues, actor Johnny Lewis of Sons of Anarchy fame murders his landlady before falling to his death off the roof of his Los Angeles home. Ever since he sustained serious head injuries due to a motorcycle accident in October 2011, Lewis had been exhibiting increasingly bizarre and aggressive behavior, including several violent outbursts and an attempt to break into an innocent woman's home.

events.title: Urban VII Dies 12 Days After Becoming Pope
events.description: Pope Urban VII dies a mere 12 days after his election, making his papacy the shortest in history. After Pope Sixtus V died just a month prior on Aug. 27, the papal conclave convened and chose Italian cardinal Giovanni Battista Castagna as the next pope. He took the pontifical name Urban VII, and during his short time in office he banned the use of tobacco in churches. But less than two weeks later, he died of malaria, and Gregory XIV became pope.

events.title: Samuel Adams Is Born
events.description: American politician Samuel Adams, one of the Founding Fathers of the United States, is born in Boston. One of the signers of the Declaration of Independence and a delegate to the Continental Congress, Adams ranked among the most crucial leaders of the American Revolution. He had a pivotal role in the events leading up to the Boston Tea Party, helped draft the Articles of Confederation and the Massachusetts Constitution, and later served as governor of Massachusetts. Meanwhile, his second cousin John Adams served as the second president of the United States.

events.title: Wild Bill Hickok Kills Samuel Strawhun
events.description: An undated photograph of Wild Bill Hickok.

events.title: 'Dear Boss' Letter Received
events.description: The "Dear Boss" Letter, believed to be the first missive sent by the serial killer Jack the Ripper, is received by the Central News Agency. Though debate has continued over whether or not the letter is authentic, it is the first to give the murderer — who had killed two women by that point — a name.

events.title: Sylvia Pankhurst Dies
events.description: Sylvia Pankhurst protesting against British policies in India. 1932.

events.title: Silent Spring Is Published By Rachel Carson
events.description: Silent Spring is published by Rachel Carson. The book exposed the chemical industry for the indiscriminate use of harmful pesticides. She accused the chemical industry of spreading misinformation about the chemicals they were producing. The book led to widespread condemnation of the chemical industry by the American public, a ban on the chemical DDT, and the creation of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

events.title: The Zodiac Killer Murders Calvin Hartnell And Cecelia Ann Shepard
events.description: At the height of his killing spree, the Zodiac killer murders a young couple, Calvin Hartnell and Cecelia Ann Shepard.

events.title: Pompey The Great Is Assassinated
events.description: Roman general Pompey the Great is assassinated in Egypt on the orders of King Ptolemy. A successful military leader, Pompey helped expand the Roman Empire and ruled alongside Julius Caesar as a member of the First Triumvirate. But the increasingly conservative Pompey soon found himself on the opposite side of the political divide from Caesar and the two former allies became bitter enemies.

events.title: William The Conqueror's Norman Conquest Begins
events.description: William the Conqueror lands at Pevensey, England and begins his Norman conquest of the country. He'd been named Duke of Normandy in 1035, but he dreamed of securing the English throne and claimed that his cousin, King Edward the Confessor, had promised him the throne.

events.title: Spanish Explorer Cabrillo Becomes First European To Set Foot In The U.S. East Coast
events.description: Spanish Explorer Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo becomes the first European to set foot in the U.S. East Coast. The governor of Guatemala selected Cabrillo to explore the Pacific because of his track record as a businessman and a leader. On day 103, Cabrillo and his crew entered the San Diego harbor. Laster, Cabrillo and his crew made it to Monterey Bay and Point Reyes before a storm forced them to turn back. After a fight with a native tribe, Cabrillo was injured and died of complications.

events.title: White Sox Players Are Indicted For The "Black Sox Scandal"
events.description: Underwood & Underwood/Wikimedia CommonsThe eight White Sox players incriminated in the 1919 fixing scandal.

events.title: Brigitte Bardot Is Born
events.description: Brigitte Bardot at the 1953 Cannes Film Festival.

events.title: David Camm's Family Is Murdered
events.description: Former state trooper David Camm returns home to find his wife and two children murdered — leading to an investigation where he was implicated and wrongfully convicted for 13 years.

events.title: Caravaggio Is Born
events.description: Caravaggio's painting David with the Head of Goliath. 1610.

events.title: Scotland Yard Is Established
events.description: Scotland Yard, the headquarters for the newly-established Greater London Metropolitan Police, opens in England. Sir Robert Peel, a British politician, established the police force while serving as Home Secretary. He's known as the father of modern British policing, and he is credited with developing the Peelian Principles, or the ethical requirements that officers must follow. The original 1,000 constables at Scotland Yard were called "Bobbies" or "Peelers," with the former especially remaining in use to this day, while the police force itself became informally known as the "Scotland Yard."

events.title: The Chicago Tylenol Murders Begin
events.description: The Daily HeraldOver the course of several days, seven people died after taking Tylenol pills they didn't realize were laced with cyanide.

events.title: NASA Launches Its First Mission Since The Challenger Disaster
events.description: NASA launches the Space Shuttle Discovery from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Known as the "Return to Flight" mission, it was the first manned space flight since the Challenger disaster nearly three years prior. The Discovery had made six previous trips into space between 1984 and 1985, but after the Challenger exploded, NASA overhauled the Discovery to ensure there would not be a repeat of that tragic event which left all seven crew members dead. During the four-day space mission of the Discovery, its crew paid tribute to those lost in the Challenger disaster.

events.title: Police Find The Body Of Regina Walters, Victim Of Serial Killer Robert Rhoades
events.description: Police find the body of Regina Walters, a victim of "Truck Stop Killer" Robert Ben Rhoades. At 14-years old, Walters ran away with her boyfriend and made it to Pasadena, Texas before crossing paths with Rhoades.

events.title: John Billington Is Hanged
events.description: John Billington, the first Englishman to be convicted of murder in America, is hanged for his crime. Billington and his family traveled to the New World on the Mayflower in 1620 — and they were troublemakers from the beginning.

events.title: Jack The Ripper Murders His Third And Fourth Victims
events.description: The Illustrated Police News reports on the murder of Catherine Eddowes.

events.title: Elie Wiesel Is Born
events.description: Author and Holocaust survivor Elie Wiesel is born in Sighet, Romania. He wrote 57 books over his prolific career, but he's perhaps best known for Night, his memoir of life as a Jewish prisoner in the Auschwitz and Buchenwald concentration camps as a teenager. After World War II, he became a journalist and later moved to the United States, where he worked as a foreign correspondent for an Israeli newspaper and then as a professor at Boston University. Wiesel was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1986 for his work as a "messenger to mankind."

events.title: James Dean Dies
events.description: John Springer Collection/CORBIS/Corbis via Getty ImagesThe wrecked remains of James Dean's Porsche 550 Spyder.

events.title: Stephen King Checks In At The Stanley Hotel
events.description: While on vacation during a short residency in Boulder, Colorado, Stephen King and his wife Tabitha spend the night at the Stanley Hotel, ultimately inspiring King's bestselling novel The Shining. The hotel was about to close for the season, and the Kings were the only overnight guests in the entire building.

events.title: The Tokaimura Nuclear Incident
events.description: Workers at a uranium processing facility in Japan accidentally create a criticality event. This leads to a release of radiation, causing severe injuries to the workers and raising concerns about nuclear safety.

events.title: Mary I Becomes Queen Of England
events.description: Queen Mary I is said to have burned some 280 religious dissenters at the stake.

events.title: The First Orphan Train Arrives
events.description: The first Orphan Train, a humanitarian project involving shipping impoverished city kids to rural American towns for adoption, arrives in Michigan.

events.title: The 'Saucy Jack' Postcard Is Recieved
events.description: The "Saucy Jack" postcard, believed to have been sent by Jack the Ripper just after the murders of Elizabeth Stride and Catherine Eddowes, is received by the Central News Agency.

events.title: Yosemite National Park Is Established
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesYosemite National Park photographed in 1951.

events.title: President Jimmy Carter Is Born
events.description: President Jimmy Carter is born in Plains, Georgia.

events.title: Julie Andrews Is Born
events.description: Iconic actress and singer Julie Andrews is born in Surrey, England. Andrews got her start as a child and appeared in plays on Broadway and in London's West End before starring in a number of historic films, including Mary Poppins (1964) and The Sound of Music (1965). She has continued working, principally as a voice actress, into the 2020s.

events.title: Levittown, New York Opens
events.description: Levittown, New York — the first mass produced suburb — opens for residents. However, it was initially only available for white homebuyers.

events.title: Pelé Plays His Last Game
events.description: Alessandro Sabattini/Getty ImagesSoccer star Pelé of Brazil celebrates after winning the 1970 World Cup in Mexico, between Brazil and Italy.

events.title: Polly Klaas Is Kidnaped
events.description: 12-year-old Polly Klaas is kidnapped out of her home during a slumber party with two of her friends. Her disappearance caught the attention of the nation, and the search for her lasted nearly two months. Unfortunately, she was killed just two hours after her abduction.

events.title: Stephen Paddock Perpetrates The Las Vegas Shooting
events.description: Stephen Paddock, a 64-year-old businessman, perpetrates the Las Vegas shooting. From his 32nd-floor room at Mandalay Bay, Paddock shot and killed over 60 people attending the Route 91 Harvest. In total, over 400 people were injured in what would be the United States' deadliest shooting. Paddock would later commit suicide in his room before investigators could apprehend him. Before the shooting, Paddock lived a relatively solitary life and did not capture the attention of law enforcement. Even today, investigators are still unsure of the motive behind the event.

events.title: John André Is Hanged
events.description: John Andre is hanged as a spy in Tappan, New York. A British major, Andre had been arrested on Sept. 23 with papers in his boot that proved that American general Benedict Arnold planned to surrender the fort at West Point, New York, to the British for £20,000. Arnold deserted and fled, and Andre was found guilty of spying and executed.

events.title: Mahatma Gandhi Is Born
events.description: Dinodia Photos/Getty ImagesMahatma Gandhi in 1944.

events.title: Tim Allen Is Arrested
events.description: Kalamazoo Michigan Sheriff's DepartmentTim Allen's mugshot.

events.title: Rock Hudson Dies
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesRock Hudson spent his career as a Hollywood heartthrob but kept his sexual orientation a secret.

events.title: St. Francis Of Assisi Dies
events.description: A depiction of St. Francis of Assisi circa 1597 and 1599.

events.title: Thanksgiving Becomes An American Holiday
events.description: At the height of the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln declares a national day of Thanksgiving following a Union Army victory at the Battle of Gettysburg. In addition, Lincoln proclaimed that every fourth Thursday in November would thenceforth be celebrated as Thanksgiving. Though President Franklin D. Roosevelt briefly moved the holiday to the third Thursday, it was permanently set to be the fourth Thursday in 1941.

events.title: Germany Becomes Reunified
events.description: Germany becomes reunified after 45 years of separation. After the Second World War, Germany was split into essentially two sections: the Allied-controlled west and the Soviet-controlled east. In November of 1989, the Berlin Wall, a wall which separated Berlin, fell. The Soviet Union would later fall in 1991, bringing an end to the Cold War. With the reunification of Germany, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization granted membership to the state and Berlin became the official capital of reunified Germany.

events.title: O.J. Simpson Is Acquitted
events.description: MYUNG J. CHUN/AFP via Getty ImagesO.J. Simpson reacts to the verdict on October 3, 1995.

events.title: Lisa Irwin Goes Missing
events.description: Ten-month-old Lisa Irwin goes missing from her home in Kansas City, Missouri in the middle of the night. Despite a number of clues, including three cell phones that were also taken from the house, Irwin has never been found. Though some believe that she was killed by her mother, others contend that she was kidnapped by a stranger and may still be alive.

events.title: The Gregorian Calendar Is Introduced
events.description: Pope Gregory XIII introduces the Gregorian calendar. The new calendar "fixed" a mistake in the previously-used Julian calendar, which had miscalculated the length of a solar year by 11 minutes and caused Easter to move further and further from the spring equinox.

events.title: The Battle Of Cable Street Takes Place
events.description: National Media Museum/Daily Herald Archive/SSPL/Getty ImagesOswald Mosley, the leader of the British Union of Fascists, triggered the Battle of Cable Street when he and his paramilitary Blackshirts marched through East London.

events.title: The USSR Launches Sputnik 1
events.description: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1 from the Tyuratam launch base in the Kazakh Republic. The first satellite to orbit the Earth, Sputnik's launch triggered the start of the Space Race between the U.S.S.R. and the United States. Americans, shocked by the Soviet satellite, poured money into their own space program and launched a satellite called Explorer 1 in 1958.

events.title: Janis Joplin Dies
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJanis Joplin at Shea Stadium on August 6, 1970.

events.title: Contact Is Made With The Korowai Tribe
events.description: Dutch missionary Johannes Veldhuizen makes contact with the Korowai Tribe of Papua, Indonesia, becoming one of the first Westerners to ever interact with them.

events.title: Rocky Dennis Dies
events.description: People MagazineRocky Dennis and his mother, Rusty, whom he shared an incredibly close bond with.

events.title: The Loomis Fargo Robbery Unfolds
events.description: The second largest cash robbery in U.S. history up until that point, the Loomis Fargo robbery saw several thieves make off with $17.3 million. Led by vault supervisor David Ghantt, the perpetrators took the money from the Loomis, Fargo & Co. facility in Charlotte, North Carolina. And though they got away with it for a time, authorities eventually tracked them down, arresting 24 people and recovering 88 percent of the money.

events.title: Shawnee Chief Tecumseh Is Killed
events.description: Shawnee Chief Tecumseh is killed at the age of 45 during the Battle of the Thames. A Native American leader and warrior from the area that would become Ohio, Tecumseh resisted the expansion of white American settlers throughout the entirety of his storied life. He founded a confederacy of tribes and allied with the British to fight American expansion, but he ultimately died during that fateful clash during the War of 1812.

events.title: The Dalton Gang Is Wiped Out
events.description: Deceased members of the Dalton gang following their failed bank robberies.

events.title: Dave Kunst Completes His Walk Around The World
events.description: Dave Kunst becomes the first verified person in history to circumnavigate the globe on foot. About four years earlier, he and his brother John left Waseca, Minnesota, and started walking east. They walked around the world — John was killed by bandits in Afghanistan in 1972 — and Dave returned to Waseca in 1974.

events.title: Timothy Treadwell, The "Grizzly Man," And His Girlfriend Are Fatally Attacked By A Bear
events.description: Lions Gate PicturesTimothy Treadwell had been warned several times by park rangers that his bear encounters would one day turn deadly.

events.title: Steve Jobs Dies
events.description: Justin Sullivan/Getty ImagesMany thought Steve Jobs looked gaunt in 2006, though an Apple spokesperson insisted his health was "robust."

events.title: The Reno Brothers Commit America's First Train Robbery
events.description: Frank Reno, one of the Reno brothers.

events.title: Alfred, Lord Tennyson Dies
events.description: Alfred, Lord Tennyson dies in Sussex, England, at the age of 83. A respected poet during the Victorian age, Tennyson penned poems like "In Memoriam," Idylls of the King," and "The Charge of the Light Brigade." From 1850 until his death, Tennyson was Queen Victoria's poet laureate.

events.title: Lonnie Johnson Is Born
events.description: Thomas S. England/The LIFE Images Collection via Getty Images/Getty ImagesLonnie Johnson with his invention.

events.title: Shawn Hornbeck Is Kidnapped
events.description: Shawn Hornbeck is kidnapped by Mike Devlin while riding his bike in Richwoods, Missouri. Devlin had bumped the 11-year-old Hornbeck with his truck before snatching the boy. For four years, Devlin would imprison Hornbeck in his apartment, physically and emotionally abusing the boy. In 2007, Devlin used Hornbeck to kidnap another boy, Ben Ownby, from Beaufort, Missouri. Tips eventually led to the identification of Devlin's truck, and the FBI soon located his apartment as well. During a raid, police found both Hornbeck and Ownby. Their rescue became known as the "Missouri Miracle."

events.title: Instagram Launches
events.description: The Instagram app is released for the first time in the Apple Store. Three months earlier, Instagram co-founder Mike Krieger posted the first Instagram photo — of South Beach Harbor at Pier 38 in San Francisco. Since then, the app has been acquired by Meta and downloaded more than 3 billion times.

events.title: William Still Is Born
events.description: William Still is born in Burlington County, New Jersey. An abolitionist known as the "Father of the Underground Railroad," Still helped rescue some 800 enslaved people from bondage. He later wrote The Underground Railroad Records (1872) the original firsthand account of this chapter in history that was written by a Black American.

events.title: Edgar Allan Poe Dies
events.description: Edgar Allen Poe in 1849, the year he died.

events.title: Mother Teresa Founds The Missionaries Of Charity
events.description: Mother Teresas missionary order eventually grew to include 4,500 nuns in 133 countries.

events.title: Myra Hindley And Ian Brady Are Arrested For The Moors Murders
events.description: Myra Hindley and her lover Ian Brady are arrested for the Moors Murders in England. During their relationship, Hindley and Brady abducted, raped, and murdered at least four children. The murderous couple was apprehended after Hindley's brother-in-law overheard the beating of one of the victims. Police would later uncover photos and audio recordings of the brutal murders. Both Hindley and Brady received life sentences for their crimes, and today they are still known as some of the worst criminals in British history.

events.title: Anna Politkovskaya Is Assassinated
events.description: Novaya Gazeta/Epsilon/Getty ImagesAnna Politkovskaya's murderers have never been found.

events.title: The Great Chicago Fire Starts
events.description: Archive Photos/Getty ImagesThe aftermath of the Great Chicago fire.

events.title: The Deadliest Wildfire In Recorded History Sparks
events.description: The Great Chicago Fire wasn't the only history-making fire to begin on this day in 1871. The Peshtigo Fire, the deadliest wildfire in recorded history, started in the nearby state of Wisconsin. While then-overshadowed in the headlines by the fire in Chicago, winds as strong as 110 mph led to the destruction of over 17 communities in northeastern part of the state. In total, anywhere from 1,500 to 2,500 people were killed in the blaze.

events.title: Ma Barker Is Born
events.description: Kate "Ma" Barker is born in Ash Grove, Missouri. She and her four sons, Herman, Lloyd, Arthur, and Fred, embarked on one of American history's most infamous crime sprees in the 1920s and '30s, robbing banks across the central United States. However, her life of crime came to an end in 1935, when FBI agents shot and killed Ma and Fred Barker in Ocklawaha, Florida.

events.title: Che Guevara Is Captured
events.description: Che Guevara in Bolivia shortly before his death.

events.title: Linate Airport Disaster Occurs In Milan
events.description: The Linate Airport disaster occurs in Milan. During the early foggy morning, Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 686 and a Cessna Citation CJ2 business jet collided during takeoff, killing 114 people. This accident came as a result of the Cessna's pilots' inability to navigate properly in the dense fog, as well as numerous safety feature failures. It is the deadliest aviation disaster in Italian history.

events.title: Martha Stewart Goes To Prison
events.description: Martha Stewart enters prison at Alderson Federal Prison Camp in West Virginia. A writer and TV personality who rose to fame with her cooking and entertaining advice, Stewart was found guilty of conspiracy, obstruction of justice, and making false statements for lying about selling stocks as part of an insider trading scheme in 2001. In the end, she served five months in prison and five months under house arrest before getting a full release and going right back to work as a media mogul whose empire remains strong to this day.

events.title: Roger Williams Is Banished From Massachusetts Bay Colony
events.description: Theologian and author Roger Williams is banished from the Massachusetts Bay Colony. A Puritan minister, Williams was expelled by the General Court of Massachusetts for calling for religious tolerance, which officials saw as "Satan's Policy." He went on to establish the neighboring Colony of Rhode Island, the forerunner of the very state itself. To this day, he's remembered for his beliefs regarding separation of church and state as well as fair treatment of Native Americans.

events.title: The Vajont Dam Disaster Kills 2,000 People
events.description: Vajont Survivor's CommissionThe city of Longarone, before and after the Vajont Dam disaster.

events.title: Oskar Schindler Dies
events.description: Oskar Schindler was named Righteous Among the Nations by the Israeli government in 1993 for his heroics during the Holocaust.

events.title: Aileen Wuornos Is Executed
events.description: Acey Harper/The LIFE Images Collection/Getty ImagesAn investigator holds a photo of Aileen Wuornos and her first victim, Richard Mallory.

events.title: Malala Is Shot By Taliban
events.description: Malala is shot by the Taliban for speaking out about women's rights to education. Malala Yousafzai was a Pakistani education activist. Growing up in Pakistan's Swat Valley, Malala went to a school owned by her father. When she was 11, the Taliban took control of her hometown, banning women from attending school.

events.title: The U.S. Naval Academy Opens
events.description: The Naval School opens in Annapolis, Maryland. Renamed the U.S. Naval Academy five years later, the school started with just 50 students and seven professors. Today, the school has more than 4,500 students who go on to become some of the highest-ranking officers in the U.S. Navy and Marines.

events.title: Fridtjof Nansen Is Born
events.description: Fridtjof Nansen in 1889.

events.title: Wuchang Uprising Begins
events.description: The Wuchang Uprising begins in Wuchang, China. This localized act of rebellion swiftly snowballed into the 1911 Xinhai Revolution, which ultimately succeeded in overthrowing the Qing Dynasty. In January 1912, revolutionaries replaced the 2,132-year-old imperial system with the Republic of China.

events.title: Joseph Harris Murders His Former Coworkers
events.description: Joseph Harris shoots and kills two former coworkers at a post office in Ridgewood, New Jersey, then barricades himself inside and throws explosives at the police. The night before, the former postal worker had also killed his old boss with a samurai sword and shot her boyfriend. Prosecutors later determined that Harris had also killed his broker, and raped both his wife and daughter, in 1988. In the end, his actions gave rise to the phrase "going postal."

events.title: Christopher Reeve Dies
events.description: Warner Bros. Pictures/Getty ImagesChristopher Reeve as Superman in 1978.

events.title: The Aleppo Earthquake Strikes
events.description: The Aleppo earthquake strikes Aleppo in present-day Syria. Occurring just one day after a smaller tremor in the area, the earthquake impacted Aleppo as well as several surrounding towns. Historians estimate that 230,000 people perished in one of the deadliest disasters of its kind in human history.

events.title: Meriwether Lewis Dies
events.description: Meriwether Lewis was just 35 when he died in 1809.

events.title: Eleanor Roosevelt Is Born
events.description: President Harry S. Truman later called Eleanor Roosevelt the "First Lady of the World."

events.title: The Boer War Begins
events.description: The Boer War begins in South Africa. The conflict, which pitted the South African Boers, self-governing republics made up of settlers of Dutch extraction, against the British Empire, lasted for three years. In 1902, the British triumphed and the signing of the Peace of Vereeniging ended the war.

events.title: The Killing Of Paul Lee Stine
events.description: Paul Lee Stine, a taxi driver, is brutally murdered by the Zodiac killer.

events.title: Saturday Night Live Debuts
events.description: NBC/TwitterThe cast of SNL in 1975.

events.title: Christopher Columbus Reaches The "New World"
events.description: Christopher Columbus reaches the Bahamas, stumbling upon the Americas while searching for a westward route to Asia. Columbus had set sail about two months earlier with a fleet of three ships, the Santa Maria, the Pinta, and the Nina. Though he had meant to find Asia — and believed, at first, that he had — he actually became the first European since the Vikings to reach North America, which was then dubbed the "New World."

events.title: The First Oktoberfest Takes Place
events.description: Zangl/ullstein bild via Getty ImagesAn Oktoberfest postcard from 1896.

events.title: Aleister Crowley Is Born
events.description: A self-styled practitioner of the dark arts, Aleister Crowley shocked and scandalized England in the late Victorian and Edwardian eras.

events.title: Inejiro Asanuma Is Assassinated On Live TV
events.description: Yasushi NagaoInejiro Asanuma's assassination shocked audiences as it unfolded on live TV.

events.title: Nancy Spungen Dies
events.description: Nancy Spungen is found dead at the Chelsea Hotel in New York City with a fatal stab wound at the age of just 20. The girlfriend of Sex Pistols bassist Sid Vicious, Spungen suffered a fate that has long mystified investigators. Though Vicious was charged with her death, he died of a heroin overdose while awaiting trial, and others have speculated that Spungen was killed by a drug dealer.

events.title: Serial Killer Luis Garavito Dies
events.description: "The Beast" of Colombia, Luis Garavito, the serial killer who murdered hundreds of children in the 1990s dies in prison while awaiting parole.

events.title: Construction Begins On The White House
events.description: The first cornerstone is laid for the White House in Washington D.C. Then known as the "President's House," it was the first public building to be erected in the country's capital. The building was designed by James Hoban, an Irish-born architect who modeled the residence after Leinster House in Dublin, today's home of the Irish Parliament.

events.title: Margaret Thatcher Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesMargaret Thatcher giving a speech in 1984.

events.title: Milton Hershey Dies
events.description: Milton Hershey dies in Hershey, Pennsylvania, of pneumonia at the age of 88. The founder of the Hershey Company, Hershey introduced the world to candies like Hershey's Kiss after inventing a new chocolate formula that allowed it to be transported long distances without melting.

events.title: Herbert Mullin Murders His First Victim
events.description: Bettmann/Contributor/Getty ImagesHerbert Mullin walking into a courthouse in April 1973.

events.title: Chilean Miners Are Rescued After 69 Days
events.description: Thirty-three miners trapped in the San Jose gold and copper mine in Santiago, Chile, are rescued after 69 days. Approximately two months earlier, they became trapped after the mine collapsed.

events.title: The Battle of Hastings Takes Place
events.description: Outside of Hastings, England, this battle pitted invading Norman forces led by William the Conqueror against English forces led by the Anglo-Saxon King Harold II. Ending in a victory for the Normans and with King Harold II dead, William became the king of England.

events.title: Dwight D. Eisenhower Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesDwight D. Eisenhower in the Oval Office in 1956.

events.title: The First Sherlock Holmes Book Is Published
events.description: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes is published. Written by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, the book was the first collection of Doyle's earliest short stories that followed the adventures of a brilliant detective named Sherlock Holmes and his assistant, Dr. John Watson.

events.title: Theodore Roosevelt Survives An Assassination Attempt
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt is shot by John Schrank in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, but survives thanks to his long speech and spectacles case in his breast pocket, which slowed the bullet.

events.title: 'Desert Fox' Erwin Rommel Dies By Suicide
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesAdolf Hitler shakes hands with Erwin Rommel circa 1940, before their relationship soured.

events.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis Begins
events.description: The Cuban Missile Crisis begins when a U-2 spy plane detects construction for Soviet nuclear missile silos in Cuba.

events.title: Virgil Is Born
events.description: Virgil is born in present-day Italy. One of ancient Rome's greatest poets, Virgil composed the Eclogues, the Georgics, and the epic Aeneid, which tells the legendary story of Aeneas, a Trojan hero who flees Troy after the events of Homer's Odyssey and eventually becomes the ancestor of all Romans.

events.title: Jack the Ripper Sends The 'From Hell' Letter
events.description: A photograph of Jack the Ripper's "From Hell" letter. The original has since been lost.

events.title: Mata Hari Is Executed
events.description: This small-town girl from Holland found fame as an exotic dancer and claimed an Indian priestess gave her the name Mata Hari, which is Malaysian for "eye of the day."

events.title: Hermann Göring Dies By Suicide
events.description: Fox Photos/Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesHermann Göring, far left, exchanges a word with Adolf Hitler, second from right, during Hitler's 50th birthday parade in Berlin, Germany, on April 20, 1939.

events.title: The Black Panthers Are Founded
events.description: The Black Panther Party for Self Defense is founded in Oakland, California by Huey Newton and Bobby Seale. The group aimed to confront politicians, challenge police, and protect African Americans after civil rights efforts in the American South failed to secure fair treatment of African Americans. The group believed that progress and freedom could not come from peaceful protest. The party disbanded in 1982.

events.title: Leonarda Cianciulli, The Soap-Maker Of Correggio, Dies
events.description: Leonarda Cianciulli dies at the women's criminal asylum in Pozzuoli, Italy. Cianciulli was sentenced to thirty years in prison for the murders of three women. After her son joined the Italian Army in World War Two, Cianciulli grew increasingly superstitious and put her energy into murdering and turning women into soap and baked goods between 1939 and 1940 as a form of human sacrifice to protect her son.

events.title: Marie Antoinette Is Executed
events.description: Marie Antoinette and Louis XVI were recaptured during their attempted escape to the Netherlands.

events.title: Oscar Wilde Is Born
events.description: Napoleon Sarony/Universal History Archive/Getty ImagesOscar Wilde lounging on a couch in an undated photo.

events.title: John Brown Raids Harpers Ferry
events.description: John Brown leads a raid on a federal armory in Harpers Ferry, Virginia (now West Virginia). An abolitionist, Brown had hoped to start a revolt among Southern slaves to abolish slavery for good in the United States. He'd even drafted a new constitution that outlawed slavery.

events.title: The Cardiff Giant Is 'Discovered'
events.description: J L Hamar/Frederic Lewis/Getty ImagesThe Cardiff Giant in 1869.

events.title: Jack The Ripper's 'From Hell' Letter Is Delivered
events.description: George Lusk, the head of the Whitechapel Vigilance Committee, receives a letter addressed "From Hell" purportedly from Jack the Ripper, which contained a piece of a human kidney that may have belonged to Jack the Ripper victim Catherine Eddowes.

events.title: Ten Nazi War Criminals Are Hanged
events.description: Ten high-ranking Nazis are hanged in Nuremberg, Germany. Two weeks earlier, the officials had been found guilty of crimes against humanity, crimes against peace, and war crimes, for their activities during World War II.

events.title: Baby Jessica Is Rescued From A Well
events.description: Barbara Laing / Liaison AgencyA police officer holds baby Jessica McClure moments after she was rescued from the bottom of a well.

events.title: Dennis Hof Dies
events.description: Dennis Hof, a Nevada brothel owner and reality star, dies at one of his brothels at the age of 72. Despite his death, Hof won an election for Nevada State Assembly over his Democratic opponent several weeks later.

events.title: The London Beer Flood Takes Place
events.description: An iron ring snaps on a wooden vat of beer that contains 3,500 barrels of ale at the Meux and Company brewery in London, England. Liquid gushed forth, penetrating several more vats of ale, ultimately unleashing some 320,000 gallons of beer onto the streets of London's poor St. Giles neighborhood in the West End.

events.title: Al Capone Is Sentenced For Tax Evasion
events.description: Imagno/Getty ImagesAl Capone, one of America's most notorious gangsters.

events.title: Albert Einstein Flees Nazi Germany
events.description: Albert Einstein arrives in the United States after fleeing Nazi Germany. The theoretical physicist, who was Jewish, had decided not to return to Germany after Adolf Hitler became the country's chancellor. He settled in Princeton, New Jersey, and found work at Princeton University.

events.title: Eminem Is Born
events.description: FacebookA teenage Eminem celebrating his birthday in the late 1980s.

events.title: Robert Berchtold Abducts Jan Broberg
events.description: Robert Berchtold abducts Jan Broberg from her home in Pocatello, Idaho. After befriending the Broberg family, Berchtold used his charisma and charm to get closer to 12-year-old Jan. After telling her family that he would pick her up from piano lessons, Berchtold drugged Jan and took her to Mexico where he started feeding her stories about aliens. There, they were legally married, and Berchtold began sexually assaulting her. Later, the two would return to Idaho without repercussions, and Berchtold would kidnap Jan for second time years later.

events.title: King Ferdinand And Queen Isabella Marry
events.description: King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella's wedding portrait circa 1469.

events.title: Edward Winslow Is Born
events.description: Edward Winslow, a Pilgrim on the Mayflower and a three-time governor of Plymouth Colony, is born in Droitwich Spa, England.

events.title: The Mason-Dixon Line Is Established
events.description: The Mason-Dixon Line is established following a survey by Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon. Though the survey was meant to resolve a dispute over the borders between Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Delaware in Colonial America, the Mason-Dixon line would have far-reaching consequences. Over the next century, it would mark the border between "slave" states in the South and "free" states in the North.

events.title: Thomas Edison Dies
events.description: Thomas Edison, American inventor and businessman, dies in New Jersey at the age of 84. Edison is one of the most prolific inventors in the world, with creations such as the lightbulb, phonograph, and movie camera under his belt. While at his home in West Orange, New Jersey, Edison died due to complications with diabetes. He is buried behind the home.

events.title: Wayne Nance Is Born
events.description: Missoula County Sheriff's OfficeWayne Nance's driver's license photo.

events.title: John Lennon And Yoko Ono Are Arrested For Drug Posession
events.description: John Lennon and Yoko Ono are arrested for possessing drugs in London, England. Police and drug-sniffing dogs searched their residence, where they found hashish and cannabis. Out of fears that Ono might be deported, Lennon pled guilty and was fined £150.

events.title: Jonathan Swift Dies
events.description: Jonathan Swift, Irish satirist and author, dies in Dublin, Ireland. Swift is mostly known for his work A Modest Proposal and Gulliver's Travels. As a writer, Swift is known for his emphasis on reason and his distrust of emotions. His writing conveys his frustrations with a political system that was wrought with inequality in a way that still shocks and entertains readers today. There is a reason why he is called the father of Western satire.

events.title: British Forces Surrender At Yorktown
events.description: The forces of British Major General Charles Cornwallis surrender to French and American forces after the Battle of Yorktown.

events.title: Thomas Jefferson Is Accused Of Having An Affair With An Enslaved Woman
events.description: Thomas Jefferson in the 1790s.

events.title: The St. Albans Raid Takes Place
events.description: The St. Albans raid takes place in St. Albans, Vermont. Two dozen Confederate soldiers raided the town from Canada, killing one man and robbing several banks. Their two primary goals were to steal funds to support the Confederacy and draw Union troops north away from the battlefields near the Mason-Dixon line.

events.title: John DeLorean Is Arrested
events.description: Tony Korody/Sygma/Sygma via Getty ImageJohn DeLorean with his famous car, circa 1979.

events.title: The City Of La Paz, Bolivia, Is Founded
events.description: The city of La Paz, Bolivia, is founded by Spanish conquistador Alonso de Mendoza. Today, the city is the highest capital in the world.

events.title: Tokugawa Family Establishes Hegemony
events.description: The Tokugawa family establishes hegemony in Japan. As Japan's military leader, or shogun, Tokugawa Ieyasu, maintained control over other houses by reorganizing them based on loyalty and requiring them to live in the nation's capital for extended periods of time. Under Tokugawa rule, Japan maintained internal stability and economic growth. The period is well-known for its anti-foreigner policies which effectively isolated Japan from the rest of the world for over two centuries.

events.title: The Louisiana Purchase Is Ratified
events.description: The U.S. Senate ratifies a treaty with France, officially approving the purchase of Louisiana Territory. The so-called Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the country overnight, adding territory that later became the states of Louisiana, Arkansas, Missouri, Iowa, Oklahoma, Kansas, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico, Montana, Wyoming, Colorado, and parts of Minnesota.

events.title: The Sydney Opera House Opens
events.description: Mariano Mantel/FlickrThe Sydney Opera House is an iconic landmark today.

events.title: Lynyrd Skynyrd Band Members Die In A Plane Crash
events.description: A plane carrying the band Lynyrd Skynyrd crashes into a forest near Gillsburg, Mississippi. The band had chartered the plane from Greeneville, South Carolina, to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, but ran out of fuel just before it reached its destination.

events.title: Muammar Gaddafi Is Killed
events.description: Mario Tama/Getty ImagesMuammar Gaddafi gestures at the United Nations during an address on Sept. 23, 2009 in New York City.

events.title: The Battle Of Trafalgar Takes Place
events.description: A British fleet led by Admiral Lord Nelson clashes with a combined Spanish and French fleet off the coast of Cape Trafalgar, Spain, during the Napoleonic Wars. Napoleon sought to invade England but was thwarted when he encountered Nelson's fleet in the Atlantic. Although Nelson was vastly outnumbered, the Battle of Trafalgar resulted in an overwhelming British victory, sinking 22 Spanish and French ships. Nelson, however, was killed.

events.title: Dizzy Gillespie Is Born
events.description: /BettmannDizzy Gillespie plays the trumpet in 1955.

events.title: Dorothy Hale Dies By Suicide
events.description: Dorothy Hale dies by suicide after jumping off a building in New York City. A socialite and aspiring actress, Hale rubbed elbows with prominent artists, writers, and even royalty. But her professional and personal setbacks proved too much for her to bear.

events.title: The Aberfan Disaster Takes Place
events.description: Jim Gray/Getty ImagesRescue workers search for survivors following the Aberfan disaster, in which a giant coal slag heap consumed the South Wales town.

events.title: Alyssa Bustamante Murders Her Neighbor
events.description: Alyssa Bustamante murders her nine-year-old neighbor, Elizabeth Olten, in St. Martins, Missouri. Before this crime, friends and family described Alyssa as a normal, happy girl. She received good grades in school, attended church regularly, and wrote poetry. That all changed after her neighbor came to her house to play and never returned home. Police found a shallow grave containing the remains of Olten in Alyssa's backyard. She was arrested and quickly agreed to a plea deal which allowed a judge to convict her of second degree murder.

events.title: The World's First Parachute Jump Is Made
events.description: André-Jacques Garnerin jumps out of a hot air balloon with a parachute 3,000 feet over Paris, France. The French innovator and balloonist landed safely on the ground, marking the first successful parachute jump in history.

events.title: Franz Liszt Is Born
events.description: Franz Liszt in 1858.

events.title: Pretty Boy Floyd Is Killed
events.description: Charles Arthur "Pretty Boy" Floyd is shot and killed by FBI agents in East Liverpool, Ohio, at the age of 30. A bank robber dubbed "Public Enemy Number One," Floyd was popular among the public because he allegedly destroyed mortgage papers at the banks he robbed, freeing people of their debts. To people impoverished by the Great Depression and whose homes had been seized by the banks, he was a hero.

events.title: Lance Armstrong Is Stripped Of Tour De France Medals
events.description: Doug Pensinger/Getty ImagesLance Armstrong raises his arms as he wins stage 17 of the Tour de France on July 22, 2004.

events.title: Philip Chism Murders His High School Teacher
events.description: Fourteen-year-old Philip Chism murders his high school teacher, Colleen Ritzer, in the high school bathroom. During an after school study session, Ritzer excused herself from the classroom the use the restroom. Chism followed behind, and violently attacked and assaulted Ritzer in the bathroom. After he was done, Chism placed Ritzer's body into a trash bin and dumped her body behind the school. He then went to see a movie.

events.title: Marcus Junius Brutus Dies By Suicide
