events.description: Marcus Junius Brutus dies by suicide, allegedly by falling on his sword, around the age of 42 near Philippi, Macedonia. Two years earlier, Brutus had infamously betrayed Julius Caesar and orchestrated his assassination.

events.title: Bethlem Hospital Is Founded
events.description: Print Collector/Getty ImagesAn 18th century depiction of mentally disturbed patients at Bethlem Hospital.

events.title: Ang Lee Is Born
events.description: Ang Lee is born in P'ing-tung, Taiwan. A renowned filmmaker, Lee has written, directed, and produced a number of award-winning films. Lee originally wanted to be an actor, but he turned to directing once he realized his struggles with English would be difficult to overcome.

events.title: Selena Quintanilla's Killer Is Found Guilty
events.description: FacebookSelena Quintanilla and Yolanda Saldívar, her future killer.

events.title: Dr. Barnett Slepian Is Killed By An Anti-Abortion Radical
events.description: Barnett Slepian is shot and killed at his Amherst, New York, home at the age of 52. One of three doctors who provided abortions in the greater Buffalo area in the 1990s, Slepian was murdered by James Charles Kopp, an anti-abortion radical.

events.title: The Thirty Years' War Ends
events.description: The Battle of Prague, the last significant battle of the Thirty Years' War.

events.title: Sarah Josepha Hale Is Born
events.description: Sarah Josepha Hale, the American writer who penned "Mary Had A Little Lamb" and pushed for Thanksgiving to be a national holiday, is born in Newport, New Hampshire.

events.title: The First Transcontinental Telegraph Line Is Completed
events.description: The Western Union Telegraph Company links the eastern and western telegraph networks at Salt Lake City, Utah. As the nation's first transcontinental telegraph line — finished eight years before the transcontinental railroad — it connected the nation like never before.

events.title: Annie Edson Taylor Goes Down Niagara Falls In A Barrel
events.description: Annie Edson Taylor poses next to her barrel in 1902.

events.title: Rose Bundy Is Born
events.description: Rose Bundy is born. The daughter of serial killer Ted Bundy and his wife Carole Ann Boone, Rose was born while her father was on death row awaiting execution for the murders he'd committed across seven states.

events.title: Rosa Parks Dies
events.description: Rosa Parks dies in Detroit, Michigan, at the age of 92. A civil rights activist, Parks is best known for refusing to move to the back of a bus on Dec. 1, 1955, in Montgomery, Alabama.

events.title: The Battle Of Agincourt Takes Place
events.description: A depiction of the Battle of Agincourt from the 15th-century.

events.title: The Charge Of The Light Brigade Fails
events.description: A British light cavalry charges Russian forces during the Battle of Balaclava. Due to a failure in communications, the "Light Brigade" attacked the wrong artillery battery. Further complicating matters, Captain Louis Nolan, the man who delivered the initial confusing order, died in the first minute of fighting.

events.title: Pablo Picasso Is Born
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesPablo Picasso with one of his paintings.

events.title: The U.S. Invades Grenada
events.description: The U.S. invades Grenada under the Reagan administration. After gaining independence from Great Britain in 1974, Grenada experienced a communist power struggle that resulted in a burst of political violence. The U.S. invaded the country following an appeal for help from the Organization of Eastern Caribbean States. Grenada's communist leader, Maurice Bishop, was deposed and replaced. Today, the invasion date is celebrated as Thanksgiving Day to commemorate the freeing of political prisoners after Bishop's removal.

events.title: Susan Smith Reports A False Carjacking After Murdering Her Children
events.description: Susan Smith falsely reports that a Black man carjacked her vehicle with her two young sons inside. In fact, Smith had murdered both her children by driving her car into a South Carolina lake. After nine days of media frenzy, Smith admitted the truth and was arrested for murder.

events.title: The Erie Canal Opens
events.description: The Erie Canal opens in upstate New York. In development since 1817, the canal connected the Great Lakes with the Atlantic Ocean. Although it was initially derided as a "Clinton's Folly" — after New York Governor DeWitt Clinton who supported its construction — it proved a swift success.

events.title: 'Bloody Bill' Anderson Is Killed
events.description: Bloody Bill Anderson shortly after his death.

events.title: The Shootout At The O.K. Corral Takes Place
events.description: The Earp brothers, joined by Doc Holliday, face off against the Clanton-McLaury gang in Tombstone, Arizona. The so-called "gunfight at the OK Corral" came out of tensions between the Earps and the cattle-rustling Clanton-McLaury gang.

events.title: Hillary Clinton Is Born
events.description: Drew Angerer/Getty ImagesHillary Clinton during a 2016 U.S. presidential debate with Donald Trump.

events.title: South Korea's President Is Assassinated
events.description: Park Chung-hee, the third president of Korea, is assassinated by the director of the Korean Central Intelligence Agency (KCIA). Prior to his assassination, President Park effectively acted as the dictator of South Korea. He had been in power for nearly 18 years, and under his rule, direct voting was disbanded and Koreans were imprisoned and tortured for speaking out against Park and his party.

events.title: Æthelstan Dies
events.description: Æthelstan depicted in a 15th-century stained glass window at All Souls College Chapel in Oxford, England.

events.title: City Of Amsterdam Is Recognized
events.description: Reference to the city of Amsterdam appears for the first time in the toll concession of Floris V, Count of Holland. Founded in the 13th century as a fishing village, Amsterdam flourished due to its location along trade routes.

events.title: Teddy Roosevelt Is Born
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt is born in New York. Roosevelt is best known as the 26th president of the United States, as well as a prolific outdoorsman. Under his administration, Roosevelt doubled the amount of national parks in the National Park system and passed the Antiquities Act of 1906. Under this act, the president could declare many different pieces of land and structures as national monuments. During his presidency, Roosevelt began construction on the Panama Canal and mediated the truce between Russia and Japan during the Russo-Japanese War.

events.title: The New York City Subway Opens
events.description: The City Hall subway station, circa 1900-1904.

events.title: The Endurance Is Abandoned
events.description: Explorer Ernest Shackleton orders his crew to abandon their ship, the Endurance, 10 months after it became trapped in ice in the Weddell Sea.

events.title: Sylvia Plath Is Born
events.description: Sylvia Plath is born in Boston, Massachusetts. A poet, short story writer, and novelist, Plath produced a number of iconic works including her novel The Bell Jar (1963) and a collection of poems entitled Ariel (1965).

events.title: John Gotti Is Born
events.description: John Gotti, American crime boss in charge of the New York-based Gambino family, is born in the Bronx.

events.title: John Locke Dies
events.description: John Locke dies in Essex, England, at the age of 72. An English philosopher, Locke wrote about ideas like the social contract, religious toleration, and citizens' right to "life, liberty, and estate." A major figure in the Enlightenment, many of Locke's ideas were influential to America's Founding Fathers.

events.title: The Statue Of Liberty Is Dedicated
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesA depiction of President Grover Cleveland's 1886 dedication of the Statue of Liberty.

events.title: Bill Gates Is Born
events.description: William Henry "Bill" Gates is born in Seattle, Washington. A software engineer, Gates co-founded Microsoft with his childhood friend Paul Allen in 1975. By the 1990s, the company had made Gates the world's richest man, a position he would keep off and on until 2017. Today, he is estimated to have a net worth of over $100 billion.

events.title: Gertrude Baniszewski Is Arrested For The Murder Of Sylvia Likens
events.description: Gertrude Baniszweski is arrested for the murder of 16-year-old Sylvia Likens. Likens and her sister found herself in the care of Beniszweski after her parents left to work in the carnival business. Her family paid Beniszweski $20 a week to take care of the girls, but after one month's payment came late, Beniszweski subjected Likens and her sister to brutal torture.

events.title: The Andrea Gail Sends Its Last Message Before The 'Perfect Storm'
events.description: NOAA/ Wikimedia CommonsA satellite image of the "perfect storm" that doomed the Andrea Gail.

events.title: Sir Walter Raleigh Is Executed
events.description: A portrait of Sir Walter Raleigh from 1588.

events.title: The Stock Market Crashes On 'Black Tuesday'
events.description: The New York Stock Exchange crashes, helping to trigger the Great Depression. Stock prices had been falling since September, and they plummeted starting on Oct. 18, leading to "Black Monday" on Oct. 28, and "Black Tuesday" on Oct. 29 as shareholders sought to take their money out in a panic.

events.title: The Suez Crisis Begins
events.description: Fox Photos/Getty ImagesA young Egyptian boy stands among rubble during the Suez Crisis. A British tank is parked behind him.

events.title: Bobby Seale Is Gagged During Trial
events.description: Bobby Seale is gagged and chained to his seat while standing trial for his role in organizing protests during the 1968 Democratic National Convention. A co-founder of the Black Panthers and one of the "Chicago Eight," Seale had been accused of conspiracy to incite a riot during the convention in Chicago, which was rocked by anti-war protestors.

events.title: China Ends One-Child Policy
events.description: China ends the one-child policy after 35 years. In the 1970s, China feared overpopulation and began implementing restrictions on the marrying age for adults, the number of children a couple could have, and the time intervals between children. The one-child policy was just one way the Chinese government hoped to curb overpopulation, and they strongly enforced it, primarily in urban centers.

events.title: Henry VII Becomes King Of England
events.description: King Henry VII ended the War of the Roses and started the Tudor dynasty.

events.title: Pope Alexander VI Holds An Orgy
events.description: Pope Alexander VI and his son, Cesare, allegedly host the Banquet of Chestnuts at the Apostolic Palace in Vatican City. The banquet was described in Protonotary Apostolic and Master of Ceremonies Johann Burchard's diary, but his account of the night's events are disputed.

events.title: John Adams Is Born
events.description: John Adams is born in Braintree, Massachusetts. Adams is best known as the second president of the United States, a Founding Father, and a political philosopher. As a young man, Adams studied law at Harvard University and used his skills to champion American independence. He served as vice president under George Washington and later became the only president to run as a member of the Federalist party. Under his administration, Adams created the controversial Alien and Sedition Acts, effectively tightening immigration policies and punishing Americans for making false or malicious statements about the government.

events.title: The 'War Of The Worlds' Is Broadcast
events.description: Orson Welles telling reporters on the day after the broadcast that it wasn't meant to cause panic.

events.title: Tsar Bomba Is Detonated
events.description: Tsar Bomba is detonated in the Arctic Circle by the Soviet Union. The nuclear warhead is still the most powerful nuclear bomb ever created.

events.title: Muhammad Ali Wins The Rumble In The Jungle
events.description: Muhammad Ali knocks out George Foreman, winning the Rumble in the Jungle in Kinshasa, Zaire (now the Democratic Republic of the Congo). The victory made him the world's heavyweight champion for the second time.

events.title: Martha Moxley Is Murdered
events.description: Martha Moxley is murdered in Greenwich, Connecticut. Michael Skakel, nephew of Robert F. Kennedy, was arrested and convicted of the murder.

events.title: Whitey Bulger Is Murdered
events.description: James "Whitey" Bulger, infamous crime boss of South Boston, is murdered by his fellow inmates in a West Virginia jail.

events.title: Martin Luther Posts His 95 Theses
events.description: Martin Luther allegedly posts his 95 Theses on the door of a castle church in Wittenberg, Germany. A monk, Luther criticized the Catholic Church for a number of its practices, including allowing the purchase of "indulgences" to forgive sins. Though the veracity of Luther's dramatic door posting is up to debate, his 95 Theses helped trigger the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Ellsworth Raymond "Bumpy" Johnson, The "Harlem Godfather," Is Born
events.description: Bumpy Johnson, the "Harlem Godfather," is born in Charleston, South Carolina. At 10 years old, Johnson's family moved to Harlem. There, he made a name for himself as a tough street fighter and bodyguard. Johnson would eventually dip his toes in the mafia world, making peace with other gangs.

events.title: Harry Houdini Dies
events.description: /Getty ImagesFamed escape artist Harry Houdini poses for a portrait while bound with chains. Circa 1899.

events.title: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory Is Founded
events.description: Thanks to the early rocket experiments carried out by the "Suicide Squad" comprised of Frank Malina, Qian Xuesen, Weld Arnold, Apollo M. O. Smith, Edward S. Forman, and Jack Parsons, NASA establishes its Jet Propulsion Lab in Pasadena, California in partnership with the California Institute of Technology.

events.title: River Phoenix Dies
events.description: River Jude Phoenix dies in West Hollywood, California, at the age of 23 from a drug overdose. An up-and-coming actor, Phoenix had already starred in a number of films including Stand By Me and Running on Empty, for which he earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Support Actor.

events.title: Bethany Hamilton Loses Her Arm To A Shark
events.description: Matt Dunbar/WSL via Getty ImagesBethany Hamilton lost her arm to a shark attack in 2003, but later returned to surfing. Here she is at the Sydney Surf Pro in March 2020.

events.title: Teresa Halbach Goes Missing After Visiting Steven Avery's Property
events.description: 25-year-old Teresa Halbach visits the Avery property to photograph an old vehicle for Auto Trader magazine and is never seen alive again. The case ultimately formed the basis of the Netflix series Making a Murderer.

events.title: The Sistine Chapel Ceiling Opens To The Public
events.description: Richard Mortel/FlickrIt took Michelangelo about four years to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.

events.title: The Great Lisbon Earthquake Strikes
events.description: An earthquake centered off the coast of Lisbon, Portugal, almost completely destroys the port city. The Great Lisbon Earthquake was estimated to have a magnitude of 7.7, which spawned a tsunami that engulfed the area.

events.title: William Tilghman Is Murdered
events.description: Oklahoma Historical SocietyLawman William "Bill" Tilghman, date unknown.

events.title: A Failed Assassination Attempt On President Harry S. Truman
events.description: Two activists for Puerto Rican independence — Oscar Collazo and Griselio Torresola — attempt to assassinate President Harry S. Truman in Washington, D.C. Because the White House was undergoing renovations at the time, Truman was living in Blair House, the presidential guest house.

events.title: The First Hydrogen Bomb Is Tested
events.description: The first ever hydrogen bomb test, code-named "Ivy Mike," takes place at the Enewetak Atoll in the Marshall Islands.

events.title: The European Union Is Founded By The Maastricht Treaty
events.description: The European Union is founded by the Maastricht Treaty. The treaty created a shared European citizenship among member states, a single currency, and common foreign and security policies. The treaty changed the name of the union from the European Economic Community to the European Community. Finally, it increased levels of democratic decision-making by granting the directly elected European Parliament more powers.

events.title: The Associated Press First Reports On Abuse At Abu Ghraib Prison
events.description: Months before the first photographs of prisoner abuse at Abu Ghraib, the Associated Press reports on the mistreatment of Iraqi inmates.

events.title: Daniel Boone Is Born
events.description: The only known portrait of Daniel Boone that was painted during his lifetime, which was done Chester Harding in 1820.

events.title: The Great Emu War Begins
events.description: The Great Emu War, a wildlife management turned military operation, begins in Western Australia. Farmers in the area had complained of large numbers of emus destroying their crops, so Minister of Defense Sir George Pearce sent soldiers armed with Lewis guns to curb the population.

events.title: 'Lady Chatterley's Lover' Is Determined Not To Be Obscene
events.description: A British court determines that D. H. Lawrence's novel Lady Chatterley's Lover is not obscene and can be published in the country. The book had originally been published in Italy, but 30 years after Lawrence's death, Penguin Books wanted to bring it to the United Kingdom.

events.title: Velma Barfield Is Executed
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesVelma Barfield was also known as "Death Row Granny."

events.title: Anatoly Moskvin Is Arrested
events.description: Anatoly Moskvin is arrested for grave digging in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia. Moskvin was a professor and journalist in Nizhny Novgorod known for his intellect and expertise on cemeteries. In 2009, families started complaining that the graves of their loved ones had been desecrated. Police were able to link the desecrations to Moskvin, who had the mummified bodies of 29 girls between the ages of three and 25 in his apartment. Moskvin stuffed the corpses into doll clothes and positioned them throughout his apartment to keep him company.

events.title: Olympe De Gouges Is Executed
events.description: French playwright and political activist Olympe de Gouges is executed or sedition in Paris, France. De Gouges began speaking out against the French slave trade in 1788 and writing political pamphlets in which she criticized the government.

events.title: Annie Oakley Dies
events.description: Annie Oakley dies in Greenville, Ohio at age 66. Oakley was a famous American marksmen who performed in Buffalo Bill's Wild West Show.

events.title: Newspaper Mistakenly Prints "Dewey Defeats Truman"
events.description: GPA Photo Archive/FlickrHarry S. Truman holds up the newspaper that incorrectly declares his opponent's victory.

events.title: Henri Matisse Dies
events.description: Henri Matisse, a French impressionist painter, dies in Nice, France. Matisse's works are most notable for his bold use of color. His art reflected an experimental flare that intrigued viewers at the time. During his lifetime, Matisse was considered one of the Fauves, a group of artists who relied on color to convey meaning rather than realistic depictions of people and things. As Matisse grew old, he became unable to paint and instead worked on collage. He died from a heart attack at the age of 84.

events.title: Sputnik 2 Launches Into Space With A Dog On Board
events.description: Sovfoto/Universal Images Group/Getty ImagesLaika the dog, also known as "Muttnik," pictured in the Sputnik 2 capsule in 1957.

events.title: Lisa McVey Is Abducted By Bobby Joe Long
events.description: Serial killer and rapist Bobby Joe Long kidnaps 17-year-old Lisa McVey as she rides her bike home from work. Long had abducted, raped, and murdered at least 10 other women in the months leading up to his attack on McVey, but she somehow persuaded him to release her and immediately called the police. The information McVey provided led to Long's arrest, conviction, and execution for murder.

events.title: William III And Mary II Of England Marry
events.description: Princess Mary of York, niece of King Charles II, and her first cousin William III of Orange are married in an arranged wedding that leaves Mary in tears. The royal family attended the public bedding ceremony between the 27-year-old groom and his 15-year-old bride, but though Mary became pregnant soon after the marriage, she and William were never able to have children. Beginning in 1689, the two ruled as king and queen regnant of England, Ireland, and Scotland.

events.title: The Entrance To King Tut's Tomb Is Discovered
events.description: Howard Carter opens the innermost shrine of King Tutankhamun's tomb — to which one of Carter's water boys found the steps.

events.title: Jane Goodall Observes Chimpanzees Creating Tools
events.description: While studying chimpanzees in Tanzania's Gombe National Park, Jane Goodall records the first documented case of a non-human animal creating a tool. A chimpanzee she had named David Greybeard used a grass stalk to extract termites from a mound, and later Goodall saw a chimpanzee named Goliath pulling the leaves from a stick to use for the same purpose. This observation forever changed chimpanzee and primate research.

events.title: Social Workers Learn Of Genie, The 'Feral' Child
events.description: Weird History/FacebookGenie Wiley's father isolated and abused her for 13 years.

events.title: Jimmy Carter Loses Reelection To Ronald Reagan
events.description: President Jimmy Carter loses reelection to Ronald Reagan in a landslide election. The former president would later return to his modest home in Plains, Georgia.

events.title: Dominique Dunne Dies
events.description: American actress Dominique Dunne dies after being strangled by her ex-boyfriend, John Thomas Sweeney, in the driveway of her West Hollywood home five days earlier. The two had broken up several weeks prior, and 22-year-old Dunne agreed to speak to Sweeney on the porch when he showed up at her house on October 30. The two began to argue, and Sweeney strangled her until she was unconscious. She remained in a coma until she was removed from life support on November 4.

events.title: Guy Fawkes Is Arrested
events.description: A 19th-century depiction of Guy Fawkes' capture.

events.title: Susan B. Anthony Illegally Votes In A Presidential Election
events.description: American civil rights activist Susan B. Anthony votes in the 1872 presidential election at a time when women were not legally allowed to vote. Two weeks later, she was arrested and fined $100. She swore, "I shall never pay a dollar of your unjust penalty" — and she never did. It wasn't until 1920 that women gained the right to vote thanks to Susan B. Anthony and the women's suffrage movement.

events.title: Vivien Leigh Is Born
events.description: Vivien Leigh won the Academy Award for Best Actress twice for her performances as Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind and Blanche DuBois in the film version of A Streetcar Named Desire.

events.title: Betty Broderick Murders Her Ex-Husband
events.description: YouTubeBetty Broderick smiles as the jury reads her guilty verdict.

events.title: DNA Testing Confirms Jefferson Lineage In The Descendants Of Sally Hemings
events.description: DNA testing confirms that someone in Thomas Jefferson's family fathered children with Jefferson's slave Sally Hemings. After Thomas Jefferson married Martha Jefferson, the Founding Father inherited his wife's slaves, including a young Sally Hemings. In 1787, Hemings accompanied Jefferson on a trip to Paris. Historians believe Jefferson first impregnated her on this trip. Hemings returned to Virginia and later had five more children, all of whom are believed to be fathered by Jefferson.

events.title: Charles II Of Spain Is Born
events.description: A portrait of Charles II by Juan de Miranda Carreño, c. 1680.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Is Elected President
events.description: Abraham Lincoln's son Robert called this 1864 photo "the best likeness of my Father."

events.title: The Bolshevik Revolution Begins In Russia
events.description: Vladimir Lenin leads an army of rebels in a coup against the Russian government, sparking the Bolshevik Revolution that ultimately ended with a communist victory. The Bolsheviks formed a new administration, and soon Lenin was the leader of the first communist state in the world.

events.title: Ronald Reagan Is Elected As 40th U.S. President
events.description: Ronald Reagan is elected as the 40th U.S. president. Reagan gained notoriety in the political sphere as the governor of California from 1967 to 1975. Prior to politics, Reagan worked in Hollywood as an actor. As president, Reagan implemented "Reaganomics," an economic policy that emphasizes trickle-down approaches, deregulation, and cuts to government spending. He also strengthened the war on drugs and oversaw the invasion of Grenada. Reagan served two terms before retiring to Los Angeles, California. He died of complications from Alzheimer's disease in 2004.

events.title: The Miami Brinks Heist
events.description: NetflixA re-enactment of the 2005 Miami Brinks heist in Netflix's Heist docuseries.

events.title: Marie Curie Is Born
events.description: Hulton-Deutsch Collection/CORBIS/Corbis/Getty ImagesMarie Curie in her laboratory, where she spent most of her adult life.

events.title: The Mary Celeste Leaves Port
events.description: The Mary Celeste, subject of one of history's most puzzling nautical mysteries, sets sail from New York City. A month later, another ship came across the Mary Celeste floating abandoned near the Azores islands. The lifeboat was gone, but all the cargo and the crew's personal items were untouched. No one aboard was ever seen again, and numerous theories ranging from mutiny to sea monsters have been put forward over the years.

events.title: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge Collapses
events.description: Howard Clifford running off the Tacoma Narrows Bridge during collapse.

events.title: Steve McQueen Dies
events.description: American actor Steve McQueen dies at the age of 50 when he suffers a heart attack after surgery to remove cancerous tumors.

events.title: Magic Johnson Announces He's HIV-Positive
events.description: American basketball player Magic Johnson becomes one of the first major stars to announce that he's HIV-positive. Many still believed AIDS could only affect gay men, so the diagnosis of Johnson — who identified as heterosexual — helped change public perception of the virus. Johnson also announced his retirement from the Los Angeles Lakers at the same time, and he soon devoted his time to becoming a spokesman for AIDS awareness.

events.title: Brothel Owner Dennis Hof Is Elected To The Nevada State Assembly — A Month After His Death
events.description: Despite being dead, Republican candidate and brothel owner Dennis Hof, the self-described "Trump of Pahrump" wins a seat on the Nevada State Assembly.

events.title: Lope De Aguirre Is Born
events.description: Spanish conquistador Lope de Aguirre, known as the "Madman," is born in the Basque Country of northern Spain. He is best known for his search for the mythical El Dorado, the ancient kingdom that was said to be filled with gold.

events.title: Doc Holliday Dies
events.description: Doc Holliday in Tombstone, Arizona, c. 1882.

events.title: X-Rays Are Discovered
events.description: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen accidentally discovers the X-ray while experimenting with electron beams. He was working in his lab in Wurzburg, Germany when he noticed a nearby screen that was coated in chemicals glowing as he tested whether the electron beams could pass through glass. He called his findings "X-rays" because he didn't know exactly what they were. His studies won him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

events.title: Esther Rolle Is Born
events.description: Esther Rolle, a 1970s actress best known for her roles in Good Times and Maude, is born in Florida.

events.title: The Beer Hall Putsch Begins
events.description: Adolf Hitler and other members of the Nazi Party attempted to lead a coup in Bavaria, Germany, in what's known as the Beer Hall Putsch. The insurrection began in one of Munich's largest beer halls, where Hitler gave a heated speech in an attempt to spark a "national revolution." The coup failed, and Hitler was arrested and convicted of high treason. He was sentenced to five years in prison, where he wrote his infamous book Mein Kampf.

events.title: Georg Elser Narrowly Misses Assassinating Adolf Hitler
events.description: During a 16th anniversary celebration for the Beer Hall Putsch in Munich, a German man named Georg Elser planted a bomb at the podium where Adolf Hitler was to give a speech. However, Hitler left the event approximately 13 minutes earlier than Elser expected and was thus gone when the bomb went off. Though the blast killed eight people and injured 62 others, Elser missed his target and was soon captured. He was imprisoned for five years before being executed at Dachau concentration camp in 1945, just before Germany surrendered.

events.title: John Paul Getty III's Ear Is Delivered To A Newspaper
events.description: Bettmann/Getty ImagesJohn Paul Getty III with his right ear missing.

events.title: John Bingham, Otherwise Known As Lord Lucan, Disappears
events.description: John Bingham, 7th Earl of Lucan, disappears after his wife is attacked and his nanny was found murdered. His wife, Veronica, claimed that Bingham was responsible for her attack and for the murder of their nanny. He has never been seen since.

events.title: Jennifer Pan Has Her Parents Murdered
events.description: Jennifer Pan organizes the murder of her tiger-parents. Her whole life, Pan grew up in a strict household environment. Never able to live up to her parent's expectations, Pan decided to falsify her life. She would create fake report cards, fake scholarships, and even fake college acceptance letters to get her parents off her back. When the lies eventually unraveled, Pan decided to enlist the help of her boyfriend, Daniel Wong, to kill them.

events.title: Jack The Ripper Kills His Final Victim
events.description: The mangled corpse of Mary Jane Kelly.

events.title: Hedy Lamarr Is Born
events.description: Austrian-American actress Hedy Lamarr is born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler in Vienna, Austria. Lamarr became interested in acting from an early age, and she enrolled in acting school at the age of 16 and was given the lead role in the controversial Czech film Ecstasy just three years later.

events.title: The Start Of Kristallnacht
events.description: Nazis burn synagogues, vandalize homes and businesses, and kill more than 100 Jewish people in what's known as Kristallnacht, or the "Night of Broken Glass."

events.title: John List Murders His Family
events.description: John List kills his wife, mother, and three children in their Westfield, New Jersey home, then flees, evading capture for nearly 18 years. List had planned the murders so carefully that nobody knew the family was dead until a month later. By then, John List was long gone and had assumed a new identity. It wasn't until 1989 that he was arrested and sentenced to five consecutive terms of life in prison.

events.title: Fall Of The Berlin Wall
events.description: Scherhaufer/ullstein bild/Getty ImagesCrowds gather at the border in anticipation of the Berlin Wall's destruction.

events.title: Henry Wirz Is Hanged
events.description: Confederate officer Henry Wirz, commandant of the notorious Andersonville Prison, is hanged for conspiracy and murder for his role in the deaths of 13,000 Union prisoners at the camp during the Civil War. Wirz had been assigned to the newly-established Camp Sumter, known colloquially as Andersonville, in April 1864. The prison held around 32,000 inmates at its peak, and up to 3,000 died every month from disease and malnutrition due to poor conditions.

events.title: Henry M. Stanley Finds Dr. David Livingstone
events.description: Henry M. Stanley traveled to Africa to find the missing Dr. Livingstone.

events.title: Hachikō The Akita Is Born
events.description: Hachikō the Akita awaiting his owner.

events.title: The Smithsonian Acquires The Hope Diamond
events.description: Centuries after it was first taken from India, the Smithsonian Institution acquires the purportedly cursed Hope Diamond from jeweler Harry Winston.

events.title: Sesame Street Debuts
events.description: Sesame Street debuts on the American public television station PBS and soon becomes the most-watched children's show in the world. Producer Joan Ganz Cooney wanted to create an educational program that underprivileged kids could watch to prepare for kindergarten. At the time of its debut, Sesame Street was one of the most racially and ethnically diverse children's shows on television, and over the decades it has dealt with topics like the AIDS epidemic and the opioid crisis.

events.title: The Sinking Of The Edmund Fitzgerald
events.description: The SS Edmund Fitzgerald sinks to the depths of Lake Superior after facing a harsh winter storm. The lake freighter is the largest ship to sink in the Great Lakes. All 29 crew members of the ship died in the disaster. The event was later recounted in Gordon Lightfoot's song The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald.

events.title: Josh Phillips Murders Maddie Clifton
events.description: Fourteen-year-old Josh Phillips murders eight-year-old Maddie Clifton. When Clifton disappeared from her Jacksonville, Florida home, the entire community went on high alert. Days later, Melissa Phillips, Josh Phillips' mom, found Clifton's body under her son's water bed. According to Phillips, Clifton approached him while he was playing baseball outside. After accidentally striking her with a baseball, Phillips panicked and decided to beat Clifton and strangle her before placing her body under his bed.

events.title: The Mayflower Compact Is Signed
events.description: Forty-one men aboard the Mayflower sign the Mayflower Compact, "a civil body politick" created to enact "just and equal laws... for the general good of the Colony." It stands as the first document establishing self-government created by Europeans in the New World.

events.title: Nat Turner Is Executed
events.description: Nat Turner, an enslaved man and minister who believed God had chosen him to help his people escape from slavery, is executed for leading 75 of his followers in an insurrection against their enslavers. The group killed around 60 people before a militia crushed the rebellion, and Turner evaded capture for two months.

events.title: Belle Gunness Is Born
events.description: Serial killer Belle Gunness is born Brynhild Paulsdatter Størset in Norway. She immigrated to the United States at the age of 22 — and everyone close to her began dying mysteriously. Gunness is thought to have killed at least 14 people, mainly men she lured onto her Indiana property after promising to marry them. She reportedly died in a fire in 1908, but it's commonly believed that she faked her own death.

events.title: Ned Kelly Is Hanged
events.description: Ned Kelly the day before his execution.

events.title: World War I Ends
events.description: World War I comes to an end at the 11th hour on the 11th day of the 11th month after four years of fighting that left at least nine million soldiers and five million civilians dead. Early that morning, Germany signed an agreement with the Allies to end the conflict. But although World War I was the "war to end all wars," the Treaty of Versailles that officially put a stop to the Great War harshly punished Germany and set the stage for World War II.

events.title: Grace Budd's Mother Receives A Letter From Her Killer
events.description: Delia Flanagan, whose daughter Grace Budd had vanished six years prior, receives a horrific letter that describes her murder in gruesome detail. In June 1928, serial killer Albert Fish murdered and then ate the remains of 10-year-old Budd in Irvington, New York. Fish wasn't initially charged with Budd's disappearance, but police were able to track Fish down based on the paper he'd written the letter on, and he was arrested a month later.

events.title: Typhoid Mary Dies
events.description: Mary Mallon (foreground) became known as Typhoid Mary after she was discovered as an asymptomatic carrier of the disease.

events.title: Police Find Bodies Buried On Dorothea Puente's Property
events.description: While searching for a missing man with developmental disabilities, police in Sacramento, California come across a body buried on the property of Dorothea Puente's boarding house. Puente was eventually charged with the murder of eight of her tenants and her boyfriend. Police say she overdosed her victims with drugs, buried them in her backyard, and continued to cash their Social Security checks.

events.title: Mary Astell Is Born
events.description: Writer and philosopher Mary Astell is born in Newcastle upon Tyne. Known as the "first English feminist," Astell spent her life advocating for women to have the same educational opportunities as men. Her most famous book, A Serious Proposal to the Ladies, suggested that women who didn't marry or become nuns should live, study, and teach together in secular convents, though her controversial idea never caught on.

events.title: Jules Léotard Performs The First Flying Trapeze Act
events.description: Jules Léotard, c. 1860s.

events.title: The Murder Inc. Trials Begin
events.description: After a series of confessions from former mob hitman Abraham Reles, high-ranking members of the infamous Murder Inc. begin their trials. The very same day, Reles was found dead after falling six stories out of his hotel room window.

events.title: First Recorded Mothman Sighting
events.description: Five men in a Clendenin, West Virginia cemetery see a strange, winged creature flying out of nearby trees, marking the first sighting of the fabled Mothman.

events.title: Johnny Gosch Is Born
events.description: Johnny Gosch is born in Des Moines, Iowa. Gosch would make headlines after disappearing while working his newspaper route in 1982. Witnesses at the scene reported that Gosch had been speaking to a man in a blue car before his disappearance. Years later, another boy disappeared from the same area, sparking rumors that a predator was operating in the area. His case inspired the practice of putting photos of missing children on the back of milk cartons.

events.title: The Charkhi Dadri Mid-Air Collision
events.description: Robert Nickelsberg/The LIFE Images Collection/Getty ImagesWreckage the morning after the Charkhi Dadri mid-air crash.

events.title: Mehran Karimi Nasseri Dies
events.description: Mehran Karimi Nasseri, who gained notoriety for living at Charles de Gaulle Airport in Paris for 18 years — and inspired the 2004 film The Terminal — dies at Charles de Gaulle of a heart attack.

events.title: St. Brice's Day Massacre
events.description: King Aethelred the Unready orders his army to kill all Danes living in England in what's now known as the St. Brice's Day Massacre. After years of violent raids, the king was told that the Danes wanted to kill him and take over his kingdom, so he decreed that they should all be exterminated. Though there are no exact records about how many people were murdered, historians believe the loss of life was significant.

events.title: Robert Louis Stevenson Is Born
events.description: Famed Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson is born in Edinburgh. Stevenson is best known for his novels Treasure Island and The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, but he also wrote many essays, poems, and books on his travels. He spent the final years of his life in Samoa, where he wrote much darker works of realism rather than the romance and adventure he was famous for.

events.title: Empress Wanrong Is Born
events.description: Empress Wangrong, the last Empress of China, is born in Beijing.

events.title: The USS Juneau Is Destroyed In The Pacific
events.description: After being struck by a Japanese torpedo, the USS Juneau sinks in just 42 seconds. Five brother serving on board the ship together — Albert, Francis, George, Joseph, and Madison Sullivan — were all killed, and the story of "Sullivan brothers" galvanized the U.S. war effort.

events.title: The Amityville Murders
events.description: The home of the DeFeo family, located on 112 Ocean Avenue in Amityville, New York, commonly known as the Amityville Horror House.

events.title: Nevado Del Ruiz Erupts
events.description: Omayra Sánchez spent three days stuck in mud and debris following the eruption before she died.

events.title: Cari Farver Goes Missing
events.description: Cari Farver, a 37-year-old woman from Iowa, goes missing after starting a whirlwind romance with Dave Kroupa of Omaha, Nebraska. Police would eventually uncover evidence pointing to Shanna "Liz" Golyar, a woman Kroupa had dated before Farver, as the person behind Farver's disappearance. Golyar abducted and murdered Farver, and took it one step further by pretending to be her for the next three years. Golyar would send texts to Farver's family and friends, and it wasn't until Golyar began escalating her crimes that the police would end the bizarre case.

events.title: Claude Monet Is Born
events.description: Claude Monet/Musée d'OrsayClaude Monet's Tulip Fields, painted in 1886.

events.title: Moby-Dick Is Published
events.description: Herman Melville publishes his esteemed novel Moby-Dick about the fictional Captain Ahab's quest to catch an elusive white whale. The book has one of the most famous opening lines in literature — "Call me Ishmael" — but it wasn't very successful when it was released. It wasn't until 30 years after Melville's death that Moby-Dick became critically acclaimed, and today it's considered one of the great American classics.

events.title: Danny Greene Is Born
events.description: American mobster Danny Greene, also known as the "Irishman," is born in Cleveland, Ohio. Growing up, Greene often fought with the Italian-American students he attended high school with, and that rivalry persisted into adulthood — when Greene competed with the Italian-American Mafia for control of Cleveland's criminal underworld.

events.title: Ruby Bridges Integrates A Louisiana Elementary School
events.description: Federal marshals escort Ruby Bridges to school to protect her from a racist mob in 1960.

events.title: NASA Launches Apollo 12
events.description: NASA launches Apollo 12, the second spacecraft to land on the Moon. The Apollo 12 spacecraft was identical to Apollo 11, the first spacecraft to land on the Moon. Commander Charles Conrad and Lunar Module Pilot Alan L. Bean oversaw the mission and spent over a day on the Moon's surface conducting experiments and setting up equipment. The launch was successful and the crew returned safely to Earth on November 24.

events.title: Marshall University Football Team Dies In Plane Crash
events.description: The Marshall University football team dies in a plane crash. All 75 people on board died in the crash, making it the worst sports-related air tragedy in U.S. history.

events.title: Rita Crundwell Is Convicted Of Largest Municipal Fraud In U.S. History
events.description: Rita Crundwell is convicted of largest municipal fraud in U.S. History. For over twenty years, Crundwell embezzled funds from the city of Dixon, Illinois to fund her lavish lifestyle.

events.title: Cherokee Slave Revolt
events.description: A group of 25 enslaved people rise up against their Cherokee enslavers in Oklahoma, locking them in their homes before they fled at night. The men, women, and children stole horses, guns, food, and other supplies and headed toward Mexico, fighting off bounty hunters as they went. The Cherokee Nation sent a militia to forcibly retrieve the group and they were captured less than two weeks later.

events.title: General Sherman Burns Atlanta And Begins His March To The Sea
events.description: The city of Atlanta after it was burned by the troops of Union General William Tecumseh Sherman.

events.title: Candance Montgomery Is Born
events.description: Candance Montgomery, eventual axe murderer, is born. After having an affair with her best friend's husband, suburban housewife Candance Montgomery struck her friend over 40 times with an axe, killing her. She later claimed self defense in court and was acquitted on all charges. Today, she remains a free woman and works as a family counselor in Georgia.

events.title: The Clutter Family Is Murdered
events.description: The Clutter family of Holcomb, Kansas, is murdered in their home in the early morning hours, inspiring Truman Capote's novel In Cold Blood. Herb and Bonnie Holcomb and their teenage children Nancy and Kenyon were tied up and shot in the head by Perry Smith and Richard Hickock, two ex-convicts who were looking for cash that they heard Herb Clutter kept in a safe in the home.

events.title: The Clinton-Lewinsky Affair Begins
events.description: William J. Clinton Presidential LibraryBill Clinton's highly publicized affair with Monica Lewinsky captivated the country in the late 1990s.

events.title: Steven Avery Is Arrested And Charged With The Murder Of Teresa Halbach
events.description: 10 days after Teresa Halbach's car is found stashed away on his property, Steven Avery is arrested and charged with her murder. However, debate around Avery's involvement — and the involvement of his nephew Brendan Dassey — eventually inspired the Netflix series Making a Murderer.

events.title: Francisco Pizarro Captures Atahualpa
events.description: Victoria and Albert Museum, LondonThe Capture of Atahualpa by John Everett Millais, 1845.

events.title: Ivan The Terrible's Son, Ivan Ivanovich, Dies
events.description: Ivan the Terrible's son dies under mysterious circumstances. According to popular legend, Ivan the Terrible struck and killed his own son in a fit of rage. The story inspired one of Russia's most famous paintings Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan.

events.title: Fyodor Dostoevsky Is Sentenced To Death
events.description: A Russian court sentences author Fyodor Dostoevsky to death for his alleged connection to an anti-government group. Dostoevsky had joined the "Petrashevsky Circle" to participate in radical intellectual discussion, but when officials began suspecting the group of subversive activities, many of its members were arrested. Dostoevsky's execution was stayed at the last minute, and he was instead sent to a hard labor camp in Siberia for four years. After his release, he began writing the novels such as Crime and Punishment that he is remembered for.

events.title: George Metesky Attempts His First Bombing
events.description: George Metesky, also known as the "Mad Bomber," places a bomb on the window ledge of a New York City office building, the first of more than 30 over the next 16 years.

events.title: Police Discover Ed Gein's House Of Horrors
events.description: A chair found in Ed Gein's home upholstered with human skin.

events.title: Edie Sedgwick Dies
events.description: American model and actress Edie Sedgwick dies from a barbiturate overdose at the age of 28. She'd suffered from mental health issues for several years, and she'd recently relapsed after giving up drugs and alcohol several months earlier.

events.title: Elizabeth I Of England Takes The English Throne
events.description: Elizabeth I — the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn — becomes Queen of England and Ireland. Also known as the "Virgin Queen," Elizabeth never married or had children, instead dedicating herself to her job and her country.

events.title: Queen Charlotte Dies
events.description: Queen Charlotte with her two eldest children. Out of her 15 children, 13 survived into adulthood.

events.title: H. H. Holmes Is Arrested
events.description: Chicago History MuseumH. H. Holmes shown in the mid-to-late 1890s.

events.title: Stalin's Great Purge Comes To An End
events.description: The Great Purge orchestrated by Soviet leader Joseph Stalin and his secret police, the NKVD, ends. It is estimated that anywhere between 700,000 and 1.2 million people were killed during the operation.

events.title: Martin Scorsese Is Born
events.description: Martin Scorsese, famous director, is born in New York. As one of the major figures of the New Hollywood era, Scorsese directed films such as Taxi Driver, Goodfellas, and The Wolf of Wall Street. Much of Scorsese's work is inspired by his upbringing in New York City. His films feature extreme violence, profanity, and the use of freezeframes and slow motion. Five of his films are held at the Library of Congress for being of "cultural, historic, or aesthetic significance."

events.title: Tony Baekeland Murders His Mother
events.description: American socialite Barbara Daly Baekeland is killed by her 25-year-old son, Tony, at her London home.

events.title: George H.W. Bush Pardons A Turkey
events.description: President George H.W. Bush pardons a turkey at the White House cementing the "turkey pardon" — which had existed unofficially for decades — into a beloved Thanksgiving tradition.

events.title: Esther Rolle Dies
events.description: Esther Rolle, an actress best known for her roles in Good Times and Maude, dies in Culver City, California.

events.title: St. Peter's Basilica Is Consecrated
events.description: Dani Salva / VWPics/Universal Images Group via Getty ImagesSt. Peter's Basilica during a Palm Sunday mass.

events.title: Mark Twain's First Story Is Published
events.description: DynamichromeIn addition to writing novels, Twain was also a prolific travel writer whose prose added depth to far-off places that most Americans hadn't seen.

events.title: Disney's Steamboat Willie Is Released
events.description: Disney's Steamboat Willie, the first cartoon with synchronized sound, is released. The cartoon was one of the first to have a post-produced soundtrack. It was also the third film featuring Mickey Mouse but the first to be distributed. The film was a huge success at the time of its release, and even today, it is still considered a foundational film that changed animation forever. The cartoon was entered into the National Film Registry for being historically and culturally significant.

events.title: Margaret Atwood Is Born
events.description: Canadian writer Margaret Atwood is born Ottawa. Atwood began writing at an early age, and she has since published 18 novels, 18 books of poetry, and numerous short stories, children's books, and works of non-fiction. Her most well-known book is The Handmaid's Tale, the award-winning dystopian novel that is frequently studied in high schools and colleges around the world.

events.title: The Jonestown Massacre
events.description: David Hume Kennerly/Getty ImagesThe aftermath of the Jonestown Massacre.

events.title: The "Man In The Iron Mask" Dies
events.description: An illustration of the Man in the Iron Mask in his cell.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Delivers The Gettysburg Address
events.description: Matthew Brady/National Archives and Records Administration via Wikimedia CommonsOne of just two confirmed photos of Abraham Lincoln (identified by the red arrow) at Soldiers' National Cemetery in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania on November 19, 1863, about three hours before delivering his historic Gettysburg Address.

events.title: Michael Rockefeller Vanishes
events.description: President and Fellows of Harvard University; Peabody Museum of Archeology and EthnologyMichael Rockefeller on his first trip to New Guinea in May 1960.

events.title: The Department of Homeland Security Is Created
events.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in the United States is created following the September 11, 2001 attacks. Prior to 2002, the U.S. had the Office of Homeland Security in the White House. In November of 2002, the Homeland Security Act by Congress created the Department of Homeland Security responsible for protecting the United States from internal and external threats. Alongside protecting U.S. borders, the DHS is active in the cybersecurity field and in the financial system.

events.title: Charles Manson Dies
events.description: A prison photo of Manson, mere months before he died./span>

events.title: A Sperm Whale Sinks The Whaling Ship Essex
events.description: Camden Public LibraryThe Essex was sunk by a vengeful sperm whale.

events.title: The Nuremberg Trials Begin
events.description: An international tribunal puts 24 high-ranking Nazis on trial in Nuremberg, Germany, for the crimes they committed during World War II. The proceedings lasted 10 months, and in the end, 12 were sentenced to death, including Heinrich Himmler, the leader of the Gestapo, and Hermann Göring, who died by suicide the night before he was scheduled to be executed. The Nuremberg trials were the first of their kind in history, but similar proceedings resulted in the conviction of more than 5,000 other war criminals.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth II And Prince Philip Marry
events.description: This is the official wedding picture of Princess Elizabeth and her new husband Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, made after their return to Buckingham Palace after their marriage in Westminster Abbey on November 20, 1947.

events.title: Francisco Franco Dies
events.description: Francisco Franco, dictator of Spain, dies in Madrid at the age of 82. Franco rose to prominence in Spain during the Spanish Civil War. As a Spanish military general, Franco had the skills necessary to overthrow the Second Spanish Republic and maintain dictatorial control over Spain until his death. In the early days of his rule, Franco used fear tactics to keep Spaniards in line. Franco oversaw the construction of concentration camps and used forced labor and executions as punishments. In total, up to 200,000 people died in Franco's brutal repression campaigns, coined the "White Terror."

events.title: Joseph Paul Franklin Is Executed
events.description: Serial killer Joseph Paul Franklin is executed for the 1977 murder of Gerald Gordon. Franklin's murder spree throughout the late 1970s and early 1980s resulted in the deaths of as many as 22 victims. He targeted Black and Jewish people and said he wanted to "cleanse the world" of those he considered inferior. After 15 years on Missouri's death row, he died by lethal injection.

events.title: The Pilgrims Sign The Mayflower Compact
events.description: The Pilgrims signing the Mayflower Compact.

events.title: Voltaire Is Born
events.description: French writer, historian, and philosopher Voltaire is born François-Marie Arouet in Paris. He adopted the name Voltaire in 1718 after he was arrested for writing a satirical verse in which he accused Philippe II, Duke of Orléans of incest. The writer was open about his criticism of slavery and the Catholic Church, and he advocated for freedom of speech and religion. His best-known work is Candide, a novella that served as commentary for many contemporary events.

events.title: Thomas Edison Announces The Invention Of The Phonograph
events.description: American inventor Thomas Edison announces his latest creation, the phonograph, which could record and play back sound. He had discovered the technology when he placed tinfoil over a grooved cylinder and shouted "Mary had a little lamb" into it, causing the needle inside to vibrate with the sound of his voice and record the movement of his diaphragm. He was surprised when it played back the recording perfectly, and he began demonstrating the phonograph in public, contributing to his worldwide fame.

events.title: The HMHS Britannic Sinks
events.description: The HMHS Britannic, the younger sister of the RMS Titanic and Olymic hits a mine and sinks. The ship had been built to be a passenger liner, but was converted into a hospital ship after the start of World War I. Of the 1,066 people on board, 1,036 people survived the sinking.

events.title: Alan Freed Is Fired From A New York Radio Station
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesAlan Freed sits in a 1010 WINS sound studio during a radio broadcast.

events.title: Birmingham Pub Bombings
events.description: Bombs explode in two Birmingham, England pubs, killing 21 people and injuring nearly 200.

events.title: Blackbeard Is Killed
events.description: Before he became Blackbeard, Edward Teach was simply a mysterious Englishman who wanted to make a fortune.

events.title: Charles De Gaulle Is Born
events.description: Charles de Gaulle, the president of France from 1959 to 1969, is born in the city of Lille in 1890. Aside from his presidency, de Gaulle is best known for his role in leading the Free France army against Nazi Germany during World War II after the official French government surrendered. After the war, he rewrote the French Constitution and founded the Fifth Republic, the system of government still used in France to this day.

events.title: President John F. Kennedy Is Assassinated
events.description: A photo taken by Mary Ann Moorman one-sixth of a second after John F. Kennedy was fatally shot.

events.title: The Max Headroom Incident
events.description: YouTubeThe masked figure from the Max Headroom incident.

events.title: Dena Schlosser Amputates Her Baby's Arms
events.description: Dena Schlosser amputates her baby's arms during an episode of postpartum psychosis. After marrying her husband, Schlosser became deeply involved in a Christian fundamentalist church in Texas. She seemed to be heavily influenced by the church, and this only became worse after the birth of her third child, Margaret. The mixture of postpartum depression and religious fervor seemed to push Schlosser over the edge one night. In her psychotic episode, Schlosser used a kitchen knife to saw off the arms of her baby and then attempted to cut off her own arms. Police later reported that Schlosser believed God commanded her to do this.

events.title: Perkin Warbeck Is Hanged
events.description: Perkin Warbeck, pretender to the English throne, is executed after attempting to escape from the Tower of London. Warbeck claimed to be Richard of Shrewsbury, Duke of York, who had mysteriously disappeared in 1483 when he was around 10 years old.

events.title: Philip Hamilton, The Son Of Alexander Hamilton, Is Shot In A Duel
events.description: Philip Hamilton, the first child of Alexander Hamilton, is shot in a duel. George Eacker, a political opponent of his father, shot Hamilton in a duel stemming from Eacker's inflammatory comments about his father.

events.title: Boss Tweed Is Imprisoned In New York City
events.description: The head of New York's Tammany Hall political organization, William "Boss" Tweed, is delivered to city authorities after being captured in Spain.

events.title: Roald Dahl Dies
events.description: Roald Dahl, author of some of the most famous children's books in the world, dies in Oxford. As a young man, Dahl worked as a fighter pilot for the Royal Air Force during the Second World War. During the war, Dahl was sent to the United States as an intelligence officer.

events.title: Harry Einstein Dies On Stage
events.description: CBS via Getty ImagesHarry Einstein as Parkyakarkus on The Al Jolson Show on February 1, 1938.

events.title: The New York City Smog Disaster Begins
events.description: The smog blanketing New York City was so deadly that it spurred anti-pollution measures.

events.title: Spanish War Of Succession Begins
events.description: The Spanish War of Succession begins in Europe. After Charles II of Spain died without an heir, several monarchs declared their right to the throne, sparking a conflict that would last 15 years. Fighting stemmed largely from Philip V's accession to the throne in 1700. Philip V became the longest reigning monarch in Spanish history, serving 44 years as king.

events.title: Philip Hamilton Dies In A Duel
events.description: Philip Hamilton, the son of Alexander Hamilton and Elizabeth Schuyler Hamilton, is killed in a duel. In 1804, his father would also die in a duel.

events.title: Charles Darwin Publishes On The Origin Of Species
events.description: English scientist Charles Darwin publishes his best-known work, On the Origin of Species. The book introduced Darwin's theory of evolution, which he began forming during his five-year voyage on the HMS Beagle two decades earlier. While traveling in the Galapagos Islands, Darwin noticed slight variations in the wildlife from island to island. When he returned to England, he began further research on natural selection, and he published his findings in On the Origin of Species more than 20 years later.

events.title: Lee Harvey Oswald Is Killed
events.description: Jack Ruby shot Lee Harvey Oswald in the abdomen with a .38-caliber revolver. He died an hour and a half later.

events.title: D. B. Cooper Hijacks Flight 305
events.description: Federal Bureau of InvestigationThe FBI sketch of D. B. Cooper, shown in black and white and in color.

events.title: Freddie Mercury Dies
events.description: YouTubeFreddie Mercury looked especially thin during the music video for "These Are the Days of Our Lives," filmed just six months before his death.

events.title: Elizabeth Of York Is Crowned Queen Of England
events.description: Elizabeth of York, consort of King Henry VII and mother of King Henry VIII, is officially crowned Queen of England. The grand celebration included a parade of barges down the River Thames, one "decorated as a huge red dragon spouting real flames." She had become the queen consort upon her marriage to Henry in January 1486, but the coronation was postponed due to her immediate pregnancy and then again because of a period of unrest in England. Ultimately, Elizabeth remained Queen until her death in 1503.

events.title: Andrew Carnegie Is Born
events.description: All told, Andrew Carnegie gave away about 90 percent of his fortune to various charitable causes. His famous 1889 article "The Gospel of Wealth" is widely credited with informing the wave of philanthropy among America's super-wealthy in the ensuing years.

events.title: The Mirabal Sisters Are Assassinated
events.description: Patria, Minerva, and María Teresa Mirabal are killed by the henchmen of Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo for leading an opposition movement against his regime. Trujillo had already had the sisters, who called themselves "Las Mariposas," or "the butterflies," imprisoned, and Patria's house had been burned to the ground.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Jr. Is Born
events.description: John F. Kennedy Jr., the first son of President John F. Kennedy and Jacqueline Kennedy, is born in Washington D.C.

events.title: Yukio Mishimia Dies By Seppuku
events.description: JIJI PRESS/AFP via Getty ImagesYukio Mishima, famed Japanese author, shortly before he committed ritual suicide after a failed coup attempt.

events.title: Junko Furuta Is Kidnapped
events.description: Junko Furuta in an undated photo, taken prior to her kidnapping.

events.title: Sojourner Truth Dies
events.description: Born into slavery in New York around 1797, Sojourner Truth liberated herself in 1826 after her master went back on his promise to free her.

events.title: Czar Nicholas II Marries Alexandra Feodorovna
events.description: The engagement photo of Czar Nicholas II and Alexandra Feodorovna.

events.title: Charles Schulz Is Born
events.description: PicrylA young Charles Schulz with a drawing of Charlie Brown.

events.title: Casablanca Premieres
events.description: Casablanca, the celebrated film starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premieres in New York City. The movie won Oscars for Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Adapted Screenplay and became one of the most iconic films in Hollywood history thanks to now-classic quotes such as "Here's looking at you, kid," and "Round up the usual suspects."

events.title: The Concorde Takes Its Final Flight
events.description: The Concorde, the supersonic jet that could travel between New York and London in roughly three hours, takes its final flight, taking off from London's Heathrow Airport and landing in Bristol.

events.title: Joel Guy Jr. Murders His Parents
events.description: Joel Guy Jr. murders his parents after they decided to cut him off financially. Guy Jr. had spent years in and out of different colleges, all at his parent's expense. Nearing retirement age, his parents decided that financially supporting him was no longer an option, and so they told him he needed to start making it on his own.

events.title: The Berners Street Hoax Unfolds
events.description: After making a bet with his friend that he could turn any house in London into the most-talked about address within a week, Theodore Hook carries out his plan in what's now known as the Berners Street hoax.

events.title: The Nobel Prize Is Established
events.description: Swedish scientist and inventor Alfred Nobel signs his will, in which he orders the bulk of his fortune to be used for the establishment of the Nobel Prize. After divvying up portions of his wealth, Nobel dictated that the entirety of his remaining estate be used for "prizes to those who, during the preceding year, have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind." When Nobel died a year later, his family and the executors of the will initially refused to follow his request, and the first Nobel Prize wasn't awarded until 1901.

events.title: The First Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Is Held
events.description: Macy's Inc.Elephants from the Central Park Zoo marched in the first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

events.title: Bruce Lee Is Born
events.description: Archive Photos/Getty ImagesBruce Lee began studying martial arts when he was a teenager.

events.title: Jimi Hendrix Is Born
events.description: Jimi Hendrix is born Seattle, Washington. As one of the most notable musicians in rock history, Hendrix rose to fame in the 1960s for his skills with the electric guitar. During his short career, Hendrix performed songs like "Purple Haze" and "All Along the Watchtower." In 1968, Rolling Stone named Hendrix as performer of the year. Later, Rolling Stone named Hendrix as the sixth greatest artist of all time. Tragically, Hendrix died at the age of 27 from barbiturate-related asphyxia in London.

events.title: The Slinky Is Introduced
events.description: Two years after inventing the Slinky, Richard T. James demonstrates the iconic toy at Gimbels department store in Philadelphia for the very first time.

events.title: Harvey Milk Is Assassinated
events.description: Flickr/HARVEY MILK ARCHIVES-SCOTT SMITH COLLECTION, HORMEL GAY & LESBIAN CENTER, SAN FRANCISCO PUBLIC LIBRARY.Harvey Milk, the first openly gay person to be elected to public office in California sitting in front of Castro Camera on Castro Street in San Francisco, 1977.

events.title: William Shakespeare Marries Anne Hathaway
events.description: Renowned playwright William Shakespeare, then just 18, marries 26-year-old Anne Hathaway in Stratford-upon-Avon, England. They had three children — one just six months after their wedding — before Shakespeare set off to London to seek work as an actor and playwright. Aside from the children, little is known about their marriage. Hathaway outlived Shakespeare by seven years, and in his will, he left her the "second-best bed with the furniture."

events.title: Anne Bonny's Trial Begins
events.description: After Anne Bonny was arrested for piracy in 1720, her exploits at sea became the stuff of legend.

events.title: Friedrich Engels Is Born
events.description: Philosopher and revolutionary socialist Friedrich Engels is born in what is now Wuppertal, Germany. As a young man, he began forming radical opinions for the time, and he soon started publishing criticisms of industrialism, capitalism, child labor, and the political economy. Engels is best known for developing Marxism with fellow philosopher and economist Karl Marx and co-authoring The Communist Manifesto.

events.title: Jeffrey Dahmer Is Killed
events.description: EUGENE GARCIA/AFP/Getty ImagesJeffrey Dahmer was sentenced to 16 terms of life imprisonment, but he was killed just two years into his sentence.

events.title: Louisa May Alcott Is Born
events.description: American author Louisa May Alcott is born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, the second of four daughters. Her relationship with her sisters inspired Alcott's most famous work, Little Women, the story of four sisters in Massachusetts during and after the Civil War. Alcott was also an avid abolitionist and feminist, and she never married. After a prolific writing career, Alcott died from a stroke at the age of 55.

events.title: The Sand Creek Massacre
events.description: Nearly 700 U.S. volunteer soldiers attack a village of Cheyenne and Arapaho people in the Colorado Territory in what's now known as the Sand Creek Massacre. Over the course of eight hours, the soldiers slaughtered around 230 men, women, and children. The attack was part of a larger series of events known as the Colorado War, which started when white settlers began moving into Native American territory there in the 1860s.

events.title: United Nations Adopts Resolution To Partition Palestine
events.description: The United Nations adopts a resolution to partition Palestine. The United Nations recommended the partition of Palestine after the end of Britain's control of the region, labeling it Resolution 181. The resolution detailed the plan for both an Arab and Jewish state, with a special zone for the city of Jerusalem. The plan was very popular among the Jewish Agency for Palestine and other Zionist groups. Among Palestinians, the plan was cause for a boycott. A civil war broke out in Palestine that effectively halted the resolution's implementation.

events.title: Enos The Chimpanzee Is Launched Into Space
events.description: Enos the chimpanzee is prepared for insertion into the Mercury-Atlas 5.

events.title: Natalie Wood Drowns
events.description: Robert Wagner and Natalie Wood at the Academy Awards dinner in 1960.

events.title: Mark Twain Is Born
events.description: Lauded American author Mark Twain is born Samuel Langhorne Clemens in Florida, Missouri. His childhood in Missouri provided the setting for two of his most famous works, The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, which were published in 1876 and 1884 respectively. Twain wrote at least 28 books and even more short stories throughout his prolific career, and he's remembered by many as "the father of American literature."

events.title: Ann Hodges Is Hit By A Meteorite
events.description: Jay Leviton/The LIFE Images Collection/Getty ImagesAnn Hodges' doctor shows off her bruise, caused by the meteorite.

events.title: Tex Watson Is Arrested
events.description: Michael Haering/Herald Examiner Collection/Los Angeles Public LibraryCharles "Tex" Watson following a court appearance on September 28, 1970.

events.title: Gary Ridgway Is Arrested
events.description: Serial killer Gary Ridgway is arrested for the murder of four women. Ridgway was living and working in Washington state when DNA linked him to the brutal murders of four women. Later, Ridgway would be connected to 49 murders that were committed throughout the 1980s and 1990s. His modus operandi included picking up vulnerable women, often sex workers, and driving them to a remote location. He would then strangle them and leave their bodies in the woods. He also engaged in necrophilia.

events.title: Paul Walker Dies
events.description: dfirecop/FlickrThe car Paul Walker was a passenger in following the deadly crash.

events.title: Marie Tussaud Is Born
events.description: A portrait of Madame Tussaud at age 42.

events.title: Mollie Burkhart Is Born
events.description: Mollie Burkhart, whose family was targeted during the Osage Indian Murders, is born in Osage County, Oklahoma.

events.title: Ford's First Moving Assembly Line Debuts
events.description: Henry Ford unveils the first moving assembly line at his automobile factory in Highland Park, Michigan. The invention made it possible for an entire car to be produced in just one hour and 33 minutes, a drastic difference from the previous 12-hour construction time. Ford was inspired by methods used in flour mills, breweries, and meat-packing plants, and he successfully innovated the system and changed the automobile industry forever.

events.title: Sergei Kirov Is Assassinated
events.description: Soviet politician Sergei Kirov is assassinated in St. Petersburg, triggering the start of Joseph Stalin's "Great Purge."

events.title: The "Somerton Man" Is Discovered
events.description: The mysterious man was carrying no identifying materials, and all of the tags in his clothes had been carefully removed.

events.title: Pablo Escobar Is Born
events.description: Future drug kingpin Pablo Escobar is born in Rionegro, Colombia.

events.title: Rosa Parks Refuses To Give Up Her Seat
events.description: Montgomery County Sheriff's OfficeRosa Parks' 1955 mugshot.

events.title: The Antarctic Treaty Is Signed
events.description: The Antarctic Treaty is signed by 12 countries in Washington D.C. The treaty was an agreement to keep Antarctica free from military influence and open to scientific research.

events.title: Armin Meiwes Is Born
events.description: Armin Meiwes, the "Rotenburg Cannibal," is born in Essen, Germany. Meiwes made international headlines after police found the mutilated body of a young man on his property. In 2001, Meiwes listed an ad for a young man to submit to his cannibalistic fantasies on the website called The Cannibal Cafe. Luckily for Meiwes, someone answered his call.

events.title: Ernest Burkhart Dies
events.description: Ernest Burkhart, who along with his uncle and others perpetrated the Osage Indian murders of the 1920s, dies in Cleveland, Oklahoma, at the age of 94.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Is Crowned Emperor
events.description: An 1812 portrait of Napoleon in his study.

events.title: Monroe Doctrine Is Declared
events.description: President James Monroe articulates the Monroe Doctrine to Congress. The Monroe Doctrine delineated the United States' responsibility in the Western Hemisphere. It shunned European influence in the region and viewed it as a threat to American sovereignty. In particular, the doctrine warned European states that any attempt to further colonize or establish puppet monarchies in the Western Hemisphere would be met with American resistance. The doctrine was invoked throughout the 19th and 20th century in both Mexico, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, and Haiti.

events.title: John Brown Is Executed
events.description: The Last Moments of John Brown by Thomas Hovenden, 1888.

events.title: "Torso Killer" Richard Cottingham Murders Two Women
events.description: Firemen responding to a call at a motel in New York City's Times Square find the burned bodies of two women, the latest victims of serial killer Richard Cottingham. Their heads and hands had been cut off, and they'd been doused in lighter fluid. It would be decades before the "Torso Killer" confessed to the murders, but he was arrested just six months later for kidnapping and torturing another woman.

events.title: Pablo Escobar Dies
events.description: Police pose with Pablo Escobar's body after his death.

events.title: Frederick Douglass Publishes The First Issue Of His Anti-Slavery Newspaper
events.description: Before becoming one of the nation's foremost abolitionists, Frederick Douglass himself escaped slavery in Maryland and fled northward.

events.title: Agatha Christie Disappears
events.description: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesNews of Agatha Christie's disappearance sent shockwaves around the world and triggered a public manhunt in England.

events.title: Ozzy Osbourne Is Born
events.description: Singer and reality television personality John Michael "Ozzy" Osbourne is born in Warwickshire, England. Osbourne became famous as the lead singer of the heavy metal band Black Sabbath in the 1970s and also released 12 successful solo albums after he was booted from the band for his drug and alcohol abuse in 1979. Later in his career, the "Godfather of Metal" went on to star in MTV reality show The Osbournes alongside his wife Sharon and their children Kelly and Jack. Known for his wild onstage antics, Osbourne remains one of the most infamous legends of rock to this day.

events.title: The First Human Heart Transplant Is Performed
events.description: The first human heart transplant is performed by Christiaan Barnard in South Africa. Barnard performed the operation on Lewis Washkansky, a 53-year-old South African grocer with chronic heart disease, using the heart of a 25-year-old car crash victim. The operation was a success, and Washkansky's heart continued to operate as normal until he died of pneumonia. The second human heart transplant was performed three days later in the United States.

events.title: The Wreck Of The HMHS Britannic Is Discovered
events.description: Jacques Cousteau discovers the wreck of the HMHS Britannic. The ship sunk after hitting a mine in November 1916. Of the 1,066 people on board, 1,036 people survived the sinking.

events.title: The Bhopal Disaster
events.description: Sandro Tucci/Liaison/ Getty ImagesResidents collect the bodies of those who died in the Bhopal Disaster.

events.title: Scott Weiland Dies
events.description: Scott Weiland, best known as the frontman for the rock band Stone Temple Pilots, died of an accidental overdose on his tour bus while stopped in Bloomington, Minnesota. His successful music career was plagued by substance abuse issues. At the time of his death, the 48-year-old was touring with The Wildabouts, having been kicked out of Stone Temple Pilots a couple years earlier.

events.title: The Shroud Of Turin Is Damaged In A Fire
events.description: The Shroud of Turin is damaged in a fire, and stains left by water and fire can be seen on the religious object to this day.

events.title: Ivan The Terrible Becomes Grand Prince Of Moscow
events.description: A rendering of Ivan the Terrible's murder of his eldest son in 1581.

events.title: Francisco Franco Is Born
events.description: Spanish dictator Francisco Franco is born to a military family in Galicia. He began his career as a cadet in the Spanish Army, eventually rising through the ranks to become the youngest general in all of Europe at the age of just 33. In 1936, he became the head of the country's new Nationalist regime, widely regarded as a fascist movement. His dictatorship, though marked by economic prosperity, quickly became notorious around the world for his brutal repression of his political opponents through forced labor camps and mass executions. He held his power through the Spanish Civil War that saw him fight off his Republican enemies, and ruled through World War II and well into the postwar years before ultimately dying in 1975.

events.title: Fred Hampton And Mark Clark Are Murdered
events.description: Fred Hampton's bedroom after the attack.

events.title: Polly Klaas' Body Is Found
events.description: Polly was kidnapped on October 1, and after two months of searching, police find her body. Her kidnapper, Richard Allen Davis, strangled her within two hours of abducting her. She was 12 years old when she died.

events.title: Jonathan Schmitz, The Jenny Jones Killer, is convicted
