events.description: Jonathan Schmitz, the Jenny Jones Killer, is convicted for the murder of Scott Amedure. In 1995, Schmitz was invited to appear on The Jenny Jones Show where someone with a secret crush on him would confess. A gay acquaintance named Scott Amedure met with Schmitz, telling him that he liked him. Schmitz seemed to take it well enough, but three days later, Schmitz would shoot Amedure to death outside his home.

events.title: Amanda Knox Is Convicted Of Murder
events.description: Oli Scarff/Getty ImagesAmanda Knox is escorted into court on Dec. 4, 2009.

events.title: Pope Innocent VIII Condemns Witchcraft
events.description: Pope Innocent VIII issues a papal bull recognizing and condemning the practice of witchcraft. Summis desiderantes affectibus — Latin for "desiring with supreme ardor" — was written when German clergyman Heinrich Kramer asked the Pope for express permission to prosecute witchcraft in his country.

events.title: Mozart Dies
events.description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, one of the greatest composers in history, dies at 35 years old. The composer's death is subject to several rumors about a poisoning scheme.

events.title: Mary Celeste Is Found Abandoned
events.description: The Mary Celeste is found abandoned near Portugal's Azores Islands.

events.title: Prohibition Ends In The United States
events.description: Imagno/Getty ImagesPatrons at a bar in New York toast to the end of the 18th Amendment.

events.title: The Great Smog Descends Over London
events.description: Fox Photos/Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesLondon's Tower Bridge in the thick smog.

events.title: Fijian Coup D'Etat Results In Presidency Of Frank Bainimarama
events.description: The Fijian coup d'état results in the presidency of Frank Bainimarama. Bainimarama was the commander of the Republic of Fiji Military Forces (RFMF) when highly unpopular bills addressing the country's ethnic divide were introduced in Fiji's parliament. Bainimarama spoke out against the bills and demanded their removal from consideration. Fiji's prime minister, Laisenia Qarase, and President Josefa Iloilo, did not attempt negotiations with Bainimarama, and a coup led by the commander overthrew them.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Dies
events.description: Nelson Mandela in Washington, D.C. in 1994, during his first-ever trip to the United States.

events.title: Henry VI Of England Is Born
events.description: After he lost a wealth of territory and was overpowered by both enemies and allies, King Edward VI gained a reputation as one of the most ineffectual monarchs in English history.

events.title: The Washington Monument Is Completed
events.description: Workers put the finishing touches on the capstone of the Washington Monument.

events.title: "Baby Face" Nelson Is Born
events.description: Bank Robber Lester Gillis, also known as "Baby Face" Nelson, is born in Chicago.

events.title: The Halifax Explosion Devastates Nova Scotia
events.description: City of Toronto ArchivesEverything within a half-mile of the explosion was completely obliterated.

events.title: Ulysses Is Ruled Not Obscene
events.description: A federal judge rules that James Joyce's Ulysses is not obscene and can be published in the United States. The novel had initially been banned in the United States after an excerpt of it that contained a masturbation scene was printed in a literary magazine and caused controversy.

events.title: Meredith Hunter Is Killed At Alamont
events.description: Jeff Hochberg/Getty ImagesMembers of Hells Angels guard the stage as the Rolling Stones perform at the Altamont Free Concert.

events.title: Susan Powell Goes Missing
events.description: Susan Powell goes missing from her Utah home. Susan Powell lived with her husband, Josh Powell, and their two sons in West Valley City, Utah. After Powell failed to show up to work, police immediately began suspecting her husband. Cryptic messages left by Powell as well as mountain of forensic evidence pointed to her husband's involvement in her disappearance and probable murder. Unfortunately, police would not be able to question her husband further after he killed himself and the couple's two young sons in his home in 2012.

events.title: Gian Lorenzo Bernini Is Born
events.description: Apollo and Daphne by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 1625.

events.title: Madame LaLaurie Dies
events.description: Portraits of Delphine LaLaurie.

events.title: Japan Attacks Pearl Harbor
events.description: U.S. Navy/Interim Archives/Getty ImagesSmoke billows from warships after Japanese forces attack Pearl Harbor.

events.title: The First Execution By Lethal Injection Takes Place
events.description: Charles Brooks Jr. is executed by lethal injection in Huntsville, Texas, marking the first such execution in history. Brooks had been convicted of murdering an auto mechanic in 1976, and he was sentenced to death two years later. The method had been developed as a more humane way to carry out death sentences, involving a barbiturate injection to render the prisoner unconscious, a muscle relaxant to paralyze the diaphragm and lungs, and potassium chloride to cause cardiac arrest.

events.title: Rossana Miliani Goes Missing
events.description: Rossana Miliani, a 24-year-old hiker from Miami, Florida, goes missing while preparing for a hike on the Appalachian Trail. She was last seen buying hiking supplies in Bryson City, North Carolina with an older man who said he was a traveling preacher.

events.title: An English Woman Appears In A Public Play For The First Time
events.description: Though some historians identify another actress named Anne Marshall as the first to take the English stage, most believe it was Margaret Hughes.

events.title: Diego Rivera Is Born
events.description: Renowned painter Diego Rivera is born in Guanajuato City, Mexico. Rivera is best known for his large murals and frescoes, including his 27-part series Detroit Industry Murals. In 2018, his painting The Rivals sold for $9.7 million, the highest price that a work by a Latin American artist had ever fetched up to that point. That record was only broken by Rivera's wife, Frida Kahlo, when her self-portrait Diego y yo sold for $34.9 million in 2021.

events.title: Sammy Davis Jr. Is Born
events.description: Sammy Davis Jr., an American singer and actor, is born in New York City. Davis Jr. began his career at the age of three when his father included him in the traveling dance group, the Will Mastin Trio. In the 1960s, Davis Jr. appeared in the film Ocean's 11, started his own variety show, and released his biggest hit, "The Candy Man." Davis Jr. was a key player in tearing down divides in the segregated entertainment industry. He continued working in entertainment until his death in Beverly Hills at the age of 64.

events.title: Frank Sinatra Jr. Is Kidnapped
events.description: Keystone/Getty ImagesFrank Sinatra Jr. with his father on the day that he was safely released from his captors.

events.title: John Lennon Is Killed
events.description: Keystone/Getty ImagesMourners gather at the Dakota apartment building in New York City, where John Lennon was shot.

events.title: Pantera Guitarist Dimebag Darrell Dies
events.description: While performing at a nightclub in Columbus, Ohio, Pantera guitarist Darrell Abbott is shot onstage by 25-year-old Nathan Gale.

events.title: The U.S. And Russia Exchange Prisoners Viktor Bout And Brittney Griner
events.description: The U.S. and Russia exchange prisoners Viktor Bout and Brittney Griner in the United Arab Emirates. Bout was an arms dealer arrested in Thailand in 2008 for selling weapons to the Middle East and Africa while Griner was an American basketball player arrested in Russia in 2022 for smuggling drugs.

events.title: John Milton Is Born
events.description: English poet John Milton is born to a wealthy family in London. He is best known for his epic poem Paradise Lost, the tale of the biblical story of the Fall of Man that's widely considered one of the best works of literature in world history.

events.title: Jesse Pomeroy's Trial Begins
events.description: A drawing of Jesse Pomeroy c. 1870s, around the time of his killing spree.

events.title: The Great Smog Of London Comes To An End
events.description: London is finally freed from what's since become known as the Great Smog. For four days, the city was besieged by the worst air pollution event in its history as a thick cloud of yellow-black smog filled the air. Caused by low temperatures and an anticyclone that exacerbated pollution from coal burning, the Great Smog made the air nearly opaque — "like you were blind," one visitor remembered.

events.title: A Charlie Brown Christmas Debuts
events.description: CBSThis iconic special has earned both an Emmy and a Peabody and has remained a fan favorite for decades.

events.title: Smallpox Is Eradicated
events.description: A victim of Gloucester, England's 1896 smallpox outbreak.

events.title: John Du Pont Dies
events.description: John du Pont, millionaire and murderer of Dave Schultz, dies. Du Pont was the heir to the du Pont organization, an American chemical company. In the 1990s, du Pont began investing in the U.S. wrestling team. In 1996, du Pont fatally shot a member of the wrestling team, a seven-time Olympic medalist named Dave Schultz in Schultz's home. Police arrested du Pont for the murder after a days-long standoff. A court later sentenced du Pont to prison, and he died there in 2010.

events.title: Antonio Bosio Starts Exploring The Catacombs Of Rome
events.description: Antonio Bosio, an 18-year-old student of Christian antiquities, begins his systematic exploration of the catacombs of Rome, which had been forgotten for centuries.

events.title: Encyclopedia Britannica Is Published For The First Time
events.description: The first part of the Encyclopedia Britannica is published in Edinburgh, Scotland. The initial edition was released in small sections between 1768 and 1771, and it consisted of three volumes that were around 2,500 pages each. The encyclopedia pledged to provide "accurate definitions and explanations of all the Terms as they occur in the Order of the Alphabet."

events.title: Ada Lovelace Is Born
events.description: Ada Lovelace is remembered as the world's first computer programmer.

events.title: King Edward VIII Of England Abdicates
events.description: King Edward VIII abdicates the throne to marry American divorcée, Wallis Simpson. The Marburg Files would later reveal the pair's Nazi ties.

events.title: The Universal Declaration Of Human Rights Is Adopted
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights during an assembly in Paris, France. The document was drafted by representatives from various cultural, legal, religious, and political backgrounds. It detailed the "basic rights and fundamental freedoms" of human beings across the globe and acted as a "common standard of achievements for all peoples and all nations." Though not legally binding, the document has been incorporated into several international treaties and national constitutions.

events.title: Otis Redding Dies
events.description: Bettmann/Contributor via Getty ImagesA crane pulls the wreckage of Otis Redding's plane out of Lake Monona in Wisconsin.

events.title: Julia Hill Climbs Into Redwood Tree In Protest
events.description: Julia "Butterfly" Hill climbs into a California redwood tree to prevent it from being cut down. She resided in the tree for 738 days.

events.title: Comedian Richard Pryor Dies
events.description: Legendary comedian Richard Pryor suffered his third and final heart attack at the age of 65. He was well known for his stand-up and various film roles, including Stir Crazy, Silver Streak, and The Muppet Movie. He suffered many health problems throughout his life, having his first heart attack at the age of 36, and was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1986.

events.title: Texas Court Of Appeals Upholds Doctor Death's Conviction
events.description: The Texas Court of Appeals upholds Doctor Death's conviction. Doctor Death, or Christopher Duntsch, was a Dallas surgeon responsible for the mutilation of dozens of his patients and the death of at least two between 2011 and 2013. Those close to him stated that he had started spiraling in 2006, taking LSD and doing cocaine frequently. While working in Dallas, Duntsch operated on at least 38 patients, 31 of whom were left seriously injured or paralyzed because of the procedures. Eventually, the Texas Medical Board would strip Duntsch of his surgical privileges, and an investigation was launched.

events.title: Louis XVI's Treason Trial Begins
events.description: King Louis XVI of France is put on trial for high treason and other crimes against his people. He'd been arrested and dethroned several months prior, but in the midst of the French Revolution, the public was still demanding that he be brought to justice after it was discovered that he was colluding with foreign powers to overthrow the revolutionary government. The trial lasted until Jan. 15, 1793, when he was unanimously found guilty. He was publicly executed via guillotine six days later.

events.title: King Edward VIII Abdicates The Throne
events.description: King Edward VIII abdicates the English throne to marry Wallis Simpson. On January 20, 1936, Edward VIII took the throne. Months into his reign, Edward expressed his desire to marry Wallis Simpson, a twice-divorced American woman. The relationship was highly controversial in the United Kingdom and caused a constitutional crisis. Edward decided to abdicate the throne to marry Simpson, resulting in one of the shortest reigns in British history.

events.title: Frank Sinatra Jr. Is Found Safe After Kidnapping
events.description: A few days after Frank Sinatra Jr. was kidnapped, the son of "Ol' Blue Eyes" is found safe in Los Angeles. His kidnappers were swiftly apprehended and jailed, but their false allegation that the Sinatra family was behind the kidnapping followed Frank Jr. for the rest of his life.

events.title: Sam Cooke Is Killed
events.description: Bettmann/Contributor via Getty ImagesSam Cooke's body is removed from the office of the motel.

events.title: The Lufthansa Heist Takes Place
events.description: Nick Sorrentino/NY Daily News via Getty ImagesA Lufthansa employee shows FBI agents where he and others were tied up during the robbery.

events.title: Bernie Madoff Is Arrested
events.description: American billionaire and financier Bernie Madoff is arrested in New York City on charges of running a Ponzi scheme that was one of the biggest investment frauds in the history of Wall Street. As early as the 1980s, Madoff was swindling his clients by lying about the returns on their investments and paying off his initial investors with funds from new clients.

events.title: Gustave Flaubert Is Born
events.description: Gustave Flaubert famously said, "an author in his book must be like God in the universe, present everywhere and visible nowhere."

events.title: Edvard Munch Is Born
events.description: Edvard Munch, expressionist painter, is born in Oslo, Norway. Munch is best known today for his work The Scream, a piece that portrays a screaming person under a blood-red sky. This work became the fourth most expensive art piece sold at auction.

events.title: Guglielmo Marconi Receives The First Transatlantic Radio Signal
events.description: Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi makes a historic breakthrough in communication when he successfully receives radio signals from across the Atlantic Ocean. Since the advent of the telegraph machine, Marconi had been experimenting with sending Morse code messages wirelessly via radio waves. On Dec. 12, he set up a receiver in Newfoundland, Canada in an attempt to receive a message coming from Cornwall, England — and successfully heard the Morse code for the letter "S" from 1,700 miles away.

events.title: Dorothy Arnold Vanishes
events.description: Socialite Dorothy Arnold before her mysterious disappearance.

events.title: Buford Pusser Is Born
events.description: Buford Pusser, sheriff and folk hero of Adamsville, Tennessee, is born. His claim to fame includes battling the Dixie Mafia and the State Line Mob and avenging his wife's murder.

events.title: The Corpsewood Manor Murders Take Place
events.description: Facebook/Corpsewood BookThe three-story chicken house where Charles Scudder and Joe Odom hosted their "sex parties."

events.title: Samuel Johnson Dies
events.description: A portrait of Samuel Johnson created by English painter Joshua Reynolds, circa 1772.

events.title: Dick Van Dyke Is Born
events.description: American actor, singer, and comedian Dick Van Dyke is born in West Plains, Missouri. Growing up, he initially planned to become a minister, but he changed his mind after taking a drama class in high school. He started as a radio DJ before joining a touring comedy group, then made his Broadway debut in 1959. Van Dyke quickly rose to fame after winning a Tony award for his role in the musical Bye Bye Birdie the following year, and he is best known for his roles in films like Mary Poppins and his television sitcom The Dick Van Dyke Show.

events.title: The Nanking Massacre Begins
events.description: Moriyasu Murase/Wikimedia CommonsDead bodies lay next to Qinhuai River during the Nanking Massacre.

events.title: Irma Grese, "The Hyena of Auschwitz," Is Executed
events.description: Irma Grese, "The Hyena of Auschwitz" is executed for her crimes against prisoners at Auschwitz. As one of the most sadistic guards at Auschwitz, Grese subjected prisoners to horrific torture, including unleashing dogs on prisoners, raping them, and whipping them. After the war concluded, British forces arrested Grese and held her trial the same year. Victim testimony proved beyond a doubt that Grese was a ruthless force at Auschwitz, and she was hanged at the age of 22.

events.title: Saddam Hussein Is Captured
events.description: Saddam Hussein immediately after his capture.

events.title: Nostradamus Is Born
events.description: Adherents claim that Nostradamus predicted everything from the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki to the September 11th attacks.

events.title: Tycho Brahe Is Born
events.description: Tycho Brahe, one of the world's most important astronomers, is born in Denmark. Brahe is most known today for his accurate astronomical calculations and charismatic personality. His interest in astronomy stemmed from his observance of a supernova in 1572. He dedicated himself to the field, opening his own observatory on an island. During his career, he conducted a comprehensive study of the solar system and accurately charted the position of more than 777 fixed stars, all before the invention of the telescope.

events.title: George Washington Dies
events.description: Junius Brutus Stearns/Dayton Art InstituteGeorge Washington on his Deathbed by Junius Brutus Stearns, 1851.

events.title: Roald Amundsen Reaches The South Pole
events.description: Roald Amundsen also led the first successful expedition to ever traverse the Northwest Passage.

events.title: Betty And Barney Hill Began Hypnotism Therapy
events.description: After allegedly being abducted by aliens in 1961, Betty and Barney Hill visit hypnotist Dr. Benjamin Simon to try and resurface their memories of the event. Under his guidance, they purportedly remembered the abduction in great detail, including how the aliens performed examinations on them.

events.title: The Sandy Hook School Shooting
events.description: Adam Lanza, a 20-year-old man from Newtown, Connecticut, kills his mother and then fatally shoots 26 people at Sandy Hook Elementary School before taking his own life. It was the deadliest elementary school shooting in American history, with 20 six- and seven-year-old students and six teachers and administrators killed. To this day, Lanza's motives remain unclear. Afterward, the tragedy sparked numerous conspiracy theories, notably by radio host Alex Jones, who claimed that the shooting was a hoax.

events.title: The Bill Of Rights Is Ratified
events.description: The Bill of Rights, which includes the first 10 amendments to the United States Constitution, is ratified. The document had initially included 19 amendments, but the U.S. House of Representatives only approved 17 of them. Then, the U.S. Senate narrowed the list down further to 12.

events.title: Alexandre-Gustave Eiffel Is Born
events.description: Civil engineer Alexandre-Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the Eiffel Tower, is born in Dijon, France. Eiffel attended France's College of Art and Manufacturing before beginning his career in metal construction. The company he co-founded in 1868 began receiving contracts for important bridges such as the Garabit Viaduct, and in the late 1880s, Eiffel began designing what would become the Eiffel Tower. The world-famous structure won Eiffel the nickname the "magician of iron."

events.title: Sitting Bull Dies
events.description: Before the Battle of the Little Bighorn, Sitting Bull reportedly had a vision that the Lakota would be victorious over the U.S. Cavalry, which soon proved correct.

events.title: Silver Bridge Collapses
events.description: Point Pleasant River MuseumThe aftermath of the Silver Bridge collapse.

events.title: John Paul Getty III Is Released By Kidnappers
events.description: John Paul Getty III, the grandson of billionaire J. Paul Getty, is released by his kidnappers five months after they abducted him in Rome and demanded millions of dollars in ransom money from his family. During his captivity, his kidnappers cut off his ear as a way to pressure the Getty family.

events.title: Joe Metheny Is Arrested
events.description: MurderpediaJoe Metheny allegedly butchered his victims and sold them as burgers.

events.title: The Boston Tea Party Unfolds
events.description: An 1846 lithograph of the Boston Tea Party.

events.title: Jane Austen Is Born
events.description: Jane Austen, one of the most prominent female authors of the 19th century, is born in Hampshire, England. Austen published her first novel, Sense and Sensibility, in 1811. She went on to write five more novels, including her most well-known work, Pride and Prejudice, though only four were published before her death at age 41 in 1817. Since her works were initially published anonymously, she received little fame during her lifetime, though she's now one of the best-known female authors in history.

events.title: Thelma Todd Dies
events.description: Thelma Todd in 1933, just two years before her untimely death.

events.title: The Battle Of The Bulge Begins
events.description: The Battle of the Bulge, Germany's last major offensive campaign during World War II, begins in the Ardennes region between Belgium and Luxembourg. American forces were not prepared for the attack, but they were able to hold out until reinforcements arrived, and the Allies eventually won the battle about a month later. The Battle of the Bulge was both the largest and bloodiest battle fought by the United States in World War II, with about 90,000 American casualties.

events.title: Michael Peterson Is Released From Prison
events.description: Michael Peterson is released from prison after eight years. Michael Peterson and his wife Kathleen Peterson lived in Durham, North Carolina with their children. In 2001, Michael Peterson called 911 after he found his wife at the bottom of their stairs in a pool of her own blood. Physical evidence did not corroborate the story he told to police, and investigators arrested him for the murder of his wife. In 2003, a jury found him guilty and sentenced him to life in prison. However, Peterson was later resentenced and is currently a free man. This case is still one of the most controversial in United States history.

events.title: Deborah Sampson Is Born
events.description: Deborah Sampson, the American woman who disguised herself as a man and served in the Continental Army during the Revolutionary War, is born in Plympton, Massachusetts. In 1782, Sampson posed as Robert Shurtliff and joined the Fourth Massachusetts Regiment. During the war, she served as a scout, led a raid on a Tory home, and dug trenches at the siege of Yorktown. Her true identity was only discovered when she became ill in Philadelphia and had to see a doctor after the war. She then received an honorable discharge and later earned a full military pension from her service in the Revolutionary War.

events.title: Simón Bolívar Dies
events.description: Venezuelan political and military leader Simón Bolívar dies in what is now Colombia. He'd resigned as the first president of Colombia earlier in the year, as he intended to leave for exile in Europe. However, before he was able, he died of tuberculosis at the age of 47 near Santa Marta. Bolívar is remembered as El Libertador, or "The Liberator," as he helped several countries in South America become independent from Spain.

events.title: The Wright Brothers Take Their First Flight
events.description: The Wright brothers, seconds into their first flight.

events.title: Simo Häyhä, The "White Death," Is Born In Finland
events.description: Simo Häyhä, the "White Death," is born in Finland. Häyhä made a name for himself during the Winter War between Finland and the Soviet Union. In just 100 days, Häyhä killed at least 500 Russian soldiers. Known as one of the most skilled snipers in the war, Häyhä is one of the many reasons why the smaller Nordic nation put up such a strong fight against the Soviet Union. Russian soldiers gave Häyhä the nickname "White Death," and it became the subject of several pieces of Finnish propaganda.

events.title: Richard Kuklinski Is Captured
events.description: Bettmann/Contributor/Getty ImagesRichard Kuklinski, the "Iceman," is escorted into court.

events.title: The Nutcracker Ballet Debuts
events.description: The now-classic ballet The Nutcracker debuts in St. Petersburg, Russia. Based on Amadeus Hoffmann's 1816 story The Nutcracker and the Mouse King, the ballet is set to music by Russian composer Pyotr Tchaikovsky and choreographed by Marius Petipa.

events.title: The Piltdown Man Is Discovered
events.description: A 1915 photograph of archaeologists examining the so-called Piltdown Man.

events.title: Steven Spielberg Is Born
events.description: reddit/mlslgnSteven Spielberg, Tom Hanks, Matt Damon, and Ed Burns on set of Saving Private Ryan. The war epic made over $481 million worldwide, making it the second-highest-grossing film of 1998.

events.title: Neilia Hunter Biden Dies In A Car Accident
events.description: Neila Biden, Joe Biden's first wife, dies in a car accident alongside her daughter, Naomi.

events.title: Alison Botha Survives Her Brutal Attack
events.description: Alison Botha survives her brutal attack in South Africa. After a night out with friends, Botha headed back to her apartment in Port Elizabeth, South Africa. When she parked, a man with a knife forced his way into the car and took control of the vehicle. Another man joined the two, and they all took off towards a deserted area outside of town.

events.title: Chris Farley Dies
events.description: Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic, Inc. via Getty ImagesChris Farley, Chris Rock, Adam Sandler, and David Spade in 1997.

events.title: Mark Felt Dies
events.description: Mark Felt, better known as the anonymous source "Deep Throat" from the Watergate scandal, dies in Santa Rosa, California, at the age of 95.

events.title: The First Poor Richard's Almanack Is Released
events.description: An early edition of Poor Richard's Almanack.

events.title: Charles Dickens Publishes A Christmas Carol
events.description: British author Charles Dickens releases the now-classic novella A Christmas Carol to immediate acclaim. Dickens was already known for Oliver Twist and the Pickwick Papers, so when A Christmas Carol was released, it sold out by Christmas Eve. The author had written the story in just six weeks while under financial pressure, and though he didn't make much money from the first few editions of the book, it accelerated his rise to literary fame.

events.title: Ella Harper Dies
events.description: Ella Harper was known as the "Camel Girl" because of her rare condition.

events.title: Titanic Premieres
events.description: James Cameron's epic film Titanic opens in American theaters to glowing reviews. A lavish retelling of the sinking of the RMS Titanic in 1912, the movie captivated audiences around the world. Starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet, the film that cost $200 million to make made more than $1.8 billion worldwide, a record it held until Avatar was released in 2009. A New York Times film critic wrote after the premiere, "The ship is afloat again, and... the audience is intimately involved in its voyage."

events.title: The House Of Representatives Approves Articles Of Impeachment Against Bill Clinton
events.description: The U.S. House of Representatives approves articles of impeachment against President Bill Clinton. The House charged President Clinton with lying under oath to a federal grand jury and obstructing justice for the statements he made about the Monica Lewinsky scandal. Lewinsky reportedly testified that she and the president had sexual encounters in the White House. When asked about these claims, President Clinton stated, "I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Ms. Lewinsky." He later acknowledged that he did in fact have an affair with her. The Senate eventually acquitted President Clinton.

events.title: The Killings Of David Faraday And Betty Lou Jensen
events.description: The infamous Zodiac killer takes the lives of his first two confirmed victims, David Faraday and Betty Lou Jensen.

events.title: South Carolina Secedes From The Union
events.description: South Carolina becomes the first state to secede from the Union, setting in motion a chain of events that would lead to the outbreak of the Civil War. The South Carolina General Assembly voted unanimously to secede, citing that the federal government had failed to uphold its constitutional obligations to the state by "denounc[ing] as sinful the institution of slavery" and assisting "thousands of our slaves to leave their homes."

events.title: Adolf Hitler Is Released From Prison
events.description: Adolf Hitler is released from Landsberg Prison after spending nine months incarcerated for his role in the Beer Hall Putsch of 1923, a failed coup against Germany's government by the Nazi Party. While in prison, the future dictator started writing the first volume of Mein Kampf, his political manifesto. After his release, Hitler quickly helped grow the Nazi Party. Within 10 years, he would be elected the chancellor of Germany.

events.title: The Cecil Hotel Opens in Los Angeles
events.description: The Cecil Hotel opens in Los Angeles. The hotel was built by William Banks Hanner. It was meant to be a destination hotel for the high-class. Instead of being known as an opulent and luxurious getaway, the Cecil Hotel has a much darker reputation. Since its opening, the hotel has been plagued by bad luck. At least 16 people have been murdered within its walls, and numerous suicides and paranormal activity have been reported. It has even served as the temporary home of many serial killers. In 2013, the Cecil Hotel made headlines once again after Elisa Lam was found naked and deceased in the hotel's water tanks.

events.title: Elvis Presley Is Drafted
events.description: Elvis Presley while stationed in Germany in 1958.

events.title: Brittany Murphy Dies
events.description: John Shearer/WireImage via Getty ImagesBrittany Murphy with her husband Simon Monjack in November 2007.

events.title: The Pilgrims Come Ashore At Plymouth
events.description: A print of the Pilgrims landing at Plymouth by Joseph Andrews. 1869.

events.title: The First Basketball Game Is Played
events.description: James Naismith holding a ball and basket.

events.title: Marie And Pierre Curie Discover Radium
events.description: Scientists Marie and Pierre Curie first discover radium, a groundbreaking moment in the history of radioactivity. The husband-and-wife duo was studying pitchblende, now known as uraninite, a uranium-rich mineral. They removed the uranium and noted that a previously unknown element was left behind. The Curies called it "radium" due to the way it emitted energy in rays. The discovery quickly led to advancements in healthcare — but the dangers of radiation poisoning weren't realized until years later.

events.title: Samuel L. Jackson Is Born
events.description: American actor Samuel L. Jackson is born in Washington, D.C. He's now one of the highest-grossing actors of all time, but he didn't discover his love for acting until college. Jackson's early roles include Coming to America and Goodfellas, but he rose to international fame with Pulp Fiction in 1994. He's appeared in more than 150 films over the course of his career, and he's won numerous awards for his performances.

events.title: President Richard Nixon Meets Elvis Presley
events.description: President Richard Nixon meets with Elvis Presley after the musician delivered a letter to the White House gates expressing his concern about anti-American sentiment, hippies, and other issues. Elvis gifted Nixon with a Colt .45 pistol, and the president gave Elvis a federal narcotics badge.

events.title: Hisashi Ouchi, The Most Radioactive Man In History, Dies
events.description: Hisashi Ouchi, the most radioactive man in history, dies from his injuries. After pouring seven times the amount of uranium into an improper tank while standing above it, Ouchi was pummeled by Gamma rays. The results were immediate. Ouchi struggled to breathe, vomited violently, and passed out. Doctors were stunned by his condition once he arrived at the hospital. He had virtually zero white blood cells in his body, and his skin was beginning to melt off his body. His family refused to end his agony, instead opting to resuscitate him every time he flatlined from heart attacks. Eighty-three days after his initial exposure to the radiation, Ouchi would die of cardiac arrest.

events.title: Congress Passes The Embargo Act
events.description: The United States Congress passes the Embargo Act, a general trade embargo on all foreign nations. During the Napoleonic Wars, the rival nations of Britain and France targeted American shipping, seizing American merchant ships as a way to disrupt each other's trade. President Thomas Jefferson asked Congress to pass the Embargo Act to put a stop to it, but it was highly unpopular and significantly damaged America's economy. In the end, the tensions it caused with Britain helped pave the way for the War of 1812.

events.title: Frank Kellogg Is Born
events.description: Frank Kellogg, statesman and lawyer, is born in Potsdam, New York. Kellogg began his career as a lawyer prosecuting financial crimes against major organizations. Then, in 1916, Kellogg was elected to the Senate representing the state of Minnesota. Later, he served as the Ambassador to Great Britain and U.S. Secretary of State. Kellogg co-authored the Kellogg-Briand Pact, an international agreement that sought to end war as a foreign policy tool. He would later win the Nobel Peace Prize for this in 1929.

events.title: Alfred Dreyfus Is Convicted Of Treason
events.description: Alfred Dreyfus, circa 1894.

events.title: John Wayne Gacy Confesses To Dozens Of Murders
events.description: A mugshot of Gacy from 1968, when he was arrested for sexual coercion in the workplace.

events.title: Nicolae Ceaușescu Is Overthrown
events.description: Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu is overthrown by protestors, ending his reign which had begun in 1965. Five days prior, the communist ruler had ordered the military to open fire on demonstrators, leading to numerous deaths. When the public realized that Ceaușescu had been the one to order the attacks, they revolted in what's now known as the Romanian Revolution. Ceaușescu tried to flee from the capital of Bucharest in a helicopter, but the military captured him. He was convicted of genocide and other crimes and executed by firing squad along with his wife on Christmas Day.

events.title: Woody Allen Marries Soon-Yi Previn
events.description: Director Woody Allen, 62, marries Soon-Yi Previn, 27, the adopted daughter of his former girlfriend, Mia Farrow, in Venice, Italy.

events.title: George Washington Resigns From The Continental Army
events.description: Charles Willson Peale/Brooklyn MuseumA 1776 portrait of General George Washington.

events.title: Madam C.J. Walker Is Born
events.description: Michael Ochs Archives/Getty ImagesMadam C.J. Walker, born Sarah Breedlove, is recognized as one of the first Black female millionaires in America.

events.title: Explorer Ejnar Mikkelsen is born
events.description: Ejnar Mikkelsen, a Danish explorer, is born. In 1909, Mikkelsen set out on an Arctic expedition with six men. It would take him three years to return home, as he was forced to spend two brutal winters in the Arctic. While exploring the region, Mikkelsen and a crewmate got lost. The two were forced to eat their sled dogs to survive and suffered daily hallucinations. The pair would spend two winters in the Arctic before being rescued on July 19, 1912 by Norwegian steamer Sjøblimsten. Later, Mikkelsen would receive a hero's welcome back in Denmark.

events.title: Vincent Van Gogh Cuts Off His Ear
events.description: Van Gogh painted Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear in January 1889.

events.title: The First Successful Kidney Transplant Is Performed
events.description: American physician Dr. Joseph Murray performs the first successful human kidney transplant on a set of identical twins in Boston, Massachusetts. Richard Herrick, the 23-year-old recipient who was suffering from kidney disease, lived for eight years following the surgery, a feat that had previously been unimaginable. Murray was later quoted as saying, "We didn't think we made history. We didn't even think of history. We thought we were going to save a patient."

events.title: Pittsburgh Becomes The First U.S. City To Generate Electricity Via Nuclear Power
events.description: The Shippingport Atomic Power Station, the world's first full-scale nuclear power plant, becomes operational, making Pittsburgh the first city in American to generate electricity with nuclear power.

events.title: The Eggnog Riot Breaks Out
events.description: The Eggnog Riot, or Grog Mutiny, takes place at the U.S. Military Academy in West Point, New York. Late on Christmas Eve, a group of cadets made large amounts of eggnog with whiskey and other spirits they'd smuggled into the North Barracks and threw a party.

events.title: The Ku Klux Klan Is Formed
events.description: A group of Confederate veterans forms the Ku Klux Klan in Pulaski, Tennessee with the aim to reverse the effects of Reconstruction in the United States and prevent the Black population from obtaining rights. The first grand wizard of the KKK was former Confederate general Nathan Bedford Forrest, and the group soon began destroying property, intimidating government officials, and murdering citizens to achieve their goals.

events.title: Dean Corll Is Born
events.description: YouTubeDean Corll in 1973, months before he was fatally shot by his 17-year-old accomplice, Elmer Wayne Henley.

events.title: The Sodder Children Disappear
events.description: Jennie Henthorn/SmithsonianTo this day, no one knows exactly what happened to the Sodder children after their family home burned down in 1945.

events.title: The Afghan-Soviet War Begins
events.description: The Afghan-Soviet War, a nine-year conflict fought between the Soviet Army and anti-communist Muslim guerrillas (the Mujahideen), begins when the Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan to prop up the country's faltering communist government against a growing insurgency.

events.title: Susan Berman, Victim Of Robert Durst, Is Found Dead In Her Home
events.description: Susan Berman, a journalist and mafia boss's daughter, is found dead of a gunshot wound to the head in her home in Los Angeles. The court would later convict Robert Durst, real estate heir and Berman's best friend, of the murder in 2021.

events.title: Laci Peterson Vanishes
events.description: Zuma PressThough Laci Peterson's husband Scott initially told police he had been golfing the day she vanished, he soon claimed he had gone fishing — and his story only disintegrated further from there.

events.title: Biographer And Forger Lee Israel Dies
events.description: Lee Israel, famous for her forgeries of letters "written" by notable public figures, dies of cancer at 75 years old. Once a biographer, Israel turned to selling forgeries to make money after one of her books didn't sell. She remained proud of her forgeries until her death.

events.title: CE: Charlemagne Is Crowned "Emperor Of The Romans"
events.description: Charlemagne is crowned "Emperor of the Romans" by Pope Leo III at St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. The sparked the beginning of a long line of Holy Roman Emperors that lasted until the 19th century. He became emperor for his efforts in ruthlessly spreading Christianity through central Europe.

events.title: William The Conqueror Is Crowned King of England
events.description: William the Conqueror, also known as William the Bastard, is crowned the next king of England after a successful invasion from Normandy. After sailing over the English Channel, William's forces faced those of the current English king, Harold Godwinson. Godwinson eventually died in battle and William took over the kingdom.

events.title: George Washington Crosses The Delaware River
events.description: The Metropolitan Museum of ArtWashington Crossing the Delaware by Emanuel Leutze. 1851.

events.title: The Great Jamaican Slave Revolt Begins
events.description: On Christmas Day, enslaved individuals in British-controlled Jamaica began a strike against plantation owners, asking for a working wage and more free time. This revolt eventually sparked the Baptist War and ended in early January 1832. Their demands were not met. Slavery was later outlawed by British Parliament in 1838.

events.title: Humphrey Bogart Is Born
events.description: American actor Humphrey Bogart is born in New York City. He began his career by acting in Broadway shows, and his breakthrough movie roles came with the films High Sierra and The Maltese Falcon in 1941. However, he's best known for his leading role in Casablanca alongside actress Ingrid Bergman. Bogart was married four times, most famously to Lauren Bacall. He died of esophageal cancer in 1957 at the age of 57.

events.title: The World War I Christmas Truce
events.description: WikipediaThe London News' illustration of the Christmas Truce: "British and German Soldiers Arm-in-Arm Exchanging Headgear: A Christmas Truce between Opposing Trenches."

events.title: James Brown Dies
events.description: James Brown, the "Godfather of Soul," dies at 73 years old in Atlanta, Georgia.

events.title: Death of Eartha Kitt
events.description: Actress, dancer, and singer Eartha Kitt dies colon cancer at the age of 81. Kitt played Catwoman in the 1960s Batman TV show, and was perhaps best known for her 1953 song Santa Baby. She was also a staunch activist of various social causes, including advocating for peace during the Vietnam War and supporting the right to same-sex marriage.

events.title: Dakota Warriors Are Executed In A Mass Hanging
events.description: TwitterAn illustration of the custom scaffold built to hang 38 Dakota warriors at once.

events.title: Mary Ann Bevan, "The Ugliest Woman In The World," Dies
events.description: Mary Ann Bevan, the "Ugliest Woman in the World," dies in England. Bevan lived a relatively normal childhood in the outskirts of London. It wasn't until her adult years that a rare disfiguring disease began manifesting. Her limbs began to grow disproportionately, causing her to lose any chance of regular employment. Bevan used her disability to her advantage by joining traveling sideshows and circuses to pay her bills. In just two years, Bevan earned the equivalent of $1.6 million in 2022 for her work, a sum which she used to pay for her children's education.

events.title: The Famous Flamingo Hotel And Casino Opens In Las Vegas
events.description: The famous Flamingo Hotel and Casino operated by mobster Bugsy Siegel opens in Las Vegas.

events.title: The Rendlesham Forest Incident
events.description: People in Suffolk, England report seeing unexplained lights in the sky above Rendlesham Forest. The strange lights were initially spotted outside of a U.S. Air Force base, though even some military personnel described the event as a UFO sighting. Over the years, the incident has been attributed to a nearby lighthouse, bright stars, and even a fireball, but it's still remembered as "Britain's Roswell."

events.title: Dian Fossey Dies
events.description: Dian Fossey poses in front of the gorilla exhibit at the American Museum of Natural History.

events.title: The Indian Ocean Tsunami Leaves More Than 200,000 Dead
events.description: A suburb of Banda Aceh on the Indonesian island of Sumatra after the tsunami struck.

events.title: The Hagia Sophia Is Consecrated
events.description: The 1,500-year-old Hagia Sophia in Istanbul, Turkey.

events.title: Louis Pasteur Is Born
events.description: Louis Pasteur, the scientist who discovered the process of pasteurization, is born in Dole, France. Throughout his career, Pasteur also helped develop vaccines for anthrax and rabies as well as the underlying principles of germ theory. He's been called the "father of microbiology" and is credited with saving countless lives due to his contributions to vaccines, medical hygiene, and public health.

events.title: Radio City Music Hall Opens
events.description: New York City's famous Radio City Music Hall opens as part of the new Rockefeller Center complex. John D. Rockefeller Jr. was the mastermind behind the Art Deco building, which was meant to be a place where regular New Yorkers could go to experience entertainment.

events.title: Pam Hupp Murders Her Best Friend
events.description: Pam Hupp murders her best friend, Betsy Faria, in Troy, Missouri. Ross Faria, Betsy's husband, went to check on his wife the night she was murdered. Betsy was supposed to catch a ride home from chemotherapy with Pam Hupp, but when Ross entered their home, he found Betsy bloody and slumped against the front of their sofa.

events.title: Carrie Fisher Dies
events.description: Sunset Boulevard/Corbis via Getty ImagesCarrie Fisher as Princess Leia in Star Wars, alongside Mark Hamill (left) and Harrison Ford (right).

events.title: The Original Westminster Abbey Is Consecrated
events.description: Westminster Abbey, England's most famous church, is consecrated in London. Construction had begun in 1042 after Edward the Confessor, one of the last Anglo-Saxon kings, ordered its construction. He died just a week after its consecration and was buried there. In 1066, the coronation of William the Conqueror took place in the Abbey. Finally, in the 13th century, the original structure was redesigned into the Gothic masterpiece known the world over today.

events.title: Rob Roy MacGregor Dies
events.description: Scottish outlaw and folk hero Rob Roy MacGregor dies in Perthshire, Scotland. He's remembered as a Scottish Robin Hood, though that reputation was exaggerated by Sir Walter Scott in his 1818 novel Rob Roy.

events.title: Messina Earthquake
events.description: Underwood & UnderwoodThe 1908 Messina earthquake was the most destructive earthquake to ever strike Europe.

events.title: Stan Lee Is Born
events.description: Stan Lee at Phoenix Comicon in 2011.

events.title: Japanese Sumo Association Is Founded
events.description: The Japanese Sumo Association is founded. The association standardized the sport and organized tournaments for sumo wrestlers across Japan.

events.title: President Nixon Signs The Endangered Species Act
events.description: U.S. President Richard Nixon signs the Endangered Species Act (ESA). After declaring conservation efforts inadequate, Nixon asked Congress to write new legislation that would protect the United States' most vulnerable plants and animals. The act prevented humans from killing, harming, or harassing endangered species. The ESA is monitored and enforced by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) and the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS).

events.title: Ronald Gene Simmons Is Arrested
events.description: Ronald Gene Simmons killed 14 of his family members and two other people in Arkansas in 1987.

events.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard Is Released From Prison
events.description: Gypsy Rose Blanchard is released from prison after serving eight years of her ten year sentence. She was convicted of second degree murder following the slaying of her mother, Dee Dee Blanchard, who had been subjecting her to unnecessary medical procedures and medications since birth.

events.title: Thomas Becket Is Assassinated
events.description: English nobleman Thomas Becket is murdered in Canterbury Cathedral by followers of King Henry II of England. Becket, who was serving as Archbishop of Canterbury at the time, had recently been involved in a small conflict with the king. The ruler apparently said something that his knights construed as an order to kill Becket — so they did. Upon seeing his killers enter the cathedral, Becket reportedly said, "I am no traitor and I am ready to die."

events.title: Pocahontas Pleads For John Smith's Life
events.description: A 19th-century depiction of Pocahontas, also known as Matoaka, saving the life of Captain John Smith.

events.title: Wounded Knee Massacre
events.description: Nearly 300 Lakota Native Americans are slaughtered by the United States Army in what's known as the Wounded Knee Massacre or the Battle of Wounded Knee. The soldiers were attempting to disarm the Lakota reservation in South Dakota to ease the fears of settlers who worried the tribe was going to attack them. Exactly how the massacre began is unclear, hundreds of Lakota men, women, and children were killed.

events.title: Ireland Is Founded
events.description: The state of Ireland is established by the Constitution of Ireland. The constitution granted religious rights to citizens of Ireland and delineated the new government. Ireland would have a president and two legislative houses, a House of Representatives and a Senate. The constitution also recognized Northern Ireland as a separate territory in which Ireland did not have governing power. The constitution was passed with 57% of participants voting in favor.

events.title: Richard Chase Commits His First Murder
events.description: The mugshot of serial killer Richard Chase.

events.title: President Jimmy Carter Dies
events.description: President Jimmy Carter, the oldest U.S. president to ever live, dies at his home in Plains, Georgia.

events.title: U.S.S. Monitor Sinks
events.description: The American warship U.S.S. Monitor sinks off the coast of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina during a storm. Earlier that year, the Monitor had taken part in one of the most famous battles in naval history when it faced the C.S.S. Virginia, previously known as the Merrimack, at the Battle of Hampton Roads. The ship was being towed through the rough open sea when some caulking came loose and water entered the hull. Many of the Monitor's crew members were rescued, but 16 died as it sank.

events.title: The Iroquois Theatre Fire
events.description: The aftermath of the deadly Iroquois Theatre Fire.

events.title: Grigori Rasputin Is Assassinated
events.description: Rasputin with Empress Alexandra Feodorovna and her children.

events.title: Notorious Gangster Al Capone Marries His Wife, Mae
events.description: Al Capone, the infamous Chicago mobster known as "Scarface," marries his wife, Mae. They stayed together until Al Capone's death in 1947.

events.title: Dennis Nilsen Kills His First Victim
events.description: Dennis Nilsen was sometimes called the "British Jeffrey Dahmer."

events.title: Saddam Hussein Is Executed
events.description: Saddam Hussein immediately after his capture on December 13, 2003.

events.title: Commodus Is Assassinated
events.description: Commodus, the son of Marcus Aurelius and the emperor of Rome, is assassinated.

events.title: Arthur Guinness Begins Brewing Beer
events.description: Arthur Guinness signs a 9,000-year lease on St. James' Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland and begins brewing Guinness beer. He agreed to pay £45 per year for the unused building, and 10 years later he exported his first shipment of ale to Britain. Guinness first sold the dark porter for which he's best known in 1778. Today, the company he founded is worth billions and is one of the most recognizable beer brands in the world.

events.title: First New Year's Eve Ball Drop In Times Square
events.description: The famous ball that drops in New York City's Times Square every year makes its first descent. The first ball was made of wood, iron, and 100 light bulbs. It had been built by Jacob Starr, a young metalworker who had immigrated to the United States from Ukraine. Waiters at restaurants surrounding the square wore top hats with "1908" emblazoned in small light bulbs as part of the celebrations.

events.title: Roberto Clemente Dies
events.description: Roberto Clemente, famous baseball player and humanitarian, dies in a plane crash. Originally from Puerto Rico, Clemente rose to fame as an incredibly talented baseball player. In the year of his death, Clemente had reach his 3,000th hit while playing his last season with the Pittsburgh Pirates. When he wasn't playing baseball, Clemente was involved in charity organizations and humanitarian efforts, primarily in the Caribbean. After an earthquake hit Nicaragua on December 23, Clemente set out to bring relief supplies to victims of the natural disaster. Tragically, he and four others lost their lives when their cargo plane crashed off the coast of Puerto Rico en route to Nicaragua.

events.title: Ricky Nelson Dies
events.description: Ricky Nelson was staging a "comeback tour" when he tragically died in a plane crash.

events.title: Brandon Teena Is Murdered
events.description: Brandon Teena was just 21 years old when he was killed.

events.title: Michael Kennedy Dies In A Skiing Accident
events.description: Michael Kennedy dies in a skiing accident. Kennedy was one of eleven children of RFK and his wife, Ethel Kennedy. He led a successful career in activism before a sex scandal ended it all. During a family vacation, Kennedy was playing football on skis when he collided with a tree. He was pronounced dead a few hours later.

events.title: Jade Janks Murders Her Stepfather
events.description: Jade Janks murders her stepfather, Tom Merriman, after claiming to have found nude photos of herself on his personal computer.
